body:
## Summary Two related fixes to the photo URL handling. ### The bug A URL pointing at a photo id the gallery doesn't have (typo, stale bookmark, deleted photo, etc.) used to spin on a "Loading" screen indefinitely. By the time that branch in `Gallery/index.tsx` runs, photos are already loaded — the missing-photo case got the same fallback as the still-loading case. ### The fix - If the URL param matches a photo's `originalFilename` (camera filename) anywhere in the gallery, redirect to that photo's canonical URL. This is the "pre-rename bookmark" + "shared the camera filename not the URL" use case the operator's archive sometimes produces. - Otherwise, navigate to the month view (`gallery.path(year, month)`). The user lands somewhere usable instead of staring at a spinner. Both use react-router's `` so the history stack stays clean. ### What changed - `PhotoModel`: new `originalFilename(): string | undefined` getter + the matching field in `PhotoData`. The server already emits `originalFilename` in the Photo response (`additionalProperties: true` on the typed schema let it flow through unconfigured); the client just wasn't reading it. - `Gallery/index.tsx` photo-not-found branch: the new fallback chain replacing the spinning `
{t("loading")}
`. ### Not in scope - Empty / filtered-out month view: confirmed already handled — line 375 `!gallery.includesPhotos()` → `` with the filter bar above, so applying filters that exclude every photo renders the empty surface cleanly. No change. ## Test plan - [x] `npm run typecheck` + `lint` clean. - [x] `npm test` green (977 tests). - [x] Visit `/////.jpg` → redirects to `////`. - [x] Visit `/////.jpg` (a filename that exists in the archive but isn't the current id) → redirects to the canonical URL for that photo. - [x] Sanity: valid photo URL still renders the photo modal as before. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jr-kenny
body:
## Why
Reviewer feedback on the submission: *"X access can be fragile, so reliability depends on validators consistently reaching the public metadata source."* This PR removes the consensus-flakiness so independent validators reliably reach the same verification result.

## What was actually flaky
- `validator_fn` required validators to agree on **live view counts** (`view_bucket` + `meets_threshold`). Views change between each validator's fetch → disagreement near any boundary → consensus fails. Self-inflicted, not just "X being down."
- **Single source** (`api.fxtwitter.com`), no fallback.
- **No transient/permanent error split** — one node's timeout vs another's success = disagreement.

## Changes (`contracts/TweetLaunchpad.py`)
- **Multi-source fetch with fallback**: `fxtwitter` → `vxtwitter`, normalized to the same fields.
- **Consensus on immutable facts only**: `tweet_id`, `author`, `author_name`, `text_hash`. Views excluded from agreement.
- **View threshold is now an advisory snapshot** (`view_bucket`), not a consensus-gated launch requirement.
- **Error classification**: 404/410 = deterministic rejection (all agree); 429/5xx/timeout = transient → launch asks the user to retry instead of locking a permanent failure.
- **Tests**: added `gltest` direct tests (valid, source-fallback, low-views-still-launches, deleted→reject, transient→retry, duplicate).
- README documents the reliability design.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `pytest tests/direct/ -v` (6 passing)
- [ ] Deploy to Bradbury, register a real tweet, confirm verification + that a low-view tweet still launches

author: imcbeth
body:
## Summary
- Split the combined Istio egress rule in 4 namespace NetworkPolicies: **kafka**, **strimzi-system**, **flink-operator**, **flink-demo**
- Port 15008 (ztunnel HBONE) now uses a **bare** egress rule with no `to` selector
- Ports 15012/15017 (istiod xDS + webhook) retain the namespace-scoped `to: istio-system` rule

## Root Cause
ztunnel sends HBONE from **within the pod's network namespace** (using the pod's source IP), so pod NetworkPolicies DO apply to HBONE traffic. However, ztunnel's HBONE destination is the **broker pod's IP on port 15008** — not an `istio-system` pod IP. The namespace-scoped egress rule `to: istio-system, port: 15008` therefore never matched actual HBONE traffic.

This caused the Kafka topic-operator to fail connecting to the Kafka broker after PR #634 enrolled the kafka namespace in Istio Ambient mesh. Confirmed via ztunnel access logs:
```
error="connection timed out, maybe a NetworkPolicy is blocking HBONE port 15008: deadline has elapsed"
src.workload="kafka-cluster-entity-operator" dst.addr=192.168.186.217:15008 (broker pod IP)
```

## Test plan
- [ ] After merge and ArgoCD sync (~3 min), verify `kubectl get pods -n kafka` shows entity-operator `1/1 Running`
- [ ] Verify `kubectl get kafka -n kafka kafka-cluster` shows `READY: True`

body:

## General information

This PR has been created by iobroker-bot. Please review the changes carefully and merge the PR if review is ok.

Feel free to contact me (@ioBroker-Bot) if you have any questions or feel that a PR is faulty. Please open an issue at repository https://github.com/ioBroker/ioBroker.repochecker to report a faulty PR.

And **THANKS A LOT** for maintaining this adapter from me and all users.
*Let's work together for the best user experience.*

*your*
*ioBroker Check and Service Bot*

@mcm1957 for evidence

## Changes provided by this PR

This PR resolves warning **W8917** logged by the ioBroker repository checker.

### What this PR does

This PR adds an ignore rule to the Dependabot configuration in `.github/dependabot.yml` to prevent Dependabot from automatically proposing major version bumps for the `@types/node` package.

The following change is applied to every `updates:` block that specifies `package-ecosystem: npm` and `directory: /` or `directories: ['**/*']`:

```yaml
ignore:
  - dependency-name: "@types/node"
    update-types:
      - "version-update:semver-major"
```

### Why this change is needed

The `@types/node` package provides TypeScript type definitions for the Node.js runtime API. The major version of `@types/node` that an adapter should use is determined by the **lowest** major Node.js version the adapter supports. The lowest supported Node.js version is specified in the `engines.node` field of `package.json`.

Allowing Dependabot to automatically bump `@types/node` to a newer major version would introduce type definitions for Node.js APIs that are not available in the minimum supported Node.js version. This can lead to incorrect type checking and potential runtime errors on older Node.js installations. Therefore, major version updates of `@types/node` must always be reviewed manually and aligned with any intentional change to the minimum supported Node.js version.

### Reference

- [ioBroker Repository Checker – Warning W8917](https://github.com/ioBroker/ioBroker.repochecker)
- [Dependabot ignore configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference#ignore)

author: storminrh
body:
## What this does

Adds a build-time guard so no API route can ship without stating who is allowed to call it.

Every route handler under `src/app/api/` now carries a one-line marker next to its handler declaring its authorization class — one of `public`, `auth` (login required), `admin`, or `cron`. A new test walks every route file and fails CI if any route is missing that declaration or uses an unknown class. The result: a future route added without an explicit class fails the build instead of slipping through unguarded.

This only records the classification that already holds today — no route's actual access rules changed. It mirrors the spirit of the existing render-mode classification gate, but runs purely off the source (no build artifacts needed) as part of the normal test run.

The marker lives next to the code it describes rather than in a central list, so each new route is forced to declare its own class where it's written, and there's no separate table to keep in sync.

## Test plan

- `pnpm test` — full suite green (604 passed, 1 DB-gated test skipped); the new guard contributes one row per route plus a non-empty check.
- `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` — both clean.
- Verified the guard actually fails by temporarily: (a) adding a route with no marker → fails naming that file, (b) setting an invalid class → fails "invalid class", (c) adding a second marker to one file → fails "more than one marker". All three reverted.

Not user-facing → no CHANGELOG entry.

author: stid
body:
## Context

Redesign of the **CPU State** and **Execution** cards in the debugger Overview tab,
using a Claude Design–assisted mockup as the visual target. The original cards were
visually flat (labels, values, and the cycle counter all at similar weight), so nothing
guided the eye. This gives them a clear hierarchy while keeping the data contract and
design-token system intact.

## What changed

- **Extracted** the two inline cards (~146 lines) out of `DebuggerLayout.tsx` into
  prop-driven presentational components — `CpuStateCard` and `ExecutionCard` — which take
  `debugInfo` and are unit-testable in isolation. Net code is roughly flat.
- **CPU State**: segmented **A/X/Y/SP register rail** (label-over-value), a clickable
  **PC pill** (reuses `AddressLink` with context menu / run-to-cursor), a labeled
  **flag-chip strip** with distinct ON / clear / unused (`-`,`B`) states, and a
  de-emphasized purple cycle counter.
- **Execution**: divider-separated rows with a **status dot** on IRQ/NMI; prominent
  semibold title and emphasized (semibold) values so it reads as redesigned, not just
  re-bordered.
- Every value maps to an **existing design token** — zero new tokens, no hardcoded colors.

## Design decisions

- The flag section stays labeled **"FLAGS"**, not the mockup's "STATUS FLAGS":
  the **AC-7 guard test** (`DebuggerLayout-debugger-exec-bar.vitest.test.tsx`) deliberately
  forbids reusing "Status" as a label here. Honored the existing decision rather than
  reverting it.
- Titles bumped to `text-base`/semibold (closest token to the mockup's 20px); the change
  is scoped to these two cards — sibling cards (Memory Map, Stack, …) keep their current
  title size. Happy to harmonize those in a follow-up if desired.

## Verification

- `yarn test:ci` (lint + type-check + vitest): **785 passed, 1 skipped** (the WASM
  benchmark that skips in Node, as documented).
- 7 new behavioral tests for the cards (flag SET→`success`, unused→`disabled`,
  IRQ/NMI ACTIVE→`warning`, register-rail values, PC renders as a button, value emphasis).
- Verified live in-browser against the mockup (register rail, flag chips, status dots,
  typography hierarchy all match).
- Version bumped `4.51.3` → `4.51.4` (refactor → patch).

## Engine parity

UI-only change — no CPU/engine code touched, JS↔WASM parity unaffected.

author: tangletools
body:
## Problem

The `auto-sync-master-with-develop` workflow ran `git merge --ff-only <develop>` onto master. That fails permanently once `master` diverges from `develop` — which happens whenever a develop→master promotion lands as a PR (a merge/squash commit on master that isn't on develop). This is exactly what stalled the **tangle-cloud v0.0.4** release: the `[RELEASE]` commit landed on develop, auto-sync failed on `--ff-only`, and the promotion had to be done by hand (PR #3254).

## Fix

Use `git merge --no-ff` (with a message). It always succeeds, is non-destructive (master keeps its own commits; develop's release commits merge in), and still changes `CHANGELOG.md` so `release-dapps.yml` deploys. Future `[RELEASE]` pushes to develop will auto-sync to master without manual promotion.

## Note
Surfaced alongside a second pre-existing infra issue (separate fix, needs a secret rotation): `create-dapp-release`'s `secrets.REPO_TOKEN` is expired — the release-tag step fails with "Bad credentials." That only tags a GitHub release (the CF Pages deploy is git-integration-driven), but it should be rotated.

YAML-only change (outside the prettier/nx-lint globs); pushed through the pre-push hook.

author: marxtu
body:
## What

Adds email/password **authentication** and a **Firestore** implementation of the history/favourites repositories, so a signed-in user's data can sync to the cloud. Built and fully unit/widget-tested **without any real Firebase project or credential** (mocks), and the running app is deliberately **left on M5.1 local storage** — connecting a real project is a separate, documented step.

## Layers

**Phase A — backend-agnostic auth** (no Firebase deps; survives a backend swap):
- `AppUser`, `AuthRepository` interface + `AuthException`
- `AuthCubit` (auth-state stream → unknown/signedOut/signedIn; sign-in/up/out with submitting + friendly errors)
- `SignInScreen` (email/password, sign-in ↔ create-account toggle, loading + error states)

**Phase B — Firebase implementations** (mock-tested):
- `FirebaseAuthRepository implements AuthRepository` (maps `User`→`AppUser`, `FirebaseAuthException`→friendly messages)
- `FirestoreRunHistoryRepository` / `FirestoreFavoritesRepository` implementing the existing M5.1 interfaces, scoped to `/users/{uid}/runs` and `/users/{uid}/favorites/{routeKey}` — matching `firestore.rules`

## Not switched on yet (by design)

`main.dart`, the router, and `dependencies.dart` are untouched; no `Firebase.initializeApp`; no `firebase_options.dart`. The app keeps running on local storage and web screenshots keep working. The exact activation steps (flutterfire configure → guarded init → `AuthGate` → repo swap → enable Email/Password → deploy rules) are in `docs/level-3-implementation/m5-2-going-live.md`, and `firestore.rules` + `firebase.json` are committed for `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules`.

## Quality

- `flutter test` → **111 passing** (auth cubit incl. a sign-out regression test, sign-in widget tests, FirebaseAuth mock tests, Firestore fake tests incl. cross-user isolation).
- `flutter analyze` → clean.
- Two independent reviews (spec + code-quality); fixed before merge: sign-out now clears `state.user` (copyWith-null bug), `isClosed` guards on post-await emits, `signOut` routed through error handling, plus `operation-not-allowed`/`too-many-requests` mappings.

## Resolved versions

firebase_core ^4.9.0, firebase_auth ^6.5.1, cloud_firestore ^6.4.1; dev: fake_cloud_firestore ^4.1.1, firebase_auth_mocks ^0.15.2.

author: ppxd
body:
## Summary

- A `flow.loop` body node that fails with no error route of its own has always failed the whole loop. That's the right default (Dify's "Terminate on error"), but there was no way to let a loop ride out a transient/partial failure.
- Add a loop-level `errorHandling` policy: **terminate** (default, unchanged) or **continue**. Under continue, a failed pass is abandoned — its loop-variable updates and the termination check are skipped (error-tainted state never threads forward), the failure is still recorded per-iteration in the ledger, and the loop moves on.
- The loop now reports `failedIterations` alongside `iterations`, so a continue-loop surfaces how many passes failed.
- A node that has its **own** error edge is still routed there first, regardless of this policy — continue only governs an otherwise-unhandled body failure. Parsed leniently in `LoopPlan` (unknown ⇒ terminate, the safe default).
- Frontend: an "Error handling" selector in the Loop inspector.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit: `LoopPlanTests` pins the error-handling parse + max-iterations clamp tables (Theory) — 634 unit pass
- [x] Integration: `LoopFlowTests` adds all-passes-fail→loop Success (`failedIterations==max`) and partial-fail-then-a-passing-pass-terminates; existing terminate + error-edge tests still green — 176 workflow integration pass
- [x] Frontend: `LoopEditor.test.tsx` selector spec — 245 vitest pass; tsc + eslint clean

author: kingfink
body:
## What

`scripts/release.sh` failed on the first real `v0.1.0` release with:

```
tag v0.1.0 exists locally but has not been pushed ... please push it before continuing
```

The script created the git tag locally and *then* called `gh release create`. But `gh` only auto-pushes a tag it creates itself — when a same-named local tag already exists unpushed, it refuses. (This was a flaw in the earlier "anti-dangling-tag" hardening.)

## Fix

Don't pre-create a local tag. Pass `--target HEAD` so `gh release create` creates the tag on the remote atomically as part of publishing — the tag appears only if the release succeeds, so a failed run never leaves a dangling tag. The existing-release branch still refreshes the `.mcpb` asset idempotently.

## Note

The `v0.1.0` release itself is **already published** (recovered manually) with `2do-mcp.mcpb` attached, and verified working via `uvx --from git+...@v0.1.0 2do-mcp doctor`. This PR only fixes the script for future releases. I re-ran the fixed script against the existing release and confirmed it exits 0 via the idempotent refresh path.

author: vusys
body:
## Summary

Adds a `reorderChildren()` primitive so drag-and-drop UIs can re-shuffle a sibling group in a single atomic CASE-WHEN UPDATE instead of N `insertAfterNode()` calls. The existing `lft` column remains the authoritative sibling sequence — no new column, no second source of truth.

Design doc: `SIBLING_ORDER_DESIGN.md` (scratchpad, not in source).

## Public API

All on `HasTreeMutation`:

- `$parent->reorderChildren(array $idsInOrder)` — strict; missing, extra, or duplicate keys throw `InvalidSiblingOrderException`. Accepts ids or models via a normaliser.
- `$parent->reorderChildrenBy(string|Closure $key)` — sugar that sorts siblings by a column name or callback.
- `$child->moveToSiblingPosition(int $position)` — 1-indexed, matches `up()`/`down()`.
- `Model::reorderSiblings($parent, $ids)` — static wrapper.

New event: `SiblingsReordered { parent, idsInOrder, rowsAffected }`.

## How it works

One CASE-WHEN UPDATE per reorder. For every row strictly between `parent.lft` and `parent.rgt`, add the containing sibling's `delta` (new_start − old_start) to both `lft` and `rgt`. `depth` and `parent_id` are unchanged because siblings stay at the same depth and ancestry doesn't move.

- **Identity reorders are a no-op** — supplying the current order skips the UPDATE entirely.
- **Aggregates are stable by construction** — reordering doesn't change ancestry, so ancestor aggregates don't change. The raw UPDATE goes through `TreeMutationBuilder`, bypassing Eloquent `saving`/`saved` so the aggregate listener never fires.
- **Scoped trees** — the UPDATE predicate includes the parent's full scope tuple; other partitions are untouched.

## Notable test coverage

- 7 files under `tests/Feature/Mutation/Reorder/` covering the contract from §5/§8 of the design.
- `ReorderFuzzerTest` — 1000 assertions over random permutations, verifies integrity and aggregate stability after each shuffle.
- `ReorderScopedTest::test_multi_scope_reorder_does_not_leak_into_other_partitions` — builds 4 partitions across `tenant_id × site_id` and asserts every other partition is bit-identical after a reorder. Closes the known `.= → =` mutation-escape gap for the scope-loop predicate.

## Deviations from the design doc

- **§7 step 2 / §10 step 5 ("rework `swap()` to share the emitter"): skipped.** There is no public `swap()` in this package — `up()`/`down()` already factor the swap via `moveAndEmitSiblingSwap()` + `NodesSwapped`. Rewiring it would either mean adding a new public method (scope creep) or rewriting `up()`/`down()` for no payoff.
- **§6.7 (materialised paths): N/A.** This package doesn't store a path column; the invariant holds by construction, no test needed.

## Test plan

- [x] Package suite passes: **1823 tests / 21736 assertions** (+33 vs master). 11 pre-existing skips, no new ones.
- [x] Fuzzer passes: **10 tests / 1000 assertions** on `ReorderFuzzerTest`.
- [x] PHPStan level 9 clean on touched files.
- [x] Pint + Rector clean on touched files.

- [ ] Reviewer eyes on the multi-scope assertion in `ReorderScopedTest`.

author: deltakosh
body:
## Problem

The demos landing-page background effect (`lab/src/demos/landing-bg.ts`) showed a vertical bar drifting left and right across the screen.

## Cause

`palette()` was a non-cyclic ramp (RED -> CORAL -> LIGHT -> CORAL) but is sampled through `fract()`. At every `x=1` wrap the colour jumped hard from CORAL back to RED. Since `hue` depends on `p.x` (horizontal position) and time, that discontinuity rendered as a moving vertical seam.

## Fix

Close the palette loop (RED -> CORAL -> LIGHT -> **RED**) so the `fract()` wrap is seamless. Verified visually via WebGPU capture over several frames — ribbons now flow continuously with no seam.

author: emirongrr
body:
**Motivation**

The txpool validation path currently enforces `POST_OSAKA_GAS_LIMIT_CAP` for every post-Osaka transaction. However, consensus validation only applies this cap while Osaka is active and Amsterdam is not active.

This makes the txpool reject otherwise valid Amsterdam transactions,even though the same transactions would be accepted when included in a valid Amsterdam block.

This is not a consensus split, but a mempool policy / fork-gating inconsistency.
**Description**

This PR aligns txpool validation with the consensus validation path by disabling the Osaka transaction gas cap once Amsterdam is active.

Ethrex consensus validation only enforces the Osaka transaction gas cap while Osaka is active and Amsterdam is not active.

https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethrex/blob/37669b7c357f43bd81431e993fed644ebf99cd4a/crates/common/validation.rs#L48

```rust
        if chain_config.is_osaka_activated(block.header.timestamp)
            && !chain_config.is_amsterdam_activated(block.header.timestamp)
        {
            verify_transaction_max_gas_limit(block)?;
        }
```
**Geth**

https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/046a10e8a79656273cfc535589085763f8b75419/core/txpool/validation.go#L95

Geth applies the Osaka transaction gas cap only while Osaka is active and Amsterdam is not active.

```rust
	if rules.IsOsaka && !rules.IsAmsterdam && tx.Gas() > params.MaxTxGas {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w (cap: %d, tx: %d)", core.ErrGasLimitTooHigh, params.MaxTxGas, tx.Gas())
	}
```

Before:

```rust
if config.is_osaka_activated(header.timestamp)
    && tx.gas_limit() > POST_OSAKA_GAS_LIMIT_CAP
```
After:
```rust
if config.is_osaka_activated(header.timestamp)
    && !config.is_amsterdam_activated(header.timestamp)
    && tx.gas_limit() > POST_OSAKA_GAS_LIMIT_CAP
```
Closes #6758

body:
## Stop ephemeral-registration churn + GC migration

### Why there are 2,000 agents
The stdio bridge minted a fresh id `agent-<host>-<pid>-<base36ts>` per process and auto-registered it whenever `FROM`/`MCP_FROM` was unset, so every CLI launch / reconnect left a throwaway row forever. On the live DB that was **~1,949 of 2,003 registrations (97%)** — e.g. `stdio-bridge-ErikaDesktop` alone had 1,297. This is what made `get_agent_status` huge and "who's online" meaningless.

### Two-part fix (both needed, or it refills)
1. **Bridge (`mcp-stdio-http-bridge.cjs`):** when `FROM`/`MCP_FROM` is unset, reuse a **stable per-host id** (`agent-<host>`) persisted to `~/.neural-mcp/bridge-identity-<host>.json` (override dir via `MCP_BRIDGE_STATE_DIR`) instead of minting a new one per process. Reconnects keep the same identity. Env override still wins. Verified: two processes return the same `agent-<host>` id, no pid/timestamp.
2. **GC migration (`src/migrations/004-gc-ephemeral-registrations.mjs`):** dry-run by default; deletes ONLY ids matching the ephemeral GLOB `agent-*-[0-9]*-*` that are also stale (not updated within `--retain-days`, default 7). Every stable/named agent is preserved; currently-active bridges (last 7d) are kept.

### Validation (dry-run on a copy of the live DB)
- `total 1997 → after 232`: deletes **1,765** (ephemeral + stale), keeps **54 stable/named + 178 recently-active ephemeral**. Sample confirms only `agent-<host>-<pid>-<ts>` rows are targeted.
- typecheck + build clean; full suite green (same 3 pre-existing intra-file failures).

### Deploy (separate, deliberate)
Bridge change ships on the next image rebuild (and clients pick it up on reconnect). The GC migration EDITS live data — run manually with the container stopped, after a backup, like migration 003:
```
node src/migrations/004-gc-ephemeral-registrations.mjs /app/data/unified-platform.db            # dry run
node src/migrations/004-gc-ephemeral-registrations.mjs /app/data/unified-platform.db --apply    # then apply
```

body:
`mod_17_TX_SFNConflictResolution.bas` was classifying every equal-SFN chunk as a Cest and resolving immediately, which over-processed normal groups. This change aligns control flow with the intended strategy: discover all Cests in a contiguous adjacent/equal-SFN pool first, then resolve inside-out, then flush once.

- **Conflict detection now keys off actual violations**
  - Replaced “equal-SFN pair” trigger with group-level Cest detection (`IsRangeCest`) so non-violating groups are skipped and scanning advances by groups.

- **Pool construction now matches contiguous adjacent/equal SFN region**
  - Pool starts only after a true Cest is found.
  - Pool bounds expand around that Cest across contiguous rows where SFN deltas are `<= 1` (equal or adjacent), not just equal-only runs.

- **Cest discovery and resolution are now separated**
  - `BuildPoolCests` scans pool groups and records only violating groups as Cests.
  - No resolution is attempted during discovery.

- **Inside-out resolution is applied after full discovery**
  - `ResolveEntirePool` resolves discovered Cests in inside-out order (distance to pool center), then applies tie-breaks deterministically.

- **Pool output buffering/flush semantics are explicit**
  - Added pool output staging buffer (`mPoolOutputRows` / `mPoolOutputCount`).
  - Pool rows are buffered post-resolution and flushed once per pool.

- **Required existing fixes preserved**
  - SafeDiv one-line compile-safe syntax remains unchanged.
  - Forward scan advance behavior remains (`mScanPos = mPoolRows(mPoolCount) + 1`).

```vb
' discovery first
conflictStart = FindNextConflictStart()
BuildPoolFromConflictStart conflictStart
BuildPoolCests  ' records only violating groups

' resolution second (inside-out), then single flush
ResolveEntirePool
BufferResolvedPoolToOutputBuffer
WriteResolvedPoolToOutput
```

1. Keep the SafeDiv syntax fix in place.
2. Preserve the existing scan-advance fix so the forward scan progresses correctly.
3. Rework pool/Cest handling so that:
   - A pool is created only after a Cest is actually found.

body:
## Summary

- **BUG 1 (MED, shutdown-stall)**: `broadcast_shutdown_sentinel()` silently dropped the shutdown sentinel when a subscriber queue was full (`queue.Full` was swallowed). At 30 Hz audio-level events a queue fills in ~2 s; a slow SSE consumer then stalled for the full `_SSE_POLL_TIMEOUT_SEC` (15 s) instead of disconnecting immediately — defeating the W1673/F3 shutdown-fast purpose. Fix: drain each subscriber queue before `put_nowait(None)`; buffered events are irrelevant at shutdown, the sentinel has absolute priority.

- **BUG 2 (LOW, silent-blackhole)**: `sse_stream()` parsed `event_filter` into a `set()` for blank/comma-only input (e.g. `?filter=,` or `?filter=+`). Because the guard checked `event["type"] not in allowed` against an empty set (not `None`), every event was filtered out silently — the client received only SSE keepalives with no error or log message. Fix: treat an empty-after-parse set as `None` (no filter = receive all) and emit a warning log.

## Files changed

- `KrabEar/backend/event_bus.py` — two targeted fixes, both with inline explanatory comments
- `KrabEar/tests/test_event_bus.py` — +7 regression tests (fail-before / pass-after); `import threading` added at module level

  ## 검증

author: d-sorgclaudeagent[bot]
body:
## Summary

Sub-PR A of #6013 — the **additive protocol + host-widget foundation** for making embedded launcher tabs closeable-in-background and pop-out-able. Per-tool adapter rollout is **Sub-PR B**, tracked separately.

## New protocol hooks

Added a new, additive `BackgroundableTool` protocol in `src/shared/python/launcher_embed/contract.py` (package version bumped `1.0.0` → `1.1.0`) with four **optional** methods:

| hook | default | meaning |
|------|---------|---------|
| `pause(self) -> None` | no-op | host backgrounded the widget |
| `resume(self) -> None` | no-op | widget re-surfaced (reopen/refocus) |
| `can_background(self) -> bool` | `True` | `False` → legacy cleanup-on-close |
| `detach_to_window(self) -> bool` | `True` | `False` → pin-only (no pop-out) |

It is kept **separate** from `EmbeddableTool` deliberately: folding the hooks into the existing `runtime_checkable` protocol would have broken `isinstance(tool, EmbeddableTool)` for the ~17 existing adapters that don't implement them. Hosts resolve every hook structurally via `getattr(tool, name, default)`, so a tool may implement any subset (or none).

## `EmbeddedHostWidget` changes (`src/launchers/embedded_host.py`)

- **`tabCloseRequested` flow**: backgroundable tools now prompt **"Close (keep running)"** vs **"Destroy"**. Background-close calls `pause()` and stashes the widget hidden in `_backgrounded: dict[str, _Backgrounded]` keyed by `tool_id` (no cleanup). Destroy keeps today's `cleanup()` behaviour. Tools where `can_background()` is `False` take the legacy destroy path with no prompt.
- **Reopen via `open_tab()`**: if a backgrounded widget exists for the `tool_id`, it is re-surfaced and `resume()` is called instead of building a fresh widget (state preserved).
- **`pop_out_tab(tool_id)`**: re-parents the live widget into a fresh top-level `QMainWindow` and removes the tab. **`dock_back(tool_id)`**: reverses it; closing the popped-out window re-docks automatically.
- **Tab context menu**: right-click offers "Close (keep running)" / "Destroy" / "Pop out" (the last two gated on the relevant hooks).
- **New public API `backgrounded_tools(self) -> set[str]`** for callers like the training-controller tab.

`embedded_host.py` is 826 lines — within the 1200-line budget, so **no split was needed**.

## Tests

- New `tests/unit/launchers/test_embedded_host_backgrounding.py` (12 cases, `pytest.importorskip("PyQt6.QtWidgets")` + offscreen `QApplication` + dummy adapters): background-close stashes + pauses; reopen re-surfaces + resumes; destroy calls cleanup; `can_background()==False` → legacy cleanup; a hook-less legacy adapter still backgrounds; pop_out/dock_back re-parent; reopen of a popped-out tool docks it back; `detach_to_window()==False` is pin-only; `backgrounded_tools()` set semantics.
- Updated `tests/launchers/launcher_embed/test_embedded_host_edges.py::test_close_tab_via_signal` to patch the new background-vs-destroy prompt (the close button now prompts).

## Verification

- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check`: clean on all changed files.
- `mypy` on `contract.py` / `__init__.py`: clean.
- New test file: **12 passed**. Contract + edges suite: **77 passed**.
- Error-handling ratchet + file-size budget: OK.
- Pre-existing, unrelated failures left untouched: `tests/ui/launcher_embed/test_sidekick_tile.py` (`AIAssistantPanel` missing `_messages`) and `tests/docs/test_launcher_embed_doc_links.py` (broken markdown link) — both fail identically on the clean base branch.

Part of #6013 (Sub-PR A); does not close it — Sub-PR B rollout tracked separately.

author: kiranmagic7
body:
## What changed

- Tracks process-local tool availability markers (`HERMES_EXEC_ASK`, `HERMES_GATEWAY_SESSION`, `HERMES_INTERACTIVE`, `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`) in the quiet tool-definition cache key.
- Invalidates the memoized tool definitions and registry `check_fn` cache immediately when those markers change mid-process.
- Adds a regression test for the gateway-style `HERMES_EXEC_ASK` flip that should expose the `cronjob` tool after it was previously hidden.

## Why

Fixes #35561.

`cronjob` availability depends on session/gateway env markers. If `get_tool_definitions(..., quiet_mode=True)` cached the hidden result before `gateway.run` set `HERMES_EXEC_ASK=1`, the later lookup reused stale tool definitions and stale `check_fn` state, so `cronjob` stayed absent until cache expiry or manual invalidation.

## Tests

- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/tools/test_cronjob_tools.py -k 'tool_definition_cache_tracks_exec_ask_env or CronjobRequirements' -q` -> 22 passed, 35 deselected
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_cronjob_tools.py` -> 57 passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_terminal_tool_requirements.py tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py` -> 84 passed
- `.venv/bin/ruff check model_tools.py tests/tools/test_cronjob_tools.py` -> All checks passed
- `git diff --check` -> no output
- Manual reproduction script: before env flip `{'pre': []}`, after `HERMES_EXEC_ASK=1` `{'post': ['cronjob']}`

## Compatibility / risk

No public API change. The existing 30s `check_fn` TTL remains for slow external probes like Docker or optional SDK availability. This only treats session-context env markers as synchronous availability inputs, so a gateway or worker transition may do one extra availability recompute and then return to the normal cache path.

body:
## Summary
Builds the explainable market-read layer on top of the Phase-0 data layer: a hard-data signal library, a composite 0–100 market stress index with per-component decomposition, and a read-only Streamlit dashboard.

## Engine
- **`data.py` — `MarketStore`**: single read gateway for signals. Refuses any series carrying an error-severity QA flag (*no signal computes on unreconciled data*).
- **`signals/{transform,base}`**: causal-only transforms (rolling z/percentile, Wilder RSI, realized vol) + `SignalResult` contract (score in [−1,+1] + one-line attribution + provenance). Signals return **full historical series** so they're reusable, leakage-free, by the Phase-2 walk-forward backtester.
- **17 hard-data signals** across technical, volatility, credit, rates, cross-asset; each degrades gracefully when inputs are absent.
- **`stress/index.py`**: fixed expert-weight composite → 0–100 with band labels, per-component decomposition (contributions sum to the latent), and ranked top drivers.

## Surfaces
- `scripts/compute_signals.py` — text engine summary.
- `dashboard/app.py` + `scripts/run_dashboard.py` — 3-tab read-only Streamlit app (Overview / Signals / Data Health). Verified rendering in a headless browser.

## Fixes (surfaced during integration)
- **NONPOSITIVE_PRICE on yields** (Phase-0 check): zero/negative short-tenor and real yields are valid (ZIRP 2008–15 / 2020–21); the error flag was silently dropping the 3m10y curve and real-yield signals via the integrity gate. Scoped the check to price columns only.
- **Dashboard import**: `streamlit run` puts the script dir (not repo root) on `sys.path`; bootstrap the repo root so `macro_advisor` imports cleanly.

## Tests
26 pass (was 5): causality/no-look-ahead, integrity gate, signal directionality, stress aggregation + weight-renormalization.

## Verification
- `python -m pytest -q` → 26 passed
- `python scripts/compute_signals.py` → 17 signals, stress 49.9/100 (NORMAL), 0 error flags
- `streamlit run macro_advisor/dashboard/app.py` → all three tabs render (confirmed via headless screenshots)

author: copilot
body:
Resolves every MEDIUM and LOW severity bug from AUDIT.md — concurrency races, aliasing/shallow-copy hazards, security leaks, logic errors, and dropped errors. AUDIT.md and PLAN.md deleted on completion.

## Security
- **L-04** `SecureFieldHash`: was logging raw 8-byte prefix of key material; now logs SHA-256 digest prefix — sensitive input never appears in logs
- **L-03** `GenerateKeyPair` / `GenerateEd25519KeyPair` / `Ed25519PrivateKeyFromSeed`: wipe source private-key buffer after copy via `ZeroBytes`

## Concurrency / Aliasing
- **M-19** `AsyncClient.Close`: double-close panicked on closed channel; guarded with `sync.Once`
- **M-20** `deliverNotification`: `Handler` read outside lock racing a concurrent `Subscribe`; now captured under `h.mu.RLock()` before invocation
- **M-17** `ImportPreKeys`: shallow `cp := *imported` aliased caller's `KeyPair` pointers; replaced with `clonePreKeyBundle`
- **M-18** `async/storage`: three sites handing back or storing caller-owned slices (`EncryptedData`/`EncryptedPayload`); all now deep-copy with `append([]byte(nil), src...)`
- **L-12** `dhRatchetStep`: mutated `rk/ckr/nr/ns/pn/dhr` before fallible KDF calls leaving partial state on error; now commits atomically from locals
- **L-13** `GetPeer`/`GetPeerList`/`GetPendingRequests`/`GetTicket(ByID)`: returned internal pointers; now return value copies

## Logic
- **M-11** `BitrateAdapter.UpdateNetworkStats` was never called in production; wired into Manager iteration via `feedRTPStatsToAdapter` and per-call adapter creation
- **M-12** Jitter thresholds in quality classification were misaligned; remapped to excellent/good/fair/poor/unacceptable correctly
- **M-14** `FriendSendMessage` returned `t.lastMessageID` (local counter) instead of the ID from `MessageManager.SendMessage`; new `sendRealTimeMessageWithID` helper returns the manager ID directly
- **M-15** `IterationPipelines.Start()` after `Stop()` silently did nothing — context was permanently cancelled; `Start()` now recreates `ctx`/`cancel`
- **M-16** UDP port-scan loop `uint16` wrap at `EndPort=65535` caused infinite spin; loop variable changed to `int`
- **L-07** `LamportClock.Update` wrapped to 0 at `MaxUint64`; now saturates
- **L-06** Replay nonce expiring exactly at `now` was retained one extra second (`<` → `<=`)
- **L-08** `CalculateDynamicRecipientLimit` panicked on `CapacityDivisor=0`; now resets to default config
- **L-09** `RetrievalScheduler.Configure` accepted non-positive intervals causing tight spin loops; inputs validated and clamped
- **L-10** `SerializeBinary` wrote 1-byte length prefix but full address, silently truncating >255-byte addresses; now returns error
- **L-11** `attemptDeliveryWithRetries` with `RetryAttempts=0` silently never sent; clamped to minimum 1

## Resources / DoS
- **M-21** mDNS `knownPeers` grew without bound; capped at 1000 entries. UPnP `io.ReadAll` calls wrapped in `io.LimitReader(64KB)`

## Errors
- **L-14** `SetReadDeadline` return discarded before `ReadFrom`; now routed through `handleReadError`. Three `%v` → `%w` wraps. `videoProcessor.Close()` error now logged instead of dropped
- **L-05** `LoggerHelper.WithError(nil, …)` panicked on nil dereference; nil-checked

author: panyam
body:
## What changes

Adds the RFC 9207 `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported` field to `client.ASMetadata` so consumers of `DiscoverAS` can read the AS's advertisement at decode time. Pointer-typed `*bool` preserves the tristate (advertised-true / advertised-false / absent) that §2.4 enforcement needs — distinguishing "AS told us no" from "AS didn't say" is load-bearing for any consumer that wants a strict-mode policy.

The field decodes automatically via `encoding/json`; `DiscoverAS` itself is unchanged. Validation logic stays in consumers per the split established by issue 235; a companion `ValidateIss` helper is tracked separately under issue 238.

Closes issue 239.

## Reviewer's guide

Read in this order:

1. [client/discovery.go](https://github.com/panyam/oneauth/pull/241/files#diff-0d6c1e4b6e6cf986699d916f9be1a95c3e25fa093ebf5237e7e166be0c786e20) — the one-field addition with its doc comment. Skim for: pointer semantics rationale (does the contract match `apiauth/as_metadata.go:64-76`?), spelling of the JSON tag.
2. [client/discovery_test.go](https://github.com/panyam/oneauth/pull/241/files#diff-7ef99ec0b4760549be429aa5e6b874113bbd22e7ee51ffafae59a9e57c9e23de) — three tristate decode tests (`AdvertisedTrue` / `AdvertisedFalse` / `Absent`). Acceptance for the JSON decode contract on the client side alone.
3. [client/as_metadata_interop_test.go](https://github.com/panyam/oneauth/pull/241/files#diff-4d88aca6954eb866de8eae1286f5e707a7feea8f2d6993621058f347bb91e84b) — apiauth↔client wire-contract test. Mounts `apiauth.NewASMetadataHandler` on httptest and calls `client.DiscoverAS` against it for all three tristate cases. Catches the class of bug where someone renames the JSON tag on one side and the other silently decodes to `nil`.
4. [client/SUMMARY.md](https://github.com/panyam/oneauth/pull/241/files#diff-3a46ff406dca6db0306228beb6a581b19e9373c5f02d6f413012ed95a05fd13c) — one-line Recent Changes entry.

Skim or skip: nothing — the PR is four files, ~150 lines.

## Decision log

- **Pointer-typed `*bool`, not `bool`.** Mirrors `apiauth.ASServerMetadata` exactly. The "absent" / "explicit false" distinction is required by the §2.4 rule set in the issue body: a default-policy consumer treats *absent* as legacy-AS (skip enforcement) but may treat *explicit false* the same way; a strict-mode consumer (FAPI 2.0 / Open Banking) wants to know which it was. A `bool` with `omitempty` would collapse both into the same wire form.
- **No change to `DiscoverAS` logic.** `encoding/json` decodes the field by structure-tag alone; adding code would be noise.
- **Interop test lives in `client_test` (external) package**, not `client` internal — follows the precedent set by `jwt_bearer_grant_e2e_test.go` and `token_exchange_e2e_test.go`. Importing `apiauth` from inside `client` would risk a cycle if the dep ever flips.
- **No `ValidateIss` here.** Out of scope per issue 239; the helper is its own ticket (238).

## Risk / blast radius

- Affects: every consumer of `client.DiscoverAS` (additive — they gain a field, lose nothing).
- Wire-compatible: omitted fields decode to `nil` on existing AS metadata documents; no behavior change for callers who don't read the new field.
- Tests covering this: three tristate decode cases in `client/discovery_test.go` plus the cross-package interop in `client/as_metadata_interop_test.go`. Full `client/` suite + `make test` are green.
- Be paranoid about: nothing structural. The downstream end-to-end signal (mcpkit's `auth/iss-supported-missing` conformance scenario flipping green) is `panyam/mcpkit#380`, not this PR.

## Out of scope (deliberately deferred)

- `ValidateIss` helper with strict-mode flag — tracked at issue 238.
- Auto-wiring iss enforcement into `BrowserLoginRequest.OnCallback` — explicitly left to consumers per issue 235.
- Keycloak interop check — only worth wiring up if Keycloak actually emits this field; not on the critical path for #239.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./client/...` — all pass (3 new decode tests + 3 new interop subtests, 0 existing weakened).
- [x] Red-before-green verified on the decode tests: removing the struct field fails compile (`ASMetadata has no field or method AuthorizationResponseIssParameterSupported`).
- [x] Red-before-green verified on the interop test: renaming the server-side JSON tag to `authorization_response_iss_param_supported` fails the `advertised_true` and `advertised_false` subtests at the `require.NotNil` assertion (the `absent` case stays green because both sides agree on field-omission — exactly the failure mode the test is designed to surface).
- [x] `make test` — full unit suite green across all workspace modules.

Introduce PostgreSQL as the source of truth while preserving the demo-safe Phase 0 experience. Replace mock-data-only reads with a service and repository architecture backed by Prisma.

- Prisma schema with Customer, ContactMethod, ConsentRecord, Signal, Opportunity, Communication, AuditEvent, PolicyDecision, RiskFlag, and VerticalPack models, plus the initial migration
- Repository layer that owns all Prisma access and returns domain types
- Service layer for dashboard metrics, pipeline, timeline, and listings
- Prisma client singleton and row to domain mappers
- Seed script that loads the Phase 0 business examples into the database
- Dynamic dashboard with metrics calculated from persistence
- Customer intelligence timeline merging signals, communications, audit events, and opportunities
- Opportunity pipeline, audit trail, and communications served from the database
- Persisted consent records and deterministic policy decisions
- Empty, loading, and not found states with graceful failure handling
- Updated README, ROADMAP, and environment example

No pages call Prisma directly. No authentication, no live integrations, no secrets, no real customer data.

author: ruben-pulido
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-83094

## What is being fixed

Creating a content page through the Headless Admin Site API required callers to supply both the draft and the published ContentPageSpecification (two page specifications). There was no way to create the page from a single ContentPageSpecification and let the API derive its counterpart and experiences.

## How it is being fixed

POST and PUT on `/site-pages` now accept a single ContentPageSpecification for a content page and expand it into the draft and published pair, deriving the missing counterpart along with its page experiences. The external reference code suffixes used for that derivation (`-default`, `-draft`, `-published`) are extracted as constants on LayoutConstants. Applying a single ContentPageSpecification to an already existing page through PUT is rejected. Integration tests cover POST and PUT with a single ContentPageSpecification, the draft and published derivations, and the rejection.

Builds on top of: https://github.com/liferay-page-management/liferay-portal/pull/18479

### Motivation

- Provide a self-contained static frontend for monitoring BTCUSDT weekly RSI, multi-timeframe FVG/SR context and compact market-prep summaries without any backend or paid APIs.
- Add lower-timeframe reaction/timing tools (Daily/4H/1H) and PDF export so users can inspect and export multi-timeframe context from a static site.

### Description

- Added a new static single-page app with `index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js`, `version.json`, and an expanded `README.md` describing the app and usage. 
- Implemented weekly dataset ingestion from Binance, RSI calculation, Lightweight Charts rendering for weekly price and RSI, weekly FVG detection and overlay, weekly S/R scanning, and weekly candle-character classification in `app.js`.
- Implemented lower-timeframe support: Daily chart + pattern detection, 4H FVG/SR scanning and clean overlay, 1H timing (stochastic, sweep, structure) and markers, plus multi-timeframe FVG conflict/quality scoring and timing zone logic in `app.js`.
- Added interactive UX features: manual horizontal lines and trendlines (persisted in localStorage), chart layer presets, chart zoom toggle, collapsible sections, drawing manager modal, and PDF export using `html2canvas` + `jspdf`.
- Styling and layout implemented in `style.css`, and app metadata/versioning added in `version.json`; `README.md` updated with feature summary and local/GitHub Pages run instructions.

body:
## Summary
Adds a new **Assets** tab to the popup that analyzes every script and stylesheet a page loads, and brings the **Links** tab to the same faceted-filter + sortable-table standard. Ships under the existing unreleased `2026.05.31` version.

## Assets tab (new)
- Scans `<script>`, `<link rel="stylesheet">`, and inline `<style>` via a new `get_assets` content-script handler.
- Columns: Source · Size · Time · Type · Load. Size/time/status/cached/render-blocking are read from the **Resource Timing API** (no extra network requests); opaque cross-origin assets show `—`.
- Faceted single-select filters (Type · Source · Loading) that AND together, with a reset; sortable headers; URL search; click-to-open (external) / expand-inline (inline source).
- Detects browser-extension-injected assets (`chrome-extension://` etc.) and keeps them out of the "External" count.
- Export to CSV / JSON / copy URLs.

## Links tab (revamp)
- Replaced the single mixed dropdown with faceted single-select filters: **Type** (Internal/External), **Follow** (Dofollow/Nofollow), **Anchor** (Text/Image/None), AND-combined with a reset.
- Made the table sortable (all columns, with sort affordance + bold headers).

## Analytics
- Added `assets_*` actions and a previously-missing set of `links_*` actions to the exhaustive `AnalyticsAction` union + `TIME_SAVINGS`/`ACTION_CATEGORIES` maps. The `links_*` actions were already being fired by the shipped Links tab but weren't registered, so those events were silently bucketing as `Other` with no time-savings credit — now fixed.

## Review & checks
- Independent adversarial review run on the diff: confirmed analytics maps exhaustive, Svelte 5 runes correct, content-script edge cases handled. One finding fixed (extension assets were double-counted as External).
- `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, and `oxfmt --check` all pass. (This WXT extension gates on typecheck + lint; no unit-test framework.)

## Notes
- No version bump: `2026.05.31` is today's CalVer and already set on `main` (unreleased); this feature joins that entry.

author: mkitti
body:
MemoryStore uses per-key asyncio.Lock / threading.Lock to serialise concurrent set_range / set_range_sync calls on the same key.

LocalStore uses a double-checked file-lock protocol: the target file is atomically renamed to a key.__lock__ sibling (via _safe_move) to signal exclusive ownership across both threads and processes, with stale-lock recovery after 60 s. The in-process asyncio.Lock / threading.Lock guards the rename so only one coroutine/thread races to the filesystem at a time.

Concurrent tests are added for both stores verifying that parallel writes to non-overlapping byte ranges produce the correct combined result.

body:
## Resumen

Arranque de **Prisma**, un *cerebro de contexto personal*: ingiere y normaliza los datos del mundo digital del usuario (chats de ChatGPT/Claude, WhatsApp, notas, fotos, vídeos) en una base de conocimiento unificada y consultable, para exponerla luego a un LLM vía MCP.

Este PR incluye el diseño completo y las dos primeras fases del roadmap, todo funcional, verificado y con tests.

## Qué entra

### 📄 Documentación de arquitectura
- `README.md` y `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: visión, realidad técnica de la extracción (sandbox → API / export oficial / export manual), detalle por fuente, esquema común, pipeline, almacenamiento, asistente MCP, seguridad/GDPR y roadmap por fases.

### ✅ Fase 0 — Cimientos
- **Esquema común `Event`** (`prisma/schema.py`): unidad atómica de la línea temporal, con `id` determinista para dedupe idempotente.
- **Object store content-addressed** (`prisma/storage/objects.py`): binarios por SHA-256, deduplica automáticamente.
- **Metadatos en SQLite** (`prisma/storage/metadata.py`): eventos, timeline, búsqueda y cursores por fuente.
- **Orquestador de ingesta** (`prisma/ingest.py`) e **interfaz de importadores** (`prisma/importers/base.py`).
- **CLI** (`prisma/cli.py`): `init`, `ingest`, `stats`, `search`, `timeline`.

### ✅ Fase 1 — Importadores de ChatGPT y Claude
- `prisma/importers/chatgpt.py` y `prisma/importers/claude.py`: parsean el `conversations.json` de cada export oficial.
- Aceptan **`.zip`, carpeta o `.json`** (localizan el fichero dentro del ZIP) y normalizan fechas (epoch Unix / ISO → ISO-8601 UTC).

## Verificación
- **29/29 tests** pasan (`python -m unittest discover -s tests`).
- Probado de punta a punta: ingesta de exports (ChatGPT + Claude) que **conviven en la misma línea temporal**, búsqueda **cruzando fuentes** y **reingesta idempotente** (0 duplicados).
- Sin dependencias externas: solo biblioteca estándar de Python (≥3.10).

## Notas
- Los importadores se basan en el **formato conocido** de cada export; son robustos ante variaciones, pero conviene validarlos con un export real.
- Los datos personales del usuario nunca se versionan (`.gitignore` excluye `prisma_data/` y `*.db`).

## Siguiente
- Fase 2: pipeline multimodal de fotos/vídeos (EXIF + caption + OCR + transcripción), con backend de análisis enchufable (local por defecto).

author: mgh3326
body:
## ROB-375 Bug 1 의미 보정 — advisory draft만 prior 인정

#1047의 `include_draft=True`는 **모든 draft**를 `prior_reports`에 포함시켜, ROB-352가 막으려던 smoke boilerplate를 다시 끌어들였습니다. "advisory draft만 prior 인정, smoke draft는 재유입 방지"라는 의도와 어긋났습니다.

### 변경
`include_draft: bool` → **`draft_policy: "exclude" | "advisory_only"`**로 교체:
- **`"exclude"`** (기본): 모든 draft 제외 — 기존 기본 동작 그대로.
- **`"advisory_only"`**: 진짜 advisory draft(`created_by_profile == "HERMES_ADVISOR"`)만 prior로 인정, smoke/test draft는 계속 제외.

**`"all"` 정책은 만들지 않음.** service는 알 수 없는 값에 `ValueError`, MCP 도구는 fail-closed로 `"exclude"` 폴백(환각성 정책이 draft를 과다 포함하지 않게).

### 구분자 (조사 기반)

author: joemooney
body:
## Mechanism (confirmed via live instrumentation, not guessed)

`AIDA_DEBUG_AUTOBUMP=1` on a real ship (PR-361) gave ground truth:

```
step 4: running `aida pull` ...
Already up to date.
  [autobump-debug] pre_code_sha=Some("c9605120") post_head=Some("c9605120") range=c9605120..HEAD
  [autobump-debug] commits in c9605120..HEAD:        ← empty
  [autobump-debug] auto_bump_done_to_completed → 0 flips
```

`aida pr ship` step 3 (`gh pr merge --squash`) fast-forwards **local** main to the squash commit *before* step 4's `aida pull` runs. So the pull is a no-op ("Already up to date"), `pre_code_sha == post_head`, and the narrow `pre..HEAD` auto-bump range is empty — the merged spec never bumps and stays Done until a manual `reconcile-status` (which uses a wide range and works). This is why every ship needed a manual chaser.

## Fix

When the pull moved nothing (`pre == post`), fall back to the wide `HEAD~50` scan instead of the empty narrow range, so a main advanced outside this pull (gh merge, or a manual merge-then-pull) is still covered. The Done-guard inside `auto_bump_done_to_completed` keeps the wide scan idempotent.

Also keeps the `AIDA_DEBUG_AUTOBUMP` instrumentation (default-off) for future visibility.

## Test

`pull_noop_still_auto_bumps_externally_advanced_main` — advances local main to a referencing commit via a raw `git pull` (no bump), then calls `handle_pull_command` whose own pull is a no-op, and asserts the spec still reaches Completed. **Proven to fail without the fix and pass with it.** Full pull (4) + auto_bump (37) suites green.

body:
Closes the silent-skip gap in cross-model peer-review. The workflow skills (autopilot, epic-design, feature-design, review, perf-scout) delegate peer-review to `peeragent --agent codex` only "when a different model class is available" — but their availability check is just `command -v peeragent`; none verify Codex is **logged in**. So a logged-out Codex fails the call mid-run and the non-blocking escape hatch silently falls back to same-model local review.

New SessionStart hook `session-start-peer-preflight.sh`:
- Inert if peeragent absent.
- Warns if peeragent present but `codex` CLI missing.
- Warns (`codex login` fix) if `codex login status` reports not-authenticated.
- **Silent when logged in**; always non-blocking (exit 0).

The warning prints to the SessionStart transcript (same channel as the knowledge-index nav banner), so it's user-visible at session start. Bumps research-pipeline 0.1.11 → 0.1.12.

author: olilebel92
body:
## What & why

Two fixes, both surfaced while verifying multiplayer loot.

### 1. Curated `ItemPool` drops now resolve on remote clients
Enemy `ItemPool` loot is rolled and injected into `LootPickup.itemPool` on the server, but `itemPool` is a plain field that does **not** replicate — so remote (non-host) clients arrived with an empty pool and couldn't turn the server-synced item GUID back into an `ItemData`. Result: no item granted, no world model. Host/singleplayer were unaffected (they resolve through the local pool), which is why it looked fine until tested with a real second client.

- **New `ItemDataCatalog`** (ScriptableObject under `Resources/`) indexes every authored `ItemData`/`WeaponItemData` by `AssetGuid`. `LootPickup.FindItemInPoolByGuid` now falls back to it when the local pool misses, so remote clients resolve the **real authored asset** — preserving `WeaponItemData.baseDamage`, icon, etc. (the serialized-copy alternative would have zeroed a curated weapon's damage).
- An editor `AssetPostprocessor` keeps the catalog in sync on item import/move/delete; `RPG → Items → Rebuild Item Catalog` is the manual fallback.
- Verified on an actual remote client.

### 2. Script filename casing (the *actual* cause of "nothing dropped")
While testing, **no** enemy dropped anything. Root cause: `EnemyReward` — the only loot component on enemies — was showing as a missing `(Script)` in Unity **with no compile error**. A filename/class case mismatch (`Enemyreward.cs` tracked in git vs `class EnemyReward`) broke Unity's script binding and silently disabled all enemy drops.

- Renamed `Enemyreward.cs → EnemyReward.cs` and `Playerattack.cs → PlayerAttack.cs` to match their class names (`.meta`/GUID preserved, so prefab/scene references stay intact).
- Added **`tools/Check-ScriptCase.ps1`** to detect/fix this class of problem repo-wide (report by default, `-Fix` to apply with Unity closed).

## Reviewer notes
- `Assets/Resources/ItemDataCatalog.asset` is committed (required at runtime); it self-maintains via the postprocessor.
- `LootPickup.cs` carries a few pre-existing in-progress edits beyond the catalog fallback.

author: dram-dev
body:
Follow-up to #8. With the token live, docket queries still **timed out at 30s** on most courts (flsd/flnd/flmd/ilnd…). Isolated the cause: **ordering the date-filtered docket set is unindexed on CourtListener**.

Validated live on a court that was timing out:
- `ilnd` **WITH** `order_by=-date_filed` → **>60s timeout**
- `ilnd` **WITHOUT** → **0.4s, 200, 20 results**

Dropped `order_by`. The 2-day `date_filed__gte` window already returns only recent dockets, so default order is fine for the daily digest. The ingest now runs without per-court timeouts.

Regression test updated to assert `order_by` is not sent. `uv run pytest` → **228 passed**.

Note: P&C *federal* dockets are sparse in a 2-day window (the ingestor filters to P&C Nature-of-Suit codes), so a given run may land few/0 dockets — that's a valid low-activity reading for Lead 4's docket velocity, not a failure. Widening `_FILED_AFTER_DAYS` is an optional future tuning.

### Motivation
- Provide safe app-managed pagination for OSM imports (Overpass lacks true offset) and make the admin import UI support importing successive OSM batches without pulling duplicates.  
- Restore and surface real backend error messages across import actions so failures are actionable instead of showing a generic "Request failed."  
- Allow publishing all publish-ready staged records without requiring a batch ID while keeping protections for CRM/QR/search fields.  

### Description
- UI: Updated `app/admin/dashboard/import/page.tsx` to add OSM controls and persistent cursor: `Limit` (default `250`), `Offset` (default `0`), collapsed `Advanced` accordion with `Category group` and `Region`, buttons `Import OSM Batch`, `Import Next OSM Batch`, and `Reset OSM Offset`, and localStorage key `theouthaven_osm_import_offset`; kept Google import unchanged.  
- Error handling: Replaced generic importer response handling with a shared `parseActionResponse` that parses backend JSON and surfaces server error messages in the import UI.  
- OSM API route: Reworked `app/api/admin/location-growth/import-osm-activities/route.ts` to validate `limit`/`offset`/`categoryGroup`, keep admin/x-internal-import-secret auth, return JSON always, and surface meaningful errors.  
- OSM helper: Rewrote `lib/location-growth/osmActivities.ts` to accept `{ limit, offset, categoryGroup }`, bound `limit`/`offset`, create `location_import_batches` records, fetch full Overpass results with timeout `AbortController`, sort elements and slice locally for app-level cursor behavior, map -> dedupe mapped rows before upsert, run `oh_refresh_staging_quality` and `oh_find_staging_duplicates`, and save batch metadata including `nextOffset` and `categoryGroup`; handles empty-cursor gracefully without throwing.  
- Publish all: Updated `app/api/admin/location-growth/publish/route.ts` to support `all` mode (body `{ all: true, limit }`) with bounded `limit` (default `500`, max `1000`), returns `remainingPublishReady`, preserves admin auth and `x-internal-import-secret`, and returns real JSON errors.

body:
The intended brand display face was never visible — every `.font(.custom("Exo 2", ...))` call was silently falling back to SF Pro because **"Exo 2" was never bundled**. The repeated console warning

author: rmednitzer
body:
Phased capability **#7 (AI-native)** — first thread: a **local inference runtime**, per your pick. Provisions [Ollama](https://ollama.com) on dedicated inference hosts (e.g. the GPU compute host) so inference stays **on-premises** — prompts/data never go to a third-party model API (GDPR Art 25 / Art 44 data sovereignty).

## What
- **Supply-chain-safe install** (ADR-002): pinned + checksum-verified — downloads the versioned GitHub release `.tgz` via `get_url checksum:` and extracts to the install prefix. **No `curl | sh`.** Requires `ollama_version` + `ollama_checksum` (asserted); no floating "latest".
- **Hardened, localhost-bound service**: `ollama` system user + data dir, and a systemd unit with `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=full`, `ProtectHome`, `PrivateTmp`, `Protect*` (moderate — GPU device access precludes `PrivateDevices`). Binds `127.0.0.1` by default because the Ollama API is **unauthenticated**.
- Optional model pulls; NVIDIA GPU auto-detected (CPU fallback; drivers not installed).

## Scope & safety
- **Off by default**; targets **inference hosts**, not the fleet — run via `playbooks/local-inference.yml` (`inference_hosts` group), **not** `site-common.yml`.
- Container-guest aware (`ollama_runtime_managed`).
- **Engine choice:** Ollama (single-GPU local serving, systemd-friendly, built-in model management, OpenAI-compatible API). A higher-throughput engine (vLLM) would be a **sibling role**, not a flag — happy to add it next if you want it.

## Compliance
Mapped to **POL-004** (data classification & handling — local inference keeps data on-premises). GDPR Art 25 / Art 5(1)(f) / Art 44, NIS2 Art 21.2(e), ISO 27001:2022 A.5.12 / A.8.9. Bidirectional validator-enforced.

## Validation
`yamllint`, `ansible-lint` **0/0** (production), `local-inference.yml` syntax-check, compliance validator (now **22 roles**, consistent), pre-commit hygiene, and a render of the hardened systemd unit.

Remaining AI-native threads (your call on order): Fleet↔MCP wiring, AI-assisted sec-ops, AI-in-CI.

author: bri-prism
body:
## What
Enlarge the bf16 GPU-vs-CPU matmul probe in `_mlx_matmul_ok` (`setup.sh`) from `64x512 @ 512x512` to `1024x2048 @ 2048x2048`.

## Why
The M5 NAX miscompile detector added in #11 is correct in approach but has a **false negative on M5**: its probe matmul is too small to select the miscompiled NAX GEMM kernel. On a broken source-built metallib the small probe reads clean (reldiff ~0), so `_mlx_matmul_ok` returns OK, the metallib swap is skipped, and a fresh M5 clone still produces gray-brown noise (issue #6).

The miscompile only manifests at the matmul sizes the model actually uses. Measured on M5 Pro (bf16 GPU-vs-CPU reldiff, source-built metallib):

| matmul | reldiff |
|---|---|
| 64x512 @ 512x512 *(old probe)* | 0.0000 ✅ false negative |
| 256x2048 @ 2048 | 0.0021 ✅ |
| 1024x2048 @ 2048 | **1.111** ❌ |
| 4096x4096 @ 4096 | **1.112** ❌ |

(Original diagnosis by @davepeckjr in #6.)

## How / verification
Verified on M5 Pro (Mac17,8), macOS 26.5, Xcode 26.5 (`metalfe-32023.883`):

- Patched probe **passes** (exit 0, no swap) on the prebuilt `mlx-metal` metallib and **trips** (exit 1, triggers swap) on the source-built one — so the swap now fires on fresh M5 clones.
- End-to-end: with the broken metallib, the same prompt+seed produces gray noise (`check_image` std 8.7, FAIL); after the swap fires, real prompt-faithful images (std 61.6, PASS), and two different prompts produce distinct images (reldiff 0.91 vs 0.008 under the bug).

Fixes #6

author: yaiba2307
body:
## Summary
Second autonomous fix/polish round. One focused correctness fix in the global Topbar, plus a test-isolation fix it surfaced. **Frontend-only, for review — not merged.**

## The bug
The Topbar resolved any **unrecognised** route to the dashboard `pageKey`, so it rendered a stray **"Overview"** title + subtitle on top of pages that render their *own* section header. Most visible on the **Billing** pages (`/billing/factures`, `/billing/devis`, `/billing/templates`) — each showed "Overview" above its real "Invoice"/"Quote"/"Templates" header. The settings sub-pages and the `persons-*` pages had the same leak. (Same bug family as the Documents double-header fixed in #127.)

### Fix
- Resolve unknown routes to a **null** `pageKey` and render **no** title block, instead of falling back to "Overview". Pages that own their header are now clean; the topbar keeps its right-side controls (notifications, theme, account).
- All topbar-driven pages (dashboard, projects, settings, planning, labor, invoices, notes, members, documents) are explicitly matched and **unchanged**.
- Added 3 topbar tests for the suppression behaviour.

### Bonus: flaky-test fix it exposed
`notes-agenda.test.tsx` had **two** `vi.mock("sonner")` calls — one exposing `toast` as an object, one as a callable. Which won was order-dependent; my added tests shifted vitest's file scheduling and flipped it, so the component's `toast(label, opts)` hit the object form -> `toast is not a function`. Collapsed to the single correct callable mock. (Pre-existing latent issue; master was green only by scheduling luck.)

## Verification (local docker stack + Chrome DevTools)
- `/billing/factures|devis|templates`: single clean header, no "Overview"; console clean.
- Regression check — dashboard still "Overview", labor still "Labor", documents/members headers intact.
- `/settings/users` is a genuine 404 (not a route — only `/settings` and `/settings/companies/[id]` exist); unrelated to this change.
- Pre-flight: **lint / type-check / 1092 tests (stable across 2 full runs) / build — all green**.

## Heads-up: concurrent "Product Library" (bibliotheque) work
While I worked, another session was building a `bibliotheque` (Product Library) feature in the same checkout. **This PR deliberately excludes all of it** — only my 3 files are committed; their WIP is left intact in the working tree. Note for whoever lands bibliotheque: `/bibliotheque` is an unmatched route under this change, so it needs either a `TOPBAR_KEYS` entry (like `documents`) or its own in-page header to show a title.

## Out of scope (flagged, not touched)
- **Dark mode toggle is a no-op**: `globals.css` declares the Tailwind `dark` variant but defines zero `.dark` token overrides, and the app themes via CSS variables — toggling does nothing visually. A real dark palette is a feature needing design direction.
- Form fields missing `id`/`name` association (a11y) on some forms (settings profile email/phone) — a broader sweep, left for a dedicated pass.

author: sjk-py
body:
## What was missing

`bp_agents` settings expose `embedding_dim` (env `SUITE_EMBEDDING_DIM`, default 1536). The knowledge_base + memory agents bake it into their LanceDB table schema on first write — `pa.list_(float32, dim)` in `bp_agents/lance/{knowledge,memory}.py` — and the tables open with `exist_ok=True`, so the dimension is **frozen for the life of the `lancedb_data` volume**. A value that doesn't match the embedding preset's output dimension breaks every KB/memory write.

But the knob was surfaced **nowhere** — not in `prod.sh`, `docker-compose.prod.yml`, or `deploy/.env.prod.example` — so it silently rode the 1536 default.

It works today only by luck: every preset prod.sh wires resolves to 1536 (Gemini `default_embedding` pins `output_dimensionality=1536`; OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` is natively 1536). The gap is that there was no safe path to change the embedding model — repointing to e.g. `text-embedding-3-large` (3072) would mismatch the baked schema with no visible setting to fix it.

## Fix (derive it from the chosen preset so it can't drift)

- **`scripts/prod.sh`** — set `EMBEDDING_DIM` alongside `PRESET_EMBEDDING` in the provider `case` (all 1536 today) and emit `SUITE_EMBEDDING_DIM` into the generated env file, with a comment on the first-write / volume-freeze caveat.
- **`docker-compose.prod.yml`** — add `SUITE_EMBEDDING_DIM` (`${...:-1536}`) to the shared `suite-env` anchor, so all 13 suite agents — including knowledge_base/memory — receive it.
- **`deploy/.env.prod.example`** — document it, the must-match-preset rule, and that changing it later needs a volume reset.

## Verification

- `build_env` emits `SUITE_EMBEDDING_DIM=1536` for all four providers, consistent with each one's embedding preset (anthropic/gemini/custom → `default_embedding`; openai → `text-embedding-3-small`).
- `docker compose config` is valid (rc=0) and renders `SUITE_EMBEDDING_DIM: "1536"` on the suite agents.
- `bash -n scripts/prod.sh` clean.

## Operator note

An existing `lancedb_data` volume is already at dim 1536, so this change is consistent with it — no action needed unless you later switch to a different-dimension embedding model, in which case update `SUITE_EMBEDDING_DIM` **and** reset the volume.

body:
## Summary

Bumps `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` **0.4.1 → 0.4.2** (now published) so the plugin gets the two robustness improvements from [OpenVTC/vti-didcomm-js#2](https://github.com/OpenVTC/vti-didcomm-js/pull/2):

- **WS-upgrade diagnostics** — a failed live-delivery socket now reports its RFC 6455 close code + cause (1008 → mediator ACL, **1006 → refused/CORS/proxy**, 1015 → TLS) and `endpoint`, instead of an opaque `WebSocket failed to open`. This is exactly the signal that pinned down the CORS issue; having it in the plugin makes the next field failure self-diagnosing.
- **Per-frame inbound resilience** — a bad inbound message is logged (via the library's `onError`, default `console.warn`) and skipped, so the session never gets stuck on one poison message.

No plugin code change required: the default `onError` already logs to the console and the diagnostics ride on the existing connect path. A custom `onError` sink can be wired through `connectMediatorSession` later if we want it in telemetry.

body:
## What

Adds a second mode to Glassbridge: a **hands-free controller for Claude Code sessions**. Open the new **Code** tab, hold **TALK**, and speak. The existing camera/vision ASK loop is untouched.

- *"Start a new session"* / *"…called parser refactor"* → opens a session
- *"List my sessions"* → Claude reads them back so you can pick by name/number
- *"Switch to the parser one"* / *"switch to two"* → changes the active session
- Anything else (*"add a health-check endpoint and run the tests"*) → forwarded to the active session; the agent does the work, then **speaks a short summary** (full text stays on screen)

No image is captured or sent in this mode — voice in, voice out.

## How sessions connect (two drivers, one interface)

Set `GB_CODE_DRIVER`:

- **`agent`** (default) — the backend runs real Claude Code sessions itself via the [Claude Agent SDK](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/agent-sdk). Run it where the work should happen; point `GB_CODE_CWD` at the repo. Needs the `claude` CLI on PATH.
- **`remote`** — the "remote control" path: run the backend on your Mac with `agent`, then point a cloud instance at it with `GB_REMOTE_BRIDGE_URL`. Phone → cloud → your machine.

## Changes

**Backend**
- `code_sessions.py` — `CodeSessionManager` over a `CodeSessionDriver` interface, with `AgentSDKDriver` and `RemoteDriver`. Intent routing maps spoken lines to create/list/switch/chat, with markdown-stripping + length-trimming for comfortable speech. Appends to the `claude_code` system-prompt preset (doesn't replace it).
- `main.py` — `GET/POST /code/sessions`, `POST /code/voice` (audio → STT → route → streaming MP3 with `X-Code-*` headers), plus JSON twins `POST /code/text` and `POST /code/send` (the raw forward the remote driver proxies to).
- `config.py` + `.env.example` — `GB_CODE_DRIVER`, `GB_REMOTE_BRIDGE_URL`, model, cwd, permission mode, speak length.
- `backend/tests/test_code_router.py` — offline routing tests (no keys/SDK needed).

**iOS**
- New **Code** tab (`CodeView`) with a TALK button, session-picker sheet, and reply view.
- `SessionCoordinator` gains code-mode state + push-to-talk that reuses the existing audio path.
- `BackendClient` gains the `/code/*` calls and longer timeouts for agent turns.

## Verification

- Backend modules byte-compile; offline routing tests pass: `cd glassbridge && python -m backend.tests.test_code_router`.
- **Not** verified here (no `claude` CLI, API keys, or Xcode in the build container): the live Agent SDK loop and the iOS build. The SDK integration is written against the documented `ClaudeSDKClient` / `ClaudeAgentOptions` API with a lazy import and a clear error if the CLI/SDK is missing.

## Notes / follow-ups

- Agent sessions default to `bypassPermissions` (voice can't approve tool calls); tune via `GB_CODE_PERMISSION_MODE`.
- Routing ambiguity: *"switch to the main branch"* parses as a session-switch command. If that bites, a wake-prefix gate (e.g. *"Glassbridge, switch to…"*) is an easy follow-up.

    update-types:
      - "version-update:semver-major"
```

### Why this change is needed

The `@types/node` package provides TypeScript type definitions for the Node.js runtime API. The major version of `@types/node` that an adapter should use is determined by the **lowest** major Node.js version the adapter supports. The lowest supported Node.js version is specified in the `engines.node` field of `package.json`.

Allowing Dependabot to automatically bump `@types/node` to a newer major version would introduce type definitions for Node.js APIs that are not available in the minimum supported Node.js version. This can lead to incorrect type checking and potential runtime errors on older Node.js installations. Therefore, major version updates of `@types/node` must always be reviewed manually and aligned with any intentional change to the minimum supported Node.js version.

### Reference

- [ioBroker Repository Checker – Warning W8917](https://github.com/ioBroker/ioBroker.repochecker)
- [Dependabot ignore configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference#ignore)

---

## Deutsche Beschreibung

Dieser PR behebt die Warnung **W8917**, die vom ioBroker-Repository-Checker gemeldet wird.

### Was dieser PR macht

Dieser PR fügt der Dependabot-Konfiguration in `.github/dependabot.yml` eine Ignore-Regel hinzu, die verhindert, dass Dependabot automatisch Major-Version-Bumps für das Paket `@types/node` vorschlägt.

Die folgende Änderung wird auf jeden `updates:`-Block angewendet, der `package-ecosystem: npm` und `directory: /` oder `directories: ['**/*']` enthält:

```yaml
ignore:
  - dependency-name: "@types/node"
    update-types:
      - "version-update:semver-major"
```

### Warum diese Änderung notwendig ist

Das Paket `@types/node` stellt TypeScript-Typdefinitionen für die Node.js-Laufzeit-API bereit. Die Major-Version von `@types/node`, die ein Adapter verwenden sollte, wird durch die **niedrigste** unterstützte Node.js-Hauptversion des Adapters bestimmt. Die niedrigste unterstützte Node.js-Version wird im Feld `engines.node` in `package.json` angegeben.

Würde Dependabot `@types/node` automatisch auf eine neuere Major-Version aktualisieren, würden Typdefinitionen für Node.js-APIs eingeführt, die in der minimal unterstützten Node.js-Version nicht verfügbar sind. Dies kann zu fehlerhafter Typprüfung und potenziellen Laufzeitfehlern auf älteren Node.js-Installationen führen. Daher müssen Major-Version-Updates von `@types/node` immer manuell geprüft und mit einer bewussten Änderung der minimal unterstützten Node.js-Version abgestimmt werden.

author: akegaviar
body:
## Problem

`solana-trader-nodes.mdx` contradicted itself on Warp transaction landing rate:

- Overview (and "No need for custom setups"): **"40% of transactions land in the first two blocks"**
- Speed-metrics table: **"37% within 2 blocks"** — same metric, different number

## Why drop the numbers (not just reconcile)

Both figures are pre-fix snapshots. The Solana landing-rate metric was buggy (it counted no-balance test cases) and was **recomputed on 2026-05-27** — now measured via `getTransaction` with no-balance cases excluded. So both `37%` and `40%` are stale, and any hardcoded figure will drift again (which is what caused the contradiction).

There's already a live source: the [Chainstack Compare dashboard](https://compare.chainstack.com/) measures Solana transaction landing continuously (every 15 min, Warp vs other providers).

## Fix

- Remove the hardcoded `40%` from the overview bullet and the "no custom setups" paragraph
- Replace the static `37%` speed-metrics table with a pointer to the live Compare dashboard
- Keep the SwQoS framing and the existing latency / priority-fee caveats

No number to maintain, points to the authoritative live source.

author: iamnamja
body:
## Summary

**Critical bug found by Opus 4.7 round-4 audit (C1).**

`SwingStrategy.run_fold` and `IntradayStrategy.run_fold` both did:
```python
trade_returns = getattr(result, "trade_returns", [])
```
But `SimResult` (in `strategy_simulator.py`) has **no `trade_returns` field**. `getattr` always returned `[]` → `compute_profit_factor([])` returns `0.0` → every `FoldResult.profit_factor` was `0.0` → `WalkForwardReport.avg_profit_factor` was always `0.0` → `gate_passed()` waived the PF gate via the `avg_profit_factor == 0` short-circuit.

**The profit-factor gate has been a complete no-op since its introduction.** A model with a profit factor below 1.10 (the gate threshold) could pass silently.

### Fix

Use `result.profit_factor` directly — AgentSimulator already computes it correctly with `PF_NO_LOSS_SENTINEL=5.0`. Fallback to `compute_profit_factor(trade_returns)` extracted from `result.trades` for backward compatibility with other simulator types.
