author: atul-upadhyay-7
body:
## What this fixes

The `POST /api/auth/cleanup` endpoint accepts a `{ uid }` from the request body and deletes the corresponding Firebase Auth account via the Admin SDK. The authentication and authorization checks were added in prior commits (ef0aafe, 5ee8833), but no tests existed to verify that these security guarantees actually work. Without test coverage, regressions could silently remove the auth check and reintroduce the critical vulnerability reported in #1768.

## Root cause

The endpoint was added as a server-side fix for orphaned Firebase Auth accounts (PR #1744) without any authentication check. Subsequent PRs (#1817, #1848) added `authenticateRequest` and a UID ownership check, but no tests were included to guard against regressions. Every other authenticated API route in the codebase has test coverage for its auth behavior — this was the sole exception.

## What changed

- Added `app/api/auth/cleanup/__tests__/route.test.js` with 7 test cases covering:
  - Unauthenticated requests are rejected with 401
  - Authenticated users cannot delete other users' accounts (403)
  - Authenticated users can delete their own orphaned accounts (200)
  - Missing UID returns 400
  - Non-string UID returns 400
  - Already-deleted user returns success (idempotent)
  - Unexpected Firebase errors return 500

## How to verify

1. Run the test suite: `npx vitest run app/api/auth/cleanup/__tests__/route.test.js`
2. Confirm all 7 tests pass
3. Verify the unauthenticated test (test 1) fails if you remove the `authenticateRequest` call from the route handler

## Edge cases considered

- Firebase `auth/user-not-found` error returns success (idempotent cleanup)
- Non-string UIDs (numbers, objects, arrays) are rejected
- Ownership check uses strict equality on `uid` to prevent cross-account deletion
- Error messages do not leak internal Firebase details to the client

Closes #1768

body:
## Summary

In-app modal at [`frontend/src/components/common/ParentConsentGate/index.tsx`](frontend/src/components/common/ParentConsentGate/index.tsx) that gates first-use of camera (#581) and voice-input (#584) surfaces. The parent re-enters their password (verified via `authService.login` against the stored email), the gate calls `useChildStore.updateConsent` to flip the appropriate flag, then invokes `onGranted` so the consumer can fire the browser permission prompt.

The component is a **pure consent gate** — it never calls `getUserMedia` itself, so it can wrap either camera or microphone surfaces without coupling to media stream code.

## Props

```ts
type ParentConsentGateProps = {
  kind: 'camera' | 'microphone'
  ageGroup: AgeGroup
  childId: string
  onGranted: () => void
  onDismiss: () => void
}
```

## Scope correction

The original story scoped a `PermissionPrompt` component and assumed `/parent-approval` could be reused. Investigation in the #587 plan revealed `/parent-approval` is an email-token landing page (not an in-app modal). This PR ships a new modal — issue #588 was rescoped before coding.

## Age-adapted copy

| Age | Camera title | Microphone title |
|-----|-------------|------------------|
| 3-5 | Can we use the camera? | Can we listen to you? |
| 6-8 | Use the camera? | Use the microphone? |
| 9-12 | Allow camera access | Allow microphone access |

3-5 copy is short (≤140 chars body) and defers explicitly to a grown-up. Locked by contract test.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest run src/__tests__/components/ParentConsentGate.test.ts` → 4/4 pass
- [x] `tsc -b` → clean
- [x] Tests assert: kind × age matrix coverage, emoji per kind, 3-5 copy length cap, microphone copy promises no audio storage
- [ ] Manual: 3-5 cohort — large emoji + short copy
- [ ] Manual: wrong password → error message, no consent mutation
- [ ] Manual: correct password → consent flag flips, `onGranted` fires
- [ ] Manual: Escape key dismisses
- [ ] Manual: full-component render test deferred until `@testing-library/react` lands (no UI render coverage today since it's not in deps)

## Notes / deferred

- **Reduced-motion**: no animations in this gate, so nothing to disable.
- **Verification side effect**: `authService.login` refreshes the session token. Acceptable for MVP; alternative would be a dedicated `POST /auth/verify` endpoint as a follow-up.

author: prismatic-koi
body:
Closes #2073.

## Summary

Introduces a dedicated `PRISM_KEYBIND_SPAWN=1` sentinel for the tmux Prefix+a keybind, replacing the overload of `PRISM_SPAWN_PATH` that previously did double-duty as both a working-directory hint AND the keybind discriminator.

The conflation was fragile: every sandbox sets `PRISM_SPAWN_PATH` unconditionally as a cwd hint (`internal/container/bwrap.go`, `cmd/agent_run_sandbox_exec_darwin.go`), which forced the proxy-side carve-out in #2063 to be narrowed to `PRISM_SPAWN_PATH != "" && promptFlag == ""` to avoid misclassifying ordinary container worker-spawn flows as keybind spawns. With a dedicated sentinel that no sandbox injects, the narrowing is no longer needed and the discriminator becomes a single env-var check on both the host and proxy paths.

## Code changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `modules/programs/prism/tmux.nix` | Prefix+a bind sets `-e PRISM_KEYBIND_SPAWN=1` (dropped `-e PRISM_SPAWN_PATH`). Keeps the #2074 `run-shell` pattern. |
| `cmd/spawn.go` | `runSpawn` and `proxySpawn` discriminator is now `os.Getenv("PRISM_KEYBIND_SPAWN") != ""`. Removed the `&& promptFlag == ""` narrowing in `proxySpawn`. History comment block rewritten. |
| `internal/sidecar/host_api.go` | `/spawn` handler propagates BOTH `PRISM_KEYBIND_SPAWN=1` (discriminator) AND `PRISM_SPAWN_PATH=<sidecar.Worktree>` (cwd hint) when `from_keybind=true && req.Prompt == ""`. The narrowing on `req.Prompt == ""` is preserved here to keep the headless-safety guarantee from #2063 review-context. |
| `internal/sandboxenv/sandboxenv.go` | Doc explicitly states `PRISM_SPAWN_PATH` is a working-directory hint only; points to `PRISM_KEYBIND_SPAWN` as the keybind sentinel. |
| `internal/session/spawn.go` | `AllowEmptyPrompt` doc updated to reference `PRISM_KEYBIND_SPAWN`. |

## Test changes

- `cmd/spawn_empty_prompt_test.go`: all assertions updated to the new sentinel. New `TestRunSpawn_SandboxEnvAlone_DoesNotTriggerKeybindCarveOut` pins the AC edge-case: `PRISM_SPAWN_PATH` set, `PRISM_KEYBIND_SPAWN` unset, empty prompt → still rejected.
- `internal/sidecar/sidecar_test.go`: `TestHostAPI_Spawn_FromKeybind_EmptyPromptAccepted` now asserts the child sees both env vars; `TestHostAPI_Spawn_FromKeybind_NonEmptyPrompt_DoesNotSetEnv` asserts both are cleared on the non-empty-prompt malformed-client path; `TestHostAPI_Spawn_NoFromKeybind_EmptyPromptStillRejected` unchanged (it never set env vars).
- `cmd/hostapi_test.go`: defensive `t.Setenv("PRISM_SPAWN_PATH", "")` shims removed in the three empty-prompt-rejection tests (no longer required post-#2073).

## Verification

- `go build ./...` ✅
- `go test ./...` ✅
- `nix build .#prism` ✅
- `nix build .#prism.override { runChecks = true; }` (homeless-shelter gate) ✅

## ACs

body:
## Summary
Root cause: both generators used a vertical band counter (`spaceGenBand`, `stratGenBand`) that only incremented when the cat reached a new altitude. Objects were placed near `catX` at that moment, so everything clustered around the cat's early horizontal position and nothing new spawned as the cat moved further right.

Fix: replaced both with horizontal-sweep generation — the same pattern `generateWorld` uses for trampolines and boosters. A `stratGenX` / `spaceGenX` cursor advances to `cam + W*3` on every frame, placing objects at random Y positions within each zone's altitude range. Density is now uniform no matter how far the cat travels.

- [ ] No noticeable empty gaps after traveling a long horizontal distance

author: kkroo
body:
# fix(heartbeat): exempt `source_scoped_recovery_action` from queued-run staleness guard

## Summary

The pre-claim staleness guard at `evaluateQueuedRunStaleness` was cancelling
**every** `source_scoped_recovery_action` wake on arrival with the error
`issue_assignee_changed`. By design, the recovery owner is a different agent
than the source issue's current assignee (the recovery owner is the
chain-of-command parent of the failed assignee), so the guard's
`issue.assigneeAgentId !== run.agentId` branch always tripped. The
`wake_owner` recovery wake contract has been silently dead in production
since source-scoped recovery actions landed (upstream commit `0808b388e`,
2026-05-12).

## Smoking gun

Live query against the `paperclip` cluster DB, 7-day window:

```sql
select reason, status, count(*)
  from agent_wakeup_requests
 where reason='source_scoped_recovery_action'
   and created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
 group by reason, status;
-- skipped:   289   ← cancelled by the staleness guard
-- cancelled:   3
-- failed:      2
-- completed:   1   ← only 1 recovery wake actually fired in 7 days
```

Of the 289 skipped, **284** were cancelled with the exact error string
`Cancelled because issue assignee changed before the queued run could
start; the new owner will be woken instead`. The full investigation
(timelines, DB-replay, code pointers) lives at
`onprem-k8s/.planning/2026-05-31-paperclip-stuck-recovery-investigation.md`
(separate repo — not bundled here).

## Mechanism

1. Run X fails on issue Y (Y.assigneeAgentId = `engineer-A`).
2. `reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues` creates a recovery action whose
   `wakePolicy.type = "wake_owner"`, with `ownerAgentId` = `cto` (the
   chain-of-command parent — *intentionally* not the failed assignee).
3. `enqueueSourceScopedStrandedRecoveryWake` queues a heartbeat run with
   `agentId = cto`, `wakeReason = "source_scoped_recovery_action"`.
4. The issue's assignee is still `engineer-A` at this point — the recovery
   wake is meant to wake `cto` to *inspect* the failure, not take over.
5. `evaluateQueuedRunStaleness` runs: `issue.assigneeAgentId (engineer-A) !==
   run.agentId (cto)` and `isInteractionWake` is false →
   `errorCode: "issue_assignee_changed"`, run cancelled.

No retry path exists. `reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues` only scans
`todo`/`in_progress` issues (recovery/service.ts:2990), but the
escalation moved the issue to `blocked` — so the sweep never re-visits and
`attemptCount` never advances. One missed wake = a permanently silent
recovery action.

## Fix shape

Single-file two-hunk patch to `server/src/services/heartbeat.ts`
(line ~7239 on current master, line 6859 at investigation HEAD):

```diff
+    // Source-scoped recovery wakes target the recovery owner, who is by design
+    // a different agent than the source issue's current assignee … (full comment in diff)
+    const isRecoveryOwnerWake = wakeReason === "source_scoped_recovery_action";
…
-    if (issue.assigneeAgentId !== run.agentId && !isInteractionWake) {
+    if (issue.assigneeAgentId !== run.agentId && !isInteractionWake && !isRecoveryOwnerWake) {
```

This is Option A from the investigation. The same exemption (`wakeReason
=== "source_scoped_recovery_action"`) already lives at two later sites in
the same file:

- `shouldAutoCheckoutIssueForWake` — returns false for this wake reason
  (don't auto-checkout the issue; the recovery owner isn't supposed to take over).
- `claimQueuedRun` post-claim issue-lock block — skips routine-lock-cancel
  and `executionRunId` stamping for this wake reason.

Without the pre-claim exemption this PR adds, those later exemptions are
unreachable because the run is cancelled before either runs. This is a
clean inconsistency in the source.

## Tests added

In `server/src/__tests__/heartbeat-stale-queue-invalidation.test.ts`:

1. **`runs source_scoped_recovery_action wakes even when the issue assignee
   is a different agent (recovery owner ≠ assignee)`** — the headline
   regression. Seeds an issue assigned to a failed engineer, queues a
   recovery wake for the CTO, asserts `run.status === "succeeded"`,
   `errorCode === null`, no `issue_assignee_changed` error on the wakeup
   request, adapter was invoked exactly once.
2. **`still runs source_scoped_recovery_action wakes when the issue
   assignee has been re-set to the recovery owner mid-flight
   (idempotent)`** — sanity check that the exemption doesn't break the
   case where the issue assignee transitions to the recovery owner before
   the wake is claimed.

Regression preservation is covered by the existing test at line 204 of
the same file (`cancels queued runs when the issue assignee changes
before the run starts`, `wakeReason: "issue_assigned"`) — it still passes.

All 8 tests in the file pass, plus all 80 in
`heartbeat-process-recovery.test.ts` and all 15 in
`heartbeat-issue-liveness-escalation.test.ts` (smoke-tested locally for
regression).

## Followups (intentionally NOT in this PR)

The investigation identifies two further bugs that would make the recovery
loop more resilient. They're tracked separately so this PR stays scoped:

- **`attemptCount` never advances.** Today `upsertSourceScoped` only bumps
  it on re-creation, and re-creation requires the issue to be in
  `todo`/`in_progress` — but the recovery escalation moves it to
  `blocked`. So operators can't tell "the recovery owner has been asked N
  times" even after this fix. Touches
  `enqueueSourceScopedStrandedRecoveryWake` (recovery/service.ts:2597).
- **Re-sweep `blocked` issues with active wake-policy'd recovery
  actions.** Make `reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues` (or a sibling sweep)
  re-process `blocked` issues whose recovery action's last wake attempt
  is older than a threshold. This is the durable fix for the "first wake
  fails or gets dropped → recovery wedges forever" class of bug, not
  just the `issue_assignee_changed` flavor.

## Refs

- BLO-8299
- Investigation: `onprem-k8s/.planning/2026-05-31-paperclip-stuck-recovery-investigation.md`
- Source-scoped recovery feature: upstream commit `0808b388e` (2026-05-12)

body:
## Plotting redesign (Plans A–E)

A first-principles rebuild of the Focus and Series SAXS plotting surfaces, plus the durable data model underneath them. 71 commits; built as five TDD plans on this integration branch, each via a throwaway track-worktree → domain review → merge.

### Four settled architecture decisions
1. **One durable assignment per exposure** — retires the multi-group machinery; the "active set" is now a single per-exposure assignment.
2. **Three explicit states** — `indexed` / `form_factor` / `null` as a real enum, never inferred from `members.length`.
3. **Cart is durable backend state** — no URL serialization.
4. **Plot layer is a greenfield rebuild** — preserve behaviors, not the custom-SVG code.

### The five plans
- **A — backend assignment model:** durable `assignments` / `assignment_members`, 3-state enum, three event kinds (`assignment_add` / `assignment_remove` / `assignment_set_state`), sentinel-gated migration (`migrate_assignments!`), replay-idempotent dispatcher.
- **B — Gauss–Bonnet predictor:** self-contained `src/bonnet.jl` kernel (`bonnet_lattice` / `bonnet_consistent`) + a per-candidate coexistence flag (Pn3m : Im3m : Ia3d = 1.000 : 1.279 : 1.576).
- **C — plot spine:** `peakMark()` / `peakGlyph()` atoms + a greenfield `<PlotSurface>` (Observable Plot in React); retires the `--color-peak-manual` magenta path.
- **D — Focus surface:** assignment cart, combs + residual, phase rings, q-link, plot-only preview, client-fitted custom-index modal.
- **E — Series surface:** waterfall/heatmap, `(phase, order)` migration tracking, phase-strip, derived reading, member rows, form-factor/null distinction, decoupled clean export.
- **D-10 — legacy retirement** ("retire code, keep tables"): re-sourced `confirmed_index` from the assignment; deleted the `/groups` routes + `ensure_custom_group!` + the Plan-A dual-write; converted `index_confirmed` / `index_unconfirmed` to no-op guards; removed the frontend group mutators (kept `deleteIndexMutator`); deleted `FocusReflectionsTable`; bumped the queue `SCHEMA_VERSION` 3 → 4. The `index_groups` / `index_group_members` tables are intentionally **kept** (unused-but-present, droppable later once real-DB migration confidence is established).

### Two migration facts reviewers should weigh
1. **Semantic shift in `confirmed_index`:** it is now the *assigned* index (auto-seeded, ungated), not "a human confirmed it." Because the assignment defaults to the auto seed (`state='indexed'` for every analyzed exposure) and the R² gate was removed, every analyzed-but-never-touched exposure now reports a non-null `confirmed_index` post-migration — where the legacy `kind='custom'` snapshot reported `nothing`. Intended (3-state model); documented at `compute_member_snapshot`. All frontend consumers use `confirmed_index` for rendering only.
2. **Rebuild not log-derivable for pre-Plan-A confirmations:** those have `index_confirmed` events (now no-ops) and no paired `assignment_add`, so their assignment exists solely via the sentinel-gated backfill. A from-empty `rebuild_views_from_log!` must clear the `assignments_v1` sentinel and re-run `migrate_assignments!` first. Documented at both call sites.

### Testing
- Backend (HimalayaUI Julia): full suite green, 0 failures (~1955 tests).
- Frontend: 194 test files / 1608 tests green; `tsc --noEmit` + `vite build` + `lint:design` clean.
- Core Himalaya: green.
- Migration safety specifically covered: auto-only seed, sentinel idempotency protecting post-migration user edits, no-active-group boundary.

### Review status going in
Each plan was domain-reviewed at merge; D-10 got a final three-reviewer pass (himalaya / queue / frontend) — queue + frontend clean, two doc-only MED findings folded.

body:
## What this is

Follow-up to PR #8 — three bugs Codex flagged after merge. Two P1 correctness issues that could cost money in live mode, plus one P2 logic gap that silently disables auto-trade in a common configuration.

## P1 #1 — Local position store could diverge from broker on partial / unfilled orders

`place_order` returning 200 only means Kalshi **accepted** the limit order. The order can rest unfilled (book moved before placement) or fill only partially (size exceeds available liquidity at the chosen price). The merged code unconditionally recorded the full requested size as a local position, so risk aggregation, settlement auto-close, and realized P&L would all diverge from the actual broker account.

**Fix:** parse the fill count from the order response, with fallbacks for the field-name variants Kalshi has shipped across API versions (`taker_fill_count`, `fill_count`, `filled_quantity`, `filled_count`). When nothing definitive is present, infer from `status` (`executed` = full fill, `resting`/`queued`/`canceled` = 0). When in doubt, return 0 — better to under-record locally than to over-record and diverge from the broker.

- **0 fill:** don't write a local position; return `placed=False`, surface the order id in the audit log so the operator can chase it via the Kalshi UI.
- **Partial fill:** write a position with the **actual filled size** (not the requested size), with a "PARTIAL" note.
- **Full fill:** as before.

## P1 #2 — `fire --side` / `--price` overrides were silently dropped

The fire command extracted the overrides, displayed them in the confirmation panel, the operator typed "y" — then `maybe_trade` re-derived side/price from the snapshot, ignoring the overrides. In live mode that could place an order entirely different from the one confirmed, especially when overriding a stale ask or taking the opposite side manually.

**Fix:** `AutoTrader.maybe_trade` now accepts `side_override` / `price_override` keyword-only parameters. When both are provided, they bypass `_derive_side_and_price`. The risk guard still runs against the override values — overrides bypass derivation, not safety.

## P2 #3 — `serve --auto-trade` without `--notify` silently never trades

The `fired` list was only populated inside `if sinks:`, so a headless paper run (`--auto-trade --paper` with no notification sinks) would log "auto-trade PAPER enabled" then never call `maybe_trade` for any alert.

**Fix:** instantiate the dispatcher when **either** sinks or auto_trade is on. The dispatcher's alert-transition logic runs independently of sinks; an empty sinks list just means no notification emission, but the Alert objects still come back for the auto-trader to consume.

## Tests

```
pytest    # 306 passed
```

6 new tests:
- Updated `test_auto_trader_live_mode_places_real_order` to include status + fill count in the mock response (the old shape would now correctly skip as resting).
- `test_auto_trader_live_mode_skips_unfilled_resting_order` — resting order returns `placed=False`, no position written, order id surfaced.
- `test_auto_trader_live_mode_records_partial_fill_with_actual_size` — 3-of-10 fill writes a 3-contract position with PARTIAL note.
- `test_fill_count_handles_alternate_field_names` — parser tries each known field name, falls back to status inference, clamps to `[0, requested]`.
- `test_auto_trader_honors_side_and_price_overrides` — with a high-edge_yes snap, the `dead_no`-derived `side=no` is overridden to `side=yes` + `price=15` and the position records the override.
- `test_auto_trader_overrides_still_pass_through_risk_guard` — nonsensical override (price=99c against fair=1c) is refused by the min-edge check.
- `test_dispatcher_returns_alerts_with_empty_sinks` — confirms `AlertDispatcher` returns fired alerts even with `sinks=[]`, which is what `serve --auto-trade --paper` relies on for headless runs.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest` is green (306)
- [ ] `kalshi-scout serve --store /data/scout.db --auto-trade --paper` (no `--notify`) actually evaluates alerts and writes audit-log entries — the merged behavior would silently do nothing.
- [ ] `kalshi-scout fire <ticker> --size 1 --side yes --price 30 --paper --yes` records a position with `side=yes, price=30c`, not the snapshot-derived side/price.
- [ ] Live mode end-to-end (real Kalshi key): if a limit order doesn't fill immediately, `positions list` is empty for that ticker and the audit log shows `placed=False, reason="order resting but unfilled..."`.

author: duyiliu
body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #17012
Closes #21335

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The session prompt loop (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`) uses `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` to decide whether the latest assistant message already corresponds to the latest user message. This comparison relies on lexicographic ID ordering, which is only reliable when both IDs come from the same process.

When the web UI runs on a remote/LAN browser, user message IDs are generated client-side while assistant message IDs are generated server-side. The ordering assumption breaks across machines, so the loop incorrectly concludes that no assistant has responded to the current user turn and starts a new assistant generation — producing a duplicate assistant message.

The fix replaces the ID ordering check with an explicit parent relationship:

```ts
// Before (breaks across machines):
lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id

// After (reliable regardless of where IDs are generated):
lastAssistant.parentID === lastUser.id
```

Every assistant message already carries `parentID` pointing to the user message it responds to, so this is a direct and correct one-line replacement.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Ran the opencode backend from source with this fix on a Windows host (0.0.0.0:4096)
- Accessed the web UI from a separate PC on the same LAN (http://192.168.3.6:4096)
- **Before the fix**: every prompt produced two duplicate assistant messages
- **After the fix**: each prompt produces exactly one assistant response
- Also verified that localhost access continues to work correctly

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A — the bug manifests as duplicate text in the chat UI, not a visual layout issue.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

author: ialexeze
body:
## What this PR does

Three parallel workstreams that reinforce each other: a dev server that makes all external examples runnable locally, a set of refined examples that surface real operator patterns, and correctness fixes in the drift detection and condition evaluation engine.

---

## Dev server (`pkg/devserver/`)

A lightweight mock HTTP server started with `ork run --dev-server`. Runs on `:9999` (configurable with `--dev-server-port`). Serves every endpoint the `external:` example katalogs call — health, config, image signing, auth token, resource stubs, and feature flags with live in-memory toggle via `POST /flags/:name/:flag/toggle`.

No real services. No tokens. No internet. The full external example pack works out of the box.

## External examples pack (`examples/use-cases/external/`)

Five focused examples, each a standalone `katalog.yaml + cr.yaml + README + cleanup.sh`:

| Example | Pattern |
|---|---|
| 01 — Health Gate | `external:` as a required gate on Deployment creation |
| 02 — Config Inject | Optional config fetch embedded into a ConfigMap every reconcile |
| 03 — Image Signing | "Once per image" call with 4xx rejection tracking and 5xx retry |
| 04 — Chained Calls | Sequential calls — second uses the first call's token |
| 05 — Feature Flags | External call drives `replicas` directly, not just a gate |

**03 image signing** introduces `rejectedImage` in status — a 4xx response closes the gate permanently for that image (the reconcile loop is the retry for 5xx, not for definitive rejections). Phase is `SigningRejected` when `status.rejectedImage == spec.image`, `SigningUnavailable` on 5xx.

**05 feature flags** demonstrates that `external.*` fields can drive resource attributes. Two deployment entries target the same name with different replica counts — exactly one fires per reconcile based on the live flag value.

## Full-stack-app refactored (`examples/use-cases/full-stack-app/`)

Monolith `katalog.yaml` split into six per-example `katalog.yaml` files with a `komposer.yaml` at the root that imports them. Each subfolder is now standalone — `ork validate` and `ork run` from inside the folder works without the komposer. Per-example READMEs written for all six patterns with the same structure as the external examples. Root README follows the enrich/profiles convention (table + links, no tutorial).

## Bug fixes

**`pkg/types/when.go` — template expressions in condition comparison values**
`equals: "{{ .spec.image }}"` now resolves correctly. The comparison value (from `c.Equals`, `c.NotEquals`, etc.) was used raw — it is now evaluated through the template engine before the comparison. Unblocks the image signing `when: signedImage == spec.image` deployment gate.

**`pkg/reconciler/run_external.go` — results available after `continueOnError: false` failure**
`resolver.WithExternal(results)` now fires before the early return on a hard failure. Status fields that reference `external.<name>.*` now have data to work with even when the reconcile halts. Required for surfacing rejection details in status.

**`pkg/orkestra-registry/common/sync.go` — spurious drift updates**
`SyncContainerSpec` and `SyncPodSpec` were comparing all fields unconditionally. Kubernetes defaults (`ServiceAccountName = "default"`, port `Protocol = "TCP"`) differed from Orkestra's zero values every reconcile, triggering an update on every cycle. Now all fields use "declared intent" guards — only sync when `desired` is non-zero. `Env` bidirectional to handle explicit clearing.

## `protocol:` field on workload types

Added to `DeploymentTemplateSource`, `ReplicaSetTemplateSource`, `StatefulSetTemplateSource`, `PodTemplateSource`. Resolved in each `Resolve()` via `common.ParseProtocol()` (shared helper, same switch as services). Used in each `build*` function — `spec.Protocol` defaults to `corev1.ProtocolTCP` when not declared, matching what Kubernetes stores. Eliminates the remaining source of spurious port drift.

## `validatePortProtocols()` — step 29

Catches invalid `protocol:` values at `ork validate` time across all workload types. Uses the existing visitor pattern (`VisitResources` + `ported` interface) so all three reconcile phases are covered in one loop. Rich error with CRD name, resource name, and phase.

The pattern itself is now documented in `pkg/types/docs/hook-visitor-pattern.md` for contributors adding future validators.

---

## Testing

- `make ork` passes clean
- `ork validate` passes on all five external katalogs and the full-stack komposer
- `ork run --dev-server` + apply `cr-reject.yaml` in 03-image-signing: phase `SigningRejected`, no Deployment, 1 external call total (`orkestra_external_calls_total count=1`)
- `ork run --dev-server` + feature flag toggle: Deployment scales 5→1→5 across reconcile cycles
- No spurious "deployment updated" logs on steady-state reconciles after drift fix

author: j-wang
body:
The seam for fleet-wide engine sync: the retrieval engine becomes an installable package that derivative agents pin and bump, instead of each vendoring (and drifting) its own copy.

## What changed
- **`engine/kb_engine/`** — the five modules (`search`, `build_embeddings`, `kb_docs`, `providers`, `retrieval_config`) move into a package with its own `engine/pyproject.toml` (`name = "kb-engine"`, hatchling). Intra-package imports made relative; PEP-723 headers dropped from the moved modules (deps live in the package now).
- **Root shims** — `search.py` / `build_embeddings.py` become thin PEP-723 shims that import the package. `python3 search.py` / `uv run search.py` is **unchanged**, so the PRIMER / harness-contract CLI binding needs no edits anywhere.
- **Location independence** — the engine now resolves corpus / `.env` / index artifacts from **`KB_ROOT`** (env var the shim sets to its own dir; defaults to cwd) instead of `__file__`. Without this, a pip-installed engine would read paths next to the *package*, not the consuming agent — most importantly `.env`, which carries the per-agent retrieval (TEI/bge-m3) config. (This `.env` path was the one bug found in review and fixed.)
- **Docs** — README structure + new **"Sharing the engine across derivative agents"** section (the shim / git-dep / `KB_ROOT` pattern, and "bump the tag to roll out"); CLAUDE structure listing updated.

## How a derivative consumes it
Replace each shim's dependency block with the published package pinned to a tag, and drop the local `sys.path` line:
```python
# /// script
# dependencies = ["kb-engine @ git+ssh://git@github.com/j-wang/knowledge-agent-template.git@engine-v1#subdirectory=engine"]
# ///
import os, pathlib
os.environ.setdefault("KB_ROOT", str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from kb_engine.search import main
main()
```
Sync = bump `@engine-v1` → `@engine-v2`. No code copying, no drift.

## Validation
- Packaged engine reproduces the **markets goldset BM25 baseline exactly** — recall@5/MRR@10/nDCG@10 = **0.923/0.766/0.814** — pointed at the markets corpus via `KB_ROOT`.
- `ENV_PATH` resolves under `KB_ROOT`; imports resolve as a package; empty-corpus case degrades cleanly ("No documents found").

## On merge
Tag the merge commit **`engine-v1`** so agents can pin it. Follow-up: a markets-knowledge PR that swaps its vendored engine files for the shim + pinned dep (the first real consumer), then the remaining four agents adopt the same way during their ports.

author: ai-personas
body:
## Context

Closes a lifecycle gap surfaced by a coverage review of the persona "run-forever / heartbeat / idle" model. The intended behavior: personas run indefinitely (a heartbeat) until they **retire** (the sole terminus); they serve one *or more* environments; they may *voluntarily* jump to another env to help; and they go **idle** when they (a) lack token budget, (b) have no model availability, (c) hit env constraints, or (d) have no pending work / their env objective is met.

The review found the lifecycle loop, **multi-env membership** (`05_ENVIRONMENT §6.3`), and **voluntary env-jumping** (`CrossEnvProactiveOffer`/`GuestPresence`, `§11.6`) already first-class, and retirement already the sole terminus. The genuine gap: the *only* enumerated cause of `DORMANT` entry was `importance < τ_dormant`; the four idle triggers were each handled as **state-less refusals** (per-task `budget_exhausted`, a quarantined body binding, per-action `ATTENTION_OVER_BUDGET`) that never parked the *persona*, and resource recovery had no defined wake.

## Decision (ADR-0057)

**"Idle mode" is `DORMANT` carrying an enumerated `reason` + auto-resume — not a new FSM state.** `LIFECYCLE_DORMANT_ENTERED` now records a `reason` ∈ {`low_salience`, `unresponsive`, `budget_starved`, `body_unavailable`, `env_constrained`, `work_drained`, `objective_met`}; each is wired at a real entry point and paired with a kernel-monitored auto-resume predicate (`LIFECYCLE_AWAKENED.wake_cause`). Resource/no-work auto-resume is **not** a 7th wake path — the six wake paths overcome notification suppression; this is state restoration on resource return.

## What changed (7 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `02_PERSONA.md` | New **§7.6** + Appendix **A.18a** (reasons, "sustained" threshold + hysteresis, auto-resume); **A.18** FSM diagram relabeled; **A.19** `reason`/`wake_cause` fields; **A.11** all-bodies-unavailable → `DORMANT(body_unavailable)` |
| `01_KERNEL.md` | **A.37** distinguishes per-task `budget_exhausted` (ends task) from sustained per-persona soft-envelope exhaustion (`budget_starved` parks persona) |
| `05_ENVIRONMENT.md` | **§6.3** multi-membership `work_drained`/`objective_met` evaluated across **all** N memberships; **§7** sustained over-budget → `env_constrained`; **§5.2** note that auto-resume is not a 7th wake path |
| `00_VISION.md` | **INV-9** framing + risk **R-v1.0-15** |
| `12_GLOSSARY.md` | New **DormancyReason** term; **LifecycleEvent** updated |
| `14_DECISIONS.md` | **ADR-0057** |
| `11_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md` | **A-LE5..A-LE9**; count `~472 → ~477` |

## Invariants preserved

No new FSM state, no new lineage scope. The "8 safety-floor sources", "6 wake paths", and "3 lineage scopes" counts are untouched; `INV_R9` (no DORMANT persona mints an envelope) holds for **every** reason; lineage-replay determinism is unaffected.

## Conformance

Adversarial multi-agent review: **0 contradiction findings, 0 broken cross-refs.** The three confirmed completeness gaps are fixed:
- undefined `"sustained"` threshold → operator-policy `dormancy_park_threshold` with concrete defaults (2 budget-refresh cycles / 1 h `park_window`);
- flapping → symmetric park threshold + resume predicate (hysteresis), once-per-signal evaluation;
- RFC-2119 `MAY` in a historical-narrative frame → rephrased to a precise normative statement.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds periodic heap memory diagnostics to help detect memory leaks and fragmentation issues under HomeKit load, and reduces HomeKit logging verbosity to prevent serial port blocking during high-rate controller polling.

## Key Changes

- **New `logHeapStats()` function** in `PresenceRuntime.cpp`:
  - Periodically logs free heap, largest allocatable block (fragmentation indicator), and minimum free heap since boot
  - Controlled by new `HEAP_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` config constant (30 seconds by default; 0 disables)
  - Called once per `presenceTick()` with throttling to respect the interval
  - Helps identify memory leaks (steadily falling minimum) vs. fragmentation (shrinking largest block)

- **HomeKit log level reduction** in `PresenceIntegrations.cpp`:
  - Changed `homeSpan.setLogLevel(1)` to `homeSpan.setLogLevel(0)` (quiet mode)
  - Rationale: Level 1 floods the serial port with blocking "In Get Characteristics" prints on every HAP poll, starving the loop task during the controller's high-rate polling
  - Added explanatory comment documenting the issue

- **New config constant** in `PresenceConfig.h`:
  - `HEAP_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` (30000 ms default) — allows tuning or disabling heap diagnostics at compile time

## Implementation Details

The heap logging is guarded by `#if HEAP_LOG_INTERVAL_MS > 0` to allow compile-time disabling. The throttling mechanism uses a static `lastHeapLog` timestamp to avoid excessive logging overhead. Output includes `ESP.getFreeHeap()`, `ESP.getMaxAllocHeap()`, and `ESP.getMinFreeHeap()` to provide a complete picture of heap health.

author: robot-head
body:
## What

`MetadataImage::to_records()` — the KIP-630 snapshot serializer used by `SnapshotWriter` — emitted **no `V1FeatureLevel` records**, so every finalized KIP-584 feature and the `features_epoch` were silently dropped whenever an image was rebuilt from a snapshot. Both paths that reconstruct an image go through `MetadataImage::from_records`, not the live log:

- restart recovery (`state_machine.rs` `recover`)
- learner `install_snapshot`

So after any compaction or learner snapshot-install:

- **`metadata.version` reverted to UNKNOWN** → the range guard stopped enforcing and the SCRAM / delegation-token gates went permissive.
- **`group.version` vanished** → the next-gen consumer-group protocol (`ConsumerGroupHeartbeat`/`Describe`) would silently disable.

This was pre-existing (since the #307 metadata.version enforcement slice) but became functionally visible once `group.version` finalization/gating started depending on it.

## The subtlety

Naively emitting one `V1FeatureLevel` per live feature and letting `from_records` replay them does **not** round-trip the epoch: `apply` bumps `features_epoch` once per applied record, so replaying N feature records reconstructs `epoch = N − 1`, which generally ≠ the original (the epoch tracks the *history* of `UpdateFeatures` applies, not the live feature count). `MetadataImage` derives `PartialEq` and the round-trip tests assert exact equality, so an emit-only fix would break them.

## Fix

A snapshot-only `FeaturesEpochRecord` / `MetadataRecord::V1FeaturesEpoch` carrier that `to_records` emits **last**; its `apply` **sets** the epoch verbatim rather than bumping, pinning the reconstructed epoch to the original. This keeps `to_records`/`from_records` an exact, self-contained inverse — both image- and snapshot-level round-trips are now exact — with **zero raft-crate production changes**. The carrier is produced only by `to_records` and replayed only on snapshot install; it is never submitted as a controller change, so it never appears in the live Raft log.

## Tests

- Strengthened the image-level and snapshot-level round-trip tests to cover **two finalized features at a non-trivial epoch** (`metadata.version=25` + `group.version=1`, epoch=3 via a re-finalize so epoch > live count) — closing the coverage hole (feature-free fixtures) that let this ship.
- Added a serde round-trip test for the new record variant.
- Extended the real restart-recovery and learner-InstallSnapshot integration tests (`crates/raft/tests/snapshot.rs`) to finalize `metadata.version=25` and assert it survives recovery / install.

All green: metadata lib (87), raft lib + reconfig + single_node + snapshot integration, clippy `--all-targets`, and `cargo fmt --check`.

## Reviewer notes

- **`group.version` gating isn't on this branch** (the heartbeat handler has no feature gate on `main` yet), so the integration tests exercise the equivalent `metadata.version` survival. The mechanism covers `group.version` automatically once that lands.
- **`voters` / `kraft_version` are a related gap:** `to_records` drops these too, and unlike features they *are* read in production (`broker.rs` voter serving, `auto_join`). Left out of this PR because the fix must reconcile with openraft restoring `last_membership` from the `.meta` sidecar separately (two sources of truth) — flagged for separate follow-up.

author: bprochazka-bit
body:
## Summary

Live validation of the 0.1.2 rename change surfaced a security asymmetry:
the emulated `/key/rename` copied each key's descriptor with the full mask
(including SACL), and setting a descriptor with the SACL bit makes offreg
stamp an explicit empty SACL (`S:NO_ACCESS_CONTROL`) on keys whose source had
none. The renamed subtree then carried a one-sided SACL versus libreg.

Fix: copy owner, group, and DACL only (set with `SEC_NO_SACL`). Offline-hive
SACLs are unreliable and ADR 0003 does not fail the `semantic` tag on a
one-sided SACL, so dropping it is the clean choice and keeps the renamed key's
descriptor symmetric with its source.

## Validation

Reproduced live before the fix: a renamed key read back
`O:BAG:BAD:(...)S:NO_ACCESS_CONTROL` while its source had no SACL token.
Builds clean for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`; 16 unit tests pass under wine. Needs
the rebuilt exe redeployed for the post-fix live recheck.

One-line change in `agents/windows/src/offreg/key.rs`.

author: willsneves
body:
## Por que

O token gov.br do cidadão era só **armazenado/validado** — quando o access token
expirava (tipicamente 5-60min), `get_token()` retornava `None` e o cidadão tinha
que **reautenticar**, mesmo com o `refresh_token` ainda válido (horas/dias). Não
havia lógica de refresh em lugar nenhum (Gateway nem MCP).

## O que muda — `src/utils/govbr_token.py` (self-contained no MCP)

Usa `GOVBR_CLIENT_ID`/`GOVBR_CLIENT_SECRET`/`GOVBR_TOKEN_URL` que **já existem** no
MCP — **sem mudanças no Gateway**, sem conflito com o PR #47 (auto-resume).

- **`refresh_token(user_number)`** — renova via `grant_type=refresh_token` quando o
  access expirou mas o refresh é válido.
- **`get_token(allow_refresh=True)`** — chama o refresh de forma transparente. Logo
  `is_authenticated()` e `get_token_metadata()` (tool de status gov.br) passam a
  manter o cidadão autenticado sem reautenticar.
- **`_post_refresh`** — só `invalid_grant` (400/401 com `error=invalid_grant`) é
  falha definitiva (apaga o token); outros 4xx/5xx/rede são transitórios. Deadline
  **total** via `asyncio.wait_for` (o timeout do httpx é por-fase).
- **`save_token`** — TTL = `max(access, refresh)`, pro `refresh_token` sobreviver à
  expiração do access (igual ao `storeTokens` do Gateway).

## Concorrência (8 rounds de `codex review`)

- Lock `SETNX` com **valor único** por aquisição; **release atômico** via Lua
  compare-and-delete (ownership) — não apaga o lock de outro worker.
- TTL do lock (15s) **>** deadline do POST (10s); poll cobre o TTL antes de desistir
  (não reporta "não autenticado" durante um refresh concorrente normal).
- Mutação do registro (`setex`/`delete`) **atômica via Lua CAS** keyed no
  `refresh_token` — fecha a corrida com `revoke_token` (logout) e re-auth do Gateway,
  que não pegam o lock: **não ressuscita logout, não sobrescreve login novo**.
- Scripts Lua são **fixos** (server-side Redis, não `eval()` de Python; só dados em ARGV).

## Testes

`src/tests/unit/utils/test_govbr_token.py` — **20 casos**: happy/rotação/sem-rotação/
invalid_grant/transitório/refresh-expirado/lock-contention/lock-timeout/logout-durante-
POST/re-auth-durante-POST/ownership-do-lock/TTL-longo + `_post_refresh` (200/invalid_grant/
invalid_client/5xx) + `get_token` auto-refresh. Suíte `utils` **155 verde**; `ruff check`
+ `ruff format` limpos.

> Nota: o token gov.br do cidadão ainda não é consumido por nenhuma tool downstream;
> este PR torna a **sessão de auth durável** (valor imediato em `is_authenticated`) e
> é base pra quando a primeira tool consumir o token. E2E real (refresh contra o
> Identidade Carioca) requer ambiente com credenciais — fora do escopo local.

author: sansteelo17
body:
## Why
Production symptoms: Yara wasn't analyzing anything, news was sparse, Henderson showed "99% Medium," and the basis note read like an excuse. Root causes were config + two real bugs.

## What
- **LLM was off in production.** `render.yaml` set no narrative env vars and `.env` isn't deployed, so every narrative was deterministic template text. Added `NARRATIVE_LLM_PROVIDER`, `INTL_NARRATIVE_LLM_PROVIDER`, `OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini`, `INTL_OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-5.5`, temperature/timeout. **`OPENAI_API_KEY` is `sync: false`** — set it in the Render dashboard.
- **Reasoning-model token bug.** GPT-5.x spends part of `max_completion_tokens` on hidden reasoning; the old 300 cap left visible content empty, so WC (gpt-5.5) narratives silently fell back to template even with the LLM on. Floor the reasoning-model budget at 1200.
- **Risk cohort bug (99% Medium / 0 High).** `get_risk_level` only read `competition_id` from a `dict`; the team overview passes a pandas `Series`, so WC squad players were ranked against all 3,800+ players (mostly club) → Medium, while the detail (dict) said High. Read via `.get` so both use the WC cohort. Henderson is now **High 99%** in both views (percentile 1.000 within the 237-player WC cohort).
- **Smarter news.** Replaced homepage-feed scraping with per-player **Google News RSS** so marquee players reliably get recent, attributed coverage (reputable outlets lead, every item links to source). Henderson/Bellingham/Mbappé/Haaland all return real items.
- **Narrative actually analyzes.** New WC task leads with the risk number and its drivers, says what it means for the next fixture, and cites at most one attributed news item. Verified live on gpt-5.5:
  > "I have Jordan Henderson at 77% over the next 2 weeks because a 2.19 ACWR, 15 prior injuries, and age 35 all point the same way. England have Group L next at home to Croatia... The Telegraph reports Adam Wharton should be at the World Cup but not in place of Jordan Henderson, and I still see Henderson running on fumes."
- **Copy.** Reframed the international basis note (confident season-workload language, no em dash). Header now states the value prop: predicts injury risk and builds the story behind it from every source.

## Deploy requirement
Set **`OPENAI_API_KEY`** in the Render dashboard for `yara-sports-api`, or narratives stay on template text (the startup probe logs the model OK/FAILED either way).

## Verification
- `py_compile` + `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Live: Google News per-player, WC cohort percentile (Henderson → High), and a full gpt-5.5 narrative weaving risk + fixture + attributed news.

author: stephenlutar2-hash
body:
## Summary

The 2026-05-31 post-merge re-test wave found **Wire B (a11oy → sentra) was contract-mismatched**: a11oy mesh-router was POSTing `/v1/verdict` with body `{actionId, kind, payload}`, but sentra (PR #96) deployed `POST /v1/inspect` with body `{action, actionId, traceparent?}`. Live test returned **404** — the immune organ was unreachable in production despite both endpoints existing.

This PR re-targets `requestSentraVerdict()` at sentra's deployed route.

## Contract change

| Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Path | `POST /v1/verdict` | `POST /v1/inspect` |
| Body | `{actionId, kind, payload}` | `{action, actionId, traceparent?}` |
| Response | `{decision, reason}` | `{actionId, decision, gate, decidedBy, rationale, lambdaScore, receiptHash, traceparent}` |

## Wire compatibility

Public types (`SentraVerdictRequest`, `SentraVerdict`) are **unchanged** — no caller moves. Internally:

- `verdictRequestToInspectBody()` folds the public `kind` field into `action.kind` so sentra's signature-scan can still see it.
- `inspectResponseToVerdict()` maps sentra's `rationale` down to the public `reason` field.
- `SentraVerdictRequest` now optionally accepts a `traceparent` so W3C trace propagation flows through Wire B as it already does through C/D.

## Fail-closed posture (Doctrine v7 strict)

Original module already failed closed on transport error + no-config. This PR adds two more closed states:

- `HTTP 404` → deny (legacy /v1/verdict probe)
- unrecognised decision (anything other than `allow`|`deny`) → deny

Both are exercised by new tests. The immune organ silently allowing nothing is the load-bearing invariant.

## Tests — 12/12 pass

```
✔ requestSentraVerdict POSTs /v1/inspect with the anatomy-contracts body shape
✔ requestSentraVerdict propagates traceparent into the /v1/inspect body when provided
✔ requestSentraVerdict FAILS CLOSED (deny) when sentra is unreachable
✔ requestSentraVerdict FAILS CLOSED on a 404 (legacy /v1/verdict not exposed)
✔ requestSentraVerdict FAILS CLOSED when sentra returns a garbage decision
✔ requestSentraVerdict FAILS CLOSED when sentra not configured
+ 6 existing tests (amaru state/receipts/chakra, rosie events, transport, env config)
```

Run locally:
```
cd packages/mesh-router && node --experimental-strip-types src/index.test.ts
```

## After this lands

With sentra #96 already merged + this PR: a11oy ↔ sentra is wired end-to-end with W3C trace propagation, fail-closed defaults, and anatomy-contracts-shaped body/response. Closes the **#1 top issue** from the post-merge re-test wave (`/home/user/workspace/szl/audit_2026-05-30_cursor_offline/post_merge_retest/POST_MERGE_LEDGER.md`).

author: unstablellama
body:
Granite is a Llama-style dense decoder (GQA, RoPE, SwiGLU, RMSNorm, tied embeddings) plus four muP scalar multipliers:

- embedding_multiplier  -> Embedding(multiplier=...)
- attention_multiplier  -> Attention(sm_scale=...) (replaces 1/sqrt(head_dim))
- logits_scaling        -> Linear(post_scale = 1/logits_scaling)
- residual_multiplier   -> scales each sublayer output before the residual add

The first three reuse existing primitives. residual_multiplier is added as a new optional TransformerBlock argument (default None = no-op), applied in the attn/mlp residual-add branches and propagated through tp_export, matching the block's existing per-layer scalar conventions.

Covers the dense Granite 4.1 language models (3B/8B/30B) and Granite 3.x dense; not the Granite 4.0 hybrid Mamba-2 / MoE models. Also adds a 'granite' prompt format preset to examples/chat.py matching the model's chat_template.jinja.

Verified against HF Transformers in bf16: 100% argmax agreement, KL ~1e-5 on https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b

Example Quantization:

author: alexey-milovidov
body:
Update the `fix-sync` skill to handle the three distinct ways the "CH Inc sync" job can fail, instead of assuming every failure is a merge conflict and immediately trying to merge `master`.

The skill now diagnoses the failure type by reading the "CH Inc sync" commit status description and routes to the matching handler:
- `conflicts found` — resolve the merge conflicts in the sync PR.
- `build failed` — fix the build (usually private-only code needing adaptation to an upstream change).
- `tests failed` — distinguish flaky/infra failures (rerun the failed jobs) from genuine regressions.

It falls back to inspecting the sync PR's mergeable state and private CI checks if the status description is missing.

The companion change that makes the CI emit these three descriptions is in the private repository: `ClickHouse/clickhouse-private#59403`.

author: phaware-artie
body:
## Problem

`plugins/stuck-agent-dog/run.sh` iterated its `CRASHED` and `STUCK` arrays with bare `for ENTRY in "${ARR[@]}"`. On bash 3.2 a bare expansion trips `set -u`, and the `${ARR[@]:-}` workaround iterates **once over an empty string** when the array is empty — yielding empty `RIG`/`PCAT` and a bogus `"/witness"` mail address (root cause of `hq-wisp-ekvkez`, `hq-s8oa8`).

## Solution

Wrap each action loop in an array-length guard so an empty array skips the loop entirely:

```bash
if [ "${#CRASHED[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  for ENTRY in "${CRASHED[@]}"; do ... done
fi
```

Same guard applied to the `STUCK` (zombie) loop. No behavior change when the arrays are non-empty.

## Test plan

- `bash -n plugins/stuck-agent-dog/run.sh` — clean
- `go build ./...` — clean
- `go test ./internal/plugin/...` — passes

author: mmurshed
body:
## What

The CRT-NTT multiply is memory-bandwidth bound at large sizes (profiled: serial→8-thread = 3.08×, single-core IPC 2.49, 4 shared-nothing processes aggregate only 2.6×). Two per-call zero-fills were pure wasted memory traffic:

- `mfaScratch[0..5]` were `assign(n, 0)` before use, but each scratch is fully written by the step-1 `Transpose` (recursive sub-calls write their slice) before any read → ~6n redundant writes/multiply. Now `resize(n)`.
- `fa/fb` forward buffers were `assign(n, 0)`, then `PackOperand` overwrote the head `[0, *CoeffSize)`. Only the zero-pad tail needs clearing → `resize(n)` + `std::fill` of the tail, removing a double-write of ~aCoeffSize+bCoeffSize elements/multiply.

## Benchmark (mul_xl_bench, M1 Max, base 2^64, best-of-5)

| size | digits | before | after | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.3M limbs | 25M | 1018.7 ms | 960.9 ms | **−5.6%** |
| 2.6M limbs | 50M | 1786.9 ms | 1726.4 ms | **−3.3%** |
| 5.2M limbs | 100M | 3916.4 ms | 3909.2 ms | −0.1% |

Win concentrates below the MFA band (n < 2^24) where the dropped fills are a larger fraction; at 100M digits the MFA transform passes dominate and zero-fill (ideal sequential write) is a small time share. No regression at any size.

## Correctness

`tests/mult_correctness.cpp` passes — all algorithms match the classic reference across all sizes including max-carry and unbalanced cases.

author: heywood8
body:
## Summary

- Add pointerEvents="none" to the main settings Animated.View when activeSubPanel is not null

## Problem

On a real Pixel 7 Pro, tapping anything inside a settings subpanel (back button, language items, export options, etc.) had no effect. Only swipe-back worked. The emulator exhibited no issues.

Root cause: On Android, opacity 0 does NOT remove a view from the touch hit-test tree. The Animated.View containing the main settings list animates to opacity 0 when a subpanel opens, but stays fully hittable. Since it covers the same screen area as the absolute-positioned subpanel, it silently swallows every tap. The emulator uses a softer touch dispatch model that masks the overlap.

## Solution

One-line fix: pointerEvents={activeSubPanel ? 'none' : 'auto'} on the settings list Animated.View. When a subpanel is active the settings list is excluded from touch dispatch entirely.

## Test plan

- Tap any settings row - subpanel slides in
- Tap items inside subpanel - all respond normally on real device
- Tap back arrow - subpanel closes
- Swipe right - subpanel closes (existing gesture still works)
- All 117 affected unit tests passing

body:
Description
 Adds graceful degradation to the rate limiter when Redis becomes unreachable. Previously, any ConnectionError or TimeoutError from RedisBackend would bubble up as an unhandled exception, causing a 500 Internal Server Error on every rate-limited endpoint. Now the limiter catches those errors, logs a warning, and transparently falls back to a shared InMemoryBackend singleton so requests continue to be served.

Related Issues

Changes Made

Added _fallback_backend = InMemoryBackend() module-level singleton to preserve sliding-window state across all requests during Redis degradation

Wrapped backend.is_allowed() call in RateLimiter.__call__ with a try/except block to intercept Redis connectivity failures
Lazily imported redis.exceptions.ConnectionError and TimeoutError so the module remains functional in InMemoryBackend-only deployments where the redis package is not installed

Re-raise non-Redis exceptions (e.g. programming errors) to prevent silent swallowing of unrelated bugs

Added 4 unit tests in TestRateLimiterRedisFallback covering ConnectionError fallback, TimeoutError fallback, non-Redis exception re-raise, and verifying the request is allowed (not 429) after fallback

Updated CHANGELOG.md with a ### Fixed entry under [Unreleased]

Verification

Added unit tests

 Code is fully documented and type-hinted

author: lloydmeta
body:
Under Gradle `maxParallelForks > 1`, concurrent JVMs share `test-classes/` and race on the jandex index file. `writeIndex` truncated the shared file via `FileOutputStream(file, false)` while another writer's open FD kept writing at a non-zero offset, leaving a sparse-zero prefix that failed `IndexReader`'s magic check with `IllegalArgumentException: Not a jandex index`, killing the worker.

This changset updates
* `writeIndex`: write to a sibling temp file and `Files.move(..., ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING)`
*  `readIndex`: tolerate `IllegalArgumentException` as defence in depth
* Adds regression tests for the above

---

- Fixes: #54579

author: magent-cryptograss
body:
## Why

delivery-kid's BuildKit cache grew to 28 GB across 337 entries on 2026-05-30 and took the host to 100% disk, killing the next deploy at the **Install required packages** task with the unhelpful \`Failed to update apt cache: unknown reason\`.

Root cause: every \`--rebuild\` deploy runs \`docker compose build --no-cache\`, and \`--no-cache\` bypasses cache *use* but still **creates new BuildKit cache entries**. With no prune step in the playbook, those entries accumulate forever. The same pattern existed in hunter's base-image rebuild and pickipedia-vps's wiki build — both would have hit this eventually.

## What

A new \`docker builder prune -f --keep-storage 3GB\` task right after every build site:

| Location | Insertion point |
|---|---|
| \`delivery-kid/ansible/playbook.yml\` | After **Start services** |
| \`hunter/ansible/roles/build-image/tasks/main.yml\` | After **Verify image was built** |
| \`pickipedia-vps/ansible/roles/docker-wiki/tasks/main.yml\` | After **Build wiki Docker image** |
| \`pickipedia-vps/ansible/roles/docker-wiki/handlers/main.yml\` | Chained inline in **Rebuild wiki container** |

## Flag choices

- **\`-f\` (force, no \`-a\`)** — prunes dangling cache only. Active layers (i.e. cache entries reusable by the current image) stay so the next cached build is still fast.
- **\`--keep-storage 3GB\`** — hard ceiling on total cache, regardless of dangling status. Even if every entry were "active" by Docker's reckoning, this caps growth.
- **No \`when:\` gate** — runs on every deploy. When cache is already under 3GB the task is essentially a no-op.

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy delivery-kid with \`--rebuild\` — confirm task runs and \`/var/lib/docker\` doesn't grow unbounded
- [ ] Deploy hunter — confirm build cache stays bounded across rebuilds
- [ ] Re-deploy pickipedia-vps — confirm the after-build prune runs
- [ ] Verify \`docker system df\` on each host after a clean deploy: build cache should be ≤ 3GB

## Followup (out of scope here)

The dedup check in \`pickipedia_client.py\` is dead code due to \`snapshot_at\` always changing — flagged in #87 review. Worth a separate small PR.

From the log:

If the root `tsconfig.json` contains `baseUrl`, update that shared config instead so all packages behave consistently:

    "ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"

([typescriptlang.org](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/erasableSyntaxOnly.html?utm_source=openai))

body: Each connector minted its own transaction ids from a per-connector counter, so the two connectors of a multi-connector charge point (e.g. a Phoenix CHARX) produced colliding ids. StopTransaction carries only the transaction id, so a stop could be routed to the wrong connector. Share one transaction sequence per charge point and match a StopTransaction against the connector's own current transaction id.

author: alee046
body:
## Bug (reported by Liam on the preview)
Booking under staff **牧之瀬 拓海** errored:
> Could not link Supabase profile `e06dc0ea-…` to a synqed-core staff record. The profile may exist in Supabase but have no matching staff entry in synqed-core (checked user_id and email).

## Root cause
On `incremental-merge`, staff are surfaced by **Supabase profile id**, and `createAppointment` translates profile → synqed via `resolveSynqedStaffId` (synqed's `appointments.staff_id` FKs to synqed `staff.id`). **Seeded** staff are inserted straight into Supabase `profiles` and never go through `createStaff` — the only path that also creates the synqed `staff` record. So they have no synqed record, the resolver can't link them, and it threw → booking blocked. This is the staff-side of the half-finished migration (issue #2 from the original handoff).

## Fix
`resolveSynqedStaffId` now **creates the synqed staff record on demand** from the profile (`name`/`email`, linked by `user_id`) and returns its id, instead of throwing. Future lookups hit the fast `user_id` path. It only refuses when the profile itself doesn't exist.

This self-heals the gap in **every environment** (preview/prod/future seeds) without a manual data backfill — better than a one-off fix, since I couldn't reach the preview's backend data from here anyway.

## Tests
`synqed-staff-map.test.ts`: the three former "no link → throws" cases are now create-on-miss (asserting `staff.create({ name, email, user_id })`); added a "profile genuinely missing → throws" case. Full suite **464 passing**; `tsc` / `eslint` / `next build` clean.

## Note
This creates a synqed staff record implicitly during booking. That matches the contractor's stated fix for #2 ("link them / recreate so they exist in both") — flagging in case you'd prefer an explicit backfill instead.

author: kousuke-irikura
body:
## Spec

`tests/e2e/url-routing.spec.ts` covers SPA URL routing, direct-URL access, and browser history navigation backed by `react-router-dom`. No product spec change; this is a test-only stabilization of an existing L1 E2E case.

## Invariants

- The "browser back/forward" L1 case must verify that `react-router-dom` history navigation (`goBack` / `goForward`) updates the SPA route deterministically.
- Test-only change: no production source, no app behavior, no public contract is touched.
- The `/sessions` auto-redirect-to-latest behavior (`<Navigate replace />` in `SessionsPage`) is intentional and remains unchanged.

## Design Decisions

- **Root cause:** the case navigated `/agents` -> `/sessions`, but `/sessions` immediately auto-redirects to `/sessions/<latestId>` once `useIPC`'s async session load resolves. `waitForURL('**/sessions')` matched the transient pre-redirect URL, so the pending replace-redirect raced the subsequent `goBack()`, leaving the history stack non-deterministic. This flaked only under full-suite load (the session load is slow enough for the redirect to fire around `goBack`); single-spec runs passed.
- **Fix:** exercise back/forward across two URL-stable routes — `/agents` <-> `/recipes` (the rebranded "Apps" screen) — which settle synchronously with no follow-up navigation, keeping the history stack stable.
- Replaced the lifecycle-dependent `waitForURL` with web-first auto-retrying `expect(page).toHaveURL()` assertions (Playwright-recommended pattern for SPA URL transitions).

## Related Code

- `src/renderer/pages/SessionsPage.tsx` — async `<Navigate replace />` auto-redirect (the source of the race; unchanged).
- `src/renderer/App.tsx` — `/recipes` route (Apps screen), URL-stable.
- `tests/e2e/url-routing.spec.ts` — the modified test.

## Out of Scope

- Changing the `/sessions` auto-redirect behavior.
- Any production source change.
- Other url-routing cases in the same spec (unchanged).

## Verification

- Full L1 run green 2/2 (184 passed / 29 skipped / 0 failed). The test previously failed 2/2 in full-suite runs while passing in isolation.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `node tools/check-release-hygiene.mjs --strict` all pass.

author: jwiedeman
body:
## Summary

**Root cause of the four-PR false-null chain found.** The cEDH gauntlet stages decks at `<root>/batch_a/*.txt` and `<root>/batch_b/*.txt` but the Freya analysis at `<root>/freya/<deck>.strategy.json`. The pre-fix `LoadStrategyFromFreya` only checked `<deckdir>/freya/<base>.strategy.json` — i.e. `<root>/batch_a/freya/...` — which doesn't exist. It silently returned nil and the tournament logged `WARNING: deck X has no Freya analysis` for every deck. Every architectural change in PRs #793 + #826 + #848 depended on `Strategy.ComboPieces` being populated; with profile=nil, all four surfaces no-op'd. The entire investigation operated on an unwired path.

The fix is 6 lines: iterate `[dir(deckPath), dir(dir(deckPath))]` as candidate roots before falling back to nil. Deck-local strategy still wins over parent-dir when both exist (per-batch override preserved).

## Validation (400-game cEDH gauntlet, same pool/seeds as PR #784)

| Metric | PR #784 baseline (profile=nil) | **This PR (strategy loads)** | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Avg turns per game | 48.40 | **43.50** | **−4.90 (−10%)** |
| Combo (Francisco) winrate | 36.4% | 36.0% | −0.4 (flat at n=400) |
| Storm avg winrate | 5.55% | 6.50% | +0.95 |
| Stax avg winrate | 30.27% | 27.83% | **−2.43** (loses to faster combo plays) |
| Midrange avg winrate | 30.80% | 33.75% | **+2.95** (Etali MDFC combo now recognized) |
| Throughput | 74–91 g/s | 8.4 g/s | 9–11× slower (signal firing) |

**The 4.9-turn game-length compression is by far the largest empirical movement across the entire investigation chain.** Larger than any of PR #793 / #826 / #848 which all reported ±0.5-turn deltas. The single 6-line loader fix delivers a larger effect than 5 days of leaf-eval / sequencer / planstate engineering.

## Test contracts (4 new, all pre-existing pass)

| Test | Setup | Expected |
|------|-------|----------|
| `DeckLocalStillWorks` | strategy at `<deckdir>/freya/` | loads (pre-existing behavior preserved) |
| `ParentDirFallback` | strategy at `<deckdir>/../freya/` | loads (new behavior) |
| `DeckLocalPreferredOverParent` | strategy at BOTH locations, different content | deck-local wins |
| `NilWhenNothingPresent` | no strategy anywhere | returns nil (graceful-degradation) |

`go test ./internal/hat/... -count=1` clean. `go build ./...` clean.

## What this means for PRs #793, #826, #848, #863

The architectural changes in PRs #793 / #826 / #848 are *correct* and *should* land — they just couldn't measure their own impact without a populated `Strategy.ComboPieces`. With this loader fix shipped, those PRs' contributions can finally be validated.

**PR #863's "honest null" verdict at 2500 games should be re-read with this PR attached: the null was correct as data but wrong as diagnosis. The chain wasn't starved, it was unwired.** Every metric in PRs #784, #808, #826, #848, #863 measured the no-strategy fallback path.

## Two upstream bottlenecks documented but NOT fixed in this PR

The full report at `docs/hat-bottleneck-r60.md` identifies and explains:

**Bottleneck #2: MCTS budget=50 is in TierGungnir, rollouts fire at Budget≥200** (`rolloutBudgetGe` = 200 in `internal/hat/rollout.go:12`). PR #848's lift to 75/100 stayed below the rollout threshold. Even with strategy loaded, the hat does single-state evaluation, not forward sim. Recommended follow-up: `--hat-budget 200` ablation on Francisco after this PR's loader fix re-baselines the metric.

**Bottleneck #3: `rollout.go resolveStack` is a state approximation, not an effect simulator.** Spells go to graveyard/battlefield but effects don't fire — Demonic Tutor doesn't fetch, Thassa's Oracle's ETB doesn't trigger, Demonic Consultation doesn't exile library. Even at budget≥200 the simulator can't see cEDH wincon resolution. Two follow-up options documented (lightweight effect simulator vs route through engine resolve); defer until Bottleneck #1's re-measurement clarifies what TierRagnarok actually needs to do.

## Recommendation

- Land this PR.
- Re-run the cEDH 2500-game gauntlet on this branch's fix to produce the *first valid* baseline + measure each previous PR's actual contribution.
- Then run the `--hat-budget 200` ablation on Bottleneck #2.
- Defer Bottleneck #3 until #2's results clarify the rollout simulator's value-add ceiling.

## Files

- `internal/hat/strategy_loader.go` — `LoadStrategyFromFreya` parent-dir fallback (6 LoC + comment block)
- `internal/hat/strategy_loader_parent_fallback_r60_test.go` — 4 regression tests
- `docs/hat-bottleneck-r60.md` — full investigation report
- `docs/hat-bottleneck-r60-data/batch_a_200g_with_strategy.md` + `batch_b_200g_with_strategy.md` — raw 400-game validation outputs

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/hat/... -count=1 -timeout 300s` clean
- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] Batch A 200-game run with strategy loaded — see `batch_a_200g_with_strategy.md` (avg turns 43.2)
- [x] Batch B 200-game run with strategy loaded — see `batch_b_200g_with_strategy.md` (avg turns 43.8)
- [x] Confirm tournament logs `loaded Freya strategy (archetype=combo, combos=7, tutor_targets=8)` for Francisco — yes, fires for all 4 batch_a decks
- [ ] Reviewer: re-run PR #784's 2500-game gauntlet on this branch to validate full-depth effect

There is a new concept of a "placeholder" (name can change if needed) where the layout will remember the previous location of a floating pane with a stub cell. Tiled panes will also remember their floating layout cell. This allows for panes to easily swap between previous floating/tiled states. Every floating pane now has a placeholder in the root layout (see `layout_make_placeholder`). This is created when the pane is spawned.

I had to make a decision regarding how to "remember" dimensions of tiled layouts where we don't have size hints and have no guarantee that the layout will be the same when a pane is tiled again. Here is the flow for how a pane is re-tiled:
1. The "nearest" layout cell in the layout to the placeholder is found. Prefers cells earlier in the parent list. (see `layout_cell_visible_neighbour`).
2. The selected layout cell is then split 50/50 with the stub.
3. The floating cell is stored in the placeholder.

A similar flow happens when a pane is hidden or floated. The "nearest" layout cell claims the empty space.

Because of this restriction, tile, float, and hide operations are not associative. This is the most intuitive method I found. I do have intentions of adding size-hints to layouts.

### Commands

`break-pane` has inherited the ability to float a pane "out" of a layout with `-W` (there is always a placeholder). Otherwise, it behaves as before. It also now respects the floating state of the targeted pane. If `breakp` is ran sourcing a floating pane, the pane will be floating in the new window.

`join-pane` can now tile a floating pane. When called with no flags, the current pane will be tiled using its placeholder cell.

`move-pane` can now move a pane to and from the floating state, as well as moving between windows like `join-pane`. It tramples slightly on `break-pane` and `resize-pane`.

`resize-pane` can now affect floating geometries. One thing I do not know how to handle is negative numbers to shrink dimensions. It should be able to do this.

`swap-pane` has been disabled for all floating panes because I have not had the time to add the new placeholder logic to the command. I added a note describing this and plan on fixing it.

### Documentation
I will update the man page once things are finalized.

### Known bugs

1. `newp; joinp; breakp; breakp -W` sends the server spiraling out of memory.
2. `resize-pane` can't accept negative numbers.

author: ruaskar
body:
## Why

The one-line install (`install.sh`/`.ps1`) and `keymd update` resolve to `releases/latest`. Today a release only happens when someone **manually** creates and pushes a `v*` tag — so the latest binary can silently lag master. This makes releases automatic so users reliably get current, working binaries.

## What

`binary.yml` now also triggers on **push to `master`** and gates on the version:

- a cheap **`check`** job reads `keymd.__version__`; if a `v<version>` release doesn't already exist, it sets `should_release=true`
- `build` + `release` are gated on that flag, so an ordinary merge that doesn't bump the version is a **no-op** past `check` (no wasted matrix builds)
- the release step uses `softprops/action-gh-release` with `tag_name: v<version>` + `target_commitish: <master sha>`, which **creates the tag from the merge commit** — no PAT, and no "GITHUB_TOKEN-pushed tag doesn't trigger workflows" recursion gotcha
- **idempotent**: re-running on the same version sees the existing release and skips
- the manual **`v*` tag push still works** as a fallback (uses the tag's version)

New flow: **bump `keymd.__version__` → merge → auto-build + publish** (documented in `RELEASING.md`).

## Hardening

Also pins `*.yml`/`*.yaml` to `eol=lf` in `.gitattributes`, so a future Windows edit can't ship CRLF into a workflow's bash `run:` block.

## Validation

- YAML parses; jobs `check → build (gated) → release (gated)`.
- On merge of *this* PR (version still 0.1.1, already released), `check` will report `should_release=false` and skip build/release — confirming the gate. The first real auto-release will be the v0.1.2 bump.

No app-code change; no PyPI publish; Linux still built on glibc-2.35 (ubuntu-22.04).

## Summary

Bundles the OAuth proxy pattern from the user's private alpaca-mcp-server. When the relevant env vars are set, the FastMCP server gets a \`GitHubProvider\` plus a middleware that rejects tool calls from GitHub logins outside the allowlist. Without those vars, local stdio behavior is unchanged.

## Why

claude.ai's custom connector form only supports OAuth (no static bearer). To deploy this server for claude.ai use, we need an OAuth proxy in front of the tools. Putting it in the same container — rather than a separate reverse-proxy service — matches the alpaca pattern that's already in production for this user.

## Key safety property

**HTTP transport refuses to start without OAuth configured.** A trade server reachable over HTTP without auth is a serious footgun. The check (\`_enforce_http_auth_policy\`) fails closed unless either (a) OAuth + an allowlist are configured, or (b) the operator explicitly sets \`MCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=1\` for local-only dev.

## Files

- \`src/kalshi_mcp_server/oauth.py\` (new) — provider builder + middleware + Redis storage
- \`src/kalshi_mcp_server/cli.py\` — wires them onto the server; adds http-auth policy enforcement
- \`pyproject.toml\` — \`[oauth]\` optional extras (redis, py-key-value-aio)
- \`.env.example\` — documents the OAuth-only env vars
- \`DEPLOY.md\` — replaces the "OAuth is deliberately not bundled" note with the actual setup guide
- \`tests/test_oauth.py\` — covers env-driven construction, http-policy enforcement

author: sahil87
body:
## Summary

`tu update` always runs an internal `brew update --quiet` to refresh Homebrew tap metadata before checking for a newer `tu`. In automated/CI contexts — or when a caller has just run `brew update` while updating several toolkit binaries in sequence — that refresh is redundant and slow, and its network round-trip makes `tu update` fail when offline even if the desired version is already cached locally. This adds a `--skip-brew-update` flag to opt out of only that internal refresh.

## Changes

- `runUpdate()` gains a boolean parameter to gate the internal refresh
- Dispatcher detects the flag and passes it in
- Help text documents the new flag
- Test asserting the gate omits `brew update` but keeps `brew upgrade`

When `--skip-brew-update` is set, `tu update` skips **only** the internal `brew update --quiet` call. The `brew info` version check, the up-to-date short-circuit, and `brew upgrade tu` are unchanged. Default (flag absent) preserves current behavior exactly (`runUpdate(skipBrewUpdate = false)`). The flag is detected at the `update` dispatch via `process.argv.includes("--skip-brew-update")` and is intentionally **not** part of `parseGlobalFlags`/`GlobalFlags` — it is specific to the `update` command, which ignores positional arguments.

This is one of six identical implementations of a cross-toolkit contract; the flag name `--skip-brew-update` and its semantics match that contract exactly.

## Summary
Replaces the 7-question scripted vehicle finder with a streaming AI concierge that conducts natural, conversational vehicle discovery. The new system uses Groq's gpt-oss-120b for streaming replies and gpt-oss-20b for structured data extraction, with lead scoring and SMS dispatch running server-side in parallel with the stream.

## Key Changes

**Backend API**
- New `/api/concierge` endpoint that streams AI responses token-by-token while persisting conversation transcripts
- Implements non-blocking post-stream pipeline: structured data extraction → lead scoring → founder/buyer SMS notifications
- Uses `streamConcierge()` for streaming replies and `extractStructuredData()` for strict-JSON buyer profile extraction
- Lead scoring and SMS dispatch never block the buyer-visible response stream

**AI & Prompts**
- Added `CONCIERGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` with conversational guidelines, expertise scope, and data collection strategy
- Implemented `streamConcierge()` generator for token-by-token Groq streaming with proper SSE parsing
- Implemented `extractStructuredData()` for non-streamed JSON extraction that merges with existing buyer profile (never overwrites non-null values with null)
- New `BuyerProfile` and `ConciergeMessage` TypeScript interfaces for type safety

**Database**
- New `BuyerOpportunity` model to track individual buyer sessions with full conversation history, extracted profile data, and lead scoring results
- Includes fields for vehicle preferences, budget, timeline, location, trade-in details, and notification status
- Added Supabase migration with proper indexes and RLS policies

**Frontend UI**
- Refactored `VehicleFinder` component to display streaming chat instead of scripted Q&A
- Real-time token rendering with visual streaming indicator (animated cursor)
- Improved message display with proper wrapping and scroll behavior
- Maintains session ID across conversation for server-side persistence
- Completion state shows success message instead of extracted data summary

## Implementation Details

- Streaming uses ReadableStream with TextDecoder to handle chunked responses
- Post-stream operations (extraction, scoring, SMS) run via `Promise.allSettled()` to prevent one failure from blocking others
- Phone capture detection (`!opportunitySnapshot.phone && updated.phone`) triggers lead scoring and alerts only on first capture
- Buyer profile extraction preserves existing non-null values, allowing incremental refinement across turns
- All server-side operations log errors but never interrupt the buyer-visible stream
