author: shion1305
body: ## TL;DR cm4 → (wg: k8s →) s2204 k8s → s2204 (through k8s) Lets workers on the same site (same LAN) talk to each other **directly over WireGuard** instead of relaying through the control plane. Opt in by giving the nodes a shared `wireguard_direct_peer_group` in the inventory. Here, `cm4` and `s2204` (same home LAN) join group `home`. - **Effect:** cm4 ↔ s2204 traffic stays inside the house → no Oracle Cloud egress, no double home-link usage, latency ~16ms → ~0.5ms. - **Compatible:** nodes without a group keep the existing hub-and-spoke behaviour (empty default = opt-out). - **Verified:** `just test` (pytest renders the template and asserts the layout) / `just lint` (production) / `--syntax-check`. Not applied to live hosts. > Rebased onto the zone-renumbered `main` (#50): overlay IPs are now cm4 `10.130.5.65`, s2204 `10.130.5.66`, k8s-proxy `10.130.5.2`, control plane `10.130.5.1`. --- ## Background — why home↔home traffic currently goes through the control plane The WireGuard overlay (`10.130.5.0/24`) is a pure hub-and-spoke. The key is the **worker-side peer config**: > **Each worker has exactly one peer — the control plane — and that peer's `AllowedIPs` is the entire overlay, `10.130.5.0/24`.** WireGuard sends a packet to whichever peer's `AllowedIPs` matches the destination. Since a worker's only peer (the control plane) covers the whole overlay, **every overlay destination has exactly one route: the control plane.** ``` cm4 (10.130.5.65) wg0 routing decision: dst 10.130.5.66 (s2204) matches 10.130.5.0/24 └─ the only peer matching it is the control plane └─ so it is sent to the control plane (OCI Tokyo) └─ the control plane relays it down to s2204 (10.130.5.66) ``` So **even cm4 and s2204, sitting in the same house, round-trip through Tokyo:** ``` ┌──────── OCI Tokyo (control plane / hub) ────────┐ │ │ home up │ cm4 → CP home down │ CP → s2204 │ ▼ [ cm4 ] 10.130.5.65 ──────same LAN (unused)────── [ s2204 ] 10.130.5.66 ``` Two machines right next to each other can't talk directly — they go via the cloud. That is what this PR fixes. Three costs: 1. **OCI egress** — the relayed bytes count as control-plane outbound (billed beyond the 10 TB/mo free tier). 2. **Double home-link usage** — the same data consumes cm4's uplink *and* s2204's downlink. 3. **Latency** — same-LAN traffic carries a ~16ms round-trip (8ms × 2); a direct LAN path is ~0.5ms. > Note: this is purely a WireGuard-overlay-layer change. Layers above the overlay (Cilium, etc.) are out of scope here. --- ## Design — how `wireguard_direct_peer_group` works ### 1. Concept > **Nodes that share the same non-empty `wireguard_direct_peer_group` add a direct peer for each other, in addition to the hub.** This is a **partial mesh** (only the nodes that need it), not a full mesh. Grouping is expressed by a single inventory tag. Empty (the default) means hub-only. ### 2. Inventory schema ```yaml # all.vars (global defaults) wireguard_port: 51820 # group members must listen too, so make it a global default wireguard_direct_peer_group: "" # empty = hub-only (opt-out) # per host cm4: wireguard_ip: 10.130.5.65 wireguard_direct_peer_group: home # ← cm4 and s2204 share "home" wireguard_lan_endpoint: "192.168.40.34" # its address on the shared home LAN s2204: wireguard_ip: 10.130.5.66 wireguard_direct_peer_group: home wireguard_lan_endpoint: "192.168.40.32" ``` `wireguard_lan_endpoint` is optional — it defaults to the node's auto-detected `ansible_default_ipv4.address`. cm4/s2204 set it explicitly so the direct-tunnel endpoint is pinned to a known LAN IP rather than depending on fact gathering. ### 3. Template logic (`wg0.conf.j2`) In the worker branch, after the hub peer, expand "nodes in my group" as direct peers: ```jinja {% set direct_peer_hosts = groups['all'] | default([]) | map('extract', hostvars) | selectattr('wireguard_direct_peer_group', 'defined') | selectattr('wireguard_direct_peer_group', 'equalto', my_peer_group) | selectattr('wireguard_public_key', 'defined') | selectattr('wireguard_ip', 'defined') | map(attribute='inventory_hostname') | reject('equalto', inventory_hostname) | sort | list %} {% for host in direct_peer_hosts %} {% set peer_facts = hostvars[host]['ansible_default_ipv4'] | default({}) %} {% set peer_endpoint = hostvars[host]['wireguard_lan_endpoint'] | default(peer_facts['address'] | default('')) %} {% if peer_endpoint %} [Peer] # {{ host }} (direct LAN peer) PublicKey = {{ hostvars[host]['wireguard_public_key'] }} AllowedIPs = {{ hostvars[host]['wireguard_ip'] }}/32 Endpoint = {{ peer_endpoint }}:{{ hostvars[host]['wireguard_port'] | default(wireguard_port) }} PersistentKeepalive = 25 {% endif %} {% endfor %} ``` The whole direct-peer block is gated on `direct_peer_hosts | length > 0` (a lone group member renders no dead header), and the per-peer `peer_endpoint` is resolved through a guarded expression so a member with no resolvable endpoint is skipped (it stays reachable via the hub) instead of crashing the render. Group members also get a `ListenPort` on `[Interface]`. The `selectattr | map('extract', hostvars)` idiom matches the existing `merge_peer_config.yml` / `validate_peers.yml`. ### 4. The crux — why this adds a direct path without breaking existing routes (longest-prefix) WireGuard dispatches a packet to a peer by **longest-prefix match on `AllowedIPs`**. After adding the direct peer, cm4's config looks like: | Destination | Matching AllowedIPs | Chosen peer | Path | |------|----------------------|---------------|------| | `10.130.5.66` (s2204) | `/32` (more specific) | **s2204 direct** | **LAN** | | `10.130.5.1` (control plane) | `/24` | control plane | hub | | `10.130.5.2` (k8s-proxy) | `/24` | control plane | hub | | `10.130.5.97` (static peer) | `/24` | control plane | hub | Only the `/32` for s2204 wins over the `/24` and takes the direct path; everything else still goes through the hub. **Carving exactly one node out of the overlay-wide route and leaving everything else untouched** is the heart of this design. ### 5. Endpoint resolution and firewall - **Endpoint**: defaults to each node's `ansible_default_ipv4.address` (its LAN IP). Override with `wireguard_lan_endpoint` only when the default-route IP isn't the address the peer can reach (multi-homed host, VM-NAT, etc.). The override now resolves even when `ansible_default_ipv4` was never gathered; a peer with neither an override nor a gathered fact is skipped rather than aborting the render. - **UFW**: group members get a `udp/{{ wireguard_port }}` allow rule (the underlay handshake arrives on the physical NIC, not on wg0, so the existing wg0-interface rules don't cover it). WireGuard never replies to unauthenticated packets, so exposing the port is low risk — the control-plane hub already opens it the same way. --- ## Generated config (cm4, before → after) **Before (hub-only) — s2204 also matches the `/24` and goes via the hub:** ```ini [Interface] Address = 10.130.5.65/24 PrivateKey = ... [Peer] # control plane (owns the whole overlay) AllowedIPs = 10.130.5.0/24 Endpoint = root.k8s.shion1305.com:51820 PersistentKeepalive = 25 ``` **After (`wireguard_direct_peer_group: home`) — only s2204's `/32` is direct:** ```ini [Interface] Address = 10.130.5.65/24 ListenPort = 51820 # ← added (to receive the peer's handshake) PrivateKey = ... [Peer]

author: arjunkhera
body:
## Summary
Follow-up fix to PR #364, found during B3 Part B end-to-end provisioning. PR #364 created vault repos via `POST /orgs/{git_org}/repos` only (dropping the old `/user/repos` fallback to remove silent ambiguity). But GitHub's `/orgs/{org}/repos` returns **404 for a personal USER account**, and the configured owner (`Arjunkhera`) is a User (`GET /user` → `type: User`) — so provisioning failed with 404.

Fix: choose the create endpoint **deterministically** (no silent fallback):
- `GET /user` to resolve the token's own login (cached per instance).
- If the resolved owner equals the token login → `POST /user/repos`.
- Otherwise → `POST /orgs/{owner}/repos`.
- If `GET /user` fails / non-200 → default to the org endpoint; the existing clear error fires if that 404s.

Collision detection, the GitHub existence check, and `git_repo` storage are unchanged.

Related: bug `2baad981`, story `f58e6ed0`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm --filter operator-service test` — 65/65 pass (30 in infra-k8s.test.ts; new cases: owner==token-user → /user/repos incl. case-insensitive; owner==org → /orgs; GET /user non-200/throw → org fallback; identity cached once; full user-account flow)
- [x] `pnpm --filter operator-service build` — clean
- [ ] Post-deploy: re-run Part B vault_create on alpha → repo created under Arjunkhera via /user/repos; full chain + teardown.

author: orantene
body:
## What
Post-audit engine hardening — the two remaining safe code follow-ups from the email-system audit.

1. **Dispatcher throw-safety** (`dispatcher.ts`) — the per-recipient `channelsForRecipient` await was unguarded; a rejection would abort the whole dispatch. Now wrapped: a throw is logged and skips only that recipient. The engine no longer depends on every producer remembering to wrap it. (Belt-and-suspenders — the Supabase client returns `{error}` rather than rejecting today.)

2. **Platform in-app skip is now observable** (`channels/in_app.ts`) — platform-alert entries dispatch with `tenantId=null`, and the in-app channel correctly skips (`user_notifications.tenant_id` is NOT NULL, no platform bell surface yet). It did so **silently**; now it logs `notif.in_app.skip_platform`. The entry's email channel still delivers, so platform admins aren't dark. Full platform-scoped in-app delivery stays a Phase 6+ feature (nullable tenant_id + RLS + UI).

Not included: the audit's "offer countered notifies no one" — on inspection that's **by-design** (counterOffer creates a *draft*; the client is notified when it's *sent* via `offer.sent`), so no change.

## Verification
`tsc --noEmit` clean (8GB heap), `test:notifications` 81/81, `lint` clean — against `main`.

author: konard
body:
## Summary

Resolves the requests in #1: SQLite/PostgreSQL persistence, telemetry feature
parity, a ForgeFed parity matrix (per [forgefed.org/spec](https://forgefed.org/spec)),
FEP-67ff support, docs/README, and a 0BSD license — all while preserving the
toolkit's dependency-free design (no external shards).

## What changed

### 1. SQLite / PostgreSQL database support
- `src/store/sql_store.cr` — `SqlKvStore` and `SqlMessageQueue` implementing the
  existing `KvStore`/`MessageQueue` interfaces over an abstract `SqlConnection`,
  with a `SqlDialect` enum that rewrites placeholders/upserts for each engine.
  KV: `get`/`set` with TTL expiry, `delete`, prefix `list`, atomic `cas`.
  Queue: delayed/ordered `enqueue`, FIFO `process_one` with retry/backoff and a
  dead-letter table, `depth`/`get_depth`, `listen`.
- `src/store/postgres.cr` — **pure-Crystal** `PostgresConnection` speaking the v3
  wire protocol over `TCPSocket` (trust/cleartext/MD5/SCRAM-SHA-256 auth,
  extended query protocol). No `libpq` or shard; builds in the default toolkit.
- `src/store/sqlite.cr` — opt-in `SqliteConnection` FFI binding over system
  `libsqlite3` (not required by default, so the core stays dependency-free).

### 2. Telemetry for Fedify parity
- `src/telemetry.cr` — `MetricsTelemetry` aggregates counters, gauges,
  histograms, and `span` timings (thread-safe) and renders OpenMetrics /
  Prometheus text exposition (`to_openmetrics` / `to_prometheus`), the
  dependency-free analogue of Fedify's OpenTelemetry metrics.

### 3. ForgeFed parity matrix
- `docs/FEDIFY_PARITY.md` — expanded ForgeFed section into a full matrix
  (object/actor types, activity/interaction types, properties & context) mapping
  Aptork against the ForgeFed vocabulary spec, with gaps called out.

### 4. FEP-67ff (FEDERATION.md)
- `FEDERATION.md` — describes supported protocols (ActivityPub, AS2, WebFinger,
  HTTP Signatures, RFC 9421, NodeInfo), a FEP support table, and storage drivers,
  per [FEP-67ff](https://codeberg.org/fediverse/fep/src/branch/main/fep/67ff/fep-67ff.md).

### 5. Docs & README
- `README.md` — new SQL stores subsection, `MetricsTelemetry` exporter docs,
  FEDERATION.md/FEP-67ff section, and a License section; parity lists updated.
- `docs/FEDIFY_PARITY.md` — Infrastructure rows for SQL stores and telemetry
  flipped to ✅; roadmap updated.

### 6. License
- `LICENSE` — BSD Zero Clause License (0BSD); `shard.yml` `license: 0BSD`.

## Testing
- `spec/aptork_spec.cr` — 8 SQL-store tests (hermetic in-memory `FakeSqlConnection`
  dispatching on `/* aptork:<marker> */`) + 6 `MetricsTelemetry` tests.
- `spec/drivers/sqlite_driver.cr` / `spec/drivers/postgres_driver.cr` — real-DB
  integration specs (not auto-discovered; run in dedicated CI jobs).
- `.github/workflows/spec.yml` — added `sqlite` and `postgres` (postgres:16
  service) jobs alongside the dependency-free `check` job.

Local CI green: `crystal tool format --check` ok, type-check ok, `crystal spec`
**314 examples, 0 failures**. Both drivers verified end-to-end against real
SQLite (in-memory) and PostgreSQL 16 (SCRAM and MD5 auth paths).

## How to reproduce / try
```crystal
require "aptork"
conn  = Aptork::PostgresConnection.connect("postgres://user:pass@localhost/aptork")
store = Aptork::SqlKvStore.new(conn, dialect: Aptork::SqlDialect::Postgres)
queue = Aptork::SqlMessageQueue.new(conn, dialect: Aptork::SqlDialect::Postgres)

metrics = Aptork::MetricsTelemetry.new
federation = Aptork::Federation.create("https://example.com", kv: store, inbox_queue: queue, telemetry: metrics)
puts metrics.to_openmetrics
```



Fixes #1

body:
## What

Adds two recipes to the root `justfile` so local checks mirror CI exactly and are discoverable:

- **`just list`** — public default recipe; runs `just --list` (bare `just` and `just list` both show the menu). Renamed from the private `_default`.
- **`just ci`** — `ci: fmt-check clippy test`, a just dependency chain that runs the existing CI-faithful recipes in CI order, fail-fast. Mirrors [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml) verbatim:
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (check-only; never edits files)
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast`

## Why

`main` has been CI-red in the past because red commits landed via admin override with nothing forcing a green local check first. `just ci` gives a single, CI-identical local command; a green `just ci` means a green CI.

## Gate

No new git hook — the push/PR gate already exists via `scripts/gh-wrapper`, which runs the superset `pre-pr-check.sh` (the `just ci` checks **plus** verify-claims) at `gh pr create` / `gh pr ready`. Documented in `README.md` and a new "Local CI gate" section in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Acceptance

`just ci` runs green on clean `main` (verified locally, exit 0).

Part of goal bead mu-g71u; closes **mu-608b** (blockedBy mu-njmp, which is already green on current main — see MORNING_2026-05-31.md).

body:
## Summary

Refreshes the blind agent tool-usability eval end-to-end and commits a clean v0.9.0 baseline (`evals/agent_tool_usability/results/scored_results.md`). Two layers of rot were found and **both fixed here** (the scenario fix folded in rather than shipping a baseline with known-meaningless FAILs):

1. **Tool descriptions were stale → now generated.** `tool_descriptions.md` documented only ~9 of 23 tools and `server_instructions.md` referenced removed tools. Now generated from the live FastMCP server via `generate_descriptions.py` (`make eval-descriptions`), so they can't silently drift again.
2. **`scenarios.py` expected removed tool names → fixed.** 9 scenarios graded against `send_email`/`send_email_with_attachments`/`reply_to_message`/`forward_message`/`get_message`; updated to the shipped surface (`create_draft` + `send_now`/`reply_to`/`forward_of`, `get_messages`).

## Baseline (5 models, blind — descriptions only)

Score = points (PASS=2, PARTIAL=1) ÷ max, MANUAL excluded.

| Model | Score | % | PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL |
|-------|-------|---|------|---------|------|
| DeepSeek V3 0324 (5 runs) | 387/390 | 99.2% | 193 | 1 | 1 |
| Claude Sonnet 4.6 (subagent, 1 run) | 76/78 | 97.4% | 38 | 0 | 1 |
| Llama 3.3 70B (5 runs) | 371/390 | 95.1% | 179 | 13 | 3 |
| Qwen 2.5 72B (5 runs) | 367/390 | 94.1% | 177 | 13 | 5 |
| Mistral Large 2411 (5 runs) | 361/394 | 91.6% | 177 | 7 | 4 |

All models land **92–99%** — strong evidence the v0.9.0 tool descriptions are clear for blind tool selection. The one cross-model miss is #3 ("most unread": models use `search_messages` per account rather than `list_mailboxes`' `unread_count` — a defensible efficiency divergence, not a tool-selection error); sub-PASS is otherwise minor parameter-formatting PARTIALs.

## Mechanics
- Claude column via Claude Code subagent (blind: only the generated descriptions, no repo access). OpenRouter models @ `temperature=0`, 5 runs. `make eval-tools` runs them (needs the `apple-mail-mcp-evals`/`openrouter` Keychain key).
- After fixing `scenarios.py`, the saved model responses were re-scored (responses are independent of the expected-tool list — no re-run / no extra OpenRouter spend).
- Raw `raw_*.json` stay git-ignored; only `scored_results.md` is committed. Not wired into CI (costs money) — per the issue's non-goal.

Closes #219
Closes #284

author: wingedsheep
body:
## Summary

Implements **Severance Priest** ({W}{B}{G}, Creature — Djinn Cleric, 3/3, Deathtouch), the TDM Tier-3 engine gap **#13** — *"choose-and-exile from a target opponent's revealed hand"* — from `backlog/tdm-engine-gaps.md`.

The backlog flagged this as needing new functionality, but it composes entirely from existing primitives. The card is a **pure pipeline chain — no bespoke effect type or executor**.

Oracle:
> Deathtouch
> When this creature enters, target opponent reveals their hand. You may choose a nonland card from it. If you do, exile that card.
> When this creature leaves the battlefield, the exiled card's owner creates an X/X white Spirit creature token, where X is the mana value of the exiled card.

## How it composes

**ETB** (mirrors Deep-Cavern Bat's hand-disruption shape):
`RevealHandEffect` → `GatherCards` from the opponent's hand → `SelectFromCollection` (up to one nonland, `Chooser.Controller`) → `MoveCollection` to exile with `linkToSource = true` (stores the chosen card in the priest's `LinkedExileComponent`).

**LTB** (the genuinely new payoff — the card stays exiled, never returned):
`GatherCards` from linked exile → `CreateTokenEffect` where
- `count = VariableReference("…_count")` — gates on the collection size, so nothing happens if no card was exiled,
- `dynamicPower`/`dynamicToughness = StoredCardManaValue` — X = the exiled card's mana value,
- `controller = ControllerOfPipelineTarget` — resolves to the exiled card's **owner** (an exile-zone card has no `ControllerComponent`, so resolution falls back to `ownerId`).

No new SDK building blocks, so no `card-sdk-language-reference.md` change is required. Per the repo's "no single-use patterns" guidance, the chain is inlined in the card rather than extracted into an `ExilePatterns` helper.

## Tests

`SeverancePriestScenarioTest` (3 cases, all passing):
1. ETB reveals the opponent's hand and exiles a chosen nonland (linked); lands stay in hand.
2. LTB creates a **4/4** white Spirit (Hill Giant, MV 4) **owned and controlled by the opponent**, and the exiled card **stays exiled**.
3. Declining the exile creates no token on leave.

Verified canonical placement with `just check-card-printing "Severance Priest"` (canonical in TDM; promo `ptdm` printings skipped).

## Summary

- Exposes 8 Connect-app-managed field-key option endpoints on the existing `FieldsResource` class (additive, no existing signatures changed)
- Full CLI coverage: 8 new actions under `atlas jira fields field-option-*` using `--field-key` flag
- Skill reference doc updated with new section; backlog items B433–B440 retired

## Architecture decisions

**Resource placement:** All 8 methods appended to the existing `FieldsResource` class in `src/jira/resources/fields.ts`. The file now sits around 1100 LOC — noted as a future split candidate but kept additive per directive.

**Distinct request/response types:** `createFieldOption` uses `CreateIssueFieldOptionData` (spec: `IssueFieldOptionCreateBean` — no `id`, `value` required) as the request, and returns `IssueFieldOption` (spec: `IssueFieldOption` — `id` required, `value` required). `updateFieldOption` uses `IssueFieldOption` for both body and response (spec: same schema; `id` in body must match `optionId` path param).

**Reuse of existing type:** `replaceFieldOptionOnIssues` (B438) returns `TaskProgressBeanRemoveOptionFromIssuesResult` — the same type already defined for `replaceContextOptionOnIssues` (B425). No duplication.

**Pagination flavor:** `listFieldOptions`, `listFieldOptionSuggestionsEdit`, `listFieldOptionSuggestionsSearch` all use `paginateOffset` / `OffsetPaginatedResponse<IssueFieldOption>` — confirmed by spec (`PageBeanIssueFieldOption` shape with `startAt`, `maxResults`, `total`, `values`).

**B438 spec note:** The DELETE /issue endpoint returns 303 (async task) with `TaskProgressBeanRemoveOptionFromIssuesResult`. It also accepts `overrideScreenSecurity` and `overrideEditableFlag` query params (Connect/Forge admin-only). Both are wired in the CLI via existing `--override-screen-security` / `--override-editable-flag` boolean flags. `project-id` and `override-editable-flag` flags already existed in router.ts — only `field-key` and `override-screen-security` were added.

author: orangemangodimz
body:
## TL;DR

Scrape runs are now stored in MongoDB for history tracking, the Discord bot has its own CI build and deploy pipeline, and the container runtime is aligned to Python 3.12.

## Summary

- **MongoDB persistence**: scrape run history is recorded after each bot post; new MCP tools expose insert and lookup of scrape runs
- **Bot CI/CD**: bot image now builds and deploys independently via GitHub Actions
- **Python 3.12 runtime**: Playwright base image upgraded from `jammy` (Python 3.10) to `noble` (Python 3.12), fixing a startup `ImportError` on `datetime.UTC`
- **Code quality gate**: pre-commit added with ruff, mypy, and detect-secrets enforced on every commit
- **Config hygiene**: MongoDB credentials, host binding, and `.env.example` cleaned up

## Changes

| Capability | Before | After |
|------------|--------|-------|
| Scrape run history | Not stored; lost after each run | Persisted to MongoDB; queryable via MCP tools |
| Bot deployment | Manual / not in CI | Automated build + deploy job in GitHub Actions |
| Container Python version | 3.10 (jammy) — crashes on `datetime.UTC` | 3.12 (noble) — starts cleanly |
| Commit quality gate | None | ruff + mypy + detect-secrets via pre-commit |
| MongoDB access | No auth, open host binding | Credentials required, host restricted |

## Note

- Requires `MONGO_ROOT_USER`, `MONGO_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `MONGO_DB_NAME`, `MONGO_COLLECTION_NAME` secrets/vars set in GitHub Actions and on the server
- Rollback: revert the merge commit and redeploy previous image tags

author: ovasylenko
body:
## Problem

After #41 merged, **main's E2E Tests job went red**. Root cause: `tests/e2e/handlers/artifacts.test.ts` calls `startServer({ env: { ORCH8_ARTIFACT_BACKEND: "local", ORCH8_ARTIFACT_PATH } })`, but in CI's **shared-server (attach) mode** that env override is **ignored** (`harness.ts` attach path) — the runner-owned server has no artifact backend. With no backend, `response_as: artifact` steps never complete, so each test hangs to its 20s `waitForState` timeout:

```
✖ response_as=artifact captures the response body as a durable artifact (20063ms)
✖ downloads to an artifact then uploads the same bytes downstream (20035ms)
✖ tests/e2e/handlers/artifacts.test.ts (60019ms)
```

## Fix

Make the suite **self-managed** so it boots its own server in spawn mode (where the artifact env override applies):

- `run-e2e.ts`: add `artifacts.test.ts` to `SELF_MANAGED_SUITES` (excluded from the shared run).

author: bavulapati
body:
Generates a record (map) type as parallel `{ keys, values, len }` arrays — a length-prefixed list of key/value pairs reusing the array element codecs. Un-skips fixtures 23 (string -> uint) and 24 (string -> compact struct), both round-tripping byte-for-byte.

Note on ordering: the JS `record` codec iterates `Object.keys` (insertion order) and does not sort, so the C arrays preserve the wire/insertion order rather than sorting — sorting would diverge from the canonical vectors for any non-presorted producer. The fixtures' keys happen to be written alphabetically, which is why the canonical output looks sorted.

Stacked on #33. With this, every construct is covered: only fixture 42 (int56) stays skipped, pending holepunchto/compact-encoding#53.

author: pdoteter
body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
The `GitSync` structure in `src/git/sync.rs` was using `std::process::Command` to execute Git commands via synchronous processes. These blocking system calls were being made within a Tokio async runtime context.
Because they can take seconds or longer (especially for operations like `git fetch`, `git push`, or `git rebase` over the network), they would tie up Tokio executor threads, potentially causing thread pool exhaustion.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
Thread pool exhaustion in an asynchronous application can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS). When all Tokio worker threads are blocked waiting for Git subprocesses to complete, the application cannot process other tasks, handle incoming network requests (like Telegram messages), or respond to heartbeats. This can render the application unresponsive to all users.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
Replaced `std::process::Command` with `tokio::process::Command` in `src/git/sync.rs`. All functions in `GitSync` that execute Git commands were updated to be `async fn` and internally use `.await` on the asynchronous `Command::output()`. Correspondingly, in `src/git/debounce.rs`, the `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` wrappers were removed since the methods are now natively non-blocking, and they are `.await`ed directly.

author: vaaraio
body:
# v0.48.0: external time anchor + EU-wedge reframe

## What this is

The audit hash chain proves order and integrity, but not *when* it existed. Every timestamp comes from the runtime's own clock and is signed on export by the runtime's own key, so a later signing-key compromise lets an attacker forge a backdated chain that nothing internal can distinguish from the original.

This adds an external time anchor that closes that gap. `AuditTrail.anchor_head(client)` takes the current chain head (already a SHA-256 digest) and obtains an RFC 3161 trusted timestamp over it from an authority the runtime does not control. RFC 3161 is the basis for eIDAS qualified electronic timestamps, so a qualified TSA makes this regulator-grade evidence under EU AI Act Article 12.

This is the anti-backdating mechanism the server-side signed execution-record SEP relies on (draft included at `docs/sep/sep-server-execution-record.md`).

## Design

- `vaara.audit.timeanchor`: `RFC3161TimeAnchorClient` (build request, parse response, verify token), `TimeAnchor`, and offline verifiers `verify_anchor` / `verify_anchor_over_records`.
- The verifier checks the token is CMS SignedData over a TSTInfo, the message imprint equals the expected digest, the signed message-digest matches the eContent, and the TSA signature verifies under the embedded certificate. Negative tests cover a wrong-digest token, a tampered token, and a refused request.
- `verify_anchor_over_records` binds an anchor to a specific record in a trail, so a rewritten chain or a token over a different value is rejected.
- HTTP uses the standard library. Only the ASN.1 and signature checks need the new optional `timeanchor` extra (`asn1crypto` + `cryptography`); core install stays dependency-free.

## Public framing

Leads back to EU AI Act runtime evidence and data sovereignty (runs in your own environment, no SaaS, no telemetry) across the README, package descriptions, MCP manifests, and vaara.io. The tamper-evident receipt stays the mechanism, not the headline.

## Also

Lands the three CodeQL "use a `with` statement" advisories from the v0.47 audit tests (the fix never reached the remote before #179 squash-merged).

## Verification

1096 passed / 12 skipped, ruff clean, mypy clean on the new module. New `tests/test_timeanchor.py` stands up a self-contained in-process TSA, so the full request / response / verify path runs with no network.

## Summary

Phase 4 MCP — wraps the two prompt-context endpoints that landed in #78 + #80 but weren't yet exposed via MCP. `tools/list` now returns **14**.

| MCP tool | Endpoint | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `cn_prompt_context_clusters` | `GET /prompt-context/clusters` | Cross-session trajectory clusters with promotion signal |
| `cn_prompt_context_capsule` | `GET /prompt-context/capsule` | Paste-ready Markdown digest of clusters |

MCP-speaking agents can now ask the substrate to compile prompt-context Markdown directly with one tool call — drop the body into the next agent's prompt without a `curl` shim.

## Markdown passthrough — the load-bearing fallback

`/prompt-context/capsule` returns `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`. The shared `get` helper in `src/mcp/tools.rs` already does `serde_json::from_str(text)` and falls back to the raw `text` on parse failure. That fallback IS the Markdown passthrough — the choice in #80 to render Markdown directly (instead of JSON-wrapping) and the choice here to reuse `get` compose into a verbatim Markdown delivery with zero new code.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --lib mcp` — 26/26 (24 prior + 2 new)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --lib --no-deps` — zero hits in `src/mcp/`
- [x] **Runtime via MCP stdio JSON-RPC against fresh substrate** (throwaway HOME with WAL copy; live `:28080` untouched):
  - `tools/list` → 14 tools
  - `cn_prompt_context_clusters` with `kind=decision_made, min_count=2, limit=2` → real JSON cluster data (619 atoms scanned, two real decision_made clusters)
  - `cn_prompt_context_capsule` with `min_count=2, max_per_kind=2` → live Markdown body starting `# Prompt Context\n\n_Window: last 30d ... ## Risks\n\n- _admin...` delivered verbatim through the MCP content channel
- [ ] CI green

## Risks

- **Additive.** Two new dispatch arms, two new tool defs. No change to existing tool behaviour. Both protocol-level and module-level tool-count assertions updated to 14.

## Follow-ups

- This closes the obvious MCP debt: every shipped prompt-context HTTP endpoint now has a tool wrapper.
- The next deterministic gain would be the embedder-based semantic dedup of clusters (paraphrase merging) — that's the "earn the LLM call" step for the v0.4 roadmap.

author: akindu-k
body:
## Problem

`_put_node_atomic` updates a `NodeAnchor` using an **aggregation-pipeline** `$set` (`find_one_and_update(..., [{'$set': set_doc}], ...)` — note the `[ ... ]` list, required for the atomic `$setUnion`/`$setDifference` edge-merge expression).

A pipeline `$set` **evaluates every field value as an aggregation expression**. That has two failure modes for serialized archetype data:

1. **Empty embedded documents.** On **MongoDB older than 6.1.0**, a bare `{}` is rejected with error **40180** (`Location40180`, "an empty object is not a valid value"). The restriction was lifted in **6.1.0** by [`SERVER-54046`](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-54046), with no 6.0.x backport. This matters because jac-scale provisions **`mongo:6.0`** on Kubernetes (`providers/database/kubernetes_mongo.jac`).
2. **`$`-prefixed keys.** A dict whose keys start with `$` is misread as an operator — e.g. the `{'$ref': ..., '$type': ...}` the `Serializer` emits for a repeated anchor reference.

`set_doc` is assembled from two sources:

| Source | Target path | Handled before #6076? |
|--------|-------------|--------------------------|
| `non_arch_top` | `data.<k>` (e.g. `access.roots.anchors`) | ✅ yes — stripped in #6076 |
| `partial_data` | `data.archetype.<k>` (dirty archetype fields) | ❌ no |

#6076 handled only the `non_arch_top` half. The `partial_data` half went into the `$set` raw, so any archetype field that serialized to an empty dict:

```jac
node MyNode { has settings: dict = {}; }
```

reached the pipeline `$set` as `data.archetype.settings = {}` and raised 40180. `_put_node_atomic` swallows the exception in its `try/except`, so **every such partial save was silently lost** on mongo < 6.1.0 — the node stopped persisting updates after its first full write.

## Why stripping is the wrong fix

The obvious fix is to strip the empty dict out before writing. That avoids 40180 but loses information: a deliberate "clear this field back to `{}`" becomes a no-op, leaving the previously stored value in place. A version-gated strip (strip only below 6.1.0) has the same flaw on exactly the version we ship.

So stripping trades a silent write loss for a silent clear loss. We want the empty dict to actually persist. Stripping also does nothing for the `$`-prefixed-key failure mode.

## Fix

Adopt **one uniform rule** for the pipeline `$set`: `data.edges` is the only expression; every serialized data value is wrapped in `{'$literal': v}` and stored verbatim.

```jac
# Build a flat $set document. This is an aggregation-pipeline $set, so
# every value is evaluated as an expression — which rejects bare empty
# dicts (error 40180) and misreads `$`-prefixed keys (e.g. a Serializer
# `$ref`/`$type`). One rule keeps it safe: `data.edges` is the only
# expression; every serialized data value is wrapped in `$literal` and
# stored verbatim. (`type`/`updated_at` are hardcoded literals.)
for (k, v) in non_arch_top.items() {
    set_doc[f"data.{k}"] = {'$literal': v};
}
for (k, v) in partial_data.items() {
    set_doc[f"data.archetype.{k}"] = {'$literal': v};
}
set_doc['data.edges'] = {'$setUnion': [...]};   // the only expression
```

`$literal` is a standard aggregation operator (since MongoDB 2.6) that returns its argument verbatim without evaluating it. Wrapping the **whole value** of both source groups — archetype fields *and* non-archetype top-level fields (`access`) — neutralizes **both** failure modes at once (empty dicts *and* `$`-prefixed keys) with a single mental model. It is safe because every wrapped value comes from serialization and is pure data that must never be evaluated, and each field is assigned as a whole value (no dot-path sub-updates within a field). `type`/`updated_at` are hardcoded literal scalars and need no wrap.

This replaces the earlier split (wrap archetype, strip non-archetype) and lets the `_strip_empty_dicts` helper be **deleted** — one fewer concept, less code, and the `access` field is now also robust against `$`-keys. Two incidental cleanups in the same function: the now-unread `arch` local (dead since the collect-pass refactor) is removed, and the stale `data.archetype.<field> — only dirty scalar fields` comment is corrected (dict fields are written there too).

**Trade-off:** stripping omitted default empty-dict leaves (e.g. `access.roots.anchors = {}`) and the loader rebuilt them; `$literal` stores them. That is a few bytes per document with **no runtime/deserialization difference** (`_deserialize_permission` rebuilds defaults regardless). One pre-existing #6076 test asserted on this stored shape and was updated to assert the real invariant ("the write succeeds and access is persisted") instead of "no empty dicts stored."

Result: an empty, cleared-to-`{}`, or `$`-keyed dict field — archetype or access — now persists identically on all MongoDB versions, with no server-version detection and no data migration.

## What is deliberately left unchanged

**`put_partial`** uses a **classic operator** `$set` (`update_one(..., {'$set': update})`, a plain dict, not a pipeline), which accepts empty embedded documents on every MongoDB version. The 40180 restriction does not apply there, so it stores `{}` as-is and must not be touched. A comment documents this.

**`data.edges`** stays an aggregation expression (`$setUnion`/`$setDifference`) — it is the whole reason the update is a pipeline, and it must be evaluated, not stored literally.

## Note on the merge with `main`

`main` refactored dirty detection into `jaclang.runtimelib.changeset` and made the runtime's **collect pass the single owner of dirty detection**, passing the dirty `fields` set into `_put_node_atomic`. This branch adopts that architecture — the backend trusts `fields` rather than re-deriving dirtiness — and narrows its own contribution to the empty-dict/`$`-key *encoding* fix. The atomic-path tests were updated to call `_put_node_atomic` with the new `fields` argument.

## Tests

Two regression tests in `test_mongo_layer123.jac`, one per failure mode. Each is included only because it **fails without the fix**:

- **Clear-to-`{}` on `mongo:6.0` via `$literal` (the #6167 regression):** seed `settings={"keep": 1}`, clear to `{}`, run the atomic path on the version that raises 40180. A non-`None` document proves the pipeline `$set` did not raise, and `settings == {}` proves the clear persisted.
- **`$`-prefixed keys round-trip on the atomic path:** stores `settings = {"$ref": ..., "$type": "node"}` (the shape the `Serializer` emits for a repeated anchor reference) and asserts it round-trips verbatim — pinning the second failure mode the whole-value wrap covers. Runs on `mongo:latest` since `$ref` is misread as an operator on every version.

A dedicated `mongo:6.0` container is required for the first test because the shared `mongo:latest` helper accepts bare `{}` and cannot reproduce 40180. A `mongo:latest` clear-to-`{}` test was deliberately omitted (6.1+ accepts bare `{}`, so it would pass with or without the fix), as was a `put_partial` test (that path uses a classic `$set` this PR does not change).

The pre-existing **#6076 test** was updated: it asserted the stored document contained *no* empty dicts (a proxy for the old strip approach). Since the uniform `$literal` rule now legitimately stores `access.roots.anchors = {}`, that assertion was flipped to the real invariant — the atomic write succeeds and `access` is persisted despite the default empty dict.

## Reproduction matrix

| Image | Server | Pipeline `$set` with bare empty dict | Behavior with fix |
|-------|--------|-------------------------------|----------|
| `mongo:6.0` | 6.0.x | ❌ raises 40180 | `$literal` wrap stores `{}` |
| `mongo:7.0` | 7.0.x | ✅ OK | `$literal` wrap stores `{}` |
| `mongo:latest` | 8.x | ✅ OK | `$literal` wrap stores `{}` |

Closes #6167.

body:
## Summary

Two critical security fixes:

**1. `.env` committed to git** — The `.env` file (containing Supabase anon key and URL) was tracked in git history. This PR removes it from tracking, adds `.env` / `.env.*` to `.gitignore`, and adds a `.env.example` with placeholder values.

**2. XSS via unsanitized HTML rendering** — The `explanation` field is stored as HTML (from a `contentEditable` rich text editor) and rendered via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in `bank.$id.tsx` and `exam.tsx`, plus direct `innerHTML` assignment in `question-editor.tsx`. All paths now sanitize through `DOMPurify` via a new `sanitizeHtml()` utility (`src/lib/sanitize.ts`):
- `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: sanitizeHtml(q.explanation) }}` in both render sites
- `explanationRef.current.innerHTML = sanitizeHtml(html)` when loading for edit
- `sanitizeHtml(explanationHtml)` before persisting to Supabase
- URL/path values in `insertHTML` escaped to prevent attribute breakout

The allowlist is scoped to formatting tags (`b`, `i`, `em`, `strong`, `img`, `a`, `mark`, `ul/ol/li`, etc.) and safe attributes (`src`, `alt`, `href`, `style`, `class`, `data-path`).

> **Note:** The Supabase anon key that was in `.env` is a *publishable* key (not the service role key), but committing `.env` files is still bad practice since future additions could leak real secrets. Consider rotating the key if the repo was ever public.

P545's Phase 3 (T562 / #657) was billed as the testable end-to-end "zakalwe runs a chore" milestone and merged as `done`. author: dichovsky
body:
## Summary

- Adds `FieldConfigurationSchemeResource` exposing the 4 CRUD endpoints on `/rest/api/3/fieldconfigurationscheme` (B914–B917)
- Wires the resource into `JiraClient` as `fieldConfigurationSchemes` and exports all public types from `src/jira/index.ts`
- Adds `fieldconfigurationscheme` CLI dispatch (`atlas jira fieldconfigurationscheme <action> [id] [--flags]`) with full help text and examples

## Architecture decisions

**New resource, not an extension of `fieldconfiguration`.** `FieldConfigurationSchemeResource` (`/rest/api/3/fieldconfigurationscheme`) is a separate concept from the existing `FieldConfigurationResource` (`/rest/api/3/fieldconfiguration`). They share no path segments and have distinct schemas.

**Pagination flavor: `OffsetPaginatedResponse` + `paginateOffset`.** GET list (B914) is offset-paginated (startAt, maxResults, id[]) per spec, same pattern as `fieldconfiguration`. `listAll()` async generator included.

**Distinct create vs list response types (spec-verified).** POST (B915) returns `FieldConfigurationScheme` (id is a `string`, not a number). GET list returns `PageBeanFieldConfigurationScheme` (values: `FieldConfigurationScheme[]`). This distinction was confirmed by resolving both `$ref`s in the spec — the item type is the same but the top-level shape differs.

**DELETE and PUT return void (204).** Spec confirms 204 No Content for both B916 and B917.

**No new router options needed.** All CLI flags used (`--ids`, `--name`, `--description`, `--start-at`, `--max-results`) are already registered in `src/cli/router.ts` as shared global options.

## Endpoints implemented

| B | Verb | Path | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| B914 | GET | `/rest/api/3/fieldconfigurationscheme` | `PageBeanFieldConfigurationScheme` (offset-paginated) |
| B915 | POST | `/rest/api/3/fieldconfigurationscheme` | `FieldConfigurationScheme` (201) |
| B916 | DELETE | `/rest/api/3/fieldconfigurationscheme/{id}` | void (204) |
| B917 | PUT | `/rest/api/3/fieldconfigurationscheme/{id}` | void (204) |

## Spec surprises

All 4 endpoints are marked `deprecated: true` in the OpenAPI spec (Atlassian points to "Field schemes" as the successor, which is already covered by `ConfigResource`). The spec is unambiguous that they remain available on Jira Cloud — implemented as-is per brief.

The `id` field in `FieldConfigurationScheme` (list item / create response) is typed as `string` in the spec schema, while the path parameter `{id}` for DELETE/PUT is `int64`. Both are honored correctly.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx vitest run test/jira/fieldconfigurationscheme.test.ts` — 20 unit tests: list (params, id filter, pagination, validation), listAll (generator, filter forwarding), create (with/without description, distinct response shape), delete (path encoding), update (with/without description)
- [ ] `npx vitest run test/cli/commands.test.ts` — 11 new CLI dispatch tests covering all 4 actions plus error paths (missing id, missing --name, unknown action)
- [ ] `npx vitest run test/cli/skill-content.test.ts` — resource documented in `skill/reference/jira.md`
- [ ] `npm run validate` — typecheck + lint + format + build + 6329 tests (135 files) + export validation + codemap all pass

## Problem

The build fails at the BUILD_IMAGE stage when Mise attempts to install Python 3.11.9. Mise 2026.5.16 enforces GitHub artifact attestation verification, but the Python 3.11.9 binary distribution lacks valid attestations, producing: "No GitHub artifact attestations found for python@3.11.9".

Created railway.toml at the repo root with MISE_PYTHON_GITHUB_ATTESTATIONS=false, which disables attestation verification during the Python installation step. The binary is still fetched from the official Python Standalone Builds repository — only the attestation check is skipped.

author: peteryuill-blip
body:
⚡ Bolt Optimization:
Found a performance bottleneck where an array was being spread into React state (`[...currentOutputs]`) during *every iteration* of a long-running batch process. As the array grows, each spread operation takes longer, resulting in an O(N^2) complexity that freezes the UI during heavy processing loads.

Fix:
Throttled the `outputs` array spread to update state every 10 items (or on the last item). `stats` updates continue on every iteration, maintaining responsive progress indicators without the massive array allocation overhead.

Includes an entry in Bolt's Journal documenting this anti-pattern.

author: fatelessdev
body:
💡 **What:** Extracted static configuration objects (`THEMES` and `CONTROLS`) out of the `Markdown` component into module scope and wrapped the component in `React.memo()`. Created `.jules/bolt.md` to document the learning.

🎯 **Why:** Passing inline objects (`controls={{...}}`) and arrays (`shikiTheme={["github-light", "github-dark"]}`) directly into the JSX props creates new object references on every render cycle of the parent. Because the `Markdown` component wraps `Streamdown` (which dynamically imports and coordinates heavy libraries like Shiki, KaTeX, and Mermaid), this referential inequality was causing severe, computationally expensive re-renders.

📊 **Impact:** Significantly reduces the React render cycle cost for expensive markdown rendering operations. The `Markdown` component will now only re-render if `children` or `isStreaming` props genuinely change, saving CPU cycles during chat updates and streaming operations.

🔬 **Measurement:** Verified that the frontend application still type-checks and builds correctly using `vite build`. The extraction prevents the object reference from changing, enabling React's shallow comparison memoization to bail out of the render phase early.

author: pannpers
body:
## Summary

Aligns backend with the rename merged in [specification#552](https://github.com/liverty-music/specification/pull/552). The underlying transport is still the W3C Push API (\`push_subscription_repo\`, \`PushNotificationUseCase\`, \`webpush\` sender — all unchanged), but the analytics surface and the NATS aggregate root are now scoped under the **notification** domain to match the user-facing concept.

## What changes

| Surface | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NATS stream | \`PUSH\` (\`PUSH.*\`) | \`NOTIFICATION\` (\`NOTIFICATION.*\`) |
| NATS subject | \`PUSH.subscription_completed\` | \`NOTIFICATION.subscribed\` |
| Payload struct | \`entity.PushSubscriptionCompletedData\` | \`entity.NotificationSubscribedData\` |
| Subject const | \`entity.SubjectPushSubscriptionCompleted\` | \`entity.SubjectNotificationSubscribed\` |
| Catalogue event | \`push.subscription.completed\` | \`notification.subscribed\` |
| Catalogue event | \`push.notification.delivered\` | \`notification.delivered\` |
| Event const | \`usecase.EventPushSubscriptionCompleted\` | \`usecase.EventNotificationSubscribed\` |
| Event const | \`usecase.EventPushNotificationDelivered\` | \`usecase.EventNotificationDelivered\` |
| Handler | \`HandlePushSubscriptionCompleted\` | \`HandleNotificationSubscribed\` |
| watermill router name | \`forward-push-subscription-completed-to-analytics\` | \`forward-notification-subscribed-to-analytics\` |

## What does NOT change

The transport-layer Web Push surface stays as is — those names refer to the actual W3C Push API, not the analytics domain:

- \`PushNotificationUseCase\`, \`PushSubscriptionRepository\`
- \`push_subscription.go\`, \`push_subscription_repo.go\`, \`push_notification_uc.go\`
- \`infrastructure/webpush/\` (sender, key management)
- \`adapter/rpc/push_notification_handler.go\`

## Production-state notes

- The analytics catalogue event \`push.subscription.completed\` shipped in backend v1.3.0 (PR #319) but **has never fired in prod** — KEDA gap on PUSH consumer + zero Web Push opt-ins since launch. The NATS/catalogue rename is purely forward-looking; no message replay needed.
- The orphaned \`PUSH\` JetStream in prod holds 0 messages — manually removed in a follow-up runbook step (\`nats stream rm PUSH\`). Stream provisioning is idempotent and additive: the new \`NOTIFICATION\` stream is created on next startup; the old \`PUSH\` stream is harmless to leave behind until cleanup.
- \`EventNotificationDelivered\` has no publisher yet (task 5.7); the const rename is a pure source-of-truth update.

## Verification

- \`make check\` (lint + lint-schema + modernize + test) passes locally.
- Unit tests updated for the renamed handler, payload struct, and event const expectations.

## Downstream

- **Frontend rename PR** (separate) — \`Events.PushSubscriptionRequested\` → \`Events.NotificationRequested\` with value \`notification.requested\`.
- **cloud-provisioning** — KEDA \`ScaledObject\` needs the new consumer name \`NOTIFICATION_subscribed\` (separate follow-up).

Refs: liverty-music/specification#532

🔧 **Fix**: Enforced `os.path.commonpath` checks for requested base routes. `request.root` variables that allow `None` now default safely during expansion to avoid `TypeError`. Handled exception stack traces gracefully with `exc_info=True` in logging and returned standard generic server errors.
✅ **Verification**: Tests all passed successfully via `pytest tests/`.

body:
## Summary

Mirrors AdventureItemNames's `release.yml` for PlayerMob:

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — dispatch-only workflow (`workflow_dispatch` with `tag` + optional `notify_discord` inputs). This becomes the **sole** creator of release tags on `bh679/playermob-mc`.
- **`scripts/notify-discord.sh`** — Discord embed announcer with `DRY_RUN=1` escape hatch; gracefully marks ✅ / ⚠️ per platform (Modrinth, CurseForge, GitHub).
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — fills in `Releasing (post-Gate 3)` + `Tag discipline` sections that were stubbed with "below when set up".

### What it does on dispatch

1. Checkout `main`, set up Java 21 + Gradle
2. Verify input tag (e.g. `v0.3.0`) matches `mod_version` on main; fail fast if not
3. Check tag does not already exist on remote (orphan-tag guard)
4. Compute release type: `MAJOR=0` ⇒ `beta` + `prerelease=true`; `MAJOR>0` ⇒ stable. Detect `X.0.0` MAJOR bumps for Discord gating.
5. `./gradlew build --no-daemon` → 3 loader jars
6. Stage jars into `release-artifacts/` (sanity-checks exactly 3 production jars)
7. Create GitHub Release with auto-generated notes + attached jars
8. Publish per-loader versions to Modrinth + CurseForge via `Kir-Antipov/mc-publish@v3.3` (`+fabric`, `+forge`, `+neoforge` SemVer build-metadata suffixes)
9. Notify Discord on MAJOR bumps or when `notify_discord=true`

### Intentional v1 simplifications

- **No wiki publishing** — PlayerMob has no wiki yet. Easy to add `publish-wiki.sh` later.
- **Project IDs as repo `vars`, not `gradle.properties`** — matches AIN; keeps build inputs separate from environment metadata.

### Mod-impact

**None.** No Gradle, Java, dependency, Mixin, entity, packet, or save-format changes. Pure CI/tooling + a 50-line CLAUDE.md doc append. The mod jars produced by `./gradlew build` are bit-identical to those on `main`.

## Test plan

- [x] `actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml` — only 4 `info`-level shellcheck messages, identical to AIN reference (verified by running actionlint against AIN's release.yml). No structural / YAML / interpolation errors.
- [x] `shellcheck scripts/notify-discord.sh` — exit 0, clean.
- [x] `diff` vs AIN's `release.yml` — only the documented substitutions (`adventureitemnames-*` → `playermob-*`, release titles) plus the wiki-step omission.
- [x] `DRY_RUN=1 bash scripts/notify-discord.sh` (all-loaders-success case) — payload assembles, URLs correct (`modrinth.com/mod/playermob/versions`, `curseforge.com/.../playermob/files`), `jq .` parses.
- [x] `DRY_RUN=1 bash scripts/notify-discord.sh` (partial-failure case) — ⚠️ marks render correctly for missing platforms, ✅ for GitHub.
- [ ] **First real dispatch (post-merge, separate user-initiated action):** `gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=v0.3.0`.

## Post-merge — required GitHub configuration

The workflow silently skips publish steps when these are missing (warnings only, won't fail the run). Add in `bh679/playermob-mc` settings → **Secrets and variables → Actions**:

**Secrets** (Secrets tab):
- `MODRINTH_TOKEN` — https://modrinth.com/settings/pats, scope `Create versions`
- `CURSEFORGE_TOKEN` — https://legacy.curseforge.com/account/api-tokens
- `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` — optional, only if Discord pings wanted

**Variables** (Variables tab):
- `MODRINTH_PROJECT_ID` — fillable once Modrinth approves the manual 0.2.0 upload
- `CURSEFORGE_PROJECT_ID` — fillable once a CurseForge project is created

After secrets/vars are in place, first release dispatch:
```bash
gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=v0.3.0
```

(assumes `mod_version` is bumped to `0.3.0` as part of Gate 3 cleanup — see CLAUDE.md versioning rule)

author: quirrel-zh
body:
## Summary

fixes #36 

Fixes a regression where the **physical controller's brake gets interrupted** in `gamepad` output mode: braking + consecutive downshifts makes the brake light flicker.

**Root cause:** the virtual XInput device (`vgamepad`) sends a *full device-state packet* on every `update()`, and its left trigger (LT = brake) defaulted to `0`. Each shift's `press→update→release→update` therefore emits two LT=0 packets that override the physical controller's live brake input for those frames.

**Fix (mirror physical brake onto virtual LT during shifts):**
- New no-op `OutputInterface.set_brake(brake)` hook — keyboard / vjoy are unaffected (they don't share an XInput state packet with the physical controller).
- `GamepadOutput` caches the per-frame brake (thread-safe) and sets `LT = int(brake*255)` *before both* the press and release `update()` calls.
- `TCULogic.process()` calls `self._kb.set_brake(td.brake)` each frame.
- Gated by new config `gamepad_preserve_brake` (default `True`). When not braking, LT stays `0` → no phantom braking on upshifts.

Also updates the optimization plan to record the **P3 (Race high-rpm no-upshift) investigation**: decoding `logs/没有触发升档.gz` + cross-gear power analysis disproved the original premise (holding the lower gear near the limiter is actually faster by 16–35 kW, and the existing code already upshifts near the limiter), so P3 is **withdrawn**, not implemented.

## Test plan

- [x] Python compiles; `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean (pre-commit hook).
- [x] Mock-`vgamepad` unit check: brake held → every shift packet carries LT=brake; `preserve_brake=False` → LT stays 0; brake=0 → LT stays 0 (no phantom braking).
- [x] **Windows + real controller:** hold brake, fire consecutive downshifts → brake light stays solid (no flicker); upshift with no brake → no phantom braking.

body: ## Bug and impact Render blueprint/all-in-one deployments serve the SPA and API from the same `*.onrender.com` host, but the recent Socket.IO routing change sent production browser sockets to the baked fallback backend (`locationsbaelish.onrender.com`). Deployments whose Render service URL differs from that fallback could create rooms via same-origin REST while viewers/sharers connected to a different Socket.IO server, leaving live location sharing broken. ## Root cause `socketServerOrigin()` treated every production browser build as a Vercel-style split deployment and returned `VITE_DEFAULT_RENDER_BACKEND` unless running on localhost/LAN. ## Fix Use direct Render Socket.IO only when the client was built on Vercel (`VITE_BUILT_ON_VERCEL === "1"`). author: antonbabenko
body:
## What

Remove the layering inversion where `core/` reached up into the `server/` transport bridges, so `core` is a self-contained, honestly publishable engine. Injection-only (the light option) - no transport relocation, no plugin/mcp.json changes.

Before: `core/providers/{antigravity,grok,openai-compatible}.js` fell back to `|| require("../../server/<bridge>/index.js")` when no bridge was injected - the only thing pulling `server/` into `core/`.

After:
- The three adapters require `opts.bridge` and throw a clear error if it is missing.
- `server/mcp/index.js` (the composition root) injects the bridges explicitly: `{ bridge: require("../gemini/index.js") }`, etc. Codex needs none (spawns the `codex` CLI).
- Dependency now runs one way: `server -> core`.

## Why

`core` is meant to be host-neutral and eventually publishable as `@antonbabenko/deliberation-core`. A "host-neutral" engine importing its own transport shims was an inversion. This removes it with a ~4-file change and no behavior change. (npm publish of core is deferred - no consumer yet.)

## Verification

- `grep -rn 'require("../../server' core/` -> zero results
- `npm run check` -> typecheck clean, 210/210 tests pass (tests already inject bridges)
- Bundled mcp server: 0 escaping requires in `dist/index.js`; clean-room install boots and `tools/list` returns 13 tools, no `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, no `requires opts.bridge`

body:
## Bug and impact - Right-clicking the map opened a context menu above track management windows, then left-clicking a track left that menu open because the track click handler stops document-level pointer propagation. - For tracks initiated from the context menu, the focus path used `track-${trackId}` even though the existing window ID is a UUID, so the window could fail to move to the top of the track-window stack. ## Root cause - `handleOpenTrackManagementWindow` opened/focused the track window without closing the active context menu. - It assumed all track management window IDs are derived from `track-${trackId}`, which is not true for initiated tracks. ## Fix - Close the context menu whenever a track management window is opened from a track click. - If a management window already exists for the track, bring that actual window ID to the front; otherwise fall back to the deterministic `track-${trackId}` ID used for newly opened windows. ## Validation - `npm run build`

author: rwlove
body:
## Summary

Closes the last open queue-substrate roadmap item — the **router scorer** (HOMELAB-SPEC Layer 6). A pure, deterministic function at the single `llm()` routing chokepoint makes the local-vs-Claude decision per call, **enforce-now and conservative**.

Until now the fleet routed 100% local as *dead code*: every agent maps to a local group in `AGENT_GROUP`, and the three Claude entry points in `llm()` have no live caller. This makes that an explicit, observable, scored decision.

## The one v1 trigger

Escalates on exactly one capability-driven condition: **estimated assembled-prompt tokens exceed a configured local-context ceiling** (`router_escalate_token_threshold`, default 24000). That's Layer 6's first scoring input ("context length needed") and Layer 5's failure-mode ("route to a stronger model" when local can't fit the task) — the only case where local genuinely *cannot* do the work. Everything else stays local.

`ChatOllama` sets no `num_ctx`, so the real local ceiling is Ollama's runtime default; the threshold is a conservative configurable bound set high so only a genuine overflow (e.g. a pasted multi-thousand-line log) trips it. Lower it once the decision metric shows real overflow rates.

Deferred (with reasons in code/commit): `cascade_count` (counts re-routes, not failures — wrong signal), `destructive` (broad/costly on day one), `priority`/"looks hard" (non-deterministic guesswork the design ruled out).

## Guards (conservative by construction)

- **Restricted-tier never escalates** — scorer refuses, and `_build_claude`'s `assert_emission_allowed` is the hard backstop regardless.
- **health-tracker stays pinned local** — enforced upstream of the scorer; it can only ever flip local→Claude.
- **Cost caps remain the floor** — `_build_claude` raises `CostCapHit` before constructing Claude, unchanged.
- **Graceful degrade** — a decided escalation with no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` falls through to the local group exactly as today; no new failure path.
- **Kill switch** — `router_scorer_enabled` (default on per enforce-now); set False to pin 100% local.

## Observability

New `langgraph_router_decision_total{agent,decision,reason}` — emitted on every `llm()` call. Per-completion provenance persisted to Postgres (which would let `hai cost`'s group breakdown report real `escalated` counts, closing #108's caveat) is **deliberately deferred** as the shared follow-up — no DB migration here.

## Changes

- `src/agents/router.py` (new) — pure `score_route` + `estimate_input_tokens`
- `src/agents/llm.py` — call scorer after group resolution, emit metric, set `escalate`
- `src/agents/observability.py` — one Counter
- `src/agents/settings.py` — `router_scorer_enabled` + `router_escalate_token_threshold`
- `src/agents/api/inbox.py`, `src/agents/queue/worker.py` — bind `est_input_tokens` contextvar at the two ingress sites
- `tests/test_router.py` (new) — pure-function matrix + `llm()` integration

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean
- [x] `mypy src/` clean (65 files)
- [x] `pytest tests/test_router.py tests/test_llm_factory.py` — 27 pass (new matrix + existing routing tests, no regression)
- [x] Full `pytest` — 373 pass / 2 postgres-skip (362 baseline + 11 new)
- [ ] No cluster change; merge/deploy is Rob's call

body:
Three new namespaces covering widely-used tools that are missing from the site.

## pnpm (11 codes)

The third major Node.js package manager alongside npm and yarn, with its own `ERR_PNPM_*` error code scheme:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION` | No version satisfies the requested range |
| `ERR_PNPM_PEER_DEP_ISSUES` | Unresolved or conflicting peer dependencies |
| `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_NETWORK_ERROR` | Network error reaching the registry |
| `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_BREAKING_CHANGE` | Lockfile written by a newer pnpm version |
| `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_LOCKFILE` | `--frozen-lockfile` with no lockfile present |
| `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` | Lockfile out of sync with package.json |
| `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` | Downloaded tarball checksum mismatch |
| `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE` | Node/pnpm version fails `engines` constraint |
| `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_401` | Registry requires authentication |
| `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_403` | Registry access forbidden |
| `ERR_PNPM_WORKSPACE_PKG_NOT_FOUND` | `workspace:` reference targets unknown package |

## pytest (exit codes 0–5)

Canonical exit codes for the dominant Python testing framework. Python is already on the site; pytest fills the testing gap.

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | OK | All tests passed |
| 1 | Tests Failed | One or more tests failed |
| 2 | Interrupted | Ctrl+C / `pytest.exit()` |
| 3 | Internal Error | Bug inside pytest itself |
| 4 | Usage Error | Bad CLI args or config |
| 5 | No Tests Collected | No matching tests found |

## Maven (exit codes 0–1)

Apache Maven exit codes, completing the Java build tool pair alongside the existing Gradle namespace.

| Code | Name |
|---|---|
| 0 | BUILD SUCCESS |
| 1 | BUILD FAILURE |

## Notes

- No code changes required — new directories are picked up automatically at build time.
- Numeric fields are included on pytest and Maven exit codes so alias pages resolve correctly.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact - Refresh tokens were accepted as bearer credentials on protected APIs because resource-server JWT validation only checked signature/expiry. A stolen or logged refresh token could access authenticated endpoints for the full refresh TTL, bypassing the intended short access-token lifetime and refresh-token revocation store. - KnowPost detail cache hits returned cached private/draft content without rerunning the DB authorization check. If an owner cached a private/draft detail response, another anonymous or non-owner viewer could receive the cached content. ## Root cause - Access and refresh tokens share the same JWT decoder, and the security filter chain did not enforce `token_type=access` for bearer authentication. - `KnowPostServiceImpl#getDetail` enforced visibility only on DB misses; L1/Redis cache hits directly enriched and returned cached responses. ## Fix - Added a resource-server JWT decoder wrapper that accepts only `token_type=access`, while keeping the primary raw decoder for refresh-token workflows. - Wired Spring Security to use the access-token-only decoder for protected endpoints. - Re-check current DB status/visibility/ownership before serving knowpost detail cache hits. - Added focused unit tests for rejecting refresh JWT bearer auth and preventing cached private/draft detail leaks. ## Validation - `mvn -Dtest=AuthConfigurationTest,KnowPostServiceImplTest test`

body: ## Bug and impact - A Sanity write token was committed in `scripts/upload-photos.mjs`, allowing anyone with repository access/history to write or delete production CMS data. - CMS-authored collection text was serialized into JSON-LD with raw `JSON.stringify` inside `set:html`, allowing `` breakout and script injection on generated pages. - Flat state photo folders were uploaded as a `.` collection with an empty slug, corrupting collection identity and metadata. ## Root cause - The upload script embedded a production write token and treated direct state-folder photos as city folder `.`. - Layout JSON-LD used raw JSON serialization in an HTML script context without escaping HTML-significant characters. ## Fix - Require `SANITY_TOKEN` from the environment and document it in `.env.example`. - Upload flat state folders using the state name as the collection identity while reading from the state directory, and reject empty generated slugs. - Add `serializeJsonLd` to escape HTML-significant characters before injecting JSON-LD. - Add node:test coverage for script-tag breakout prevention and JSON parseability. ## Validation - `npm test` - `npm run build` Note: the exposed Sanity token should be rotated because it remains present in git history.

body:
## Summary

Splits the 637-line `LinkStore` god object into a shared `Database` class plus five focused stores, each owning one domain. All stores share a single SQLite connection via the `Database`, which also owns versioned migrations via a `_schema_version` table.

Closes #100.

## What changed

### New modules (`src/lorekeeper/services/`)

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `database.py` | 320 | Shared SQLite connection (WAL, FKs), versioned migrations |
| `memory_store.py` | 135 | \`memories\` table CRUD |
| `reflection_store.py` | 142 | \`reflections\` + \`sessions\` (FK-coupled) |
| `metrics_store.py` | 68 | \`api_metrics\` per-hour counters |
| `config_store.py` | 50 | \`config_overrides\` dashboard-persisted settings |

### Trimmed

- \`link_store.py\`: **637 → 150 lines** (link CRUD + \`_row_to_link\` only)

### Rewired

- **\`orchestrator.py\`**: \`MemoryService\` now accepts focused stores; **public attributes** \`svc.memories\`, \`svc.links\`, \`svc.reflections\`, \`svc.metrics\`, \`svc.config\`, \`svc.settings\` (no more \`_store\` / \`_settings\` private access)
- **\`server.py\`**: \`init_service()\` instantiates \`Database\` + 5 stores, runs \`db.migrate()\`, passes everything to \`MemoryService\`
- **\`dashboard/app.py\`**: 17 \`_store\` + 2 \`_settings\` private accesses replaced with typed focused-store / public-settings access
- **\`scripts/seed_lancedb.py\`, \`scripts/migrate_from_json.py\`**: updated to new wiring

### Tests

- \`tests/_helpers.py\`: \`build_stores()\` + \`build_service()\` factories for clean fixtures (Stores bundle + MemoryService construction)
- \`tests/test_database.py\`: **11 new tests** covering migrations, idempotency, legacy DB dedup, WAL+FK pragmas, version tracking
- Existing 156 tests adapted to use focused-store accessors

**Final count: 167 passed** (156 → 167, +11 new database tests).

## Migration strategy

The bootstrap migration (version 1, \`bootstrap_schema_and_fixups\`) captures all pre-LKPR-51 schema + idempotent fixups verbatim:
- Base schema (all CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS)
- Dedup memory_links + unique pair constraint
- Dedup memories by title (legacy DBs)
- Add session content columns
- Add \`last_used\` column
- Add \`namespace\` column
- Migrate unique title index to namespace-scoped

Future schema changes append to \`MIGRATIONS\` with strictly-increasing version numbers. Each migration runs in its own transaction; applied versions tracked in \`_schema_version\`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] All existing LinkStore functionality preserved (167 tests pass)
- [x] \`Database\` class owns connection lifecycle + versioned migrations; ad-hoc \`_migrate_*\` methods removed
- [x] \`MemoryService.__init__\` accepts focused stores instead of one \`LinkStore\`
- [x] Dashboard accesses stores via named attributes (\`get_service().memories\`) not \`_store\`
- [x] All stores return dict-shaped rows (typed Pydantic model conversion deferred to follow-up)
- [x] All 121+ existing tests pass with minimal fixture changes
- [x] \`LinkStore\` file drops from 637 to ~150 lines (exact: 150)

## Required updates

- [x] **CLAUDE.md**: Architecture section updated with the SQLite decomposition table + migration mechanics
- [x] **lorekeeper-dev skill** (v1.25.0): New \`SQLite Architecture\` section documenting stores, factories, and how to add migrations

author: sebbogit
body:
## What & why

The single v1.0-release blocker from the readiness audit. A fresh `docker compose up` ran migrations but never seeded the `countries` table — only `pnpm db:seed` did, and the deploy docs called that "optional development seed data." Because `trip_countries` and `user_visited_countries` both FK to `countries.code` with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, a clean install hit a foreign-key violation the moment you tried to mark a country visited on `/map`, and the world choropleth had nothing to colour. The minimal-deploy docs meanwhile promised the world map worked — a direct contradiction.

## Change

- Extract the idempotent insert into a shared `seedCountries(db)` (`src/lib/countries/seed.ts`), reused by both callers so a Docker deploy and a bare-metal `pnpm db:seed` load identical reference data.
- Call it from the worker boot right after migrations (`scripts/worker.ts`), before pg-boss / status sweep / ready marker. A failure fails the boot and the orchestrator restarts us — same model as migrations, and safe because the seed is `onConflictDoNothing`.
- Fix `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` (the "optional seed data" wording, and point manual installs at `pnpm db:setup`) and `docs/WORKER.md` (new boot step) so the docs match reality.

## Verification

Booted the real worker against a migrated-but-empty database: `countries` went **0 → 250** before the ready marker, with `worker.seed.completed count:250` logged. Typecheck, lint, prettier clean; full unit suite green; new `seed.test.ts` guards load + idempotency (DB-gated, runs in CI).

Part of the v1.0 readiness work. Does **not** bump the version or tag — that stays a separate, deliberate step.

author: davydog187
body:
## Goal

`table.unpack(list, i, j)` built the entire `i..j` slice before
returning, so a large `j` (e.g. `math.maxinteger`) sent the VM into a
multi-billion-element loop. Lua 5.3's `ltablib.c` checks the range up
front and raises `too many results to unpack` when the element count
`(j - i) + 1` reaches `INT_MAX` (its count-overflow and `lua_checkstack`
arms both reduce to this). This adds that guard before any slot is read.

This is the single most tractable concrete failure triaged out of the
A24 stdlib/data-structure cluster (#262): the first assertion `sort.lua`
hits, at line 16, is driven by `checkerror("too many results", unpack,
{}, 0, maxi)`.

## Changes

- `lib/lua/vm/stdlib/table.ex`: `table_unpack/2` raises
  `Lua.VM.RuntimeError` with `too many results to unpack` when
  `i <= j and j - i >= 2_147_483_646` (count `>= INT_MAX`), before
  materialising the slice. This models both PUC rejection arms, including
  the `lua_checkstack` arm that fires at count exactly `INT_MAX`. The
  subtraction uses Elixir bignums, so it cannot overflow.
- `test/lua/vm/stdlib/table_test.exs`: regression coverage for the
  rejected range, the `(1 << 31) - 1` boundary, the count-exactly-INT_MAX
  case, a normal range, and a reversed (empty) huge range.
- `test/lua53_skips.exs`: `sort.lua` stays a whole-file skip — its first
  assertion no longer fails, but the file still times out on the
  O(n^2) sort sections and the unimplemented `os.clock` timing harness.
  The skip reason is updated and now carries `issue: 262`.

## Out of scope

- `constructs.lua` os/debug/short-circuit cases (other PRs in the batch).
- `literals.lua` parse-error wording / `debug.getinfo` line skips.
- `table.sort` "too big" / "invalid order function" detection and the
  `table.move` "materialise-before-write" interruption semantics
  (sort.lua line 174) — separate, larger follow-ups.

## Verification

- `mix format`, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean.
- `mix test`: 2040 passed, 22 skipped, 0 failures.
- `mix test test/lua53_suite_test.exs --only lua53`: 14 passed, 15
  skipped, 0 failures (no lua53 delta — `sort.lua` was and remains a
  whole-file skip; the unpack correctness fix is proven by the new unit
  tests).

Plan: A24a

Closes #262

## What

phase-advance Edge Function의 첫째 밤 룰(P2-1)을 구현하고, 모든 페이즈 duration을 `GOMDORI_RULES` 매니페스트에서 읽도록 한다.

- `role_assign → night` 전환 시 duration = `GOMDORI_RULES.firstNight.durationSec` (8초, 안내성).
- `night` 페이즈에서 `phase_number === 1 && firstNight.skipsAbilities` 이면 능력 해석(`resolveNightActions`)을 건너뛰고 `first_night_silent` 이벤트(`payload: { day_number: 1 }`)를 발행한 뒤 `night_resolve`를 거치지 않고 바로 `day`로 전환 — 야간 사망/조사 없음.
- 둘째 밤부터는 기존 능력 해석 로직 그대로.
- 하드코딩돼 있던 duration(60/3/180/60/60)을 전부 `GOMDORI_RULES.phases.*`로 치환.

규칙 정본([[Universes/BoW/Lore/Gomdori-마피아-규칙]]) 및 사용자 결정(2026-05-31): "첫째 밤은 직업 배정 이후 바로 아침 돌입, 능력 사용 X" + "하드코딩 박지 말기". 매니페스트(`_shared/gomdori-rules.ts`)에 `firstNight.skipsAbilities`가 이미 정의돼 있었으나 phase-advance가 이를 사용하지 않아, 첫 판 첫 밤에 능력이 발동되는 상태였다. 라이브 end-to-end의 0→1 blocker.

body: ## Bug and impact Reactive Mongo write/delete calls were created and then discarded in WebFlux paths. Because no subscriber was attached to those publishers, form create/update/delete operations and REST delete endpoints could return success while no database mutation happened. ## Root cause Controller/handler methods invoked `Mono`-returning repository/service methods for side effects, then returned a plain view name or a separate `Mono`. ### Motivation
- Introduce the platform technical foundation to support typed configuration, observability (tracing, logging, metrics), correlation/request ID propagation, and centralized exception-to-API-error mapping. 
- Reserve package boundaries and scaffolding for future platform features like persistence, events/outbox, security and tenancy without adding business domain code. 
- Provide Spring Boot wiring points (configuration properties, beans) and stable MDC handling for safe logging and sensitive value masking. 
- Update the roadmap status to mark initial platform tasks as completed and document the current progress. 

### Description
- Add typed platform configuration via `HidraPlatformProperties` and enable it with `PlatformConfiguration`, plus lightweight beans: `ClockConfiguration`, `OpenApiConfiguration`, and `JacksonConfiguration`. 
- Implement correlation propagation with `CorrelationContext`, `CorrelationIdResolver`, `CorrelationIdFilter`, and header constants in `CorrelationHeaders`, and wire MDC entries for correlation and request IDs. 
- Add logging support including `LoggingContext` and `SensitiveValueMasker` to safely write platform context into the MDC while masking sensitive values. 
- Implement global exception handling and mapping to kernel error responses via `GlobalExceptionHandler`, `ApiErrorFactory`, and platform exception types `PlatformException` and `InfrastructureException`. 
- Add numerous `package-info.java` files to define package boundaries for observability, events, persistence, security, tenancy and other platform subpackages. 
- Update `docs/roadmap/platform.md` to mark tasks `PLAT-002` through `PLAT-006` as completed with notes indicating successful compilation.

## Bug
`feature_discovery_teacher` returned only the permission line; the controller resolved Teacher Mode content in a **separate post-win fetch**. On null/throw, the line still fired with no content → Gemini called `end_teaching_session` and closed the overlay the moment the user said "yes" (VTID-03112 / VTID-03160).

## Fix
- Provider resolves content **inside `produce()`** and bundles it on the candidate (`TeacherContinuation.teacherMode`).
- On null/throw → `status:'errored'` → ranker falls through to `voice_wake_brief`. **Teacher never fires without content.**
- Controller reads `picked.teacherMode` off the winner; the separate `resolveTeacherModeContent` call is removed.
- Dynamic import avoids the resolver↔provider runtime cycle; `types.ts` stays teacher-agnostic (localized `TeacherContinuation` cast).

## Parity
- **Vertex** ✓ — `live-session-controller.ts` consumes `candidate.teacherMode`.
- **LiveKit** ✓ — shared provider → identical errored-fallthrough; LiveKit doesn't deliver Teacher Mode content today (pre-existing gap, separate PR) → no regression.

## Tests
3 new provider tests (bundled / null→errored / throw→errored) + 561 assistant-continuation+session + 11 resolver tests green; `tsc` (build mode) clean.

## Note
PR-3 (Vertex turn-1 collision) was **retired**: the live `[wake-decision]` logs showed `turn1_collision:true`, but diagnosis proved `journeyGreetingBlock` is not concatenated into the Vertex prompt (VTID-03162) — the collision flag was a measurement artifact, not a real prompt conflict.
