author: sentry[bot]
body:
This PR addresses SURE-APP-Y9, a `NoMethodError` occurring when a user attempts to create a buy or sell trade without providing a ticker symbol.

**Root Cause:**
The `security` method in `Trade::CreateForm` returns `nil` if no `ticker` or `manual_ticker` is present. The `create_trade` method then attempts to call `.ticker` on this `nil` value, leading to a `NoMethodError`.

**Solution:**
Implemented a nil check at the beginning of the `create_trade` method, mirroring the pattern used in `create_dividend_income`. If `security` resolves to `nil`, an `Entry` with a validation error is built and returned early, preventing the `NoMethodError`. A new i18n key, `trade_requires_security`, has been added to `config/locales/views/trades/en.yml` for the error message.

Fixes SURE-APP-Y9

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Summary Deep bug scan of recent Phase B userspace commits found several high-severity issues in boot-critical components. This PR applies minimal, targeted fixes. ## Bugs fixed ### ramfs (boot logging filesystem) 1. **fchown used FD as inode** — `fchown(5, …)` could change ownership of inode 5 instead of the file behind handle 5. 2. **write ignored O_RDONLY** — writes succeeded on read-only opens, allowing content corruption. 3. **path resolution panicked on `.` / `..`** — could crash the ramfs daemon (DoS on `ramfs@logging`). 4. **unlinkat always returned EACCES** — stray `!` on inode check blocked all deletes. ### randd (CSPRNG at boot) 5. **rdrand failures seeded ChaCha20 with zeros** — x86_64 did not check the carry flag; VMs without reliable RDRAND got predictable random. ### init scheduler 6. **circular `requires_weak` caused infinite boot loop** — mutual weak deps re-queued forever; now capped with a cycle warning. ## Validation - `cargo test -p ramfs` (new `resolve_dot_and_dotdot` test) - `cargo check -p ramfs -p randd -p init` ## Not in this PR - redox-rt `SIG_IGN` trampoline race (panic → early return) — moderate fix, left for follow-up - bootstrap spawn pipe read failure handling — high but less boot-common

## Purpose / Description

Move the insights engine from enterprise-only (`ee/observal_insights/`) to the open-source core (`observal-server/services/insights/`). Insights is now freely available to all users without requiring an `OBSERVAL_LICENSE_KEY`.

## Fixes

## Approach

1. Moved all 8 insight modules (`generator`, `facets`, `sections`, `batch`, `session_meta_extractor`, `transcript`, `html_export`, `_deps`) from `ee/observal_insights/` into `observal-server/services/insights/`.

The insights engine was already designed with dependency injection (`_deps.py` pattern) so the move was straightforward. The `configure()` function self-references via `import services.insights._deps as _self`, which works correctly in the new location.

body: ## Bug and impact - Bulk transfers with duplicate SKU lines could silently keep the last non-null branch sale price, corrupting the destination branch retail price for future POS sales. - Branch stock request fulfillment transferred stock in a separate context before marking the request fulfilled, so concurrent approvals or a retry after a status-save failure could duplicate stock movements. - The EF model snapshot omitted `Expenses.VisibleInBranchExpenseList` and `Invoices.ContainsEstimatedCost`, and legacy DB startup fallback did not add `Invoices.ContainsEstimatedCost`, risking dropped flag columns in future migrations and sale failures on upgraded databases that skipped EF migrations. ## Root cause - Duplicate bulk-transfer line normalization merged quantities but resolved conflicting prices with last-write-wins semantics. - Stock-request resolution loaded a pending row, called `ITransferService` which committed independently, then updated request state afterward. - Snapshot/runtime schema fallback drifted from the domain model and existing migrations. ## Fix - Reject duplicate bulk-transfer rows for the same product when both rows specify different branch prices; preserve matching/null price behavior. - Fulfill branch stock requests in one serializable transaction and shared DbContext via the transfer write helper; use conditional pending-state updates for reject/cancel races. - Restore the missing snapshot properties and add startup fallback for `Invoices.ContainsEstimatedCost`. ## Validation - `git diff --check HEAD~1 HEAD` passed. - Attempted `dotnet build OilChangePOS.sln`, but this runner does not have `dotnet` installed (`dotnet: command not found`).

author: esse
body:
Implements the Scribe SPEC as a Rails 8 monolith. Record a screen + narration in the browser, stream it to storage while recording, transcribe the voice, extract frames aligned to what's said, have Claude generate a structured manual, review/edit it, and export to Markdown/HTML/PDF. Processing is gated on prepaid Stripe credits.

All **7 milestones** are implemented, with the contractual core (data model §6, pipeline §8/9, export registry §11, credit ledger §12/13) fully built and tested.

## Pipeline

A linear state machine on `recordings.status`, each stage an idempotent job that advances status and enqueues the next:

```
recording → uploaded → transcribing → extracting_frames → generating_manual → complete
                                  └─────────────── failed (records failed_stage) ◀┘
```

Transient errors (network/timeout) auto-retry with backoff; permanent/exhausted failures record `failed_stage`, void the credit hold, and report to Sentry. A failed recording can be re-run from its stage via `POST /recordings/:id/retry`.

## Where Claude is / isn't used

The Anthropic API has no speech-to-text, so transcription goes through a provider abstraction (`Transcription::Base.build` — offline `Stub` default, plus Deepgram and faster-whisper impls). Claude does step segmentation, frame selection (vision), and prose via a forced `emit_manual` tool schema, with an offline `FakeClient` so dev/CI never spend.

## What's included

- **Data model** — recordings, transcripts/segments, frames, manuals/steps, exports, credit_packs, credit_transactions (ledger), stripe_events.
- **Media** — real `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe`: audio extraction, scene-detected frames with periodic fallback, on-demand seeks, thumbnails.
- **Exporters** — `Registry` + Markdown (zip + images) / HTML (self-contained base64) / **PDF via WeasyPrint** (HTML/CSS → PDF CLI, no browser). Adding a format = one subclass + register.
- **Credits/Stripe** — append-only ledger (`hold!`/`settle!`/`void!`), derived balance, per-user row-locked reservation, flat per-minute metering, Stripe Checkout, idempotent webhook, 402 gating on `/complete`.
- **Upload/UI** — resumable tus upload + Stimulus recorder, status polling, review/edit UI, data-driven export buttons, signed-URL storage (disk dev / S3 prod adapters).
- **Hardening (M7)** — automatic + manual per-stage retries, failure/retry + delete UI, `RecordingPurge` (full delete + raw-video retention purge) with a daily `PurgeExpiredRecordingsJob`, and token-usage logging.
- **Local full-flow dev** — `docker compose up -d` brings up Postgres + MinIO (auto-creates the bucket); `dotenv-rails` (dev-only) loads `.env`, which documents the keys to run real transcription + manual generation against MinIO storage.
- **Ops** — Rails 8 auth, Sentry, CI (Postgres + ffmpeg + WeasyPrint + RuboCop + Brakeman), `bin/web-setup` SessionStart hook, and `bin/dev` one-command bring-up (web + Solid Queue worker).

## Tests (SPEC §15)

`bin/rails test` → **48 runs, 0 failures, 0 skips**. RuboCop and Brakeman clean.

- Ledger math + hold/settle/void + no double-spend under concurrency
- Exporter golden files (Markdown/HTML) + registry + PDF render (WeasyPrint)

body: ## Bug and impact The scoring pipeline consumed articles when the relevance or importance model returned unparseable text. Ambiguous relevance output was written as `isRelevant=false`, and relevant articles with unparseable importance were written as `isRelevant=true` with `finalScore=null`. Because future score runs only select `isRelevant=null` and daily top requires `isRelevant=true` plus `finalScore`, those articles were permanently dropped from scoring/top-news selection. The relevance parser also treated natural `NOT RELEVANT` / `irrelevant` responses as relevant, allowing off-topic items into daily top candidates. ## Root cause `parseRelevance` only recognized the exact `NOT_RELEVANT` token and then matched any remaining `RELEVANT` substring. The score job also persisted terminal article state for parse failures instead of leaving the row retryable. ## Fix - Normalize relevance responses and parse `NOT_RELEVANT`, `NOT RELEVANT`, and `irrelevant` as false. - Leave unparseable relevance/importance responses untouched so the next score cron retries them. - Count retry outcomes separately from processed items. - Add focused parser tests. ## Validation - `npm test` - `npm run lint` (passes with existing warnings in `articleDisplayDefaults.ts` and `dailyTopJob.ts`) - `npm run build`

author: sparky100
body:
## Summary

Fixes a regression where clicking **Discard Changes** would briefly revert the model but then immediately re-dirty it, making the discard appear to have no effect.

### Root cause

`ConditionBuilder` has a `useEffect` that compares `JSON.stringify(externalValue)` against the last prop value to decide whether to call `onChange(normalized)`. After a discard, the model reverts to the saved state — but `migrateLegacyCondition` was:

1. Preserving extra/legacy fields via `...condition` spread in the logical-condition case, so the serialised form still differed from what ConditionBuilder had last seen.
2. Returning leaf values with non-canonical types (e.g. `"5"` as a string instead of `5` as a number), so `JSON.stringify` still differed after normalization.

Both mismatches caused `onChange` to fire, which called `setDirty(true)` — re-dirtying the model immediately after the discard.

### Fixes

- **Strip extra fields in logical conditions** (`migrateLegacyCondition`): remove the `...condition` spread so only `operator` and `clauses` are preserved in the canonical form.
- **Canonicalize leaf value types** (`migrateLegacyCondition`): pass `rawValue` through `parseScalarValue` so numbers/booleans are stored as their native JS types, matching what ConditionBuilder reconstructs on the next render.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a model with a C-event condition, make an edit, then click **Discard Changes** — the model should revert and the dirty indicator should clear (not re-appear)
- [ ] Verify existing condition-format unit tests pass: `tests/model/conditionFormat.test.js`
- [ ] Verify no regression in condition-builder UI tests: `tests/ui/editors/c-event-editor.test.jsx`

author: mikelward
body:
## What

Adds a `UserPromptSubmit` hook that keeps the Claude Code **session title in sync with whatever's being worked on**, so parallel sessions are findable in the picker without manual `/rename`. Answers "how are session names chosen, and can we auto-pick a short name that evolves?" — the answer is the `sessionTitle` hook output field, wired up here.

## How it works

- **`.claude/hooks/session-title.sh`** — on each prompt, asks `claude -p` for a short kebab-case label (**≤16 chars**, trimmed on whole-word boundaries, short punchy words preferred — `kill` over `delete`), and emits it via the `sessionTitle` field of `hookSpecificOutput`. The name **evolves** as the conversation pivots.
- **Registered in `.claude/settings.json`** alongside the existing `SessionStart` hook (both preserved).
- **Recursion guard (two layers).** The naming call is itself `claude -p`, and `UserPromptSubmit` hooks run under `claude -p`, so a naive call would re-enter this hook and loop. (1) The inner call runs from a fresh per-invocation `mktemp -d` (cleaned up on exit), so it never discovers any `.claude/settings.json` / `CLAUDE.md` — no hooks load, and the namer isn't distracted by repo context. (2) `CC_TITLE_HOOK_ACTIVE` is exported before the inner call and short-circuits the hook at entry.
- **Portable timeout.** Prefers `timeout`, falls back to `gtimeout` (Homebrew coreutils on macOS), and if neither exists runs the call unwrapped rather than failing the hook into a silent no-op.
- **Configurable model.** Defaults to the `haiku` alias (cheap + fast, resolves on current CLIs); override with `CC_TITLE_MODEL=<full-id>` for builds where the alias doesn't resolve.
- **Manual-name protection is best-effort.** Per the docs, `session_title` is a `SessionStart` input, not `UserPromptSubmit`. Where a build supplies it, a marker file lets the hook detect a manual `/rename` and back off; where it's absent, the title keeps auto-updating — an accepted trade-off in favor of the evolving behavior.
- **Degrades silently.** Missing `jq`/`claude`, an unauthenticated/timed-out/failed headless call, or empty output all leave the title unchanged — never blocks or errors the prompt.

## Caveats

- **Per-prompt cost:** every prompt triggers a short, blocking model call before submission. Deliberate trade-off for meaningful names over a cheap heuristic. Remove the `UserPromptSubmit` block from `.claude/settings.json` to opt out.
- **Engine version:** `sessionTitle` requires a recent Claude Code (≈ v2.1.96+). Verified on v2.1.158.

## Notes

- Rebased onto latest `main` (which already gitignores `.claude/settings.local.json`), so the branch is a clean single-commit diff with no `.gitignore` churn.

## Test plan

Verified with a deterministic mock `claude` on `PATH` plus payloads on stdin:

- `bash -n` syntax check.
- Recursion guard (`CC_TITLE_HOOK_ACTIVE=1`) → silent, ~0s, no inner call.
- Multi-word output → trimmed to ≤16 on a hyphen boundary (`fix-the-feels`), no trailing hyphen.
- Single over-long word → hard-cut to 16 (`supercalifragili`).
- Short label → passes through unchanged (`kill-flake`).
- Simulated manual `/rename` (current title ≠ last-set marker) → silent, marker flips to backed-off.
- Model selector: default sends `--model haiku`; `CC_TITLE_MODEL` override honored.
- Fresh `mktemp -d` per run, cleaned up afterward (no temp leak).
- `settings.json` validated with `jq`, contains both `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit`.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the long-standing "spin turns half the commanded angle" bug and two related PID issues surfaced while building a drive-test routine, plus folds in pending chassis/motor tuning from the working tree.

## Bug fixes (this session)

### IMU gyro reads 2x true rate
`bsp_IcmGetRawData()` converted raw gyro counts as ±1000 dps (FS_SEL=2, register read-back confirmed). But this **ICM-45686 unit reports a robust 2x the true rate** — a commanded 90° spin physically rotated ~45°, stable across angles. Verified the integration `dt` (5 ms, matches the single 5 ms sensor-task path) and the byte assembly are correct, isolating the factor to the raw→dps scale. Now converts at the **effective ±500 dps** full scale (`raw*500/32768`). This is an empirical, per-unit calibration — re-verify if the IMU is swapped.

### PID integral windup across mode transitions
These affect **all** spin/cruise motion (CLI included), not just the test:
- `clear_car_control()` now also clears `pid_spin`. Previously a new spin inherited the **opposite** integral from the prior spin and briefly drove the wrong direction before correcting (e.g. a left turn began by rotating right).
- `Set_Car_Stop()` now clears `pid_v_angle`. The inner angular-velocity integral was frozen (not cleared) on stop, so resuming into cruise right after a spin kept the car turning until it unwound (veered left after a left spin).

### Spin overshoot tuning
`MAX_V_ANGLE` 60 → 10 °/s to reduce momentum coast past the stop trigger (~2–3° overshoot at higher rates). Documented inline as the primary overshoot knob (with the `D_SPIN` alternative and the `MOVE_TIMEOUT_MS` interaction noted).

## New: drive-test routine (`AppReserved_Task`)
Sequence on boot: **1000 mm straight → right 90° → 100 mm → left 90° → cruise 100 mm/s for 10 s → cruise 1000 mm/s for 3 s.** Includes:
- `wait_operation_done()` with a per-segment **timeout + force-stop** (prevents a runaway/hung spin if a move never completes),
- a **gyro-calibration gate** before any motion (yaw is frozen until calibration latches),
- `IMU_IsCalibrated()` accessor added to the IMU module to support the gate.

## Pre-existing working-tree changes (folded in)
- `platform_config.h`: chassis geometry updated for **72 mm wheels** (wheel dia/perimeter, half-track, half-wheelbase); fixed malformed literal `WHEEL_DIR 72F` → `72.0F`.
- `motor_config.h`: `MAX_MOTOR_DUTY` 0.999 → 0.3 (PWM output cap).
- `read_aux_data_mode.c`: added a `GYRO_CONFIG0` read-back diagnostic at init.

## Reviewer notes
- The ±500 dps gyro scale and `MAX_V_ANGLE=10` are **hardware-calibrated values** — expect a flash-and-measure pass to confirm. At 1000 mm/s, cruise is clamped to `MAX_V_REAL` ≈ 452 mm/s.
- Not compiled here (no ARM toolchain in this environment).
- `current_work.md` is an included session debugging log (Chinese); drop it from the PR if you'd rather keep it out of the repo.

body:
## Bug (H1)

`_param_metrics` in `reference_compare.py` collapsed event dims to a per-sample scalar mean before computing statistics. For a d-dim parameter this gives `emp_std = true_element_std/√d`, so `std_ratio_max_dev ≈ 1−1/√d` even for **perfect draws** (d=8: 0.646; verified against committed eight_schools recipe: 0.6445).

The runner (`_recipe_runner.py:1259`) compounded the bug by also collapsing per-element ref arrays via `.mean()`, making both sides wrong in the same direction.

## Fix (two locations)

1. **`reference_compare.py`**: `_param_metrics` now reshapes `flat` to `(N, d)`, computes per-element mean/std/q05/q95, broadcasts scalar or array ref stats to `(d,)`, and reduces by max over elements (mirrors headline's min/max aggregation per Design invariant #3).
2. **`_recipe_runner.py:1259`**: passes ref stats as-is (`_v[_stat]` — float or list/array) without `.mean()` collapse.
3. **Type update**: `_RefSummary = dict[str, Any]` (values may be float or list[float]).

## Regression tests (3 new fast tests)

- Perfect scalar draws → all metrics < 0.05
- Perfect 8-D draws → `std_ratio_max_dev` < 0.05 (was 0.646 pre-fix, demonstrating the artefact)
- 2-D draws matching per-element ref std=[1,2] → correctly passes (grand-mean approach would fail)

## Backfill (123 recipes)

- **19 re-stamped** from draws cache: `std_ratio_max_dev` 0.64→0.04, `q05/q95_error` 1.06→0.07
- **104 nulled** (`q05/q95/std` → null): draws cache not available → unknown > wrong
- `mae_vs_reference` unaffected (linear operation; unchanged)

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] 44/44 metrics tests pass, pre-commit clean, marker gate clean
- [x] Probe: `std_ratio_max_dev` 0.648 → 0.005 for perfect 8-dim N(0,1) draws
- [x] Branch clean off `origin/main` (2436b57)
- [x] SMC api-pin failures in worktree are pre-existing (blackjax upstream batch_size change; unrelated)

## Summary
Native Windows 11 rewrite of the Sentinel Forge Book Reader as a **hybrid C# (WinUI 3) + C++** app, packaged as a signed MSIX.

## Architecture
- **C++ engine** (`cpp/SentinelForge/core`) → `SentinelForgeCore.dll`, exposing a C ABI consumed from C# via P/Invoke (`Services/SentinelCore.cs`). Handles txt/md/log + HTML parsing and chapter detection.
- **C# WinUI 3 app** (`csharp/SentinelForge`) — Reader, Focus, and Library areas behind a NavigationView.
- Each language used where it's strongest; proven C# libraries for PDF/DOCX.

## Features
- **Reader** — open txt/md/log/html (C++), pdf (PdfPig), docx (Open XML); chapter navigation, font sizing, read-aloud (WinRT speech), highlights, bookmarks, notes.
- **Focus** — Pomodoro timer (25/5/15 cycles) + Eisenhower matrix.
- **Library** — folder scan + GREEN/YELLOW/RED cognitive-load zones.
- **Persistence** — SQLite (`Microsoft.Data.Sqlite`): highlights, notes, bookmarks, tasks, zones.
- **Windows 11** — Mica, custom title bar, toasts, file associations, jump list; MSIX packaging (built, signed, installed locally).

## Notes
- Build artifacts (C++ outputs, `bin/obj`, `AppPackages`) are git-ignored. Build the native engine with `cpp/SentinelForge/core/build_core.bat` before building the C# app.
- The Python reference app (`book_reader/`) is intentionally not included.

body: ## Bug and impact - `POST /user/{email}/{role}` was covered by the generic `/user/**` rule, which only required `USER` authority. - Any authenticated regular user could add `ADMIN` to their own account or another account, causing privilege escalation. ## Root cause - The role-changing endpoint had no method-level authorization and the route matched the broader `/user/**` security rule before any admin-only check. ## Fix - Require `ADMIN` for `POST /user/*/*` in `SecurityConfig` before the generic `/user/**` matcher. - Add `@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ADMIN')")` directly on the role-changing controller method. - Add a focused MVC security test proving `USER` receives 403 and `ADMIN` can perform the role change. ## Validation - Passed: `bash ./mvnw -Dtest=UserControllerSecurityTest test` - Full `bash ./mvnw test` still fails in the pre-existing `BackendApplicationTests.contextLoads` because no datasource URL or embedded test database is configured in this environment.

author: githouson
body:
Two bugs fixed in this PR.

**SK6805 / vibro pin conflict (#541)**

`gpio_vibro` and `SK6805_LED_PIN` are both mapped to `GPIOA, LL_GPIO_PIN_8`. `SK6805_update()` calls `SK6805_init()` on every invocation which drives the pin low and reconfigures it, cutting off any active vibration mid-buzz. After the bit-bang loop completes the pin is left at whatever state the final data bit required, not the vibro state.

Fix: read the pin state before the update and restore it afterward.

**NTAG21x write blocked after password clear (#538)**

After clearing a password (`PWD=0x00000000`, `PACK=0x00000000`, `AUTH0=0xFF`) the Flipper incorrectly treats the tag as still protected. Two places were responsible:

- `mf_ultralight_is_all_data_read()` returns false when `PWD==0 && PACK==0`, hiding the Write button in the menu. This is wrong when `AUTH0=0xFF` because there is no active protection regardless of what the password pages contain.
- The write poller rejects writes if `auth_success` is false, even when `AUTH0=0xFF` means no authentication is required at all.

Fix: both checks now skip the password gate when the config page reports `AUTH0=0xFF`.

author: drbaher
body:
## b170 — golden eval gate + reporting

The nightly `golden_eval` step printed `[OK] completed` unconditionally then returned `composite>=0.5`, so the log said OK while the JSON recorded `golden_eval=false` (composite 0.30). Golden generation was also non-deterministic (b166 only wired autoresearch), making the composite noisy night-to-night.

### Changes
- **Honest reporting:** `step_golden_eval` prints `[OK]` only when composite ≥ the 0.5 quality **target**, else `[WARN] below target` — log now matches JSON.
- **Deterministic golden eval:** `deterministic=True` + `seed=EVAL_SEED` + `no_cloud_fallback=True` on the eval `DraftRequest`s (nightly step, `run_golden_eval`, `run_eval`). Eval-path only; **production drafting unchanged**.
- **Gate semantics (not number-unifying):** 0.5 is a reported *target*, not the promotion gate. `should_promote` stays a **non-regression** rule — promote iff `candidate ≥ baseline − tolerance` (cold-start always promotes; degenerate refuses), so the best-available adapter is always served. `min_floor` defaults to **0.0 (disabled)** — a 0.5 hard floor would roll back every sub-0.5 retrain and **freeze the loop** at the current ~0.30 quality. A kept sub-target adapter logs "below target 0.5 but kept (doesn't regress vs prior)" so WARN + keep no longer look contradictory.

### Deferred (separate reviewed PR — they change production drafting for all users)
Draft **length-cap enforcement** and **personal-mode routing** — the two behaviors actually depressing the 0.30 composite.

### Tests
`tests/test_golden_eval_gate_b170.py` — honest [OK]/[WARN]; eval determinism flags; warm non-regressing sub-0.5 promoted; regression rolled back; cold-start; degenerate. 53 passed; ruff clean.

author: soulware
body:
## Summary

Reworks how a role declares it issues a third-party caveat. The old shape was a global `[auth].endpoint` (the TPC `location`) plus a per-role `issues_with_tpc = true` bool. The new shape is a per-role section:

```toml
[[role]]
name = "volume-rw"
# ...
[role.tpc]
location = "https://auth.example/"   # or unix:… in the demo
```

Presence of `[role.tpc]` enables the TPC; its `location` is where the discharge is fetched. `location` is the macaroon-paper term — it matches our own `Caveat::ThirdParty { location }` and libmacaroons/every reference impl (Fly's "url" is the lone dissenter).

## Changes

- **config:** `RawTpc`/`Tpc { location }`; `RawRole`/`Role` drop `issues_with_tpc`, gain `tpc: Option<Tpc>`. The `TpcRoleWithoutAuth` check is **repurposed** — a TPC role still needs `[auth]` for `K_M-A` (the caveat key), independent of the location, so the cross-field requirement is shifted (to K_M-A), not eliminated.
- **issuance (`http.rs`):** stamp the caveat from `tpc.location`; the `[auth]`-guard branch is gone (the `K_M-A`/`org_id` runtime guards stay).
- **seal:** `SealedRole.tpc: Option<Tpc>` replaces the bool, so the per-role `location` is now **sealed** — adding/removing the section or repointing the location requires a re-seal and is caught at startup. The exhaustive destructure forces the new field; `tpc_is_sealed` asserts MAC, diff, and semantic-equality all reflect it.
- `[auth].endpoint` now backs only the operator **cli-token**'s TPC location.

## Scope (follow-up deferred)

`location` stays in today's self-dialing base format (`unix:…`/`https://…`, path appended by code), so the demo client is unchanged. The full-URL `/v1/discharge` form, the `[demo_auth]`/`[operator]` config split (separating the demo serving socket, the `/v1/login` endpoint, and the cli-token location), and the Bun-style transport refactor are a **stacked follow-up**.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check` clean · `clippy --all-targets` clean · 183 lib tests pass
- `examples_load` / `discharge_verify` / `admin_discharge` pass sandboxed
- `assume_role_discharge` + 11 `enroll` tests pass unsandboxed (the sandboxed failure is a UDS-bind `EPERM`, not a regression) — `enroll` includes `tpc_role_credential_carries_third_party_caveat`, exercising the per-role `location` end-to-end.

import / 禁止 dep を一切追加していない。validator pass=1, pytest 20 passed 1 skipped。

## D: build_index 構文補強 7 件

1. `Public Const X As Type = value` / `Private Const Y = value`
   → `variables` に `const: true` / `scope: public|private` で記録
2. 複数行引数 `Sub Foo( _\n a As Long, _\n b As Long _\n)`
   → `_parse_args` が VBA 行継続 (`_\n`) を strip して comma split
3. `Call HelloWorld` / `Call Module2.Helper` (parens 無し)
   → 新規 `CALL_STMT_RE` で `_detect_calls` が拾い、call_graph に追加
4. `Public Type Person ... End Type` (UDT 定義)
   → `module.udts` に `{name, scope, fields[], start_line, end_line}` を記録
   → UDT body 内の `Field As Type` 行が variables / procedures に漏れない隔離も実装
5. 同名 procedure overload (`Sub Foo(a)` / `Sub Foo(a, b)` 同モジュール)
   → 各 procedure に `unique_key: "Mod.Foo#argc"` を付与、衝突回避
6. `Property Set` (既存 Get/Let に加え) → `kind: property-set` を確認テスト追加
7. `Option Explicit` / `Option Base 1` / `Option Compare Text` / `Option Private Module`
   → `module.options` に `[{name, arg}]` で記録

副次変更: `_parse_args` の修飾子処理を loop 化し `Optional ByVal name As T = default` の
順序ぶれを吸収。SKILL.md の Phase 表 / 制約節を Phase 1 状態に更新。

## E: prompts 詳細化 (host が読む推論プロンプト)

| prompt | before | after | 追加した主要節 |
|---|---|---|---|
| pass1-procedure.md | 77 行 | 325 行 | Field 意味表 / complexity_signal 判定基準 / Few-shot 3 / 失敗パターン 7 / Edge case (protected / Variant / Option Explicit 欠落 / overload / Property 3 つ組) |
| pass2-module.md    | 67 行 | 286 行 | Field 意味表 / cohesion_signal 判定基準 / Few-shot 3 / 失敗パターン 7 / Edge case (Class / UserForm / UDT 多用 / Option Private Module) |
| pass3-cross-module.md | 79 行 | 371 行 | Field 意味表 (entry_points / cross_module_flows / user_scenarios 別) / Few-shot 3 (単一 / 3 モジュール跨ぎ / 全 protected) / 失敗パターン 7 / Edge case (動的 dispatch / Worksheet event / Workbook_Open 二重定義 / overload / Form event chain) |

各 prompt が `procedure.unique_key` / `module.options` / `module.udts` 等 Phase 1
build_index 補強の出力スキーマを前提として参照するよう更新。

## F: refactor-suggest design

Phase 3 で本格 refactor 実装エンジンを起票する前に、prompt 側の design を確定。

- **動作不変制約 B-1〜B-7** (behaviour-preservation invariants)
  - B-1 出力同値 / B-2 副作用順 / B-3 浮動小数 / B-4 例外パス / B-5 型推論 /
    B-6 state lifetime / B-7 Excel 固有契約
  - 提案 1 件ごとに 7 項全てをセルフチェック (`behaviour_preservation.checks`)
- **提案 ID 管理**: `R-NNN-<slug>` 形式 (3 桁連番 + kebab-case)、`refactor-log.jsonl` 台帳
- **依存関係**: `depends_on` (順序) / `conflicts_with` (排他)、循環は host 側 DFS で reject
- **承認 workflow**: `proposed → applied / rejected / deferred`、再走時の重複防止規約
- **risk 分類**: low / medium / high の適用条件と人間 review 要否を表で
- **type 一覧 (14 種)**: 閉じた語彙を導入し refactor-log の集計破綻を防ぐ
  (`extract-pure-helper` / `tighten-signature` / `replace-select-with-range` 等)
- Few-shot 3 件 / 失敗パターン 8 件 / Edge case 6 種

## ADR-0036 準拠確認

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `requirements.txt` 変更 | なし (oletools / jinja2 / pyyaml のみ) |
| Python script から LLM SDK import 追加 | なし |
| Python script から LLM API URL 直叩き / subprocess CLI 起動 | なし |
| 動的 import (`importlib.import_module` / `__import__`) 追加 | なし |
| `scripts/validate-skill-backend-neutrality.py templates/skills/vba-docgen` | `pass=1 warn=0 fail=0` |
| `pytest templates/skills/vba-docgen/tests/ -v --no-cov` | `20 passed, 1 skipped` (旧 13 passed → +7 新規) |

## Phase 2 へ向けた残課題 (本 PR scope 外)

- 実 macro book (`tests/fixtures/sample_simple.xlsm`) の配置
  (sensitive macro を repo に入れない方針との両立を含めて要検討)
- ANTLR / vba-language-server 採用判断 — Phase 1 regex で不足する VBA 構文
  (`Enum ... End Enum`、ネストした UDT、API `Declare PtrSafe`、With ブロック内の暗黙
  メンバ呼出等) が実 macro book で表面化したらツール選定を起票
- refactor 提案の実装エンジン (動作不変 transform) — 本 PR で design を確定したので、
  Phase 3 の別 PR で `transform_*.py` を skill 内に追加するか、host 側エンジンに委ねるか
  を ADR で判断

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest templates/skills/vba-docgen/tests/ -v --no-cov` → 20 passed 1 skipped
- [x] `python scripts/validate-skill-backend-neutrality.py templates/skills/vba-docgen` → pass=1
- [x] D の 7 新規 test それぞれが事前 red → impl 後 green を確認
- [x] 既存 `test_build_index_call_graph_cross_module_qualifies_unique_candidate` の
      "Phase 0 gap" コメント箇所を Phase 1 で解消 (Call HelloWorld → Module1.HelloWorld
      が call_graph に乗ることを追加 assert)
- [ ] CI (build-rules verify workflow) で同 validator + pytest が green

body:
## Summary - add encrypted per-guild Discord bot token storage, metadata, and token resolution with global-token fallback - add admin-only token update/delete APIs with Discord validation and recovery auth using the global token when a stored override is broken - add settings UI/API helpers for token status, write-only update, and delete without redisplaying raw tokens ## Validation - rtk cargo fmt --all -- --check - rtk cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features - rtk cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features - rtk cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings - rtk pnpm install --frozen-lockfile - rtk pnpm run lint - rtk pnpm exec tsc --noEmit - rtk pnpm run build - rtk git diff --check ## Review - Harness reviewer approved after recovery-path fix.

Greptile Summary

 This PR adds encrypted per-guild Discord bot token storage (AES-256-GCM + HKDF), admin-only token set/update/delete APIs with pre-persistence Discord validation, and a settings UI with write-only token input and status metadata. It also wires a `tokio::sync::watch` channel so a token update gracefully drains and restarts the Serenity gateway client to pick up the new effective token. - **Backend**: new `BotTokenCipher` (HKDF key derivation, AES-GCM encrypt/decrypt with guild ID as AAD), `GET_GUILD_BOT_TOKEN_SQL` with `AND`-guarded `WHERE` clause aligned to the `discord_bot_token_registered` computation, settings-recovery-aware admin checks limited to an explicit three-route allowlist, and a `BotTokenCache` that coalesces concurrent DB resolves with a 5-second failure TTL. - **Startup**: The main loop resolves the effective token per iteration; crypto/cipher failures fall back to the global token (keeping the web server up for recovery) while DB errors are still fatal. - **Frontend**: `SettingsPage` shows token registration status, metadata (username, validated-at, updated-at), a write-only password input, and a two-click delete confirmation; raw token values are never re-displayed.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. All three recovery paths (startup fallback, settings admin recovery, gateway restart) are correctly scoped and tested. The implementation is thorough: HKDF key derivation is purpose-bound, AES-GCM uses OsRng nonces with guild ID as AAD, the SQL WHERE clause and the discord_bot_token_registered flag both use AND semantics, the recovery admin check is limited to an explicit three-route allowlist, and BotAccessDenied propagates as Err(BAD_GATEWAY) through into_status_result in the non-settings path. The bot token cache correctly coalesces concurrent refreshes and is invalidated before the watch channel is notified. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/infrastructure/bot_token.rs | New file: BotTokenCipher (HKDF + AES-256-GCM), EncryptedBotToken, StoredGuildBotToken, and resolve helpers; guild ID as AAD; OsRng nonces; comprehensive unit tests. | | src/interfaces/web.rs | Adds BotTokenCache with coalesced refresh, GuildAdminCheck enum with BotAccessDenied mapping to Err(BAD_GATEWAY), settings-recovery-aware checks on explicit route allowlist, PUT/DELETE bot-token endpoints, and cache invalidation + watch notification. | | src/main.rs | Wraps run_bot in a restart loop; crypto/cipher errors fall back to global token; watch::Receiver signals gateway restart on token change. | | migrations/0013_guild_bot_tokens.sql | Adds seven nullable columns via IF NOT EXISTS; fully backward-compatible. | | src/infrastructure/sql.rs | GET_GUILD_BOT_TOKEN_SQL uses AND across all three token columns matching the registered flag; UPSERT and CLEAR SQLs added. | | src/application/runtime.rs | run_bot gains watch::Receiver arm; returns BotRunExit::TokenChanged to trigger gateway restart. | | web/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx | Discord Bot section with status badge, metadata, write-only password input, and two-click delete confirmation; raw token never populated from API. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Admin as Guild Admin participant UI as SettingsPage participant API as Web API participant Discord as Discord API participant DB as PostgreSQL participant Cache as BotTokenCache participant Gateway as Serenity Gateway Admin->>UI: Enter bot token, click Update UI->>API: PUT /api/guild/settings/bot-token API->>API: check_guild_admin_permission_for_settings API->>Discord: "GET /users/@me (validate token)" Discord-->>API: bot user info API->>Discord: "GET /guilds/{id} (verify access)" Discord-->>API: guild info API->>API: BotTokenCipher.encrypt_for_guild (HKDF + AES-256-GCM) API->>DB: "UPSERT guild_settings bot_token_*" API->>Cache: invalidate (clear + bump revision) API->>Gateway: advance_bot_token_revision (watch::Sender) Gateway->>Gateway: drain voice, shutdown shards Gateway->>DB: resolve_effective_bot_token DB-->>Gateway: decrypted new token Gateway->>Discord: reconnect with new token API-->>UI: GuildSettingsResponse (status + metadata, no raw token) ```

Comments Outside Diff (3)

 1. `src/interfaces/web.rs`, line 1002-1011 ([link](https://github.com/xpadev-net/discord-transcript/blob/d6b38e29db4732b30360024fc22ed1202b161a7d/src/interfaces/web.rs#L1002-L1011)) **Recovery retry fires for every non-admin settings access** `should_retry_settings_admin_check_with_global` returns `true` when the guild-token check returns `Ok(false)`, which covers both the intended recovery case (token revoked → Discord returns 401/403 which is mapped to `Ok(false)`) and the normal case (user genuinely not an admin). In the normal case this causes `check_guild_admin_permission_for_settings` to make a full second round of Discord API calls (guild info + member lookup) with the global token on every settings page visit for non-admin users — the cache is also bypassed for the global-token leg (`use_cache: false`). A tighter gate such as checking whether the HTTP status returned by the inner calls was 401/403/404 (indicating the token lacked access) versus a clean non-admin answer would avoid the extra requests for the common case.
Prompt To Fix With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: src/interfaces/web.rs Line: 1002-1011 Comment: **Recovery retry fires for every non-admin settings access** `should_retry_settings_admin_check_with_global` returns `true` when the guild-token check returns `Ok(false)`, which covers both the intended recovery case (token revoked → Discord returns 401/403 which is mapped to `Ok(false)`) and the normal case (user genuinely not an admin). In the normal case this causes `check_guild_admin_permission_for_settings` to make a full second round of Discord API calls (guild info + member lookup) with the global token on every settings page visit for non-admin users — the cache is also bypassed for the global-token leg (`use_cache: false`). A tighter gate such as checking whether the HTTP status returned by the inner calls was 401/403/404 (indicating the token lacked access) versus a clean non-admin answer would avoid the extra requests for the common case. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````

author: criteriaenv
body:
## Resumen

Añade un módulo Python independiente (`hidrogeologia/`) para **visualizar análisis de tránsito de contaminantes en hidrogeología** sobre un sistema acuífero multicapa. El módulo es autónomo y no tiene relación con el modelo de teledetección TESSERA del resto del repositorio; comparte únicamente el contenedor del proyecto.

## Funcionalidad

- **Capas configurables**: número de capas con nombre, espesor y permeabilidad (`K`), más datos opcionales por capa (porosidad eficaz, dispersividad, densidad seca, `K_d`).
- **Propiedades equivalentes** del sistema estratificado: transmisividad total, `K` horizontal/vertical equivalente y anisotropía (Freeze & Cherry, 1979).
- **Transporte advectivo-dispersivo** (Ogata & Banks, 1961): perfiles `C(x)`, curvas de llegada `C(t)` y penacho 2D en planta (Domenico, 1987).
- **Desplazamiento lateral opcional** del contaminante por capa cuando se aporta el gradiente hidráulico: `L(t) = (K·i/n_e)·t / R`.
- **Tres salidas**, todas con referencias bibliográficas y capítulo hidrogeológico:
  - HTML interactivo y autónomo (edición de capas en vivo, recálculo en JavaScript sin librerías externas)
  - Informe PDF multipágina (matplotlib)
  - Artefacto JSON de resultados

## Uso

```bash
pip install -r hidrogeologia/requirements.txt
python -m hidrogeologia                                              # caso de ejemplo (TCE)
python -m hidrogeologia hidrogeologia/examples/ejemplo_acuifero.json -o salidas
```

## Verificación

- 9/9 pruebas unitarias del núcleo científico (`hidrogeologia/tests/test_core.py`).
- PDF de 10 páginas renderizado y revisado visualmente.
- La aproximación de `erf` en JavaScript coincide con SciPy con error < 2·10⁻⁷.
- Salidas de ejemplo incluidas en `hidrogeologia/ejemplo_salidas/`.

## Fundamento científico

Darcy (1856), Ogata & Banks (1961), Bear (1972), Freeze & Cherry (1979), Domenico & Robbins (1985), Domenico (1987), Gelhar et al. (1992), Xu & Eckstein (1995), Fetter (2001), Zheng & Bennett (2002), US EPA (1989).

> ⚠️ Modelo analítico de cribado preliminar. No sustituye a una modelización numérica (MODFLOW/MT3D) ni a la caracterización de campo.

body:
## 무엇을 / 왜

다음 작업 큐(HANDOFF)의 **작업 2 — 스펙 030(체결 정교화 P2: 주문 수명 관리)**. 운영자가 2026-05-31 "작업 1·2·3 전부 순서대로" 승인.

스펙 028(체결 품질 측정)이 드러낸 비효율을 줄이는 세 가지 **옵트인** 정교화. `TradingRule.lifecycle` 가 `None`(기본)이면 모든 경로가 byte 동일 — 기존 룰은 영향 0.

1. **미체결 TTL 취소(G1)** — `ttl_seconds` 초과한 미체결 자동 취소.
2. **취소-재호가(G2)** — 지정가가 현재 중간가에서 `requote_drift_pct` 이상 벌어지면 취소 후 **게이트 체인을 다시 통과**시켜 재제출.
3. **marketable-limit(G3)** — 제출 시 시장가 가까운 공격적 지정가(매수=ask 위/매도=bid 아래)로 빠른 체결 + 슬리피지 상한.

## 변경 파일

- `specs/030-order-lifecycle/spec.md`(신규) — 스펙 문서(FR-030-01~07, SC-030-01~08).
- `src/auto_invest/execution/lifecycle.py`(신규, 비커널) — 순수 로직(`marketable_limit_price`·`is_ttl_expired`·`price_drift_pct`·`should_requote`·`plan_order_lifecycle`) + DB 리더.
- `src/auto_invest/config/rules.py`(비커널) — `OrderLifecycleConfig` + `TradingRule.lifecycle`.
- `src/auto_invest/execution/order_router.py`(비커널) — marketable-limit 제출 가격(호가 없으면 표현식 폴백).
- `src/auto_invest/worker/loop.py`(비커널) — cadence(`_LIFECYCLE_GAP_SECONDS=10s`)로 수명 관리 배선.
- `src/auto_invest/persistence/audit.py`(**K4 추가-전용**) — `ORDER_TTL_CANCELLED`, `ORDER_REQUOTED`.

## 안전 경계

- **Kernel 터치 0건** — `worker/schedule.py`·`risk/gates.py`·`config/caps.py` 무변경.
- 재호가도 **K1 캡 게이트 체인을 다시 통과** → 노출 상한 무변경(재호가가 안전 경계 위로 못 올림).
- 취소는 **브로커 확인 우선** — `cancel_order` 성공 뒤에만 로컬 CANCELLED 전이. 실패(이미 체결/종료)는 스펙 015 체결 동기화가 정합화. 부분 체결분은 `fills` 에 별도 기록.
- 부분 체결 주문은 재호가 제외(잔량 재계산 필요 — TTL 취소에만 맡김).
- 모든 예외 격리(거래 무중단). paper·lifecycle 미설정이면 미동작. 측정 단일 잣대(헌법 X.2).

## 검증

- 신규 테스트 31건(순수 23 + 워커/라우터 통합 8, SC-030-01~08), 전체 **1331 통과, 4 스킵**(라이브 KIS smoke 게이트), 린트 깨끗.

author: alireza29675
body:
Closes #359.

## What

`teamctl --version` now bakes a `git describe` build version so dev/local builds self-identify, while tagged releases and no-git builds stay clean.

- **Dev/local build** → `0.8.6-55-ge4adf50` (last tag + commits-since + short hash), `-dirty` appended when the tree has uncommitted changes.
- **Tagged release** (HEAD on a clean tag) → plain version (`0.8.7`).
- **No git** (extracted tarball / crates.io / no `.git`) → falls back to `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. The build never fails when git is absent.

## How

- **New `crates/teamctl/build.rs`** runs `git describe --tags --always --dirty`, strips the leading `v` (tags are `v`-prefixed, `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` is not — so dev/release formats match), and emits `cargo:rustc-env=TEAMCTL_BUILD_VERSION=…`. Rerun hints (`.git/HEAD` + `refs`, resolved via `git rev-parse --git-path` so they're correct in linked worktrees) keep the value fresh across commits.
- **`main.rs:41`** — the one-line clap change: `version,` → `version = env!("TEAMCTL_BUILD_VERSION")`. The existing `{version}` in the help template renders it; no other version path changes.

## One spec nuance, resolved

The issue specifies `--always`, but `--always` makes a *tag-less* repo emit a bare commit hash instead of failing — which contradicts the issue's stated "no tags → fall back to `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`" intent and would surface an ugly `teamctl 5aba5f3` in shallow CI checkouts. I honor both: use `--always` as specified, then route the bare-hash case (detected by the absence of a `.` — a real version-describe always carries the semver tag's dots) to the fallback. Net: the version is always a clean dotted semver, never a bare hash.

## Deliberately not touched

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/safevitals-xr-demo/agent-runs/6a1c28b68e0db2894626ed7f

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 ()
ezgif-frame-093.png:1  Failed to load resource: net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR
ezgif-frame-033.png:1  Failed to load resource: net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR
ezgif-frame-081.png:1  F...

✅ **Result:** The browser was reporting `ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR` for dozens of `ezgif-frame-*.png` image files. Both scroll-animation components — `hero-sequence.tsx` (100 frames) and `bridge-scroll-fullscreen.tsx` (25 frames) — were preloading every image frame simultaneously by firing all `new Image()` requests in a tight `for` loop. Sending 100 concurrent HTTP/2 stream requests at once saturates the connection's stream limit, causing the server to reset streams mid-flight with a protocol error.

Both components were refactored to load images in sequential batches of 8 concurrent requests at a time. Each batch fully resolves before the next starts, keeping concurrent stream usage well within HTTP/2 limits while still completing the full preload before scroll-animation begins. Error handling (`onerror`) was also added so a single failed image no longer silently stalls the entire preload sequence. A cleanup cancellation flag was added to both effects so that if the component unmounts mid-load (e.g., fast navigation), the async loop stops and no stale state is set.

author: roitsch-code
body:
Three issues from the Orea Apex brew (screenshots): a swirl icon on a recipe that explicitly wanted no agitation, the chat reporting the **wrong grind** for what was actually brewed, and no recipe name attached to the brew.

## 1. The no-go: chat reported the wrong grind (398° vs the 405° brewed)
`buildRecentRecipes` read `recommendation.primaryRecipe` instead of the candidate the user actually selected (`selectedCandidateIdx`) — so brewing a non-primary candidate made the chat confidently state the *primary's* numbers. Same bug class as #193, one layer up. `offlineLibrary.usedRecipe` (method-name match) and `brewSignature`/`buildTimingStats` had the same shortcut.

**Fix:** one shared `resolveBrewedRecipe(session)` (`src/lib/utils/resolveRecipe.ts`) reads the selected candidate everywhere — chat history, timing stats, offline cache, brew-signature, brew detail — so the bug can't reappear per call. The chat now quotes the numbers actually brewed.

## 2. Swirl icon on a reduced-agitation recipe
`LivePourSequence` hardcoded the swirl/stir button onto every bloom/final pour and the drawdown card, and `pourStepsFromStructured` discarded swirl/stir steps entirely.

**Fix:** agitation is recipe-driven. Each pour milestone carries an explicit `agitation` derived from adjacent swirl/stir steps (`null` = none); the renderer shows the button only where set. Legacy grams strings keep a bloom-only default — **no more stray final/drawdown swirl**. A title/notes guard suppresses agitation outright for minimal/reduced-agitation recipes. The recommend model now emits agitation as explicit `pourSteps` steps (none for minimal recipes), so the data is authoritative.

## 3. Recipe name attached + visible + known to the chat
The candidate `title` was never surfaced. Now the recipe name shows on the brew screen, the brew detail page, and the recommend screen; it's in the chat's recent-recipes context plus a **"Most Recent Brew"** block so *"what did I just brew?"* is answerable with the right name and numbers. New `basedOn` field (per the user's choice of a stable reference name) — each candidate names the documented recipe it adapts (e.g. "Kasuya 4:6") or "Own recipe".

## Commits
- **Commit 1 `fix(brew)`** — deterministic: shared resolver + all consumers, recipe-driven agitation, name display. Fully tested here (29/29 pour-math + resolver tests, `tsc` clean).
- **Commit 2 `feat(recommend)`** — AI-behavioral: explicit agitation steps + `basedOn`. ⚠️ **Hard Rule:** prompt/output change; before/after model sampling couldn't run in the work env. **Validate on the PWA:** reduced-agitation recipe shows no swirl (incl. drawdown card); brew a non-primary candidate then ask the chat its grind → must match the brew screen; ask the chat the recipe name → title + "based on …".

author: proggeramlug
body:
## Summary

Closes the largest behavioral cluster in #3662: built-in **collection prototype methods now perform the spec `this` brand check** and throw a `TypeError` on an incompatible receiver.

`Set`/`Map`/`WeakSet`/`WeakMap` prototype methods reached as plain values — `Set.prototype.add.call(x, v)`, `Reflect.apply(Map.prototype.get, m, [k])`, method extraction, etc. — resolved to a shared no-op thunk (`global_this_builtin_noop_thunk`). The reflective path therefore did nothing and never brand-checked `this`, so an incompatible receiver produced **no exception** (the #3662 "no exception was thrown at all" cluster).

## What changed

`populate_builtin_prototype_methods` now installs real per-method thunks for the four collection prototypes. Each thunk:

1. reads the `IMPLICIT_THIS` receiver (set by the `.call`/`.apply`/`.bind` dispatch),
2. brand-checks it — a registered `Set`/`Map` heap pointer, or the reserved `CLASS_ID_WEAKMAP`/`CLASS_ID_WEAKSET` `class_id` — and throws a `TypeError` on a mismatched or primitive receiver, and
3. otherwise dispatches to the existing runtime helper (`js_set_add`, `js_map_get`, `js_weakmap_set`, …) — so reflective collection calls now also **work** on a correct receiver (previously they silently returned `undefined`).

New receiver-resolution helpers: `set::set_ptr_from_receiver_bits`, `map::map_ptr_from_receiver_bits`, `weakref::weak_class_id_from_receiver` (the last pre-filters on `GcHeader.obj_type == GC_TYPE_OBJECT` before reading `class_id`, so a `Set`/`Map` pointer or primitive resolves to `None` without an out-of-bounds read).

## Why it's safe

The fast direct-call path (`s.add(v)`) is lowered straight to `js_set_add` by codegen and **never touches these thunks**, so it is unaffected. A wrong `this` is only reachable via the reflective path, which previously no-op'd — so this is strictly additive.

## Verification

- `test-files/test_gap_3662_collection_brand_check.ts` (new) — **byte-identical to Node** in both `PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE` and auto-optimize build paths. Covers wrong/primitive receivers (TypeError), cross-brand receivers (Set↔Map, WeakMap↔WeakSet), working reflective dispatch on correct receivers, and the unchanged direct-call path.
- 14/14 existing collection/iterator gap tests byte-identical.
- `cargo test -p perry-runtime` → 930 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

## Scope / follow-up

This PR covers the collection brand-check sub-cluster. The rest of #3662 remains open: `Function.prototype` apply/bind/`Symbol.hasInstance` not-callable checks, and the node-core `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`/`ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` arg-validation cases across fs/buffer/process/zlib/ArrayBuffer.

author: schrockn
body:
This PR introduces a new ASDL objective, `structured-grill-ui-deepening`, which defines the scope, completion criteria, and roadmap for refining the structured grill question UI stack without altering its core `grill-me` behavior.

The objective targets five specific architectural candidates identified in a prior stack review:

1. Centralizing the structured grill contract (currently duplicated across skill prose, tool prompt guidelines, schema descriptions, validation errors, and result text) into a single authoritative module.
2. Making the question presentation seam explicit by treating inline custom UI and legacy `select`/`editor` paths as sibling adapters behind a shared interface.
3. Deepening the Pi runtime adapter to localize Pi/TUI drift rather than spreading it across grill UI code.
4. Moving only genuinely generic terminal escape, width, wrapping, and truncation behavior into the shared terminal presentation layer, leaving grill-specific layout in place.
5. Auditing and reducing test-only helper exports so production modules expose smaller effective interfaces and tests target user-visible behavior rather than internal implementation details.

The roadmap tracks each candidate as a discrete work item with a validation step (`bun run --cwd ts check` and `bun run --cwd ts test`) and requires an explicit human sign-off before closure. Every candidate must reach a recorded disposition—implemented, rejected with reason, parked with rationale, or split into a follow-on objective—before the objective can close.

author: olafkfreund
body:
## What happened

PR #687 added `--refresh` + a regression guard. Empirical proof that wasn't enough: yesterday's `nhs p620 all` (PR #688) **still regressed nixpkgs through the script**. Both `original.ref` ("nixos-unstable" → "nixos-25.05") AND `locked.rev` (`64c08a7c` → `59e69648`) got rewritten, and the regression guard either never fired or only restored `.locked` (it doesn't cover `.original`).

## The actual fix

Stop trusting `nix flake update` for the nixpkgs family entirely. New flow:

1. Bulk `nix flake update` (fine for the 25 other inputs)
2. **Force-splice** `nixpkgs` and `nixpkgs-unstable` with ground truth fetched via `gh api`:
   - `gh api repos/NixOS/nixpkgs/branches/nixos-unstable --jq .commit.sha` → real SHA
   - `nix flake metadata "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/<explicit-sha>" --refresh --json` → fresh narHash + lastModified (explicit-SHA URL always works because it bypasses every cache layer)
   - `jq` rewrites both nodes' `.locked` and `.original` to ground truth

Idempotent. Doesn't trust any nix cache. Doesn't depend on `--refresh` honoring its name.

## Lock hotfix

flake.lock on main was at the bad state after PR #688 auto-merged. This PR also re-fixes the lock to ground truth via the same splice.

## Verification

- `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.{razer,p620,p510}.config.system.build.toplevel` — all exit 0
- Lock matches GitHub HEAD ✓
- Script syntax valid ✓

## Test plan

- [ ] After merge, run `nhs` on p620 — splice should run, lock should stay correct
- [ ] Read the journal to confirm the splice log line fired
- [ ] `git diff` should NEVER show nixpkgs going backwards in any future PR from the script

body:
## Why

On `/clusters` and the **Cluster Topology** overview tab, the physical/implicit clusters (`all-replicated`, `all-sharded`, `default`) were:
- **unlabelled** (you couldn't tell which dotted box was which),
- drawn as **uniformly gray dotted** concentric rings, and
- their **deeply-nested rings climbed into the Keeper region**, overlapping keeper nodes and their FQDN labels.

Reported via screenshot: keeper text/nodes overlapped the cluster boxes, and the dotted boxes had no names.

## What changed

**Physical clusters**
- **Hidden by default** behind a legend eye-toggle (`Implicit (N)` / `Hide implicit`). They're structural scaffolding that clutters the graph.
- When shown, rendered **solid (not dotted)** in their own color, like every other cluster, with a **solid label pill** (no more dotted borders).

**Colors — Claude style**
- Every cluster (logical + physical) gets a distinct **warm, editorial palette** color led by the Claude clay/coral, hues alternated warm↔cool so adjacent nested rings stay legible. No more flat gray.

**Keeper never overlaps a cluster box**
- `buildClusterHulls` clamps each cluster rect's **top edge** to `max(keeperBottom) + KEEPER_CLUSTER_GAP`, guarded so it only trims the decorative outset band — never a node's own box. A keeper (a non-member) always sits **outside** the CH cluster boxes, at any nesting depth.

**Data-driven viewBox height**
- New `model.vbHeight` computed in `fitContent`: grows to fit the keeper region + deepest ring nesting + bottom pills for *this* model, floored at `VB_H` (now a minimum). Simple graphs stay compact (big glyphs); dense ones grow taller and letterbox. The canvas reads `model.vbHeight`.

**Cleaner intersections**
- A **card-colored casing** under each colored boundary so crossing/nested borders read cleanly instead of tangling.
- `NEST_STEP` 20 → 30 so adjacent concentric rings never overlap.
- `boundaryReserve` now counts all hull-producing clusters (outline included).

## Tests
- `bun test apps/web/components/cluster-topology/__tests__/` → **39 pass** (+3: data-driven height floor/growth/determinism, keeper-separation, physical toggle drops hulls + shrinks height + keeps node x).
- `bun run type-check` ✅, biome ✅.

## Verification
Eyeballed every state with `scripts/topo-harness.tsx` (real `<TopoCanvas>` + true OKLCH theme), incl. the reported screenshot scenario in **both** toggle states and the overlap-lens case. Harness frame now matches the production fixed-height container.

body:
## O que foi feito

Refatoração completa aplicando princípios SOLID, Design Patterns e base para
arquitetura de microsserviços — realizada com Claude Code no terminal.

## Princípios SOLID aplicados

### S — Single Responsibility Principle
Cada módulo agora tem uma única responsabilidade:

| Módulo criado | Responsabilidade |
|---|---|
| `src/api/security.py` | JWT, API Key e Rate Limiting |
| `src/api/metrics.py` | Métricas Prometheus |
| `src/api/model_loader.py` | Carregamento e gerenciamento do modelo |
| `src/api/prediction_service.py` | Lógica de predição |
| `src/data/transformers.py` | Transformers de dados |
| `src/models/evaluation.py` | Cálculo de métricas de avaliação |

### O — Open/Closed Principle
- `ModelRepository` interface permite trocar a implementação de carregamento
  sem modificar o código cliente
- `LocalModelRepository` é a implementação concreta

### D — Dependency Inversion Principle
- `PredictionService` depende da abstração `ModelRepository`
  não da implementação concreta

## Design Patterns implementados

- **Repository Pattern** — `ModelRepository` / `LocalModelRepository`
- **Service Layer Pattern** — `PredictionService` encapsula a lógica de negócio
- **Dependency Injection** — via FastAPI `Depends()`

## Base para Microsserviços

A separação de módulos facilita a extração futura em serviços independentes:
- `security.py` → Serviço de Autenticação
- `prediction_service.py` + `model_loader.py` → Serviço de Predição
- `metrics.py` → Serviço de Monitoramento

## Resultados

- 43/43 testes passando
- Cobertura: 69% → 70%
- `src/api/app.py`: 84% → 86%
- `src/api/metrics.py`: 100%
- `src/api/security.py`: 91%

author: jasonnoble
body:
## JAS-39 — Implement background worker: stock reservation

Fills in the `StockReservationJob#perform` placeholder created by JAS-35. **Stacked on `jas-35-implement-work-order-creation`** (base) — parallels JAS-36, which also branches off jas-35. This story touches **only the job and its spec** — no routes, controllers, or OpenAPI changes (`git diff doc/openapi.yaml` is empty).

### What it does
For each `PENDING` work order step:
- Resolves the required part as `step.bom_item.child`.
- Row-locks the stock row (`Stock.lock.find_or_create_by!`) inside a transaction.
- `available = quantity_on_hand - quantity_reserved`.
- `available >= 1` → increment `quantity_reserved`, write a `StockAuditLog` (`change_amount: -1`, reservation reduces availability), step stays `PENDING`.
- `available < 1` (or no stock row) → AASM `block` the step → `BLOCKED`.
- If any step ends up blocked, `block` the work order → `BLOCKED`.

### Reservation qty rule
**1 unit per step**, per the track-06 planning doc (`available >= 1: increment quantity_reserved`) and the JAS-39 acceptance criteria. (Not the full BOM-line `quantity`.)

### Idempotency guard
Each successful reservation writes a `StockAuditLog` whose `reason` embeds the step id (`"Reserved for work order step #{step.id}"`). Before reserving, a step whose reservation log already exists is skipped; already-`BLOCKED` (non-`PENDING`) steps are skipped too. Re-running the job never double-reserves. Atomicity comes from `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the stocks row (mirrors the JAS-31 PO-receive stock pattern).

### Tests
`spec/jobs/stock_reservation_job_spec.rb` (real PostgreSQL, no mocking): in-stock reserve, out-of-stock → step + WO BLOCKED, missing stock row, run-twice (no double-reserve), and partial availability (one line reserved, one blocked). 11 examples, all green.

### CI note
`bin/ci` is green except a **pre-existing flaky check on the base branch** — the "OpenAPI doc is committed and current" step drifts a non-deterministic factory value (`partName: Part 43` vs `Part 91`) in an unrelated PO endpoint example. Reproduced on a clean `jas-35` checkout with my changes stashed, so it is not introduced here. rubocop, brakeman, bundler-audit, and rspec (109 examples) all pass.

body:
## Summary

`handle_get_blob` served CAS-hit and virtual-local blobs by reading the whole object into heap (`storage.get(&key)` → `Body::from(data)`), so pulling a multi-GiB layer from object storage loaded the entire layer into the backend's memory.

This streams the blob straight from the backend instead: `storage.get_stream(&key)` → `Body::from_stream(...)`, with `Content-Length` sourced from the authoritative `oci_blobs.size_bytes` column (rather than `data.len()`). Memory is now bounded per chunk. Both the migrated-CAS-hit branch and the virtual-repo local-member branch are converted.

Cloud backends already override `get_stream` for true streaming; the trait default falls back to `get`, so no backend regresses. The upstream-proxy fetch branches are left as-is. The OCI **push** path is handled separately (#1448).

Closes #1528.

## Regression test (required for `fix/*` PRs)
- [x] This PR is a `fix/*` AND adds/updates a test that would have caught the bug
  - `get_blob_streams_from_backend_with_size_bytes_content_length`: stores a blob + `oci_blobs` row, GETs it, and asserts 200, a `Content-Length` taken from `size_bytes`, and a body that round-trips through the streaming path.

author: muhammadidhammaarif
body:
## Summary

Phase 5 backend half. Adds the inline-reply landing endpoint the Chromium service worker will POST to when a user types in a notification's text input.

`POST /notifications/:id/quick-reply` with body `{ text: string }`. Returns `{ ok, messageId, channelId, projectId, link }` so the SW can either dismiss the notification cleanly or open the thread on the result link.

## Flow

1. Load the notification scoped to the caller (404 if not theirs).
2. Reject non-`CHAT_MENTION` types (400). Task-comment quick-reply can be added in the same controller later without the SW caring about the routing.
3. Re-walk `ProjectAccessService.assertInsider` — a stale notification fired before the user was removed from the project must not let them write into that channel (403).
4. Re-use the exact `chat.controller.createMessage` pipeline: `messages.create` → `realtime.messageCreated` → `chatNotifications.onMessageCreated`. From any other observer's perspective the reply is indistinguishable from a regular chat POST.
5. Mark the source notification `readAt = now` so the user's bell badge drops immediately on their other tabs/devices.

## Where it lives

Controller is in `chat` module, not `notifications` module — chat already imports `NotificationsModule`, `ProjectsModule`, and `MediaModule`, so the handler has every collaborator without widening `NotificationsModule`'s exports. The route is mounted under `/notifications/...` regardless so the SW has a stable URL.

## Production safety

- Pure additive route — no schema changes, no env changes.
- Identical authorization gate as the regular chat-message POST.
- If the SW path isn't supported (Safari/Firefox), this endpoint simply never gets called — Phase 5 frontend adds a focus-input fallback that hits the existing chat-message POST instead.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Post-deploy: `POST /api/v1/notifications/<id>/quick-reply` with a session bearer + valid CHAT_MENTION notification id creates a chat message in the right channel
- [ ] Non-owner gets 404
- [ ] Stale notification after project removal gets 403
- [ ] Non-chat notification type gets 400
- [ ] Source notification's `readAt` is set after a successful reply

This pull request introduces a ranker module for improved document retrieval and ranking, adds support for Gemini embeddings as an alternative to local sentence-transformer models, and enhances configuration flexibility for embedding and ranking throughout the engine and ingestion pipeline. The changes also include updates to ingestion scripts and environment variable loading, and add initial tests for the new ranker functionality.

**Retrieval and Ranking Enhancements:**

* Introduced a new `engine.core.ranker` module with `BaseRanker`, `DummyRanker`, and `CrossEncoderRanker` classes, enabling high-accuracy document ranking using HuggingFace cross-encoders. Updated the engine to optionally use a ranker in the retrieval pipeline, with configurable top-k parameters and timing metrics. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-202e789f636c3d6ec093f88a09278690c32b6657b6b99b29ec8fba40a0eb3cdaR1-R50) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-132c0f370b73650e6db4a7f46910d94f8b68c37111f1938e978a7f6a4f47cb45R8) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-132c0f370b73650e6db4a7f46910d94f8b68c37111f1938e978a7f6a4f47cb45R23-R30) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-132c0f370b73650e6db4a7f46910d94f8b68c37111f1938e978a7f6a4f47cb45L62-R78) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-132c0f370b73650e6db4a7f46910d94f8b68c37111f1938e978a7f6a4f47cb45L89-R102) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-132c0f370b73650e6db4a7f46910d94f8b68c37111f1938e978a7f6a4f47cb45R167-R178) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-c8e20846483d93a4a465a433f21fa3123ca5adc5f9d2953c66bc68573b76a968R1-R19)

body:
This pull request removes all files, configuration, dependencies, and scripts related to Cypress end-to-end (E2E) testing from the frontend project. The changes clean up both the codebase and the `package.json` by eliminating E2E test support, fixtures, and related dependencies.

The most important changes are:

**Removal of Cypress E2E Testing Infrastructure:**

* Deleted the entire Cypress configuration file (`cypress.json`), effectively disabling Cypress E2E test runs.
* Removed the E2E test scripts, Cypress-related dependencies (`cypress`, `@vue/cli-plugin-e2e-cypress`), and related dev dependencies from `package.json`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-da6498268e99511d9ba0df3c13e439d10556a812881c9d03955b2ef7c6c1c655L12-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-da6498268e99511d9ba0df3c13e439d10556a812881c9d03955b2ef7c6c1c655L55-L65) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-da6498268e99511d9ba0df3c13e439d10556a812881c9d03955b2ef7c6c1c655L75-L77)
* Deleted all E2E test support files and plugins, including `tests/e2e/plugins/index.js`, `tests/e2e/support/commands.js`, and `tests/e2e/support/index.js`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b127f89da22bc0f7a0b00f4e5ac3b654510137fbc0ba27b2e13c94efa46d3b55L1-L25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e6123ca33b1f0bac12c35dcc33199e58c30826a0d9d8d9a4aca79078fab7ef56L1-L25) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f950b1b66cd2d1504c554cc074a208fb2ecf0af2c3f946351bbb65e74043af53L1-L25)
* Removed Cypress-specific ESLint configuration (`tests/e2e/.eslintrc.js`).

**Removal of E2E Test Data and Specs:**

* Deleted all E2E test fixtures and mock data used by Cypress, such as user and domain-specific JSON files in `tests/e2e/fixtures/`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-397d7251939883b760de2437dfd03b6b2cb7cc0935910309d6d8651558735847L1-L8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-00b82538a45e380baf12f51fd133764ef37583245784244505b45b8c202755e7L1-L5) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-807c7b8c3ce59c265e074ba8097c5cbdf7614db52fcbea4800c3e7907f967732L1-L323) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-77e6a60d9b59552e10ca3f2b466d5ed13065b08fe0b860b07da72fde07bcc912L1-L3) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-179fcccc633b124e842b0f37e2ad5a7cbbc7beab4130365b968d78320e4fe917L1-L59) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-28ac2c951c3bf2d4f18265e3b95720c57718e8a2e033fea0a5507f18cd395470L1-L112)
* Removed E2E test specification files, including example test specs like `tests/e2e/specs/etusivu.js`.

**Other Dependency Cleanup:**

* Removed additional dependencies and devDependencies that were only used for E2E or related build steps, such as `register-service-worker`, `@vue/cli-plugin-pwa`, `bootstrap`, `copy-webpack-plugin`, and `node-forge` from `package.json`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-da6498268e99511d9ba0df3c13e439d10556a812881c9d03955b2ef7c6c1c655L37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-da6498268e99511d9ba0df3c13e439d10556a812881c9d03955b2ef7c6c1c655L55-L65) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-da6498268e99511d9ba0df3c13e439d10556a812881c9d03955b2ef7c6c1c655L75-L77) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-da6498268e99511d9ba0df3c13e439d10556a812881c9d03955b2ef7c6c1c655L87)

These changes fully remove Cypress-based E2E testing from the project, reducing maintenance overhead and simplifying the frontend codebase.

author: ryceg
body:
## Problem

The `@nocturne/ui` design-system package's `check` (`svelte-check-native`) reported **14 errors**.

**13 of 14** were `Cannot find module` — the drawer, resizable, and sonner components import `vaul-svelte`, `paneforge`, and `svelte-sonner`, but those packages were never added to the package manifest when the design system was extracted from `@nocturne/app`. They only resolved transitively via the app, so the standalone check failed:

| Module | Components | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `vaul-svelte` | `drawer/*` | 9 |
| `paneforge` | `resizable/*` | 3 |
| `svelte-sonner` | `sonner/sonner.svelte` | 1 |

The **14th** was `calendar.svelte`: bits-ui's `Calendar.RootProps` is a discriminated union (single/multiple/range) that tsgo reports as *"too complex to represent."* The component works at runtime; the app's own check never saw it because `@nocturne/ui` resolves through `node_modules`, where `skipLibCheck` skips it.

## Changes

- Declare `vaul-svelte`, `paneforge`, and `svelte-sonner` as devDependencies (matching the versions pinned in `@nocturne/app`).
- Drop a duplicate `@internationalized/date` entry.
- `--ignore` `calendar.svelte` in the check script (cosmetic tsgo union-complexity limitation).

## Verification

`pnpm run check` on `@nocturne/ui` now reports **0 errors** (was 14). Lockfile change is purely additive.

author: dtzp555-max
body:
## Summary
Fixes the four error-output / process-lifecycle findings from the 2026-05-31 audit (#111, 3×P2 + 1×P3).

1. **`sanitizeError()` helper** — streaming error paths sent raw claude `error_message`/`stderr` (home-dir/credential paths) to clients while the non-streaming path redacted them. One helper now applied at all 9 client-facing `jsonResponse`/`sendSSE` error emits; 3 pre-existing inline `.replace()` sites de-duped. Operator logs + admin-gated endpoints left raw by design.
2. **`res.on("close")` SIGKILL escalation** — client disconnect sent only SIGTERM; a SIGTERM-resistant child held its slot until the request timeout (narrow #37 on the hottest exit path). Now escalates to SIGKILL 5s after SIGTERM, cleared on exit. Per review, gated on the child still being alive (`exitCode===null && signalCode===null`) so the normal-success close no longer fires a spurious SIGTERM or leaks the timer; `killTimer.unref()`.
3. **Quota TOCTOU** — documented as best-effort (inline + README): overshoot bounded by `MAX_CONCURRENT`, cache hits uncounted. Chose documentation over an in-flight counter to avoid a decrement-on-all-paths liability (the #37 class) on a low-blast-radius internal family limiter.
4. **[P3] `overallTimer` cleared on semantic completion** — new `clearOverallTimer()` (clears the timer ONLY — never touches the `cleaned` slot flag, so no slot leak) called in the streaming stop-success path; `cleanup()` on exit still clears + decrements.

## ALIGNMENT.md (server.mjs hard requirements)
1. **cli.js citation: N/A** — error-shaping/process-lifecycle/rate-limit-doc forward no Anthropic operation. Rule 2.
2. **CI blacklist:** no blacklisted tokens / port literals introduced; `alignment.yml` passes.
3. **Independent reviewer (Iron Rule 10):** fresh-context opus reviewer verified the two CRITICAL concerns clean — `clearOverallTimer` does not reintroduce the #37 slot-leak class (only clears timer, never sets `cleaned`; slot still decremented via the untouched `proc.once("exit", cleanup)`), and no SIGKILL double-kill hazard — plus full sanitizeError coverage, quota-doc honesty, ALIGNMENT N/A. Verdict **APPROVE WITH MINOR**; MINOR #1 (success-path kill-timer leak) folded in; MINOR #2 (pre-existing path-regex over-redaction of ratios/URLs) left out-of-scope. `npm test` → **152 passed, 0 failed**.

Closes #111.

author: dawntide
body:
## 배경

새 프로그램 만들기 화면의 "세션 규칙" 토글에서 **A/B 분할**과 **숫자 분할(count=2)** 은 동작이 완전히 동일했습니다. 코드 추적 결과 둘의 유일한 차이는 세션 키 라벨뿐이었습니다.

`makeSessionKeys` 기준:
- A/B 분할 → `["A", "B"]`
- 숫자 분할 count=2 → `["1", "2"]`

이 키는 단순 식별자/라벨로만 쓰이고(UI 표시, 정의 저장, 플랜 스케줄 매칭), 스케줄 순환·세션 선택·자동 진행 등 다운스트림 로직은 `"AB"`/`"NUMERIC"` 으로 분기하지 않습니다. 즉 A/B 분할은 라벨만 다른 중복 옵션이었습니다.

## 변경 사항

A/B 옵션을 제거하고 숫자 분할 방식으로 통합했습니다 (별도 A/B 라벨 지원 없음).

- `SessionRuleType`에서 `"AB"` 제거, `makeSessionKeys`의 AB 분기 제거
- 기본 draft rule을 `{ type: "NUMERIC", count: 2 }` 로 변경
- 생성 시트에서 A/B · 숫자 분할 세그먼트 토글 제거 → 세션 개수(1~7) 선택을 항상 노출
- `changeCreateRuleType` / `onChangeRuleType` 배선 및 미사용 import 정리

기존에 저장된 `A`/`B` 키 프로그램은 manual 정의의 키를 그대로 읽으므로 영향 없습니다.

## 검증

- `pnpm typecheck` ✓
- `pnpm lint` ✓
- `pnpm lint:design` ✓ (baseline 준수)

author: bartvandebiezen
body:
### Highlights

- **Slotted content is isolated from host CSS** across the text components — projected text no longer accidentally inherits host styles, keeping rendering predictable and accessible.
- **The progress bar and circle are more consistent** — they share a unified `value-display` API and aligned naming, so switching shapes is largely a one-name change: swap `nldd-progress-bar` for `nldd-progress-circle` and the attributes carry over.
- **A consistent corner-radius hierarchy** via one semantic surface token: banner, list, box and card share a single radius, and the menu aligns with the (sharp) overlay radius.

### Added

- **`nldd-segmented-control`**: an `icon-and-text` variant — items render an icon and label together (like the toggle button); the visible text carries the accessible name.
- **`nldd-toggle-button`**: shows an `icon-placeholder` when an icon variant has no icon (and for `icon-and-text` only when there is no text to fall back on).
- **`nldd-card`**: an inner highlight border that paints over the content (including full-width media), white-with-opacity and light/dark aware.
- **`nldd-banner`**: an `accent` variant with its own default icon and color.
- **`nldd-progress-circle`**: a 1px token-colored highlight border with per-size stroke widths.
- **Tokens**: `--semantics-surfaces-corner-radius` (a unified surface radius) and a medium body font-weight variant.

### Changed

- **BREAKING — `nldd-progress` / `nldd-progress-circle`**: unified `value-display` (`inline` / `tooltip` / `none`), added `value-text` to the circle, and aligned naming across the bar and circle (e.g. `header`→`caption`, `value`→`supporting-text`, `fill`→`background`, `hover-area`→`tooltip-area`).
- **BREAKING — Icons**: `login`/`logout` replaced by `arrow-right-in-bucket` / `arrow-right-out-bucket` (the glyph changed; `login`/`logout`/`exit` remain as aliases).
- **Corner radius**: banner, list, box and card now share one surface tier, and the menu container follows the (sharp) overlay radius. The medium body font-weight is adopted where appropriate.

### Fixed

- **`nldd-code-editor`**: a 16px font on touch devices prevents the iOS focus-zoom (without disabling pinch-zoom).
- **`nldd-form-field`**: a tighter gap for the top-aligned header; the label stays readable over the focus ring.

author: noeljackson
body:
## Summary
Closes #19. Multi-vendor news pipeline with a pluggable LLM sentiment scorer. Future news sources (RSS, Twitter, paid feeds) plug into the same path.

## Pipeline
- Both vendors poll per-ticker
- Articles dedupe by URL (or symbol+title+published_at fallback)
- Massive articles use upstream sentiment (\`insights[].sentiment\`)
- FMP articles get LLM-scored via \`prompts/score-sentiment.md\`
- All LLM scoring is audited in \`llm_invocation\`

## What's wired
- \`db/migrations/0014_news_article.sql\` — news_article table + dedup indexes
- \`prompts/score-sentiment.md\` — first-class prompt with calibration rules (e.g. "clickbait headlines = neutral", "bullish article about a competitor = negative for us")
- \`src/sentiment/\` — reusable classifier module (5 unit tests)
- \`src/ingest/fmp_news.rs\` — FMP \`/stable/news/stock\` adapter
- \`src/ingest/massive_news.rs\` — Massive \`/v2/reference/news\` adapter (flattens insights, carries upstream sentiment)
- \`src/ingest/news_service.rs\` — service loop with idempotent upsert + LLM scoring of unscored rows
- \`src/bin/ingest.rs\` — spawns news service on 2h interval

## Test plan
- [x] 11 new unit tests (5 sentiment, 3 fmp_news, 3 massive_news); 166 total pass
- [x] Live: ingested 148 FMP articles + 137 Massive articles across universe in one pass
- [x] Live: Massive's upstream sentiment populated for all 137 (97 positive / 27 neutral / 13 negative)
- [x] Live: LLM scorer started processing FMP queue; correctly tagged a bullish AI article as \`positive\` and a "Should You Buy" clickbait as \`neutral\` (per prompt calibration)

author: jedi12many
body:
## Why

You spotted the gap: there's no persistent listener, so a chat request to probe has nowhere to land. This ships the listener **and** the Summon feature it enables — the operator-initiated counterpart to the scheduled run. *"Someone just pinged me about prod"* → send the agent to look, instead of SSH-ing in.

It also surfaced something bigger: steadystate has **two runtime shapes** — the ephemeral scan (cron/CI, what we shipped) and the long-lived listener (chat). Chat approvals already needed the second one; we only shipped the first. This closes that.

## What

**`@steadystate probe <target>`** — resolve a named target → run a scan → post what's wrong back to the thread. Across all three providers (Teams `@steadystate probe`, Slack/Discord `/steadystate probe`).

- **`engine.build_report()`** — factored the scan orchestration out of the CLI into one reusable, side-effect-free path. The `scan` command and the chat probe now run the **same engine** — one reasoning path, not two. (Net `cli.py` −107/+… as the inline orchestration + four now-dead `_*` builders collapse into the engine.)
- **`targets.py`** — a named-target registry (`STEADYSTATE_TARGETS` → name → `source + path + label`). Adding a target is a file edit, no redeploy.
- **`probe` verb** — one entry in the shared `Command` grammar, so `help` lists it automatically; Discord gets a `probe` subcommand. `run_command` runs the engine **read-only** (observe, stateless): it reports drift + health, never records or applies — *chat stays a trigger, not a bypass*. An engine failure is reported, never crashes the listener.
- **`deploy/kubernetes/listener.yaml`** — the persistent listener (Deployment + Service + Ingress + targets ConfigMap), the long-lived counterpart to the CronJob, reusing the read-only ServiceAccount.

## What the operator sees

```
@steadystate probe prod-argo
  prod-argo: 3 alert(s)
    HIGH     payments is failing -- likely root cause: drift
    HIGH     web is Degraded
    MEDIUM   modified Deployment apps/Deployment/prod/cache
```

## Read-only by design

Unlike `approve` (which runs `terraform apply`), `probe` mutates nothing — so it carries no new guardrail surface. The internet-facing listener runs a scan and reports; "chat is a trigger, never a bypass" holds trivially.

## Known limit (documented)

A slow scan (terraform plan) can exceed a chat provider's ~3s interaction timeout. Fast/health targets (k8s, argocd, docker) are the sweet spot; **async deferral** (ack now, post when ready) is the next step — noted in ARCHITECTURE roadmap.

## Gates

`ruff` · `ruff format` · `mypy` (only the known local `llm.py` noise) · `bandit` · `pytest` **586 passed** (+19) · coverage **92.2%**.
