author: skynavga
body:
Sub-PR in the post-12.N stack (close remaining wave-1 ZPFs). Target: PAMILYA/sent-16 `Kung minsa'y kapisan din ang wala pang asawang kapatid ng ama o ina.` ("Sometimes the unmarried sibling of the father or mother also comes together.")

**The full sent-16 does NOT close in this PR** — it remains `parse-timeout` due to chart density on the combined `Kung minsa'y` + `din` + wala-pa modifier + GEN-OR-coord. But the underlying structural mechanism (existential clause as pre/post-N modifier with proper Wackernagel-domain handling for `pa`) is in place. Five core sub-cases close, including `Kapisan din ang wala pang asawang kapatid.` (matrix `din` + embedded `pa`) and `Kapisan din ang walang asawang kapatid ng ama o ina.` (was failing before this PR).

## Three commits in this sub-PR

1. **b8f9b84** — Initial implementation: two-layer fix (chart rules + placement gate + Wackernagel anchor extension).
2. **27955ab** — Reviewer-fix: matrix-side marker `(↑ EXIST_NEG_PREMOD) = true` (vs original daughter-side `(↓3) = true`); documented framework constraint on self-guards.
3. **5cd14a2** — Structural anti-reapply via `N_CORE` category-feat (reviewer's revised prescription).

## Trace diagnosis (b8f9b84)

`tmp/trace_placement_walapa.py` showed the placement engine separates `pa` from `wala` when both `din` and `pa` are 2P clitics competing in the Wackernagel cluster after the verbless anchor `Kapisan`. Root cause: `_enclosing_anchor_for_clitic` line 587-588 short-circuit "if matrix anchor is not VERB, return matrix anchor" — too strong for NP-embedded existentials.

## Layer breakdown

**Layer A — placement.py:**
- New `_is_existential_head` helper (PART[EXISTENTIAL=True]).
- New `_looks_like_existential_nominal_complement` lookahead.
- New `_is_post_existential_pa` adjacency gate (narrowly scoped to NP-embedded contexts via DET-upstream check). Added to `adv_indices` filter.
- `_enclosing_anchor_for_clitic` Layer-1 extension: existential head can be inner anchor even under verbless matrix.

**Layer B — clause.py:**
- Existing 3-daughter existential-NEG S rule + new 4-daughter `wala pa -ng N` S rule now project as `S[CLAUSE_TYPE=EXISTENTIAL, POLARITY=NEG]` — LHS carries category-feats so chart-level consumers can gate on them.
- New 4-daughter S rule required because the placement gate keeps `pa` adjacent in NP-embedded contexts; the existing 3-daughter rule can't compose with `pa` in the middle.

**Layer C — extraction.py:**
- New pre-N modifier rule: `N → S[CLAUSE_TYPE=EXISTENTIAL, POLARITY=NEG] PART[LINK] N[N_CORE]`
- New post-N modifier rule: `N → N[N_CORE] PART[LINK] S[CLAUSE_TYPE=EXISTENTIAL, POLARITY=NEG]`
- Both tag matrix N with `(↑ EXIST_NEG_PREMOD) = true` (marker for downstream consumers).
- Daughter `N[N_CORE]` gates head daughter at the chart-symbol level to prevent self-recursion (the modifier's output is plain `N`, no N_CORE → reapplication can't match).

**Layer D — nominal.py:**
- Base `N → NOUN` rule LHS changed from `N` to `N[N_CORE]` so the canonical base-N projection carries the chart-symbol gate.

## Reviewer dialogue (2026-05-31)

Original reviewer prescription: add self-guard `¬ (↓3 EXIST_NEG_PREMOD)` to the modifier rule. Empirical test showed this is unsatisfiable in this framework — equations are simultaneous constraints, not ordered operations. SET + GUARD on the same f-structure (with `(↑) = ↓3` sharing) contradict.

Reviewer revised guidance (after framework-constraint acknowledgement): use **c-structure / type-shape** anti-reapply, not f-structure negation. Implementation: `N_CORE` category-feat on base-N rule + `N[N_CORE]` daughter pattern on modifier rule. Zero functional impact (audit byte-identical); 11 test-label assertions updated to accept either `N` or `N[N_CORE]` via new `_bare_cat()` helper.

## 10.M FU deferred-defining (parked)

The reviewer's ORIGINAL prescription (self-guard + matrix-side marker SET) would be implementable if the framework supported FU deferred defining-equation evaluation (`tgllfg-out-of-scope.md:62`, Phase 7+ U-bucket). With deferred-defining, the GUARD would see the input N's state (no marker), then the SET would apply AFTER, breaking the simultaneous-constraint contradiction. The current N_CORE structural restriction is the framework-compatible alternative.

## Chart-level category-feat gating

The daughter pattern `S[CLAUSE_TYPE=EXISTENTIAL, POLARITY=NEG]` gates at the CHART level (not just FU-solve). This prevents the modifier rule from over-exploring on every S in the chart — critical for not regressing PANAHON/sent-33 (`Masasabing may dalang malas at suwerte ang panahong ito.`, positive-existential modifier).

The `_is_post_existential_pa` gate is narrowly scoped (DET upstream + LINK+N lookahead) so it doesn't disturb standalone `Wala pang asawa.` (no DET upstream): in that case `pa` moves to clause-end via standard reorder + outer-S clitic absorption.

## Audit (post-12.1 → post-12.2)

| Wave | Pre | Post | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wave 1 exemplars | 108/123 | 108/123 | 0 (sent-17 preserved; sent-16 ZPF → parse-timeout) |
| Wave 2 ramos1971 | 78/209 | 78/209 | 0 |
| Wave 2 rc1990 | 219/1022 | 220/1022 | +1 |
| Wave 2 rg-intermediate | 476/1919 | 476/1919 | 0 |
| Wave 3 rg-conversational | 322/666 | 322/666 | 0 |
| Wave 3 so1972 | 314/1265 | 314/1265 | 0 |
| Wave 4 kroeger1991 | 58/215 | 58/215 | 0 |
| Wave 5 zamar2023 | 151/498 | 151/498 | 0 |
| Unattributed | 145/145 | 145/145 | 0 |
| **XWAVE TOTAL** | **1871** | **1872** | **+1** |
| True regressions (text-keyed) | — | — | **0** |

## Tests

- **New** `tests/tgllfg/test_phase10_j_post12_2.py` — 15 tests across 4 classes (TestEmbeddedWalaPangModifier / TestGENPossessorOnModifiedN / TestStandalonePreserved / TestAntiRegression incl. PANAHON sent-33 positive-existential preservation).
- **Updated** `test_phase5j_neg_existential.py::test_walang_aklat_c_tree` — c-tree label now starts with `S[` (category-feats) rather than bare `S`.
- **Updated** `test_phase5g_np_modifier.py` — new `_bare_cat()` helper + 9 label-strict assertions updated for `N[N_CORE]`.
- **Updated** `test_phase5n_c4_feats_audit.py` — BINARY_FEATS count 67 → 69 (`EXIST_NEG_PREMOD`, `N_CORE`).

## Performance impact (pre-post-12.2 → now)

- `audit_corpus`: ~97s → ~100.5s (+3.6%, within run-variance).
- `test-both`: 172.63s → 184.31s (+6.8%) — mostly from the new modifier rules / 4-daughter S rule / manner-DEM rule instances; N_CORE itself contributes ~1%.

## Sent-16 status (carry-forward)

Sent-16 itself remains parse-timeout. The chart-density issue on the combined `Kung minsa'y` + matrix `din` + wala-pa modifier + GEN-OR-coord exceeds the 5000-tree iteration cap. N_CORE only prevents the post-12.2 modifier rule from self-recursing; OTHER modifier rules in nominal.py still freely wrap modifier-output Ns. Full forest-density mitigation parks for post-12.2.X follow-on (the structural-restriction work continued, FU deferred-defining via 10.M, or further chart-density investigation).

author: vellum-apollo-bot[bot]
body:
## Concern

The `VellumAgent` "hatches a fresh docker assistant…" test in `evals/src/lib/__tests__/vellum-adapter.test.ts` asserts `env: {}` on the spawned hatch call, but `VellumAgent`'s `processEnv` constructor option defaults to `process.env`. On any host that has a recognized provider key exported (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, etc.), the adapter — correctly — forwards it into the hatch subprocess, and the assertion fails:

```
- env: {},
+ env: { ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: "<redacted>" },
```

Caught on the AWS Mac sandbox where the shell exports a real provider key. Locally green because my host has no provider keys set, so the leak silently no-ops.

## Fix

Pin `processEnv: {}` on the single test that asserts `env: {}`, and leave a comment that captures *why* so future edits don't reintroduce the leak. The companion tests in the same file — "forwards LLM provider API keys from process env into the hatch subprocess" and "forwards an empty env to hatch when no provider keys are set" — already inject `processEnv` explicitly for this exact reason. This is the one test that missed the pattern.

The provider-forwarding contract still has its own dedicated tests; this PR doesn't relax or alter that surface.

## Test plan

- Locally with no provider keys set: 355/0 (was 355/0).
- Locally with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=fake OPENAI_API_KEY=fake FIREWORKS_API_KEY=fake`: 355/0 (was 354/1, with `vellum-adapter.test.ts` failing on the docker-hatch assertion).
- Greenlight gate (`bun run typecheck && bun test && bun run lint && bun run format:check && bun run lint:unused`) clean.

## Lesson

Logged in `references/unit-testing.md` (Lessons section): when a test asserts on env-derived output, the test must inject `processEnv` explicitly. Production defaults to `process.env` for the right reasons — that's fine for prod, fatal for test determinism. The sandbox surfaced what local greenlight gates can't.

author: jacobpevans-personal
body:
## What

Make `dryvist/.github` a **lean Nix flake** that exposes `flakeModules.dev-hygiene` — the org's treefmt + git-hooks + zizmor config as one importable flake-parts module.

- `flake.nix` — inputs: `nixpkgs` + `treefmt-nix` + `git-hooks` only (no devenv/crate2nix/devshell). Output: `flakeModules.dev-hygiene`, pre-bound to this repo's inputs and its own `zizmor.yml` (`${self}/zizmor.yml`).
- `nix/dev-hygiene.nix` — the module (formatter set, pre-commit hooks, markdownlint with the `CHANGELOG.md` exclude, zizmor via `--config`). Includes the **treefmt `CHANGELOG.md` exclude** so prettier stops fighting release-please's generated bullets.

## Why

Global dev-hygiene settings should live in `.github` and be **inherited**, not redefined per-repo. Today `nix-claude-code` inlines a full copy (PR #27, to dodge nix-devenv's ~30-node transitive closure) and only `zizmor.yml` is inherited. This gives every Nix repo a single, lean home to import from — the same source they already pull `zizmor.yml` from.

Consumer:
```nix
imports = [ inputs.dryvist-github.flakeModules.dev-hygiene ];
```

First consumer: dryvist/nix-claude-code#33 (drops its inlined `flake/dev-hygiene.nix`). Later, nix-ai/nix-home/nix-darwin can migrate off nix-devenv's copy.

## Verification

`.github`: `nix flake check` passes (only the expected "flakeModules is unchecked" note); lock closure is lean (`nixpkgs`, `treefmt-nix`, `git-hooks`). Consumer-side: `nix flake check` in nix-claude-code passes end-to-end importing this module (markdownlint/statix/treefmt/zizmor all green), with the local copy deleted.

Plain-source consumers (`flake = false`, e.g. nix-devenv reading `${dryvist-github}/zizmor.yml`) are unaffected by adding `flake.nix`.

Refs: dryvist/nix-claude-code#33

author: ashtaralon
body:
## Summary

Surfaces the Layer D Phase 4 replay capability inside the operator UI. Phase 4 backend (PRs ashtaralon/saferemediate-backend#54, #55, #56, #57, #58) lands the replay endpoint + persisted (:SimulationRun) replay-state fields; this PR turns that data into something a customer can actually use on a Tuesday.

## State machine (7 states)

| State | Trigger | CTA | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `never_verified` | `replay_count = 0` | "Run replay verify" | slate, neutral |
| `historical_untracked` | `replay_count > 0` + `last_verdict IS NULL` | "Re-verify to capture verdict" | slate, neutral |
| `byte_equivalent` | `last_verdict = "BYTE_EQUIVALENT"` | "Re-verify" (subtle) | emerald, calm |
| `engine_drift` | `last_verdict = "ENGINE_DRIFT"` | "Re-verify" (prominent) | amber, **self-healing** |
| `plan_drift` | `last_verdict = "PLAN_DRIFT"` | footer link only | sky, informational |
| `source_missing` | `last_verdict = "SOURCE_MISSING"` | footer link only | rose, archival |
| `verifying` | POST in flight | disabled spinner | slate, transient |

Drift self-heal is **refetch-driven**, not optimistic local — backend truth drives UI state. On successful re-verify, the parent refetches the SimulationRun and the panel resolves to whatever new resting state the backend reports. The transition is `engine_drift → verifying → byte_equivalent` (or back to `engine_drift` on a persistent diff), with the transient state visible mid-flight (test asserts this explicitly).

## Files

| File | Δ |
|---|---|
| `lib/types/atlas-simulate.ts` | +52 — `ReplayVerdict` literal, 4 new fields on `SimulationRun`, `ReplayResponse`, `ReplayJewelDrift` |
| `app/api/proxy/iam/shared-roles/simulate/[sim_id]/replay/route.ts` | +68 (new) — POST passthrough, 15s timeout, 504/503 error map |
| `components/iam-shared-roles-replay-verify.tsx` | +537 (new) — 7-state machine, pure `deriveReplayState`, pure `formatRelativeOrIso`, copy verbatim |
| `components/iam-shared-roles-detail-view.tsx` | +31 — plumb under `ChainDeltaResults` in COMPLETED branch + extend seeded RUNNING state with replay defaults |
| `__tests__/replay-verify-panel.test.tsx` | +461 (new) — 18 tests inc. self-heal contract |
| `__tests__/simulate-proxy-pass-through.test.ts` | +74 (new) — proxy contract test against captured live payload |
| `__tests__/fixtures/replay-sim-fcfcc161d02e.json` | +1 (new) — captured 2026-05-31 post-PR-A.1 deploy, all 4 fields populated |
| `scripts/check_signal_language.sh` | +141 (new) — accusative-copy gate, baseline grandfathering |
| `scripts/signal_language_baseline.txt` | +22 (new) — pre-existing hits (cleanup chip filed) |

## Gates

- **Signal-language gate**: 68 files scanned, no new accusative copy (22 pre-existing hits grandfathered via baseline)
- **Vitest**: 19/19 pass — `replay-verify-panel` + `simulate-proxy-pass-through`
- **tsc**: no new errors. Total dropped 159 → 158 (adding the 4 fields to `SimulationRun` resolved latent gaps)

## Discipline alignment

- **`feedback_amber_must_self_heal`** — drift state clears via refetch (test: `ENGINE_DRIFT → BYTE_EQUIVALENT clears amber when parent refetches`). No permanent "this plan once drifted" label anywhere.
- **`feedback_signal_language`** — all 7 state headers descriptive, never accusative. Gate enforces.
- **`feedback_no_mock_numbers_in_ui`** — all counts (`replay_count`, `jewels_total`, etc.) bind directly to Aura data via the existing GET proxy. Graceful degradation when jewel counts are null/zero.
- **`feedback_polish_boundary_engine_vs_operator`** — engine vocab (`counterfactual_id`, `ATLAS`, `catalog_version`) stays in disclosure layers, never headline copy.
- **`pattern_double_verify_at_persistence_and_serialization`** — empirically verified the full Aura → backend GET → proxy → component data path before the FE code shipped (PRs #57, #58).

## Step-10 prod verification — flagging the test-fixture gap

To verify all 6 resting states on prod, we need at least one sim per state. Difficulty varies:

| State | Difficulty | How to seed |
|---|---|---|
| `byte_equivalent` | easy | `sim-fcfcc161d02e` is already in this state |
| `never_verified` | easy | trigger a fresh simulate on any plan |
| `historical_untracked` | hard | requires a sim with `replay_count > 0` AND `last_verdict IS NULL` — pre-PR-A.0 shape no longer reproducible |
| `engine_drift` | very hard | requires catalog/engine drift between simulate and replay |
| `plan_drift` | medium | edit `(:SharedRoleSplitPlan).plan_body_json` between simulate and replay |
| `source_missing` | medium | delete the plan between simulate and replay |

**No test-fixture seeding script exists today.** Honest options:

1. **Verify only the easy 3 on prod**, rely on unit tests for the rest. Ship-safe.
2. **Build `scripts/seed_replay_states.py`** as a follow-up PR — takes a sim_id + target state, mutates Aura to produce that state. Worth it for PR-B's cycle smoke-test.
3. **Manually seed via Cypher one-off** for the prod verification, then delete.

Recommend (1) for the PR-A merge gate, (2) as a separate task for PR-B.

## Followup chips filed

- Clean up 23 grandfathered accusative-copy hits across operator UI, then regen empty baseline.

author: elementalcollision
body:
**Chip 1 of the S1+S2 "self-charter" direction** — the move from *executing* human-written charters to *originating* them. This is the foundational safety primitive.

## Why first

The v46 arc gave Chimera genuine autonomous delivery (author → stage → green → self-commit) — but always against a **human-written** acceptance test, which is the ground truth that makes self-commit safe. For Chimera to write its *own* charter (S1), the self-written test must be trustworthy: a vacuous test (`assert True`, or one that never exercises the logic) passes on *any* implementation, so Chimera could "converge" on code that does nothing. **Before self-authored charters are safe, we need a deterministic gate that proves a test actually pins behaviour.** Same "judgment + deterministic gate" pattern the v46 arc validated.

## The verifier

`chimera/core/mutation_teeth.py::verify_test_teeth(target, test_cmd, …)` — lightweight mutation testing:
1. **Baseline** — the test must pass on the correct target (else can't assess).
2. **Mutate** — single-point AST mutants: comparison-op swaps, arithmetic swaps, bool flips, `int n→n+1`, string alteration. One change each, stable order, capped.
3. **Kill** — a mutant the test FAILS on is *killed*; one it PASSES on *survived* (a blind spot).
4. **Score** — `teeth_score = killed/applied`; `has_teeth(0.8)`.

**Docstrings are excluded** (not behaviour) — found by running against the real `chimera/soak_report.py`: **0.67** with docstring mutation → **1.0** without.

**Safety:** target file restored unconditionally (`try/finally`); only the target is ever written; never raises on a mutant.

## Validated against real code

| Test | Score |
|---|---|
| real `tests/test_soak_report.py` | **1.0** (13/13 killed) |
| vacuous `assert True` | **0.0** |

Clean separation of strong vs worthless tests.

## Honest scope

A small fixed operator set — a teeth **floor**, not full mutation testing; equivalent mutants slightly depress the score (docstring exclusion removes the common systematic case). The caller should point it at the focused acceptance test, not a whole suite (cost = test-time × mutants).

## Tests

`tests/test_mutation_teeth.py` (10): generation across families, docstring exclusion, `max_mutants` cap, strong≥0.8 / vacuous=0.0 separation, baseline-failure handling, file-restore guarantee (normal + baseline-fail), report math. ruff clean.

## Next

Chip 2 — self-charter generation gated by this check → Chip 3 — approved charter feeds the proven v46 self-commit loop.

## Context

Commit [`40be6fd`](https://github.com/actions-gateway/github-actions-gateway/commit/40be6fd) on `main` landed an implementation of #44 from a parallel session, but it has two latent issues that this PR fixes:

1. **Rule 3 silently never fires.** The Notes-extraction regex `\| ([^|]+)$` expects the line to *end* with a non-pipe character, but every Queue row ends with ` |`. `match()` returns 0, the length check compares against an empty string, and over-long Notes pass linting. Demonstrated by running the landed linter against current `main`: returns ✓ despite 17 rows exceeding 250 chars (worst is #42 at 691).
2. **CI gate doesn't trigger on the changes it's meant to guard.** The lint step was added to `unit-test.yml`, which carries `paths-ignore: ['**.md', 'docs/**']` — so any PR that edits only `docs/STATUS.md` skips the lint entirely.

## What this PR changes

- **Rewrites `scripts/lint-status.sh`** with a correctly-anchored Notes parser (splits on `|` into 8 fields per row; field 7 is Notes). All 3 rules now actually run. Includes GitHub Actions `::error::` annotations when run in CI.
- **Adds `.github/workflows/status-lint.yml`** that triggers on `docs/STATUS.md`, the script itself, and the workflow file. Complements (does not replace) the existing `unit-test.yml` step.
- **Brings 17 over-long Queue rows under 250 chars** without losing content — diagnostic detail moves to (or already lived in) the linked plan docs.
- **New `docs/plan/go-best-practices.md`** holds the previously-inline detail for #38–#41.
- **Closes Queue row #44** and bumps `Last touched: 2026-05-31`.

- [x] Synthetic fixtures with duplicate `Last touched:`, duplicate Queue IDs, and over-length Notes all reject correctly

body:
## 概要

Companion のチャット体験を Phase 4 MVP 向けに仕上げる。エージェント応答の表示速度を制御し、アバターのモーション連動・メッセージリストの追従スクロール・タブキーボードショートカットを追加する。

## 背景・目的

Phase 4 MVP として、Companion UI Lab の延長線上でチャット体験（ストリーム表示・アバター連動・タブ操作）を整える。

## 実装内容

- **character-runtime**: Idle/Talk モーションプールを追加し、ランダムループ再生。thinking/waiting は idle プール、talking は Talk_* プールを使用。ステージ layout の refresh とプレースホルダ CSS を拡張
- **ストリーム reveal**: 受信テキストとは独立した chars/sec で吹き出しを段階表示。完了は表示が追いついてから finalize。runId 単位で assistant メッセージを dedupe
- **stick-to-bottom**: ストリーミング中にメッセージリストを下端追従。セッション切替でリセット、送信時は強制スクロール
- **タブショートカット**: Cmd/Ctrl+1..8 でタブ位置、9 で最後のタブ（Chrome 相当）
- **送信時アバター**: プロンプト送信時に thinking 状態へ遷移

## 確認手順

Companion を手動起動し、以下を確認済み。

1. エージェント応答が一定速度で段階表示され、完了後に最終テキストへ確定する
2. ストリーミング中、下端付近にいる場合はメッセージリストが追従する
3. Cmd/Ctrl+数字でタブ切替が動作する
4. 送信時にアバターが thinking になり、モーションプールが切り替わる

## レビュー観点

全体をざっと見てほしい（大きな設計変更や見落としがないか）。

## 変更結果

- チャット吹き出し: 即時全文表示ではなく、制御された速度での reveal 表示
- アバター: idle/thinking/waiting/talking でモーションプールに基づくランダムループ
- タブ: Cmd/Ctrl+1..9 による位置指定切替
- スクロール: ストリーム中の stick-to-bottom 追従


Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

# PR Summary: Companionのストリーム表示・アバター演出・タブ操作改善

## 変更の目的
Phase 4 MVP に向けて Companion のチャット体験を改善するための一連の実装。主な狙いは以下。
- ストリーム受信コンテンツを受信速度と独立した chars/sec 指定で段階表示する演出（StreamRevealController / streamReveal）
- ストリーミング中にメッセージリストを自動で下端追従する UX（useStickToBottomScroll）
- Chrome 準拠のタブショートカット（Cmd/Ctrl+1..9）とタブ選択 API（parseModDigitTabIndex / selectTabByIndex）
- 送信時にアバターを thinking 状態へ遷移、完了/失敗/キャンセル時に idle に戻す挙動の整理（CharacterDirector, SpineStageController, motionPools）
- runId 単位で assistant メッセージを upsert して重複除去する共通実装（packages/shared/src/sessionMessages.ts）

主要追加物：StreamRevealController と util、useStickToBottomScroll フック、motionPools / SpineStageController のループ選択、upsertAssistantTurn、タブショートカット拡張 等。

## 現状の自動検査結果
- pnpm typecheck: ワークスペース全体で実行。大半のパッケージは型チェック成功。ただし apps/cursor-extension の typecheck が失敗（TS2688: 'node' と 'vscode' の型定義ファイルが見つからない）。結果としてワークスペース全体の typecheck は失敗扱い。
- pnpm build: build 実行時も apps/cursor-extension のビルドで同様の型定義欠落により失敗。その他パッケージはビルド済み／成功ログあり。

（備考）CI/環境差で turbo のローカル版未インストール警告や pnpm 設定の警告が出ていますが、今回の致命的失敗は cursor-extension の型定義欠如に起因。

## 重要なリスク（要注意点）
1. StreamReveal の時刻進行と RAF ループ
   - 長い delta（タブ切替やサスペンド）での carry/clamp の境界で finalize のタイミングや表示欠落が起きないか要検証。
2. upsertAssistantTurn の境界条件
   - streamId と runId の混在、セッション切替中の race で誤った行の重複除去や意図しない削除が発生する恐れ。
3. CharacterDirector の setState 挙動変更
   - force 引数削除と cooldown ロジック変更により、期待した遷移（例: 即時 idle 復帰）が別ケースで抑止される可能性。
4. motionPools と skeleton 不整合
   - motion-map の名前が骨格側に存在しないケースで fallback に依存し、視覚的 freeze や不自然な遷移が起きる可能性。
5. useStickToBottomScroll の環境差
   - ResizeObserver 未定義環境や Electron 固有レンダリング差分で追従挙動が崩れる可能性。

## CodeRabbit（レビュー観点）で注力した点
- StreamRevealController / advanceRevealCount
  - RAF の起動・停止条件、tick 内の増分算出と carry の取り扱い、resolveFinalizeContent の選定ロジック、drainPendingComplete / drainForAbort の副作用確認。
  - codePoint 単位での切り出し（絵文字／サロゲート対）の安全性。
- upsertAssistantTurn と agentSessionUpdate の置換
  - runId/streamId をキーにした更新・重複除去が既存呼び出し契約に合うか（idempotency の保証）。
- useAgentEvents の変更
  - revealRef の同期（setContext）と onFrame/onFinalize での setAllSessions 更新、directorRef/setIsStreamingRef 等の ref を介した最新参照利用が安全に行われているか。
- useStickToBottomScroll のトリガ判定
  - contentVersion に含めた値（messageCount / trailingContentLength / showThinkingIndicator / isStreaming）が不要な再遷移や過剰スクロールを生まないか。
- motionPools / SpineStageController のランダム選択
  - プール生成、avoid ロジック、filterAnimationsOnSkeleton の扱いで候補枯渇や偏りがないか。
- chatTabShortcuts の parseModDigitTabIndex
  - key/code/meta/control の組合せでプラットフォーム差異（macOS の meta vs Windows の control）や modifier 組合せの扱いが正しいか。

## 優先度つき指摘（修正が必要なら）
1. 高: apps/cursor-extension の型定義エラーを解消して pnpm typecheck / pnpm build が通るようにする（'`@types/node`' や VSCode 拡張の dev 環境設定、CI キャッシュ/インストールの整備等）。ワークスペース全体CI合格の前提。
2. 高: StreamRevealController の長-delta / サスペンド復帰ケースを単体テストまたは統合で再現・検証し、表示欠落や早期 finalize を防ぐ補償ロジックが必要なら修正。
3. 高: upsertAssistantTurn の runId/streamId 混在境界をユニットテスト化し、セッション切替や重複除去の副作用を検出・修正する。
4. 中: Spine/motionPools で候補が空の場合の確実なフォールバック（視覚停止回避）と skeleton フィルタ後の動作確認。
5. 中: useStickToBottomScroll の ResizeObserver 非対応環境（Electron 旧版など）でのフォールバックの確認と不要スクロール副作用の検証。
6. 低: CharacterDirector#setState の cooldown 意図を改めて確認し、必要ならドキュメント追記。

## 優先的に必要な検証（必須）
- CI / 開発環境:
  - pnpm -w typecheck（修正後に成功を確認）
  - pnpm -w build（修正後に成功を確認）
- 手動動作確認（docs/project-kickoff.md / docs/requirements.md に従いローカルで実施）:
  - Companion 起動でストリーム受信が chars/sec 指定で段階表示される（絵文字・サロゲート対含む）。
  - ストリーミング中にメッセージリストが下端追従し、セッション切替でリセットされる。送信時は scrollToBottom({ force: true }) による最下部表示が行われる。
  - Cmd/Ctrl+1..9 でタブ切替が正しく動作（9 は最後のタブ）。
  - 送信でアバターが thinking に遷移し、完了/キャンセル/エラーで idle に戻る（cooldown バイパスケース含む）。
  - Motion pool による Idle/Talk のランダムループが視覚的に自然であること。
  - 複数 runId/streamId にまたがるストリーミングで assistant メッセージが upsert され重複が生じないこと。

## 結論・次アクション（推奨）
1. まず apps/cursor-extension の型定義問題を解決して CI の typecheck/build を通す。
2. StreamRevealController と upsertAssistantTurn の境界ケースをユニット化してテスト追加（長-delta、abort、重複 runId 等）。
3. Spine/motionPools と useStickToBottomScroll の環境差を手動で検証し、必要ならフォールバック実装/ドキュメント追加。
4. 上記が確認でき次第、視覚や UX 関連は QA（実機／Electron）での受け入れテストへ回す。

## 🤖 New release * `oxideav-avi`: 0.0.8 -> 0.0.9
Changelog

## [0.0.9](https://github.com/OxideAV/oxideav-avi/compare/v0.0.8...v0.0.9) - 2026-06-04 ### Other - OpenDML dmlh.dwTotalFrames muxer-side override (round 234) - per-stream strh.dwLength parse + emit (round 229) - per-stream strh.dwSampleSize parse + emit (round 222) - per-stream strh.dwSuggestedBufferSize parse + emit (round 217) - per-stream strh.fccHandler parse + emit (round 210) - per-stream strh.dwStart parse + emit (round 203) - OpenDML super-index bIndexSubType surface (round 197) ### Added - **OpenDML `LIST odml dmlh.dwTotalFrames` muxer-side override (round 234).** Surfaces the cross-segment frame-count stamp as a caller-controlled value. Clean-room source: `docs/container/riff/opendml-avi-2.0.pdf` page 16, OpenDML 2.0 §5.0 "Extended AVI Header (dmlh)" / "Total Frames": *"The dwTotalFrames field indicates the real size of the AVI file. Since the same field in the Main AVI Header 'avih' indicates the size within the first RIFF 'AVI' chunk."* — i.e. the cross-segment count, distinct from `avih.dwTotalFrames` which §5.0 "Main AVI Header (avih)" / "Total Frames" pins to *"the size (number of frames) within the first RIFF 'AVI' chunk."* The 32-bit `ODMLExtendedAVIHeader.dwTotalFrames` DWORD inside `LIST odml dmlh` was already auto-derived to the primary video stream's cross-segment `packet_count` (= `total_video_frames` from `patch_post_counts`) at `write_trailer` time. This round adds: * `AviMuxOptions::with_dmlh_total_frames(n)` builder writing the supplied 32-bit value verbatim into the 4-byte `dmlh` body in `patch_post_counts`, replacing the auto-derived `total_video_frames` value; * `AviMuxOptions::dmlh_total_frames_override: Option` field as the public surface of the override. The override only changes the 4-byte stamp inside `LIST odml dmlh`; it does NOT touch `avih.dwTotalFrames` (the primary-RIFF count stays the muxer's auto-derived `packet_count`, so the file-level duration `Demuxer::duration_micros` keeps tracking the auto-derived primary segment count), nor any downstream `idx1` / `ix##` / per-stream `strh.dwLength` derivation — a caller that stamps a `dmlh.dwTotalFrames` incompatible with the file's actual cross-segment chunk count is creating an internally-inconsistent file on purpose (e.g. to reproduce a half-written legacy capture dump whose `dmlh` landed before the encoder finalised the last segment, a fixed-budget streamer that pre-declares a known frame budget, or fuzz / regression fixtures). Pairs with the round-101 demuxer accessor `AviDemuxer::dmlh_total_frames` (typed `Option`, widened from the raw `u32` for arithmetic against `i64` pts/duration values) and the `avi:total_frames_all_segments` metadata key for a builder→ writer→demuxer round-trip of any value. Unlike `strh.dwLength` / `dwSampleSize` / `dwSuggestedBufferSize` / `fccHandler` / `dwStart` / `wPriority` / `dwQuality` / `dwInitialFrames` / `wLanguage` / `rcFrame` / `strn` / `IDIT` (which all map their spec-documented `0` sentinel back to `None`), OpenDML 2.0 §5.0 does not define a "no length declared" sentinel for `dmlh.dwTotalFrames` — `0` literally means zero frames, so the override of `0` round-trips as `Some(0)` (distinct from `None`, which means no `LIST odml dmlh` was present). Only meaningful for `AviKind::OpenDml`; ignored for `AviKind::Avi10` (which never emits a `LIST odml dmlh`). Covered by a 10-test suite exercising the auto-derived baseline (3 packets ⇒ `Some(3)`), override round-trip via the typed accessor + metadata key, builder idempotency (last call wins), independence from `avih.dwTotalFrames` (file duration stays anchored to the auto-derived avih count), independence from per-stream `strh.dwLength` (both video and audio stamps keep their auto-derived `packet_count` / `sample_count`), boundary values (`1` / `u32::MAX` / a typical 90 000-frame long-form-capture count / explicit `0` → `Some(0)`), and the `AviKind::Avi10` mode no-op (override present in options but surfaces as `None` because no `LIST odml dmlh` is written). - **Per-stream `strh.dwLength` parse + emit + round-trip (round 229).** Surfaces the `dwLength` field at byte offset 32 of the 56-byte AVISTREAMHEADER per AVI 1.0 §"AVISTREAMHEADER". Clean-room source: `docs/container/riff/avi-riff-file-reference.md` (`dwLength` row, line 244): *"Length of this stream. The units are defined by the dwRate and dwScale members of the stream's header."* The 32 raw byte was already read internally as the `length` local used to derive `StreamInfo::duration`; this round adds the public per-stream surface: * typed `AviDemuxer::stream_length(stream_index) -> Option` accessor mapping the `0` "no length declared" value back to `None` so an unspecified length reads the same as an absent one — mirroring the round-222 `dwSampleSize` / round-217 `dwSuggestedBufferSize` / round-210 `fccHandler` / round-203 `dwStart` / round-182 `wPriority` / round-176 `dwQuality` / round-153 `dwInitialFrames` / round-119 `wLanguage` / round-115 `rcFrame` / round-80 `strn` / round-107 `IDIT` "default == absent" convention, * `avi:strh..length` metadata key (omitted for the `0` value to keep absence observable), * `AviMuxOptions::with_stream_length(stream_index, n)` builder writing the supplied 32-bit value verbatim at byte offset 32 of the strh at the `write_trailer` / `patch_post_counts` site, replacing the auto-derived per-stream packet / sample count (last call per stream-index wins via retain-then-push; no validation against the actual chunk count). Pre-round-229 the muxer always patched the auto-derived value (video: `packet_count`; audio PCM / CBR: running `sample_count` from the muxer's `size / sample_size` formula) — those byte writes are preserved verbatim when no override is supplied. The override only changes the byte stamp at offset 32; it does NOT touch `avih.dwTotalFrames` (per-stream length and the file-global total are spec-independent fields), and does NOT alter any downstream `idx1` / `ix##` / `dmlh` derivation, so a caller that stamps a `dwLength` incompatible with their actual chunk count is creating an internally-inconsistent file on purpose (e.g. to reproduce a half-written legacy capture dump, a fixed-budget streamer's playlist-boundary stamp, or a pathological writer for fuzz / regression purposes). The `StreamInfo::duration` exposed by `Demuxer::streams` continues to track the raw stamp (the framework already derives duration from this same DWORD). author: adminquest
body:
## Étape 8b-1 — normalisation structurelle du registre citations

Dote le corpus citations (962, figé) d'un **backbone structurel** et d'une **porte de validation**, **sans canonicalisation** (aucun `QUOTE-`) et **sans renommer aucun id** — l'identité reste **source + ordinal**, ce qui préserve les 30+ références repo et la parité du classifieur (`-Q`/`-CIT-`/`CIT-`). **Attribution** et **split fin paraphrase/concept** → 8b-2. Gel `EVENT-`/`CONCERT-` **intact**.

> **Base** : empile sur 8a (PR #42, non encore mergée — le corpus 962 n'existe qu'au-dessus de 8a). À fusionner après #42 ; le diff propre à 8b-1 apparaîtra une fois #42 dans `main`.

### Approche — backbone dérivé (pas de réécriture des 962 source)
Réécrire 962 records dans ~100 fichiers / 3 structures serait fragile et contredirait « corpus figé ». Le backbone est **dérivé** par `build_registers.normalize_quote_record` et matérialisé dans l'export canonique (`quotes.json`), validé par la même logique (parité build ↔ `validate_quotes` ↔ loader runtime).

| Champ | Dérivation | Couverture |
|---|---|---:|
| `source_id` | présent, sinon recouvré depuis l'id (`CIT-S65-001`→`S65`) | **962/962 (100 %)** |
| `texte` | 1er champ de texte ; sentinelle `(non transcrit)` pour fiches-pointeur | 962 (dont **75** sentinelles) |
| `type` | `verbatim` si verbatim présent, sinon `non_verbatim` | **706 / 256** |
| `page` | localisateur réel, sinon `inconnue` (pas de fabrication) | 909 réels / **53** `inconnue` |

Lossless : ancien `type` (descripteur de longueur) préservé en `type_legacy` (**82**) ; `langue_originale: anglais` → `en` (**20**).

**Conformité schéma : 8 % → 100 %** (962/962 : `id + kind + source_id + texte + type`).

### `same_as` — doublon réconcilié (sans renommage)
`S75-Q016` (Ott) → `S45-Q052` (Curtis, biographie primaire) — additif, déprécié→retenu, mono-valué, point fixe (NAMING §10.3).

### Porte `tools/validate_quotes.py` (gate-able, exit 0/1)
INV1 schéma · INV2 convention d'id ∈ {`S\d+-Q\d+`, `S\d+-CIT-\d+`, `CIT-S\d+-\d+`} · INV3 provenance (`source_id` ; `page` réelle ou `inconnue`) · INV4 `type` ∈ {verbatim, non_verbatim} · INV5 `same_as` (mono-valué, cible existante, point fixe) · INV6 gel. → **errors = 0**.

### Schéma & dépendances
- `schema_validation.py` + `schemas/quote.schema.yaml` : requis backbone, ancien socle (`citation_originale`/`langue_originale`/`statut_verification`) rendu optionnel ; `type` controlled.
- `jsonschema` (déjà déclaré) noté pour `validate_quotes` — `validate_places`/`validate_songs`/`validate_quotes` tournent désormais réellement.

### Chaîne
`build_all --strict` **errors=0** (warnings 31088→28713) · `validate_quotes`/`places`/`songs`/`chronology`/`concerts` **tous verts** · **sentinelle en phase** (594 artefacts, rebuild déterministe) · arbre propre.

### Reste pour 8b-2
Attribution (locuteur/rapporteur/auteur-source → `PERSON-`) · split fin du `non_verbatim` · transcription des 75 fiches-pointeur · sourçage des 53 `page: inconnue`.

body:
## Summary
Settings opens locked by default. A small banner shows the lock state with an **Unlock changes** action (40px secondary per UI_RULES Part 1). Unlocking opens a minimal password modal; correct password makes Settings editable for the current React session, page refresh re-locks. Subnav (Data / Accounts / Rules / Contracts) stays clickable while locked so partners can navigate around.

**Password:** \`gracie2026\` — hardcoded constant in \`Dashboard.tsx\`, flagged with a comment as a casual-edit speed bump only (anything in the client bundle is visible to a determined viewer; this stops accidents, not attackers).

## Why \`<fieldset disabled>\` (and not button-disabling)
Discovery confirmed Settings has **no Save button anywhere** — every input persists to Supabase \`onChange\`/\`onBlur\` via \`updateBusinessRules()\` / \`saveSharedWorkspaceSettings()\`. Disabling Save buttons alone would let partners save by typing into a field. \`<fieldset disabled>\` cascades the disabled state to every nested form control, so:
- Real \`.click()\` on a button inside the fieldset is a no-op
- Real \`.focus()\` on an input inside the fieldset is a no-op
- No on-change handler can fire because no user interaction reaches the controls

## Scope decisions (per Wesley's direction)
- **Forecast leak NOT extended.** Forecast Business Valuation card and forecast events remain editable. Settings-only protection.
- **Button height: 40px** — secondary card/page action per UI_RULES Part 1 taxonomy.

## Files
- \`src/pages/Dashboard.tsx\` — state, banner, fieldset wrap, password modal
- \`src/dashboard.css\` — banner styles, fieldset reset + 0.7 opacity disabled cue, modal styles

## Test plan
- [x] Settings opens locked; banner is yellow with lock icon
- [x] Subnav (Data/Accounts/Rules/Contracts) clickable while locked
- [x] \`.click()\` on a button inside fieldset is a no-op
- [x] \`.focus()\` on an input inside fieldset is a no-op
- [x] Unlock modal opens on \"Unlock changes\"
- [x] Wrong password → \"Incorrect password.\" error, modal stays open, fieldset stays locked
- [x] Correct password → modal closes, banner turns green with unlocked icon, fieldset becomes editable
- [x] After unlock, an input accepts focus and value change
- [x] Page refresh → returns to locked state (React state, no sessionStorage)
- [x] \`npm run build\` passes

author: ffroliva
body:
## Problem

`/gflow:plan` was named as if it created plans but only read existing ones. CLAUDE.md pointed agents to it with "Starting a feature → `/gflow:plan`" — an agent following that would get a phase summary and have no tool to actually write a plan.

## Changes

Split into four purpose-named commands:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/gflow:status [feature]` | Full state: active plan file, goal, progress, next task (replaces old behavior) |
| `/gflow:next [feature]` | Next unchecked task only — no context noise |
| `/gflow:active` | Which plan is active and its goal — no task detail |
| `/gflow:plan <feature>` | **Creates** `docs/superpowers/plans/<date>-<slug>/PLAN.md` |

The new `/gflow:plan` follows the predict→scenario→plan workflow:
1. Reads `/gflow:predict` and `/gflow:scenario` output from context
2. Asks ≤3 clarifying questions if scope/module/acceptance criteria are unclear
3. Decomposes into atomic committable tasks with step + test checklists
4. Shows the draft plan for user review, then writes on approval

Updated all references in `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `docs/INDEX.md`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `/gflow:status` — confirms it surfaces next task from active_plan.py
- [ ] Run `/gflow:next` — confirms only the task block is returned, no header
- [ ] Run `/gflow:active` — confirms only plan path/title/goal/progress is returned
- [ ] Run `/gflow:plan <feature>` after a predict/scenario session — confirms it writes a plan file to docs/superpowers/plans/
- [ ] CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md no longer reference the old read-only `/gflow:plan` usage

author: gastly92
body:
## Summary

First stage of the Battle Frontier sandbox: makes the **Battle Factory** fully playable from a fresh save as a **6v6, always-level-100** facility. The Factory is a natural first facility because it rents you a team — so it works even though a new game starts with no Pokémon (the "start at Battle Frontier" piece already shipped in #6).

This is **Stage 1**. The only thing intentionally left for a follow-up PR is **endless mode** (removing the 7-win challenge cap so a run continues until you lose).

## What it does

- **6-mon Factory teams** instead of the vanilla 3, gated behind a new reusable config flag.
- **Always level 100** — the lobby no longer asks Lv50/Open; challenges are forced into Open Level (which already creates both teams at `MAX_LEVEL`).
- **Auto-rents a full team of 6** — the rental select screen is skipped; you're handed a generated team and the attendant tells you so (instead of the misleading "choose from our selection").
- **Post-win swap works at 6v6** — after a win you can still swap one of your Pokémon for one of the defeated opponent's. All 6 balls are reachable and positioned correctly on both the player and opponent sub-screens, including the slide-cycle animation.
- **Debug menus always on** (`DEBUG_OVERWORLD_MENU`, `DEBUG_BATTLE_MENU`) for sandbox testing — warp around, set flags, and auto-win battles.

## Config flags (new `include/config/frontier.h`)

- `B_FRONTIER_PARTY_SIZE_6V6` — gates `FACTORY_PARTY_SIZE` (scoped to the Factory so other facilities keep their vanilla 3-mon coordinate tables) and the auto-rent path.
- `B_FRONTIER_FORCE_LVL_100` — forces Open Level.

Both are wired so they can be extended to other facilities as the sandbox grows.

## Implementation notes

- **Saveblock space:** the 6v6 `rentalMons` array adds 72 bytes to `SaveBlock2`, which overflowed the sector. Reclaimed via `FREE_BATTLE_TOWER_E_READER` (−188 bytes, unused in a sandbox). The save-size regression test (`test/save.c`) is updated to match (3884 → 3768).
- **`MAX_FRONTIER_PARTY_SIZE` left unchanged** — only a new `FRONTIER_TEMP_PARTY_SIZE` / `FACTORY_PARTY_SIZE` widen, so the saveblock tower-record party arrays don't grow.
- **Config flags in scripts:** the lobby/pre-battle text branches use assembler `.if FLAG` (the `MtChimney` precedent), **not** cpp `#if` — the script cpp pass has no `TRUE`/`FALSE`, so `#if FLAG` silently takes the wrong branch. This footgun is now documented in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **No transition flash on auto-rent:** the team is built synchronously via a `callnative`, staying in the overworld instead of routing through the rental screen's callback/fade.
- **Swap ball layout** is factored into `SWAP_BALL_X(i)`/`SWAP_BALL_GAP` macros (35px/x=32 for 6v6, reusing the rental select screen's known 6-ball coordinates; vanilla spacing otherwise).

## Not in this PR (Stage 2)

- **Endless mode** — remove the 7-win cap so a run keeps going until a loss. (The post-win single swap above is already here.)

## Testing

- `UNUSED_ERROR=1 DEPRECATED_ERROR=1 make -O all` — clean, both flag states (ON and OFF).
- `make -O release` — clean (debug menus compiled in).
- `make check` — 4775 passed, exit 0 (baseline: 12 KNOWN_FAILING, 6 EXPECT_FAILING — unchanged).
- Playtested: fresh save → Factory lobby → 6v6 level-100 battles, auto-rent, and post-win swap all working.

author: tejassudsfp
body:
Follow-up to the off-box pipeline (#17).

Diagnosing the reference VPS during this session, `top` showed **95% steal (`st`)** with 1-min load ~38 but user CPU ~2% and `/login` still sub-4s — a host-level Hostinger CPU throttle, not real app load (ClickHouse also had 4 background merges running underneath). A load-average gate would refuse to ever deploy on this box; an idle-only gate that ignores steal would green-light a deploy onto a VM with no real cycles.

The guard now samples `/proc/stat` over 1s:

```
idle% = (idle + iowait) / (user + nice + sys + idle + iowait + irq + softirq + steal)
```

so **steal counts against available headroom**. On a throttled box this collapses toward 0 and we abort; on a healthy box steal≈0 and it reflects true free CPU. Threshold via `DEPLOY_MIN_IDLE_PCT` (default 20). awk math unit-tested for both healthy (→80%) and throttled (→0%) cases.

body:
Adds a new endpoint to `OrderController`:

```
POST /orders/{id}/cancel
```

This is the canonical demonstration of `api.type: openapi-from-controllers`:

1. The controller is in the red zone (`*Controller.java`), so the path
   classification fires `api-review` immediately.
2. The CI workflow runs `./gradlew generateOpenApiDocs` at the PR's base
   SHA and at its head SHA, producing two OpenAPI specs.
3. The agent-redline reporter consumes both specs and computes a
   *structural diff* — added paths, removed paths, modified operations.
   That diff appears in the PR comment alongside the verdict.

The PR has the `api-reviewed` label applied (or a CODEOWNER approval)
satisfying the api-review checkpoint, so the PR can merge once CI is
green.

body:
## Summary
This is the initial implementation of CloudWay, a cannabis deals aggregator for New Jersey dispensaries. The application provides a modern, responsive interface for browsing and filtering cannabis deals across NJ dispensaries with features like real-time countdown timers, location-based search, and multi-platform deal aggregation.

## Key Changes

### Core Application Structure
- **Next.js 16 app router setup** with TypeScript configuration
- **Theme system** with light/dark mode support using CSS custom properties
- **Global styling** with Tailwind CSS, glassmorphism effects, and custom animations (falling leaves, twinkling stars)
- **Mock data layer** with 8 NJ dispensaries and 20+ sample deals for development

### Pages & Routing
- **Home page** (`app/page.tsx`) - Main deals feed with county/category filtering and map view toggle
- **Category pages** (`app/deals/[category]/page.tsx`) - Dedicated pages for Flower, Pre-Rolls, Vapes, Edibles, Concentrates with advanced filtering
- **API routes** for deals, dispensaries, and scraper orchestration

### Components
- **Header** - Search bar with trending suggestions, theme toggle, "Near Me" geolocation
- **DealCard** - Grid and list view variants with countdown timers, discount badges, and progress indicators
- **MapView** - Interactive map with radius filtering and open-now toggle
- **Filters** - County, category, and sidebar filters (brands, strain types, weights, subtypes, stores)
- **Marquee** - Horizontal scrolling featured deals carousel
- **Background** - Animated falling cannabis leaves and twinkling stars (theme-aware)
- **CountdownPill** - Real-time deal expiration countdown with urgency states (safe/warning/urgent)

### Data & Utilities
- **Type definitions** (`lib/types.ts`) - Deal, Dispensary, Category, StrainType, Platform types
- **Utility functions** (`lib/utils.ts`) - Open status detection, countdown calculations, distance calculations, price formatting
- **Scraper infrastructure** (`lib/scrapers/index.ts`) - Placeholder for multi-platform scrapers (IHeartJane, Weedmaps, Blaze, Dutchie, Treez) with NJ-only validation

### Styling & UX
- **Custom CSS** with glassmorphism, smooth transitions, and responsive design
- **Skeleton loaders** for async content
- **Accessibility features** - ARIA labels, semantic HTML, keyboard navigation support
- **Mobile-responsive** layout with collapsible filters and touch-friendly controls

## Notable Implementation Details

- **NJ-specific validation** in scraper infrastructure ensures only New Jersey dispensaries (zip codes 07001–08999, 21 NJ counties)
- **Real-time countdown system** with urgency states (green/yellow/red) and pulsing animations for urgent deals
- **Geolocation support** with fallback to mock location (Mullica Hill, NJ) for development
- **Multi-view support** - Grid/list toggle for deals, separate map view with radius filtering
- **Platform abstraction** - Deals can come from multiple ordering platforms (IHeartJane, Weedmaps, etc.)
- **Store hours parsing** - Automatic open/closing status detection with countdown to closing time
- **Distance calculation** - Haversine formula for calculating dispensary distances from user location

## Future Integration Points
- Database connection (Prisma ORM ready in structure)
- Real scraper implementations for each platform
- Cron job scheduling for periodic deal updates
- User authentication and saved favorites

## Summary

Fixes the chat system - responses were not rendering on screen due to an SSE field mismatch, and upgrades the RAG pipeline with smart routing.

### Critical Bug Fix: Responses Not Displaying

**Root Cause**: The backend SSE stream was sending `{"text": chunk, "done": false}` but the frontend `ChatPage.jsx` checks for `parsed.content`. This field name mismatch meant streamed content was silently dropped - no AI response ever rendered on screen.

**Fix**: Changed backend `chat_service.py` to yield `{"content": chunk, "done": false}` matching the frontend's expected field name. Also fixed the final done event to use `"event": "syrabit_done"` which the frontend explicitly checks for.

### RAG Pipeline Upgrade

**Generic Query Detection**:
- Added `is_generic_query()` - regex detects greetings (hi, hello, hey, thanks, bye, etc.)
- These skip RAG entirely and go straight to LLM knowledge
- Integrated in both streaming (`/chat/stream`) and non-streaming (`/chat/`) endpoints

**Real Relevance Scores**:
- Replaced synthetic positional scores (`1.0 - i * 0.1`) with actual Discovery Engine `model_scores`
- Added `_extract_score()` helper method to extract scores from the API response
- Heuristic fallback when scores unavailable: content >50 chars = 0.65, else 0.3

**Similarity Threshold**:
- Added `SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.70` constant
- Chunks below 0.70 are filtered out before prompt building
- When all chunks filtered, triggers LLM-only mode (existing "no context" system prompt)

### Flow After Fix
```
User sends message
  → Is it generic? (hi/hello/etc) → Skip RAG → LLM knowledge only
  → Otherwise → Search Discovery Engine → Filter by score ≥ 0.70
    → Has quality chunks? → RAG mode (context in prompt)
    → No quality chunks? → LLM knowledge only
```

### Files Changed
- `apps/backend/app/services/chat_service.py` - SSE field fix, generic detection, threshold filtering
- `apps/backend/app/services/search/vertex_search.py` - Real score extraction from Discovery Engine
- `apps/backend/app/api/v1/chat.py` - Generic query skip in both endpoints, done event fix

### Testing
- 4 new unit tests added (generic detection, threshold filtering, SSE field)
- 205 existing tests pass
- Python syntax validation: clean

author: aruneem-bhowmick
body:
## Summary The `/repos` route is the core of the Depo workflow: it is where authenticated users land after OAuth, see all their public repositories, and make their deletion selection. This PR wires up the server-side entry point for that route — `app/repos/page.tsx` — completing the data-fetch boundary between the GitHub API and the interactive `` client component. ### What this PR does - **Implements `app/repos/page.tsx`** — an async server component that fetches the authenticated user's public repositories and passes them to ``. The fetch is made by calling `listPublicRepos()` directly rather than via `fetch('/api/repos')`, avoiding a needless HTTP round-trip to the same process. - **Handles the error path** — if `listPublicRepos` throws (token revoked, GitHub outage, rate limit), the page renders an inline `role="alert"` with the error message and a "Try again" anchor that re-navigates to `/repos`, re-triggering the server fetch. - **Handles the empty-repos case** — `` is passed through normally; the component's built-in empty state ("No repositories to show.") renders without any special-casing in the page itself. - **Adds a comprehensive test suite** (`tests/components/ReposPage.test.tsx`) — six focused tests covering the heading, repo forwarding, empty-array path, error alert content, "Try again" link target, and `` suppression on error. - **Expands documentation** — `docs/COMPONENTS.md` gets a dedicated Repos Page section; `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` gets the new test entry and a concrete explanation of a Jest mock-factory constraint discovered during testing. --- ## Architecture notes ### Server/client rendering boundary `app/repos/page.tsx` is the **server boundary** for the `/repos` route. The Next.js middleware already guarantees `session.accessToken` is present before this component runs, so no additional auth check is needed in the page itself. The page's sole responsibility is fetching data and deciding which UI to render: ``` GET /repos └── app/repos/page.tsx (server component) ├── getSession() — reads the encrypted iron-session cookie ├── listPublicRepos(token) — Octokit paginate, all pages, type-mapped │ ├── error? → inline alert + "Try again" link └── ok? → (client component boundary) └── checkbox state, search, fork toggle, sessionStorage write ``` ### Why call `listPublicRepos` directly instead of `fetch('/api/repos')` Server components can import and call library functions directly. Going through `fetch` would serialize and deserialize the repos array over an HTTP connection that begins and ends inside the same Node.js process — unnecessary overhead. Direct function calls are synchronous to the module graph, avoid network stack overhead, and keep the server-side data path as a single call in a single stack frame. ### Error propagation `listPublicRepos` throws an Octokit `HttpError` on GitHub API failures. The page wraps the call in a `try/catch` and uses the Error's `.message` as the alert text. Non-Error throwables (rare but possible) fall back to the string `'Failed to load repositories.'`. This covers the realistic failure modes: a revoked token, a transient GitHub 5xx, or a secondary rate-limit hit. --- ## Test suite The test file mocks `@/lib/session`, `@/lib/github`, and `@/components/RepoList` at the module boundary and drives `ReposPage()` as an async function: | Test | What it asserts | |------|-----------------| | `renders the page heading` | `

Your repositories

` is always present | | `passes fetched repos to RepoList` | mock `` receives and displays the correct repo count | | `passes empty array to RepoList when user has no repos` | 0-count display — no special-casing needed in the page | | `shows error alert when listPublicRepos throws` | `role="alert"` present, contains the thrown message | | `shows Try again link on error` | anchor has `href="/repos"` | | `does not show RepoList on error` | `data-testid="repo-list"` is absent on the error path | ### Jest mock-factory constraint (documented in DEVELOPMENT.md) During testing, a previously undocumented project constraint surfaced: `jest.mock()` factories are hoisted by `babel-plugin-jest-hoist` **before** ts-jest's TypeScript compilation pass. The factory body is parsed by plain Babel (no TypeScript or JSX plugins), so type annotations and JSX inside a factory cause a parse error: ```ts // ✗ Fails at Babel extraction — type annotation not supported jest.mock('@/components/RepoList', () => ({ RepoList: ({ repos }: { repos: unknown[] }) =>
{repos.length}
, })) // ✓ Correct — plain JS with React.createElement jest.mock('@/components/RepoList', () => ({ RepoList: (props) => require('react').createElement('div', { 'data-testid': 'repo-list' }, props.repos.length + ' repos'), })) ``` This constraint applies to all future component tests that need to mock components which themselves render JSX. The fix and the rationale are now documented in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` with a concrete example. --- ## Test results ``` Test Suites: 21 passed, 21 total Tests: 178 passed, 178 total File | % Stmts | % Branch | % Funcs | % Lines ---------------------|---------|----------|---------|-------- All files | 89.18 | 85.80 | 91.48 | 90.70 app/repos/page.tsx | 100.00 | 75.00 | 100.00 | 100.00 ``` Overall coverage: 89% statements, 86% branches, 91% functions — above the 80% threshold. The `app/repos/page.tsx` branch gap (75%) is the non-`Error` throwable fallback path; covering it would require throwing a plain string or non-Error object from `listPublicRepos`, which is not a realistic scenario for Octokit. --- ## Checklist - [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes - [x] `npm test` — 178/178 tests green - [x] Coverage ≥ 80% across all metrics - [x] All functions in new files have JSDoc docstrings - [x] `docs/COMPONENTS.md` updated with Repos Page section - [x] `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` updated with test inventory entry and mock-factory constraint note - [x] No secrets, `.env` files, or co-authorship lines committed ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a new `/repos` page that displays your public repositories with integrated error handling and a "Try again" option for failed requests. * **Documentation** * Updated component and development documentation to describe the repos page functionality and testing guidelines. * **Tests** * Added comprehensive tests for the repos page covering successful repository loading and error scenarios.

## Summary

Adds 5 names to the suffix-translation block in `railway_worker.py::build_subprocess_env`:
- `SINK_TYPE`
- `EXECUTOR_API_KEY`
- `EXECUTOR_BASE_URL`
- `EXECUTOR_ACCOUNT_ID`
- `EXECUTOR_ACCOUNT_TYPE`

This mirrors the existing `ALPACA_API_KEY_<SUFFIX>` pattern from lines 126-134.

## Why

EXP-V8A-IBKR is the 10th experiment and the FIRST to use a non-Alpaca broker
(`ExecutorOrderSink` from PR #85). Without this patch, the only way to wire its
broker creds was to either (a) hard-code per-experiment branches in the
supervisor, or (b) leak `SINK_TYPE=executor` and the executor URL into every
other subprocess's env. The suffix-translation pattern keeps the 9 Alpaca
subprocesses completely unaffected — their env doesn't contain any
`*_EXPV8AIBKR`-suffixed vars, so the for-loop no-ops for them.

## Architectural context

Per `~/.openclaw/media/v8a_ibkr_architecture_analysis.md` §3.2: this is the
Plan A 3-step change set to land EXP-V8A-IBKR.

1. ✅ Already done in PR #86 — config + registry entry + CREDENTIALS.md
2. ⏳ This PR — supervisor translation
3. ⏳ After this merges — Railway env vars on `attix-worker` + registry status `registered → active`

## Behaviour for the 9 Alpaca experiments

Unchanged. The for-loop runs but finds no matching env vars
(`SINK_TYPE_EXP400`, `EXECUTOR_API_KEY_EXP400`, etc. are not set on
`attix-worker`), so it injects nothing. The subprocesses get exactly the
env they get today.

## Behaviour for EXP-V8A-IBKR (once active + Railway vars set)

The supervisor injects into the V8A-IBKR subprocess:
```
SINK_TYPE=executor
EXECUTOR_API_KEY=<key>
EXECUTOR_BASE_URL=https://executor-production-1f58.up.railway.app
EXECUTOR_ACCOUNT_ID=ibkr_tafintech-p11-paper
EXECUTOR_ACCOUNT_TYPE=paper
```

`compass.live.vrp_runner._resolve_sink_type()` (shipped in PR #85) reads
`SINK_TYPE=executor` → builds an `ExecutorOrderSink` → routes intents to
IBKR paper via the Railway-deployed executor.

body:
## Life of Fry — mobile joystick + 5–6 grabs to fill

Two changes that rebuild the same game bundle, so they ship together (splitting would just conflict on the build artifact).

### 1. Mobile controls
The game was unplayable on phones (no keyboard, no pointer-lock mouse-look). On a coarse-pointer device — or `?touch` to preview on desktop:
- **On-screen joystick** (bottom-left) to move
- **Drag** the right side of the screen to look
- **CROUCH / HOP** buttons (bottom-right)
- **Tap to play** (no pointer-lock)

Desktop is unchanged: WASD + mouse-look + pointer-lock.

### 2. ~5–6 grabs to fill (measured with the playtest harness)
Heads-up from the harness: the live build (radius 3) already took **~15 grabs** to fill, so hitting 5–6 meant *fewer, bigger* bites — and counterintuitively, **more fries helps** (a denser basket = each scoop grabs more).
- HUNGER_TARGET 15 → **16**, FRY_COUNT 20 → **28**, grab radius → **4**
- Human now fills in **~5.9 grabs avg** (your 5–6 target), still **fair** (skilled bot 100% win) with real stakes (doing-nothing bot **dies**).

> Supersedes the open **#75** ("double the grab area"); close it if you merge this.

Only the `games/life-of-fry/` build artifact changes (new JS+CSS hashes + the two index.html references).

body:
Two small follow-up fixes to Glide (`/apps/glide/index.html`) from playtest feedback.

## 1. Tilt was too sensitive
Widened `TILT_RANGE` from **24° → 38°** of phone tilt for full up/down deflection. Small movements now produce gentler response, so the glider is less twitchy and easier to hold steady. (Direction and neutral-calibration are unchanged — still tilt left to climb, right to dive.)

## 2. The moon's "weird dark circle"
The old crescent effect drew a **sky-coloured disc offset *outside* the moon's silhouette** at 50% alpha — the part hanging past the moon's edge tinted the sky next to it, which is the dark circle you saw.

Replaced it with **soft terminator shading clipped to the moon disc**: a subtle radial shadow on the side away from the light, masked to the moon's circle so it can never bleed into the sky. The moon now reads as a clean lit sphere and the surrounding stars stay crisp right up to its edge.

## Verification
JS passes `node --check`; rendered the night sky in-scene and the moon in isolation at large scale on the night gradient — shading sits cleanly on the disc with zero sky bleed (stars crisp to the rim), no console/page errors.

> Note: tilt feel itself can't be exercised in headless Chromium; 38° is a sensible calmer default and is a one-line tweak if you'd like it even gentler.

author: afadesigns
body:
## What

Inside `((…))` / `$((…))` the lexer fused only `+= -= *= %=`. The operators `/= &= |= ^= <<= >>= **=` were emitted as their bare token plus a separate `=`, so `(( n /= 2 ))` parsed as division with no right operand and errored. An arithmetic operand carrying an embedded `${…}` (e.g. `(( x >= PFX_${state}_SFX ))`) also broke arithmetic-word scanning.

## Fix

- Route `/ & | ^ << >> **` through the arithmetic compound-assign path when `inArithmetic()`.
- `parseIdentifier` absorbs an embedded `${…}` operand in arithmetic context.
- Behaviour outside arithmetic is unchanged and test-pinned: background `&`, pipe `|`, redirection `<< >>`, globs `* **`.

## Verification

- New token-stream regression tests in `pkg/lexer` and `pkg/parser` covering every operator + embedded `${…}`, plus negative tests for the outside-arithmetic forms.
- `go test ./...` green; `gofmt -s`/`go vet` clean.
- Pinned-corpus gate: 78 files, 0 parser errors, 0 regressions.

These operators are pervasive in real Zsh configs; the fix removes a class of false parser failures.

author: devonjones
body:
## wyrd-vm8t — pronunciation coverage

The grapheme→IPA converter (`registers.phonology.to_ipa`) was correct but had **zero production callers** — all IPA came from Wiktionary, which is uneven (Old Norse 1.8% covered) and rendered OE `h` as the velar fricative /x/ even word-initially (the wrong `-ham` → /xɑːm/ the inspector surfaced). This wires the G2P in as a rebuildable enrichment pass and fills the long tail.

### Four loops
1. **G2P fill + positional OE h-rule.** `Phoneme` gains `coda_ipa`/`coda_respelling`: OE `h` is now positional — [h] onset (`hām`→/hɑːm/), [x] coda (`burh`→/bʊrx/, `niht`→/nɪxt/); hl/hr/hn/hw clusters still match first. `derive_pronunciation_ipa` fills `pronunciation_ipa` for the table languages and fixes OE onset-h, wired into `run_full_enrichment` (re-derived for free on rebuild — like english-shaped/stratum, **no jsonl**). → OE 66%→99%, **ON 1.8%→83%**, welsh 59%→86%.
2. **Celtic via the welsh table.** The lexicon's "celtic" elements are Brittonic (`bedd`→/bɛð/, `llan`→/ɬan/), so the Welsh G2P fits. → celtic 0%→83%.
3. **LLM tier for the no-G2P-table languages.** Goidelic / Romance / Middle English / Breton have no clean table; `mine-pronunciation-llm` (Ollama, qwen2.5:7b) writes a broad IPA to the **lower-confidence** `data/mining/_pronunciation.jsonl`, replayed deterministically at enrichment (high+medium confidence only; artifact-filtered). PAID/non-deterministic → `non_rebuild_commands`, round-trips through L2. → generation-reachable gap 978→481.
4. **Export-side surface fallback.** Many bundle forms are variants/reflexes, not etymon canonical_forms, so they carried no IPA. `_subject.py` now derives one via the G2P for table-language surface forms (gaps only). → dominant-language bundle coverage ~87%→~99%.

### Rebuildability
Two tiers, both survive a wipe: deterministic G2P (OE/ON/welsh/celtic) re-derives from `canonical_form` (enrichment pass, no jsonl); the LLM tier replays `_pronunciation.jsonl`. Registered in `_rebuild_layers.json` + `REBUILD.md`; the byte-identical round-trip test passes.

### Tests
Full suite green (4654, +new). New: `test_pronunciation_backfill.py`, `test_pronunciation_mining.py`. Four export unit tests updated for the surface fallback. ruff clean.

## Summary
Closes ap-ba v1 review issue #1 (Tab.1 «tables-of-players» cells = «—»). Synth LLM correctly refuses to fabricate HQ/founded/IPO data when harvest snippets lack it; this PR fills empty cells deterministically post-synth via a 4-resolver chain.

**Resolver order (per cell):**
1. **Wikipedia infobox** — deterministic regex parse of `{{Infobox company|...|key=value}}`. Covers HQ, founded year, products, traded_as. No LLM.
2. **Corp /about** — LLM narrow-extraction (only when homepage is verified via Wiki infobox; refuses to guess URLs).
3. **Industry news whitelist** — Bloomberg/Reuters/Argus/IEA/IRENA/SEC via Tavily site-restricted, LLM narrow-extract.
4. **SEC EDGAR / HKEX filings** — Tavily site:sec.gov + site:hkexnews.hk.

**Anti-fab gate** (mandatory before any cell is filled):
- Substring-match in source text (normalized punctuation/whitespace)
- Field-specific format regex (year=4digit, capacity=`<n>(GWh|т/год|tons)`, share=`<n>%`)
- Hard ban on generic phrases («производит батареи», «major player», «various solutions»)
- Fail → cell stays «—», no footnote added

Augmented cells render as `<value> [N]` where N is the new ref appended to §5 sources. SYNTH_TABLES_PROMPT hardened to forbid generic prose explicitly.

**Acceptance** per ap-ba ТЗ:
- Hydrogen Tab.1 ≥21/35 cells filled (60%)
- LFP Tab.1 ≥17/28 cells filled (60%)
- 10% spot-check substring-match against cited URL
- Every filled cell has footnote-URL

**Failure mode:** non-fatal — if augmenter throws, report ships with pre-augment «—» cells; user still gets the rest of the обзор.

author: mvanhorn
body:
Losing the connection on a remote project, or restarting Zed, while editing a git commit message cleared the in-progress text, because the Git panel rebuilds the commit buffer from the repository and discards unsent input.

This persists the draft, scoped to the active repository's work directory, in the panel's serialized state and restores it when the panel is rebuilt from that state: at construction when the active repository already matches, and again in `reopen_commit_buffer` once the commit buffer loads. The restore only applies to an empty target buffer whose work directory matches the active repository, so it never replays committed or cleared text and never leaks a draft across repositories. The persisted draft is cleared after a successful commit.

Self-Review Checklist:

author: aleksandr-novikov
body:
Closes #104. Sprint 4 production-readiness — без флагов любая экстренная отмена фичи требует hotfix-релиза. С флагами — env-var + рестарт воркера за секунды. Минимальная инфра: ничего распределённого (Unleash / LaunchDarkly — отдельный тикет если масштаб потребует).

## Что внутри

### `app/feature_flags.py`

- `is_enabled("name")` читает env `FF_<NAME>`; truthy = `{1, true, yes, on}` case-insensitive; всё остальное (включая отсутствие env) → OFF. Default OFF не случайно: never-set флаг не должен случайно показать half-finished функционал в проде.
- `require_flag("name")` — decorator: `abort(404)` если флаг off. **404 а не 503/501** чтобы снаружи фича выглядела как отсутствующий endpoint — сканер не найдёт, мониторинг не заальертит на легитимный 503 во время cut-off.
- `wrapper._feature_flag = name` для интроспекции admin-инструментами.
- `KNOWN_FLAGS` registry + `snapshot()` для /admin.

### Реальный пример: `/api/forecast` (явное требование тикета)

```python
@api.route("/forecast/<table_name>")
@require_flag("forecast")
def forecast_endpoint(...): ...
```

`FF_FORECAST=false make server` → /api/forecast 404 без редеплоя.

### `GET /admin/feature-flags`

Read-only JSON-список `{name, env_key, enabled}`. **Write-API намеренно отсутствует** — toggling требует env+restart; runtime mutation нуждался бы в собственной auth/audit истории, out of scope для env-flag системы.

### Обновление существующих тестов

`tests/test_forecast.py::client` теперь выставляет `FF_FORECAST=1` — forecast-тесты должны тестировать forecast-логику, а не feature-flag машинерию.

## Acceptance из тикета

- [x] `app/feature_flags.py` с `is_enabled` + `require_flag`
- [x] Pydantic-settings не трогаем — через `os.environ`
- [x] `/admin/feature-flags` GET с текущими значениями
- [x] Один реальный пример — `/api/forecast` обёрнут `FF_FORECAST`
- [x] Тесты: декоратор 404 на off, 200 на on; admin показывает состояние
- [x] README: новый раздел "Feature flags"

## Тесты (23 новых кейса)

**`is_enabled` matrix** (parametrized): truthy/falsy/whitespace/unknown — все 12 кейсов.

**`require_flag` decorator**:
- 404 когда off (не 503, не 501 — точная семантика)
- 200 + payload когда on
- per-request lookup: toggling env между запросами flip-ает route без rebuild
- `_feature_flag` attribute сохраняется

**snapshot / admin**:
- `/admin/feature-flags` возвращает `list[{name, env_key, enabled}]`
- forecast row отражает текущее значение `FF_FORECAST`

**Integration** (важное):
- `/api/forecast/<table>` → 404 когда `FF_FORECAST=false` (точная формулировка acceptance из тикета)
- `/api/forecast/<table>` → не-404 когда `FF_FORECAST=1`

## Verification

- **618 passed** (+23 + 4 обновлённых test_forecast)
- ruff clean

## Test plan

- [x] Юнит-тесты на all paths
- [x] Real `/api/forecast` за реальным flag-ом, обе стороны
- [x] /admin/feature-flags JSON-shape
- [ ] Manual smoke после merge: `curl /api/forecast/users` → 404, `FF_FORECAST=1 make server` + same curl → 200/422

author: trevorwieland
body:
## What

Make the secret store + credential registry **durable**, and purge the in-memory and legacy import variants from production.

### `SecretStore.list(prefix)`
- New contract method `list(prefix: string): Promise<string[]>` returning the agnostic refs (never values) under a prefix.
- Implemented in **every** backend:
  - `InMemorySecretStore` — filter map keys.
  - `VaultSecretStore` — recursive KV v2 metadata `LIST` walk over the path tree.
  - `GcpSecretManagerStore` — `ListSecrets` + the original ref is now preserved **losslessly** as hex `ref0..N` **labels** at create time (the secret-id sanitization is lossy, so labels are how `list` recovers the ref).
  - `AwsSecretsManagerStore` — paginated `ListSecrets`, strip the configured name prefix.
  - `OnePasswordStore` — list vault items, title == ref.
- Conformance suite extended with list specs (under-prefix only, nested paths, delete reflection, empty result); all 5 backends pass.

### Durable credential registry
- New `SecretStoreCredentialRegistry`: each `CredentialRecord` is persisted as JSON in the **same SecretStore** under a parallel `credregistry/<base64url(ref)>` namespace. `list` enumerates via `SecretStore.list` + filters by scope/owner; `get` is a direct keyed read. The credential **LIST now survives an orchestrator restart**.
- Wired as the default in `main.ts` (built from the same `secrets`).

### Deletions (no compat shims)
- `InMemoryCredentialRegistry` removed from **all production code**; the in-memory double now lives only in `tests/helpers/inMemoryCredentialRegistry.ts`.
- Legacy unscoped top-level import routes deleted: `registerAuthBundleImportRoutes` (`/credentials/{codex,claude,opencode}/import`), the `authBundleImports.ts` module, and `/credentials/github/import` + its dead `githubCredentialImportSchema`. These wrote the secret store **without** a registry put, so their imports never appeared in the list.
- The org-scoped surface (`POST /orgs/:orgId/credentials`, `/credentials/me`) is now the **only** credential import path.
- Tests that exercised the deleted legacy routes were removed; the underlying `store*AuthBundle`/`storeGithubToken` functions remain covered by their own unit tests.

## Seam note for other agents
- The registry `get(ref): Promise<CredentialRecord | undefined>` signature is **unchanged** — the real-writer agent consumes it. Only `list`/durability were added.
- New `credregistry/...` namespace is reserved in whatever SecretStore is configured; it sits alongside `credential/...` values.

## Validation
- `just fast-check`: **green** (2303 passed, 70 skipped, 0 failed). Pre-push fast-check also green.
- Full `just ci` / `just smoke` run in CI on this PR.

author: kinaqu
body:
## What

Pins the **Problem→CTA** sections as glass cards that **stack and recede on scroll** (React Bits "ScrollStack" look), floating over **one shared, fixed Antigravity WebGL particle field** (React Bits), brand-tinted `#2F7BFF`.

Built without Lenis — native scroll + CSS `position: sticky` + Framer Motion scroll transforms — so the sticky nav, `#anchor` links, `whileInView` reveals, and in-view lazy charts all keep working. One WebGL `<Canvas>` total (not one per section).

## How

- **`antigravity.tsx`** — vendored React Bits R3F instanced-particle field; default color set to ArbiFlow `#2F7BFF`.
- **`antigravity-field.tsx`** — single `dynamic(ssr:false)` Canvas, `fixed inset-0 z-0 pointer-events-none`, scroll-linked opacity (faint over hero → present over the deck). Renders nothing under `useReducedMotion()` or below `md`.
- **`stack-section.tsx`** — `Stack`/`StackCard`. One shared scroll progress drives each card's scale→0.94 / dim→0.5 in its index window. Sticky stacking is `md+` only; below `md` cards flow as normal glass panels. Reduced-motion + SSR-safe.
- Problem→CTA condensed to fit one viewport as centered glass cards (no clipping).
- Footer set `relative` so the fixed field (at `z-0`, since body bg is opaque) doesn't overlay it.
- Deps: `three` + `@react-three/fiber` v9 (React 19).

## Verify

- `tsc --noEmit` ✓ · `eslint` ✓ · `next build` ✓ (23/23 pages)
- Puppeteer @1440×900: sections pin & overlay with scale/dim, **1 WebGL canvas** (context not lost), no card clipping (all ≤ viewport), `#opportunities` anchor lands correctly.
- Reduced motion: no Canvas, static cards, no hydration mismatch.
- Mobile 390px: no Canvas, no horizontal scroll, sections read normally.

author: mopeps
body:
In compact mode both tab panes share the one window scroll, so swiping
previewed the incoming tab at the outgoing tab's scroll position, then the
per-tab restore snapped the window to the destination's saved scroll — a
visible jump on release.

Keep the single window-scroll model (so the arrow overlay, trace-follow, and
hop-inspector padding all keep working) but give each inactive pane a
translateY offset of (activeScroll - savedScroll), so it previews at its own
remembered position during the swipe. SwipeViews now owns the per-tab scroll
memory and restores the incoming tab's scroll while resetting the offsets in
the same paint, so the outgoing and incoming panes stay visually put across
the swap and the page no longer jumps. App skips its own restore in compact
mode to leave scrolling to the pager.

author: robzilla1738
body:
## Why

`TerminalMetalRenderer.encode(...)` rebuilds three instance arrays every frame (`backgrounds`, `glyphs`, `decorations`) and previously created a **brand-new Metal buffer per array per frame** via `device.makeBuffer(bytes:length:options:)`. At terminal refresh rates that allocates and frees three GPU buffers on every redraw, adding allocation and copy pressure to the hot render path.

## What changed

Instance data is now copied into a small pool of reusable, growable Metal buffers instead of allocating fresh ones each frame. In steady state (a stable grid size) the render path performs only a `memcpy` — no Metal allocation.

### New: `DynamicInstanceBuffer.swift`
A triple-buffered ring of CPU-writable (`.storageModeShared`) Metal buffers.
- `upload<T>(_:slot:)` returns `nil` for an empty array, so callers skip the pass — preserving the prior "never create or bind a zero-length buffer" behavior.
- Grows a slot's buffer on demand with doubling headroom (`max(needed, capacity * 2)`) via `makeBuffer(length:options:)` — the only allocation, on first use or growth, never in steady state.
- Copies with `withUnsafeBytes` + `memcpy` into `buffer.contents()`.

**Why a ring:** the live-view `present(_:to:…)` path commits its command buffer *without* waiting for the GPU, so the GPU may still be reading frame N's instance buffer while the CPU builds frame N+1. Reusing one buffer would corrupt the in-flight frame. Cycling through 3 buffers, paired with an in-flight semaphore that caps queued frames at 3, guarantees the slot the CPU writes was last used 3 frames ago and is no longer GPU-referenced.

### `TerminalMetalRenderer.swift`
- Added three `DynamicInstanceBuffer` rings (bg / glyph / deco), a `DispatchSemaphore(value: maxFramesInFlight)` (`maxFramesInFlight = 3`), and a `frameSlot`.
- `encode(...)` now: `wait()` → advance `frameSlot` → create command buffer (signal + return `nil` on failure, so no slot leaks) → `addCompletedHandler` signals the semaphore (captures the semaphore, not `self`).
- The three `device.makeBuffer(bytes:...)` call sites are replaced with `…InstanceBuffer.upload(…)`. Pipeline binds, vertex/fragment bytes, gamma/texture/sampler, and `drawPrimitives` are unchanged.

### Unchanged on purpose
- Draw ordering: background → negative-z images → glyph → decoration → non-negative-z images.
- Image rendering (`drawImages`, per-image `setVertexBytes`).
- Storage mode (`.storageModeShared`).

## Tests

Adds `testRepeatedRendersReuseInstanceBuffersWithoutCorruption`: renders the same frame 6 times (past the ring depth so slots wrap) and asserts stable pixels, proving reused slots don't corrupt output. Existing golden-image tests remain the primary "no visual change" guard.

## ⚠️ Verification status — action needed before merge

Developed in a Linux container with **no Swift toolchain**; the renderer is Metal/QuartzCore (Apple-only), so it could **not be compiled or tested here**. Verified by review + grep only (the sole remaining `makeBuffer(bytes:` is a comment; the only allocating call is the helper's growth path).

**Please run on an Apple machine before merge:**
```sh
swift build
swift test --package-path Packages/HarnessTerminalRenderer
```
Metal tests self-skip when no GPU is present (e.g. headless CI).

## Threading note

Shared `frameSlot` / ring buffers assume `encode` is submitted serially from one thread. This invariant already held (the renderer shares mutable `imageCache`, `atlas`, and pipelines), so no new threading hazard is introduced.

A handoff doc is included at `docs/HANDOFF-terminal-buffer-pooling.md`.

author: ajanistewart
body:
Animate cards moving hand->table on a play, the trick resolving, and the phase-1 deal from stock into both hands, plus turn-indicator, trump-flip, and score-pulse touches.

The rules engine resolves a trick atomically, so clients never received the completed two-card trick (the opponent's finishing card was invisible). Expose a redaction-safe last_trick {cards, winner} on PlayerView so the client can replay the resolution. Both played cards and the winner are public; the loser's drawn card stays hidden (count only).

Frontend uses hand-rolled FLIP (no new deps): useAnimatedGameState keeps a displayView that lags the authoritative serverView, classifies each snapshot (play / resolve / snap), and sequences clone flights via an .anim-layer overlay. Reconnects and rejected plays snap instantly; all motion is gated by prefers-reduced-motion. The server stays strictly authoritative.
