body:
### Motivation
- Ensure reliable smooth-scrolling to in-page sections across navigations and service pages by handling pending scrolls and avoiding negative scroll offsets. 
- Centralize the `Navbar` so it's rendered once in the app layout and can change variant per-route instead of being embedded in individual pages. 
- Harden mobile navigation behavior and simplify service page config typing for clearer maintenance.

### Description
- Moved `Navbar` out of `Home` and `ServiceLandingPage` and added it to the root layout (`RootLayout`) with route-aware visibility and `service`/`home` variant selection. 
- Improved scroll-to-section logic by introducing `PENDING_SCROLL_KEY` session storage, making all scroll targets use `Math.max(0, y)`, increasing retries to 100, reducing retry interval to 50ms, and scheduling initial attempts with `requestAnimationFrame`. 
- Updated `navigateToHref`/`handleNavClick` to set a pending scroll key before navigation when needed and to defer navigation when closing the mobile menu with a slightly longer timeout. 
- Reworked service page types by replacing `ServiceLandingPageProps` with `ServicePageConfig` and adjusted `ContactSection` props to use the new types; removed page-local `Navbar` imports. 
- Small nav changes including renaming a nav item id from `contact` to `social` and added constants `NAVBAR_SCROLL_OFFSET`, `PENDING_SCROLL_KEY`, `SERVICE_NAV_PATHS`, and `NAVBAR_HIDDEN_PATHS` in `routes.tsx`.

body:
### Motivation

- Упростить поведение компилятора, убрав блокировку/модалку для «запретных» схем и позволить пользователю видеть результат без прерывания.  
- Расширить систему комбинаций знаков (больше реакций и новый элемент для «вода + лозы») и показать их в легенде.  
- Улучшить управление — добавить привычные горячие клавиши и redo/undo-стек для рисования.  
- Смягчить визуальные эффекты сцены, исправить отрисовку барьера и добавить декоративные цветы для комбинации лоз/воды, сохранив прежний UX и кнопки.

### Description

- Убрана блокировка/уведомление о «запретных» заклинаниях: `SpellCompiler._assessRisk` теперь возвращает только уровень риска, поле `forbidden` всегда `false`, и UI больше не показывает warn-модалку перед активацией. (изменён `game1/js/SpellCompiler.js`, `game1/js/UIController.js`).
- Расширена логика комбо и элементы: добавлены `bloom`/`prism` элементы и новые сочетания (`water+plant` → `bloom`, `light+water` → `prism`, и др.), а также обновлён `DEFAULT_SHAPE`. Комбинации показаны в легенде сцены (`game1/index.html`, `game1/js/EffectEngine.js`, `game1/js/SpellCompiler.js`).
- Визуальные изменения эффекта: палитры новых элементов, уменьшено использование additive-смешивания и уменьшены вспышки/glow, переработана отрисовка барьера (меньше пересвета, более читаемый купол), добавлена отрисовка цветков на лозах и мягкие вспышки (`game1/js/EffectEngine.js`, `game1/js/Particle.js`).
- Частицы и структуры: `Particle` получил `flower`-шейп, `EffectEngine` умеет эмитировать `bloom`/`prism` эффекты и помечать лозы как цветущие (`flowers`/`blooms`), плюс новые палитры (`game1/js/Particle.js`, `game1/js/EffectEngine.js`).
- Управление и отмена/возврат: добавлен `redoStack` в `StrokeRecorder`, методы `redo()`/`undo()` и очистка стека; `UIController` теперь привязывает горячие клавиши (`Ctrl+Z`, `Ctrl+Shift+Z`/`Ctrl+Y`, `Ctrl+Enter`, `Ctrl+Backspace`) и вызывает соответствующие действия (`game1/js/StrokeRecorder.js`, `game1/js/UIController.js`, `game1/index.html`).
- Вёрстка/стили: визуальная полировка без изменения расположения и поведения кнопок — добавлена рамка, мягкая подсветка сцены, блок с комбинациями в легенде и новые цветовые классы для элементов (`game1/css/style.css`, `game1/index.html`).

author: teoleg
body:
QEMU TCG was burning 3 host cores at 100% with the raspi3b machine -- one per parked secondary vCPU.  The park loop was:

    .Lpark:
        wfe
        b .Lpark

WFE wakes on the global event register, which gets set by any DSB / STREX / SEV anywhere in the system (including legitimate cache-maintenance and barrier instructions on core 0).  In TCG that turns the loop into a tight branch with a 2-instruction period -- one host CPU per parked vCPU, hot.

Switch to WFI.  WFI only wakes on a real interrupt, and timer_init routes CNTPNSIRQ exclusively to core 0, so the secondary cores have nothing wired and stay asleep.  QEMU's vCPU threads then actually block.

Mask DAIF before the WFI so a stray IRQ (none routed today, but defensive against future GIC mistakes) can't drag the core back into the spin.  Once we add SMP we'll undo this -- right now secondary cores have no work and are pure wasted host CPU.

Verified: kernel still boots and shell works.  Real check is on the user's box where they were seeing 3/4 host cores pegged.

Reconciling the ~447 contested Latin first-translation calls (#2234 #2). **Finding: not auto-reconcilable — no flag was written.**

The contested set is contaminated by upstream bugs that make any automated flip unsafe:
- **Language mis-tagging** — English *originals* (Jefferson's *Notes on the State of Virginia*, Spenser's *Faerie Queene*, *Washington's Farewell Address*, Reid) tagged `language: Latin` + `confirmed_first`. Not translations; also inflates the Latin count.
- **`confirmed_first` unreliable** — applied to non-translations and minor works where it just means "catalog search found nothing."
- **Qualified firsts** (`first_from_source`/`complete`/`modern`) explicitly allow prior translations — a `false` flag is often correct.

**Honest worklist** (`ft-reconciliation-candidates.json`, 447 rows): 45 keep-false · 11 language-mistag · 18 reference · 373 needs-manual-review.

**Recommendations** (none auto-applied): fix the language mis-tags (separate corpus-integrity bug), re-verify with a stricter prompt distinguishing "first ever" from "found nothing," per-work human review of the 373, and a fresh catalog-FT run for the ~1,323 unverified.

author: robrigo
body:
## Why
Every blockchain write burst (~1000+ W/s mint/transfer storm) makes the WAX reader fall behind, and twice it wedged into a multi-hour outage needing a manual restart. Root cause: the HIGH-priority `update_atomicmarket_sales_filters` drain recompute **spills to temp files (~1 GB/call, ~16–20s)** and starves the reader's block writes → deserialize queue backs up → `blocksUntilHead` climbs → watchdog (6h) kills it → restart **re-wedges** because the drain immediately contends with the catching-up reader.

## Fix — three layers for robustness
1. **Reader-priority drain gate** (`Filler.shouldDeferDrain`, hysteresis 200→60 blocks): the sales-filter drain + all mint drains **defer while the reader is catching up**, so the reader keeps block-write priority during bursts and post-restart catch-up. This re-introduces the gate removed in 1.6.3 (`bdebfd2a`) — which doom-looped with the *then-unbounded* drain — and is **safe again because 1.6.4 dedup caps the queue** at distinct changed keys while gated. Env-tunable (`ATOMICMARKET_DRAIN_GATE_STOP_BLOCKS` / `_RESUME_BLOCKS`). atomicassets mints moved from `isFallingBehind()` to the shared hysteresis gate.
2. **`SET LOCAL work_mem`** in the drain batch txn (`ATOMICMARKET_SALES_FILTERS_WORK_MEM_MB`, default 2048): keeps the recompute in memory instead of spilling ~1 GB to temp → each call ~1s, so the deferred backlog clears fast once caught up. Same pgbouncer-safe, txn-scoped pattern as the `statement_timeout` fix.
3. **Watchdog timeouts env-tunable + capped low** (`READER_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` default 15m, was hardcoded 6h): a wedged reader self-restarts in minutes, and layer 1 keeps the restart from re-wedging — multi-hour outage → self-healing blip.

## Tests
`filler.test.ts`: `shouldDeferDrain` hysteresis (defer >200, hold in band, resume <60). `sales-filters-drain.test.ts`: batch issues `SET LOCAL work_mem` before the drain query. `pnpm test` + `check-types` + `eslint` green.

## Validate post-merge / rollout
Confirm `work_mem=2048MB` actually eliminates the spill on real batches (time `update_atomicmarket_sales_filters(500)` at 128MB vs 2GB + temp-bytes delta in a calm window; tune the env if needed). Then tag `v1.6.6` → two-source monorepo bump → dev→blockchain. Observe the next burst: reader stays caught up or recovers in minutes, queue stays bounded (dedup) while gated and drains promptly after, no "Stopping in"→exit→wedge.

_(Feature-branch commit unsigned — local signing agent hiccup; GitHub re-signs on squash-merge.)_

author: sbuchweitz
body:
## Summary

Phase 5a: web-forms **Mode B (`contact.php` / PHP `mail()`)** + the form-mode selection infrastructure — plus a **comprehensive hardening pass over the entire forms pipeline** (you asked to harden contact forms as much as possible).

### Mode B + mode selection
- Form `mode` is part of `FormPublic`; the renderer picks the endpoint by mode — `contactPhp` posts to the exported `contact.php` (root-relative, on the customer's host) with a hidden `_form` dispatch field; all other modes post to the platform. hCaptcha is intentionally **not** applied to contactPhp (the platform can't verify on the customer host).
- Publish generates one `contact.php` (PHP `mail()`) for all contactPhp forms, dispatched by `_form`. **Recipients are baked server-side** (never in page HTML, never served over `/sites`); no credentials in the export.
- `GET /…/form-modes` exposes the admin-enabled modes; the editor adds a **mode selector** listing only those.

### Hardening (security + code review + a whole-pipeline adversarial audit)
- **Per-form storage cap** — silent accept-and-drop beyond `MAX_SUBMISSIONS_PER_FORM`, bounding storage-exhaustion from distributed floods.
- **contact.php**: POST-only guard, CORS + OPTIONS, 128 KB raw-body cap, `json_decode` depth limit, host-rate-limit guidance. **Verified against real PHP 8.4** (`php -l` + executed every control-flow branch: 204/405/400/404/silent-200/mail-path).
- **Mailer**: structured `from: { name, address }` (a special-char `fromName` can't break the From header).
- **FORM_JS**: prompts "complete the captcha" instead of posting a token-less submission the server would 400.
- **Schema**: reject control chars/CRLF in form `name` + `subject` (both feed the mail Subject); shared `MIN_SUBMIT_ELAPSED_MS`; contact.php uses the schema field-name constants (no drift).
- **Rate/body limits**: `rl(30/60)` on form-modes / single-GET / DELETE; 96 KB `bodyLimit` on the public POST; form-modes cached.

### Confirmed already-hardened (audit, no change needed)
SQLi (Drizzle), inbox XSS (React-escaped), email header injection (schema + nodemailer + PHP CRLF-strip), secret confidentiality (encrypted/masked/redacted), recipient never in exported HTML, cross-tenant isolation, hCaptcha fail-closed, CSRF (`sameSite=strict`; public `/f` no-creds).

### Accepted / deferred (documented in code)
- Off-site `redirectUrl` — trusted authors (owner/admin), legitimate external thank-you pages.
- Form recipient readable by same-project `content:read` tokens — forms are one MCP-authorable entity, recipient never in HTML; a `form:config` capability split is possible future work.

## Test plan
- contact.php unit (escaping / dispatch / guards / multi-form / empty) **+ executed PHP 8.4**, build integration, per-form-cap + form-modes API integration, renderer endpoint-by-mode, mailer structured-from, editor mode selector, and an HTTP **E2E** (enable contactPhp → publish → `contact.php` + `../contact.php` endpoint + recipient-not-in-HTML + `.php` 404 over `/sites`).
- `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm lint` clean; api **444** / blocks 145 / schema 116 / editor 91; `pnpm audit --audit-level high` passes; all 5 API E2E green on DinD.

## Scope
Only `globalSmtp` + `contactPhp` are server-routed today; `userSmtp` (Phase 5b: per-project SMTP) and `thirdParty` (Phase 6) are selectable-if-enabled but not yet routed (the endpoint stores + warn-logs them).

body:
## Summary

Brings `terraform/backblaze/` CI into compliance with **ADR 0004 Decision D** — *"the master b2 key MUST NOT exist in CI."* Implements the owner ruling (2026-05-26): **read-only plan key + workstation apply, no ADR change.** Decision D stays authoritative.

The `B2_MASTER_*` CI wiring predates ADR 0004 (live since 2026-05-09; ADR authored 2026-05-18). Decision D was written as a prescription to remove that condition, not a description of the status quo — the live jobs are the drift.

## Changes

- **`plan-backblaze`**: `B2_MASTER_{KEY_ID,APP_KEY}` → read-only scoped plan key `B2_BACKBLAZE_PLAN_{KEY_ID,APP_KEY}` (production GH Environment secrets).
- **`apply-backblaze`**: **removed from CI**. A CI apply requires the master key (`writeBuckets`+`writeKeys` = full B2 account takeover). Replaced with an inline comment recording why the job is absent + the supersede gate (ADR 0004 L302).
- **`terraform/backblaze/README.md`**: `## Apply (workstation only)` made explicit + new `## CI plan: the read-only scoped plan key` section documenting the minimal capability set, provisioning, and secret loading.

## Minimal plan-key capability set (verified)

`terraform plan` for this module is **read-only**:
- `b2_bucket.pipeline` refresh → `listBuckets`, `listFiles`, `readFiles`
- `b2_application_key.pipeline_rw`/`pipeline_ro` refresh → `listKeys`

Application-key *secrets* are stored in state at create time and **B2 never re-returns a key secret after creation** — so refresh reconciles metadata via `listKeys`, never a write. Verified against the pinned provider `Backblaze/b2 ~> 0.10` (`versions.tf`).

Minimal set: `listBuckets, listKeys, listFiles, readFiles`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `grep B2_MASTER terraform.yml` returns nothing.
- [x] `plan-backblaze` runs with a read-only scoped key; CI plan still posts on backblaze PRs.
- [x] `apply-backblaze` removed from CI (provably un-runnable — absent); workstation apply path documented.
- [x] Minimal plan-key capability set documented (verified against pinned b2 provider).
- [x] No change to ADR 0004 (Decision D remains authoritative).

## Validation (local, PR-time)

- `grep B2_MASTER .github/workflows/terraform.yml` → none.
- `python3 scripts/check_tf_apply_locking.py` → PASS (2 apply jobs, both compliant).
- `actionlint .github/workflows/terraform.yml` (shellcheck on PATH) → clean.
- `terraform fmt -check -recursive` + `terraform validate` (backblaze) → clean.

## Runtime-gated / cannot verify at PR-time — post-merge Test Plan

These require operator/account actions and are **not** PR-time verifiable:

1. **Provision the read-only plan key** in B2 (from a workstation holding the master key): `b2 key create noorinalabs-backblaze-plan listBuckets,listKeys,listFiles,readFiles`.
2. **Load `B2_BACKBLAZE_PLAN_{KEY_ID,APP_KEY}`** into the `production` GH Environment.
3. **Confirm a live `plan-backblaze` run** posts a plan with the scoped key on a PR touching `terraform/backblaze/` (proves the read-only cap set is sufficient for the pinned provider's refresh path against the real account).
4. **Retire `B2_MASTER_KEY_ID` / `B2_MASTER_APP_KEY`** GH Actions secrets once (1)–(3) are green (owner-operational secret deletion).
5. **Regenerate `docs/env-inventory.md`** (`scripts/env-inventory.py`) AFTER this lands on the canonical wave-13 branch — the generator scans working trees of all 7 sibling repos, so it cannot be regenerated cleanly from this worktree. It still lists the retired `B2_MASTER_*` and not the new plan-key secrets; a post-merge regen reconciles it.

## Note

The "full automation vs reminder-only" rotation decision and #331 calendar-reminder placement are separate owner-decisions — **not bundled here** (per the issue's closing note).

…security scanner services

Closes #412 — [Contracts] Implement Contract Registry contract Closes #384 — [Backend] Create contract documentation generation service Closes #381 — [Backend] Create contract monitoring alert service Closes #370 — [Backend] Add contract security scanner service

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ISSUE #412 — Contract Registry (backend/src/services/contract_registry.rs) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ What was done:
  Introduced ContractRegistry, a new backend service that acts as the central
  store for deployed Soroban contracts. It tracks each contract by a UUID-based
  id, its on-chain address, the target network (mainnet/testnet/futurenet/
  sandbox), the ABI JSON blob, the WASM hash, creation/update timestamps, and
  an arbitrary list of string tags.

How it was done:
  - Defined ContractEntry (Serialize/Deserialize/Clone) to represent a single registry record.
  - Defined ContractRegistry wrapping a sqlx::PgPool (ready for real SQL once a migration is added).
  - Implemented five async methods following the same pattern as the existing CompilationService and DependencyAnalyzer:
      register()   — generates a UUID v4 id, stamps created_at/updated_at with
                     Utc::now(), and returns the new entry.
      get()        — looks up a single entry by id (stub; returns None until a
                     DB migration is wired up).
      list()       — returns all entries, optionally filtered by network.
      deregister() — removes an entry by id; returns true if a row was deleted.
      search()     — full-text search over name and address fields.
  - Registered the module in backend/src/services/mod.rs.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ISSUE #384 — Contract Documentation Generation Service
         (backend/src/services/doc_generator.rs)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ What was done:
  Introduced DocGeneratorService, which parses Soroban/Rust contract source
  code and produces structured documentation in both Markdown and JSON formats.

How it was done:
  - Defined four data structs (all Serialize/Deserialize/Clone):
      ParamDoc   — a single parameter (name, type_name, description).
      FunctionDoc — a function entry (name, description, params, returns,
                    visibility).
      EventDoc   — an emitted event (name, description, fields).
      ContractDoc — the top-level document (contract_name, version,
                    description, functions, events, generated_at).
  - Implemented DocGeneratorService::generate() which iterates source lines:
      * Lines starting with /// are accumulated as pending doc-comment text.
      * Lines starting with pub fn / fn trigger a FunctionDoc entry, consuming
        the pending comment as the function description.
      * Lines containing env.events().publish() trigger an EventDoc entry.
      * The first non-empty, non-comment line after a leading doc block sets
        the top-level contract description.
  - Implemented generate_markdown() which renders a ContractDoc into a
    Markdown string with ## Functions and ## Events sections.
  - Implemented generate_json() which delegates to serde_json::to_value().
  - Registered the module in backend/src/services/mod.rs.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ISSUE #381 — Contract Monitoring Alert Service
         (backend/src/services/contract_monitor.rs)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ What was done:
  Introduced ContractMonitor, an in-memory, async-safe monitoring service that
  evaluates metric values against configurable threshold rules and fires
  severity-graded alerts when thresholds are exceeded.

How it was done:
  - Defined MonitorRule (id, contract_address, rule_type, threshold, enabled) and MonitorAlert (id, rule_id, contract_address, message, severity, triggered_at, resolved), both Serialize/Deserialize/Clone.
  - ContractMonitor holds two Arc<RwLock<Vec<...>>> fields (rules and alerts) so it can be shared across async tasks without a database dependency.
  - Implemented six async methods:
      add_rule()        — appends a new enabled rule and returns it.
      remove_rule()     — removes a rule by id; returns true if found.
      list_rules()      — returns all rules, optionally filtered by address.
      check_and_alert() — iterates enabled rules for a contract address;
                          for each rule whose threshold is exceeded it creates
                          a MonitorAlert with severity derived from how far the
                          value exceeds the threshold (info / warning / critical)
                          and appends it to the alerts store.
      list_alerts()     — returns alerts filtered by address and/or resolved.
      resolve_alert()   — marks an alert as resolved by id.
  - Implemented Default for ContractMonitor (delegates to new()).
  - Registered the module in backend/src/services/mod.rs.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ISSUE #370 — Contract Security Scanner Service
         (backend/src/services/security_scanner.rs)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ What was done:
  Introduced SecurityScanner, a static-analysis service that inspects Soroban
  contract source code for common security anti-patterns and produces a scored
  SecurityReport.

How it was done:
  - Defined SecurityFinding (id, severity, title, description, line_number, recommendation) and SecurityReport (contract_name, findings, risk_score, scanned_at, passed), both Serialize/Deserialize/Clone.
  - Implemented SecurityScanner::scan() which runs four pattern checks:
      1. Unsafe blocks (unsafe { / unsafe{) → severity: high (+15 pts). Reports the first line number where unsafe appears.
      2. Missing authorization — transfer or mint present without require_auth / require_auth_for_args → severity: medium (+5 pts). 3. Potential integer overflow — raw + or * operators without checked_add / checked_mul / saturating_ variants → medium (+5 pts). 4. Hardcoded Stellar address heuristic (G...AAAA pattern) → low (+1 pt).
  - risk_score is the sum of per-finding point values, capped at 100.0. passed is set to true when risk_score < 50.0.
  - Registered the module in backend/src/services/mod.rs.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Files changed:

## Summary

Both are **opt-in, shadow only, recommendation-only** siblings of the existing serving rho controller and the Training Safe Utilization Frontier v1.

**This is research / backtest / shadow-mode only.** No production execution, no controller default change, no robust energy engine change, no production savings claim, no oracle headline, no ML training.

## Phase A — bounded ingestion + schema validation

| Dataset | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **ShareGPT** (`RyokoAI/ShareGPT52K`, `old/sg_52k.json`) | **Implemented (bounded)** | HTTP-Range head download capped at 50 MB; lenient JSON parser handles truncation; unknown record / turn keys rejected; processed summary committed (~600 KB for 500 records); raw head gitignored |

## Phase A acceptance — Azure 2024 deadline-slack sanity sweep

> **Is there a visible deadline-slack-vs-rho slope? Does higher rho improve goodput/$ before deadline misses explode? Does the result remain positive under conservative assumptions?**

- At `deadline_slack=0` every candidate is **UNSAFE** (100 % deadline miss).
- At `deadline_slack=60 s` the frontier flips: every candidate is **SAFE**.
- `goodput/$` slope visible rho 0.45 → 0.55 (**+30.4 %**) with `deadline_miss=0`.
- Result remains positive under conservative assumptions (anticipatory mode, prefill_savings=0, pre-registered safety ceilings).

Pinned by `tests/test_batch_inference_frontier.py::test_azure_2024_phase_a_sanity_deadline_slack_slope`.

## Phase B — frontier modules

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `aurelius/traces/eval_schema.py` | `EvalWorkloadRequest` contract (separate from `NormalizedLLMRequest`) |

## Summary

- `computeVerticalOriginY` (and its mirror in the docs in-place editor) wrapped the middle/bottom offsets in `Math.max(0, …)`. On overflow that clamp silently fell back to top-alignment, breaking visual parity with PowerPoint / Google Slides — which keep the last line at the frame bottom for `'bottom'` and the content centered on the frame for `'middle'`, even when text extends above the frame top.
- Removed the clamp; updated tests (the prior "falls back to top" test is replaced by "preserves the anchor" tests for both middle and bottom, with top behavior unchanged).
- Updated the `<a:bodyPr anchor>` row in `slides-themes-layouts-import.md` to describe the new overflow contract.

Slide 22 of `Yorkie, 캐즘 뛰어넘기.pptx` (the "특징"/"문제" right-side description boxes) has fixed-height text boxes (~69px) whose two-line description content overflows by a few pixels. Before this change the text was pinned to the top of its dark band instead of sitting centered within it; users reported the misalignment on a shared deck.

Authors who want the overflow to stay inside the frame already have an opt-in: `<a:normAutofit>` / `autofit: 'shrink'`, which the layout pass honors before this offset is computed.

author: tyrbujac
body:
## What was happening

The `flutter-checks` macOS job kept hanging on **Run integration tests** for ~13 min, then failing — and it's happened on most recent runs (#27, #28, #30).

Reading the live log told the real story: **the tests all pass**, but the macOS *test-host app never exits* afterwards:

```
Failed to foreground app; open returned 1
✅ create MIDI track → save → reload …
✅ MIDI note in clip → save → reload …
✅ … (all 5 golden paths pass)
##[error]Final attempt failed. Timeout of 240000ms hit
```

On the headless runner, `flutter_tools` launches the app with `open`, which can't foreground it (`open returned 1`) — so the tool loses the handle it uses to terminate the app. A desktop app won't self-quit, so each attempt runs green then hangs until the 4-min timeout, retries, hangs again. The retry added in #24 couldn't help because the hang is *persistent within a runner*, not transient. The rate jumped after the Phase-3 title work — but the root cause is the foreground/lifecycle limitation, not our window code (this suite is pure-FFI, it never pumps a widget).

## Fix

Under `--dart-define=BOOJY_CI=true`, the suite calls `exit(0)` in a top-level `tearDownAll` once it finishes. Results are streamed to the test reporter as each test completes, so `flutter_tools` has already recorded pass/fail before the exit — **this can't mask a failure, the gate is preserved.** Local runs are unaffected (flag off by default). Retry trimmed to 2×5 min as a light net.

Run should now finish in ~1-2 min.

## What

Adds the **lone LLM step** Mimir was missing. When `classify_trust` flags an ambiguous web source (`needs_llm`) **and** a router/curator are wired, one `WORKHORSE` call (`mimir.certify`) breaks the `web_reputable`/`web_unknown` tie. Everything else stays on the ~95% zero-token deterministic path.

author: prixus
body:
## Summary

Adds a Claude Code project skill at `.claude/skills/aws-infra-best-practices/SKILL.md` that codifies the patterns and gotchas learned during this stack's initial bootstrap. Auto-triggers on any work in `infra/*.yml`, service infra templates, deploy/validate/teardown scripts, the Dockerfile, or workflows.

Also adjusts `.gitignore` so `.claude/skills/` is checked in (project-level knowledge) while `.claude/settings.local.json` (user-specific paths) stays ignored.

## What the skill covers

| Section | Lessons captured |
|---|---|
| ECS Fargate | Dual health checks, grace periods for Prisma migrations, deployment circuit breaker, Service Connect for east-west traffic, scale-to-zero limits |
| RDS PostgreSQL | Two-secret pattern (master-credentials JSON + database-url string), `ExcludePunctuation: true` rule, `SecretTargetAttachment` for credential augmentation, 7-day soft-delete window, major-version-only convention |
| ALB | Default 404 action, `/health` not routed publicly, unique listener rule priorities, path-based routing trade-offs |
| CloudFormation | Deploy/teardown order via `Fn::ImportValue`, stack rollback ≠ resource deletion, two-role IAM model (`github-actions-deploy` vs `cfn-deploy-role`) |
| Docker on Alpine | Multi-stage with `prisma generate` in both stages, `openssl` requirement, `chown` before `USER appuser`, `CMD` runs migrate before app |
| CI/CD | Job-vs-step retry granularity (deploy/validate split), OIDC trust policy locked to `main` |

The "Recurring lessons" section at the end captures the cross-cutting hygiene rules that would have prevented half this session's debugging if they'd been followed (run the prod Docker image locally before pushing; verify before documenting; don't reach for StackSets when plain stacks work).

## .gitignore change

```diff
-.claude/
+.claude/*
+!.claude/skills/
```

`.claude/` (no glob) excludes the directory itself so git doesn't even recurse — `!.claude/skills/` un-ignore never fires. `.claude/*` excludes *contents*, which makes the un-ignore work. `settings.local.json` stays ignored as before.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge
- [ ] In a future Claude Code session, open `infra/rds.yml` and ask about secret rotation — verify the skill auto-triggers and the answer cites `GenerateSecretString` only firing on create
- [ ] Verify `.claude/settings.local.json` is still excluded: `git check-ignore -v .claude/settings.local.json` should still show the rule matching

author: chen3feng
body:
Implements #492. `cc_library` / `cc_binary` / `cc_test` / `cc_plugin` gain three per-language compile-flag attributes, **in addition** to `extra_cppflags` (which applies to all C-family sources):

| attribute | applies to |
|---|---|
| `extra_cflags` | C sources (`.c`) |
| `extra_cxxflags` | C++ sources (`.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`) |
| `extra_asflags` | assembly sources (`.s`, `.S`, `.asm`) |

Use these when a flag is only valid for one language (e.g. a C++-only `-std=`/`-fno-rtti`) so it isn't passed to the others.

## Implementation
A single per-object ninja variable `${extra_compile_flags}`, set in `_cc_objects` by source extension (`_extra_compile_flags_for`) and consumed by the `cc`/`cxx` rules (GCC **and** MSVC). The value for each object is the language-appropriate list, so one var covers all three with no extra rules. The attributes default to `[]` and thread through the rule-entry functions exactly like `extra_cppflags`; non-compiling targets (prebuilt/foreign/cu) are unaffected via `CcTarget.__init__` defaults.

## Tests / docs
- `ExtraCompileFlagsForTest` pins the per-language selection (cxx/asm/c/unset).
- Documented in `doc/{en,zh_CN}/build_rules/cc.md`.
- pyright clean; full unit suite green (the 8 failures are the pre-existing Windows-platform tests).

**Verified on MSVC**: a `.cc` source gets `extra_cxxflags` in its compile (`extra_compile_flags = -DEXTRA_CXX_OK=1`) while a sibling `extra_cflags` value correctly does **not** appear.

author: seilk
body:
Closes #456

### Summary

Adds a small inspection API for system prompt assembly:

- `PromptSection`
- `SystemPromptBuilder.sections()`
- section metadata: `name`, `content`, `source`, `cache_segment`
- `cache_segment` is `frozen_prefix` or `dynamic_suffix`

`build()` output is unchanged. This PR does not add a cache implementation or invalidation policy; it only exposes the already assembled prompt in a structured form for tests, debugging, and future token/cache telemetry.

### Notes

- Frozen-prefix sections keep the existing stability behavior.
- Dynamic sections cover `session_context` and `previous_state`.
- Joining section contents with double newlines matches `build()`.

### Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src uv run pytest tests/prompt/test_builder.py -q
uv run --with ruff ruff check src/openjarvis/prompt/builder.py tests/prompt/test_builder.py
uv run --with ruff ruff format --check src/openjarvis/prompt/builder.py tests/prompt/test_builder.py
```

This gives OpenJarvis a stable inspection boundary between "the prompt as one runtime string" and "the prompt as ordered components." That boundary makes it easier to build:

- section-level token accounting: which prompt parts dominate context use
- prompt debugging: which files or dynamic state contributed to a prompt
- regression tests around persona and session-state assembly
- future frozen-prefix cache telemetry: how much of the prompt belongs to the frozen prefix vs dynamic suffix

Without this, each caller has to infer prompt structure by parsing the final string.

author: goodvids56
body:
## Summary
This PR adds graceful handling for unsupported matrix modes in the GLES1 on GL2 emulation layer. Instead of panicking when an application selects an unsupported matrix mode (such as `GL_MATRIX_PALETTE_OES` from the OES_matrix_palette extension), the emulator now logs a warning and silently ignores subsequent matrix-stack operations until a supported mode is selected again.

## Key Changes
- Added `unsupported_matrix_mode` flag to `GLES1OnGL2State` to track when an unsupported matrix mode is active
- Modified `MatrixMode()` to detect unsupported modes and set the flag instead of asserting, with a one-time warning log
- Added guards to all matrix-stack operations (`LoadIdentity`, `LoadMatrixf`, `LoadMatrixx`, `MultMatrixf`, `MultMatrixx`, `PushMatrix`, `PopMatrix`) to skip GL calls when in an unsupported mode
- Removed `GL_OES_matrix_palette` from the advertised extensions list since it cannot be properly emulated on desktop GL 2.1

## Implementation Details
The solution prevents matrix corruption by dropping matrix-stack writes while an unsupported mode is active, rather than attempting to apply them to the real MODELVIEW/PROJECTION/TEXTURE matrices. This allows applications that check for the extension and fall back to CPU skinning to continue functioning, while also tolerating stray calls from applications that don't properly check for extension support.

author: jdereklomas
body:
## Why

Derek flagged that Google Search Console showed the catalogue not getting indexed ("0 discovered pages"). Investigation cleared the suspected cause (Cloudflare bot protection) and found the real one.

**Cloudflare is fine.** Verified crawlers (Googlebot et al.) skip all WAF challenges via the top-priority skip rule; `robots.txt` and `sitemap*` are always reachable; sampled book pages return clean 200s to a real Googlebot UA with no noindex headers. The "0 discovered" figure was a GSC artifact — reading the sitemap-*index* row instead of the 6 child sitemaps (which carry all 16,119 URLs).

**The real drag is crawl budget.** The latest GSC Coverage report shows the biggest not-indexed bucket is **Soft 404 (1,241)**, overwhelmingly `/encyclopedia/<term>` pages — auto-generated thin concept stubs Google refuses to index. Crawling thousands of them starves the ~15,352 `/book/` landing pages, which are technically clean (200, self-canonical, no noindex, in-sitemap) but indexing slowly on a young site.

## What

Add `/encyclopedia/` to the `disallow` list in `src/app/robots.ts` (the Next.js route that generates robots.txt). This stops the crawl waste so budget flows to the catalogue.

## Scope

**In scope:** one entry + explanatory comment in robots.ts. Nothing else.

**Out of scope (deliberate):**
- `/search?q=` and `/author/` pages also draw crawl budget but are already `noindex` — lower priority, separate change if wanted.
- The 245 GSC "Server error (5xx)" entries: probed 1,536 book URLs (every 10th across the corpus) as Googlebot — **100% returned 200, zero 5xx**. Those were transient crawl-time blips; "Validate Fix" in GSC will clear them. No code fix needed.
- A few noindex pages (`/languages/`, `/gallery/image/`) are still listed in the sitemap — minor consistency nit, not addressed here.

## Verification

- Pre-commit import check + `npx tsc` (robots route) clean.
- Diff is the single `/encyclopedia/` disallow entry in the `userAgent: '*'` rule.
- No code path treats `/encyclopedia/` as an indexable ranking surface.

author: aniketmaurya
body:
## What & why

Snapshots always stored a **full copy of the disk**, which is space-hungry when many snapshots are taken. This adds a `snapshot_type` option so production systems can opt into storing **only the difference**, while keeping the self-contained full snapshot as the **default** for easy, no-surprises restore.

```
smolvm snapshot create <sandbox> --snapshot-type diff   # space-saving
smolvm snapshot create <sandbox>                         # full (default)
```

Also available in the SDK: `SmolVM.snapshot(snapshot_type="diff")` and `SmolVMManager.create_snapshot(snapshot_type=SnapshotType.DIFF)`.

## How it works

| | `full` (default) | `diff` |
|---|---|---|
| **QEMU** | flatten the qcow2 into a standalone image | keep the thin qcow2 overlay → only changed clusters are stored |
| **Firecracker** | byte-for-byte disk copy | copy-on-write reflink clone (`cp --reflink=auto`, falls back to full copy off CoW filesystems) |

- On **Firecracker**, the VM state (`vmstate.bin`) and guest memory (`mem.bin`) are **always full**, so a diff snapshot still restores on its own — `diff` only changes how the *disk* is stored. (Disk-only diff, per design discussion.)
- On **QEMU**, a diff snapshot depends on its base image still being present; restore validates this and fails with a clear, actionable message (with the missing path and the `--snapshot-type full` hint) if the base is gone.
- `snapshot_type` is persisted on `SnapshotInfo` (sqlite + postgres column with migrations) and shown in `snapshot list` and `--json` output.

## Compatibility

Default behavior is unchanged — snapshots are `full` unless `diff` is requested. Pre-existing snapshot rows (no `snapshot_type` column/value) read back as `full`.

## Tests

New unit tests for both backends and the CLI (full default + diff). Full affected suites green: `test_snapshot`, `test_snapshot_qemu`, `test_cli`, `test_storage`, `test_types`, `test_api` — 386 passed. `ruff format` clean on all changed files.

author: alkhatibsy
body:
## Summary

Next **P0 Foundations** increment (backlog F1.2). Adds the boundary that lets any UI — the upcoming Livewire/Filament packages or a host's own front-end — resolve a participant's **display identity** without the domain assuming host schema. Additive and backward-compatible.

### What's added
- **`ParticipantPresenter` contract** — `displayName`, `avatarUrl`, `handle`, `profileUrl`, `timezone`. The single, swappable presentation boundary.
- **`DefaultParticipantPresenter`** — convention-based resolution, in order:
  1. an opt-in model method (`messengerDisplayName()`, `messengerAvatarUrl()`, …) for hosts that want explicit control;
  2. conventional attributes (`name`, `avatar_url`/`avatar`/`profile_photo_url`, `username`/`handle`, `timezone`, …);
  3. a graceful fallback (`"User #5"` for the name, `null` for optional fields).

  Null-safe by design — a deleted participant, a non-Eloquent participant, or missing attributes yield fallbacks, never an error.
- **`messenger.presenter` config key** + container binding in the service provider, so hosts swap the implementation with one line.

### Why a contract (not host columns)
The domain stores only a participant's morph type + key. Reading host columns directly would couple the package to an unknown schema; a contract with a sensible default keeps the domain headless while giving the UI everything it needs.

## Tests
- 9 presenter tests (attribute resolution, fallback label, opt-in method precedence, blank-value handling, null-safety, container + config-swap binding) + contract-stability snapshot extended.
- **Full suite: 281 passing (653 assertions).** Pint clean.

## Context
Follows merged #91 (planning) and #92 (inbox scopes + API contract test). Product decisions accepted at defaults, so P1 is unblocked; next up: GitHub issue backbone and the `…-messenger-ui` package scaffold.

author: jasoncarreira
body:
Fixes **chainlink #298**. Surfaced by two questions during the Codex migration: "wire the usage view for the agent + ops" and "is muninn even seeing its Minimax quota?"

## The bug

The agent's **"Resource usage"** block (`rate_limits.py`) built `_LABEL` / `_WINDOW_HOURS` / `order` from a central list covering **only Anthropic** keys. So `minimax_*` (muninn) and `openai_*` (mimirbot Codex) windows:
1. rendered with the raw fallback label (`"minimax five hour"`), and
2. got **no off-pace burn-rate projection** — `off_pace_buckets` skips any key absent from `_WINDOW_HOURS`, so neither bot ever saw a "scale back / quota at risk" warning for its own quota.

The data was also **duplicated**: `billing.py`'s `QuotaProvider` classes each carried a literal `_*_WINDOW_HOURS` dict.

(Diagnosis: muninn *is* capturing Minimax fine — 4,943 `minimax_usage_ok` events, live snapshots, and the ops page already charts it per-provider. The gap was purely the agent-facing view.)

## Fix — provider-owned single source

New **`mimir/quota_windows.py`** declares each subscription type's windows once (logical key, label, hours, store-key prefix), organized **by provider**. Both consumers derive from it instead of duplicating:

- `rate_limits.py` → `_LABEL`/`_WINDOW_HOURS`/`order` from `store_label_map()` / `store_window_hours()` / `store_key_order()`
- `billing.py` → `_ANTHROPIC/_MINIMAX/_OPENAI_WINDOW_HOURS` from `<PROVIDER>.window_hours()`

Adding a provider or window is now a one-place edit, and the agent view stays in lockstep with what the pollers write. Acyclic: `quota_windows.py` imports nothing internal; both `rate_limits` and `billing` import it.

## Result

The agent now sees, e.g.: `Minimax 5-hour — 50% used — resets in 4h 0m — ⚠ on pace: 250% by reset`.

Value-preserving for the billing arbiter (derived dicts equal the old literals — guarded by a test). New tests: `test_quota_windows.py` (registry + anti-drift guards) + provider-key render/off-pace tests. Full suite: **3966 passed, 5 skipped**.

## Deploy
mimirbot picks this up via `git pull`. **muninn is on PyPI 0.2.3** — it needs a 0.2.4 release to get the Minimax-view fix (it's the bot actually on Minimax).

author: kevingyori
body:
**What:** 
Added an `Items()` method to the `DomainList` struct which returns a zero-allocation reference to the internal domains slice, replacing the deep-copy `Get()` method during read-only UI render and filter loops in `ui.go`.

**Why:** 
In Bubble Tea TUI applications, the render function and standard UI interaction loops execute very frequently. Continuously calling `Get()`—which performs a full array allocation and deep copy—on every tick causes excessive and unnecessary memory allocations, leading to high garbage collection overhead and potential UI micro-stutters.

**Impact:**
Massively reduces memory allocations and garbage collection pressure during navigation, rendering, and searching. `Get()` is now preserved solely for asynchronous `tea.Cmd` operations where data races might occur, maintaining perfect thread safety.

**Measurement:**
Memory profiling and GC metrics will show significantly fewer allocations per second when a user actively interacts with the TUI (e.g., navigating lists or typing in search). All existing unit tests pass, confirming no regressions.

author: nimrodbusany
body:
## Problem
For API-key auth the SDK emitted **both** `X-API-Key` **and** `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` (`_get_api_key_headers`). A backend that tries JWT auth before API-key auth parses the Bearer value as a JWT, fails, and rejects the request **before** the valid `X-API-Key` is considered.

Reproduced end-to-end against the optimization session routes:

| Headers sent | Result |
|---|---|
| `X-API-Key` only | auth passes |
| `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` only | 401 |
| **both** (what the SDK sent) | **401** |

This blocked every API-key SDK→backend session call (surfaced by the `FR-SDK-SMART-OPTIMIZATION-V1` live SDK↔BE E2E).

## Fix
Send one unambiguous credential — `X-API-Key` only. `Authorization` is reserved for JWTs; backend key validation (`/keys/validate`) already uses `X-API-Key`.

## Verification
- New regression test `test_api_key_headers_use_x_api_key_only_no_bearer` (asserts `X-API-Key` present, `Authorization` absent).
- `tests/unit/cloud/test_authentication_headers.py`: 20 passed.
- Live Python hybrid suite (bayesian/tpe/hyperband/frontier_scout) passes against a real backend with this change.

## PR checklist (policy surface: auth)
1. **Worst-case prod path** — narrows what's sent (removes an ambiguous credential). No new auth is granted; if anything it tightens the wire contract. Fails closed unchanged (no key → no header).
2. **Production-branch test** — `tests/unit/cloud/test_authentication_headers.py::test_api_key_headers_use_x_api_key_only_no_bearer`.
3. **Contract regeneration** — no schema change. Cross-SDK parity: matching `traigent-js` fix in a sibling PR.
4. **Public surface delta** — none (`_get_api_key_headers` is private; wire behavior corrected).
5. **Review threads** — n/a at open.
6. **Quality gates** — unchanged (no gate relaxed).

Companion backend hardening (so a stray Bearer can't lock out a valid X-API-Key) tracked in a separate TraigentBackend PR.

author: mwolter805
body:
### Background

Three contact services resolve a contact-select entity by `unique_id` on their `entry_id` code path, and each did so via `registry = hass.helpers.entity_registry.async_get()`. The `hass.helpers.*` accessor was removed in a recent Home Assistant core release, so on current HA that line raises `AttributeError: 'HomeAssistant' object has no attribute 'helpers'`.

Affected services (the `entry_id` branch only):

- `meshcore.add_selected_contact` (`async_add_selected_contact_service`)
- `meshcore.remove_selected_contact` (`async_remove_selected_contact_service`)
- `meshcore.remove_discovered_contact` (`async_remove_discovered_contact_service`)

### Impact

Calling any of these services **with** an `entry_id` raises the `AttributeError` (surfaced as a 500 to the caller) and the add/remove silently does not happen. The bare call (no `entry_id`) takes a different branch that uses `hass.states.async_all()` and is unaffected — which is why this stayed latent on single-config-entry installs that omit `entry_id`. Multi-entry installs, and any automation or UI that passes `entry_id` to disambiguate which radio to act on, hit the crash.

### The fix

Replace the three `hass.helpers.entity_registry.async_get()` calls with the supported module-level `er.async_get(hass)` (`homeassistant.helpers.entity_registry`, already imported as `er` in `services.py` and already used elsewhere in the file). This is a pure accessor swap — the surrounding select-entity lookup logic is unchanged, and there is no behavior change beyond the entity-registry handle now resolving instead of raising.

### Tests

- The integration's test suite passes — **66 passed** — including `tests/test_services_parsing.py` (functional-command parsing + contact-resolution coverage). `ast.parse` clean on `services.py`; a grep confirms no `hass.helpers.*` accessors remain anywhere in the integration.
- Verified on a live Home Assistant 2026.5.4 install: `meshcore.add_selected_contact` and `meshcore.remove_selected_contact` called **with** an `entry_id` now reach the handler (e.g. the "no contact selected" early-return) instead of raising `AttributeError`.

author: petlenz
body:
Implements \`tensor_projector\` codegen for the four presets currently exposed by numsim-cas at \`acts_on_rank=2\` (rank-4 projector on rank-2 tensors):

| Preset | Space | Emitted form |
|---|---|---|
| \`P_sym(d)\`  | \`{Symmetric, AnyTraceTag}\`   | \`0.5 * (otimesu(I,I) + otimesl(I,I))\` |
| \`P_skew(d)\` | \`{Skew, AnyTraceTag}\`        | \`0.5 * (otimesu(I,I) - otimesl(I,I))\` |
| \`P_vol(d)\`  | \`{Symmetric, VolumetricTag}\` | \`(1.0/d) * otimes(I,I)\` |
| \`P_dev(d)\`  | \`{Symmetric, DeviatoricTag}\` | \`0.5 * (otimesu(I,I) + otimesl(I,I)) - (1.0/d) * otimes(I,I)\` |

Component derivation (δ = Kronecker, d = dim) is documented inline at the override:
- P_sym_{ijkl}  = ½(δ_ik δ_jl + δ_il δ_jk)
- P_skew_{ijkl} = ½(δ_ik δ_jl − δ_il δ_jk)
- P_vol_{ijkl}  = (1/d) δ_ij δ_kl
- P_dev_{ijkl}  = P_sym − P_vol

## Design notes

- **Standalone materialisation, not applied form.** The cas IR can hand us a bare \`tensor_projector\` not adjacent to an inner-product (e.g. as the LHS of an outer product, or as the argument to a differentiation), so this emit always builds the rank-4 tensor explicitly. The applied-form short-circuit (\`P_sym : A → tmech::sym(A)\`, etc.) belongs in the \`inner_product_wrapper\` emit when that lands — same place numsim-cas's tensor_evaluator does it (\`tensor_evaluator.h:110\`).
- **(1.0 / d.0) literal**, not \`1.0 / d\` with an integer denominator — avoids any chance of integer division if a future refactor breaks the literal.
- **CSE** is preserved: the same \`tensor_projector\` DAG node used twice in one recipe shares a single \`auto tN = …;\` line (test \`ProjectorCSEReusesTemp\`).
- **Out-of-scope cases** (acts_on_rank ≠ 2, P_harm, PartialTrace, Young) throw with an actionable message naming the four supported presets. Tracked for follow-up if a recipe needs them.

## Tests

8 new tests, all rank/preset/dim/CSE/throw cases. 59/59 total pass.

- \`ProjectorSymEmitsSymmetricBuildup\`
- \`ProjectorSkewEmitsSkewBuildup\`
- \`ProjectorVolEmitsTraceProjector\`
- \`ProjectorDevEmitsSymMinusVol\`
- \`ProjectorDim2UsesCorrectDim\` (catches dim hardcoding)
- \`ProjectorCSEReusesTemp\`
- \`ProjectorHarmonicThrowsClearly\` (unsupported space)
- \`ProjectorActsOnRank1ThrowsClearly\` (unsupported rank)

Numerical correctness of the emitted formulas will be exercised end-to-end by the compile-check driver when a recipe using projectors lands.

## Stack

Based on \`phase-1.1-tensor-stubs\` (PR #42). Merge order: #40 → #42 → this.

Part of Phase 1.1 of the [NumSim roadmap](https://github.com/NumSim-Stack/numsim-codegen/issues/28).

author: noletu
body:
## Findings

| ID | Status | O que foi feito |
|----|--------|-----------------|
| SER-17 | ✅ Fechado | Guard CORS baseado em `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` substituído por flag explícita `CORS_ALLOW_NO_ORIGIN === 'true'`. Default fail-secure. |
| SER-31 | 🆕 Catalogado | `socket.server.ts` ainda usa padrão `NODE_ENV` para CORS (inconsistência arquitetural). Severidade baixa, PRE-STAGING. |
| SER-32 | 🆕 Catalogado | Rejeição CORS propaga HTTP 500 em vez de 403 Forbidden (semântica). Severidade baixa, PRE-STAGING. |

## Commits

| Hash | Descrição |
|------|-----------|
| a0aafdc | fix(security): CORS exige flag explícita para aceitar sem Origin [SER-17] |
| d67f14f | docs(env): adicionar CORS_ALLOW_NO_ORIGIN em .env.example |
| bba9ca2 | docs(audit): SER-17 fechado, SER-31/SER-32 catalogados (v1.22) |

## Mudança aplicada

**Antes** (`apps/api/src/index.ts`):
```javascript
if (!origin && process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {
  return callback(null, true);
}
```

**Depois**:
```javascript
const allowNoOrigin = process.env.CORS_ALLOW_NO_ORIGIN === 'true';
if (!origin && allowNoOrigin) {
  return callback(null, true);
}
```

E log enriquecido com `nodeEnv` + `allowNoOriginFlag` no contexto pra facilitar debug.

## Por que importa

O guard anterior dependia de `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` para decidir se aceitava requisições sem header `Origin`. Em containers com `NODE_ENV` não setado (undefined), o guard avaliava como "não-produção" e aceitava — comportamento fail-open em ambientes mal configurados (staging, novos deployments).

Com a flag explícita `CORS_ALLOW_NO_ORIGIN`:
- Default é `false` (fail-secure)
- Qualquer ambiente que não setar a flag rejeita sem origin
- Containers com `NODE_ENV` undefined agora protegem por padrão
- Dev local mantém o comportamento esperado setando `CORS_ALLOW_NO_ORIGIN=true` no `.env`

## Validação manual

Matriz 5/5 confirmada via curl:

| Cenário | Flag | Origin | Status | ACAO header | Bloqueio |
|---------|------|--------|--------|-------------|----------|
| A1 | false | ausente | 500 | ausente | ✅ Bloqueado |
| A2 | false | válido | 200 | presente | ✅ Permitido |
| A3 | false | inválido | 500 | ausente | ✅ Bloqueado |
| B1 | true | ausente | 200 | ausente* | ✅ Permitido |
| B2 | true | inválido | 500 | ausente | ✅ Bloqueado |

*ACAO ausente em B1 é esperado: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` ecoa o `Origin` da request; sem origin, nada pra ecoar.

A diferença A1=500 / B1=200 prova que a flag governa exclusivamente o aceite de requisições sem Origin, sem afetar a whitelist.

## Escopo restrito (intencional)

- ✅ Mudanças: `apps/api/src/index.ts` + `apps/api/.env.example` + AUDITORIA
- ❌ NÃO tocado: `apps/api/src/socket/socket.server.ts` (tem padrão `NODE_ENV` similar, categoria diferente — catalogado como SER-31 para sessão dedicada)
- ❌ NÃO refatorado: comportamento 500 em rejeição (pré-existente, catalogado como SER-32)

## Findings catalogados durante a sessão

**SER-31** — `socket.server.ts:17-26` usa `NODE_ENV === 'production' ? ALLOWED_ORIGINS : [localhost]` para CORS de WebSocket. Após esta sessão, há inconsistência arquitetural: HTTP usa flag explícita, socket usa NODE_ENV. Risco prático baixo (socket não tem branch "sem origin"), mas vale alinhar em sessão dedicada.

**SER-32** — Quando origin é rejeitado, `callback(new Error('Not allowed by CORS'))` propaga via Express error handler como HTTP 500 em vez de 403 Forbidden. Comportamento de segurança correto (request bloqueado), mas semantica HTTP subótima. Trivial mudar para `callback(null, false)` em sessão futura.

## Observação epistêmica

O plano original da Fase 3 previa "200 OK + headers ausentes" para casos rejeitados (comportamento genérico do pacote `cors`). O Claude Code identificou na execução que este projeto usa `callback(new Error(...))`, que propaga via Express como 500. **Erro do plano, identificado e reportado pelo executor sem mascarar.** É o ciclo de revisão funcionando.

author: mwolter805
body:
Fixes #243.

### Background

On instances with many discovered contacts, the recorder logs repeated `State attributes for select.meshcore_discovered_contact exceed maximum size of 16384 bytes` warnings and stores the entity's states **without** attributes. The mechanism is Home Assistant's recorder per-state attribute cap, `MAX_STATE_ATTRS_BYTES = 16384` (16 KiB). `MeshCoreDiscoveredContactSelect` carries every discovered contact in its `options` list; once that list pushes the serialized attributes past 16 KiB, the recorder drops the attributes for that state and warns. The live select keeps working — only its recorded history loses `options`, and the log fills with warnings. (See home-assistant/core#102964 for the recorder mechanism.)

Measured on a live instance: each option in the current `f"{name} ({pubkey_prefix})"` format costs ~31.7 bytes in the options list on top of ~112 bytes fixed overhead, so an instance crosses the 16 KiB ceiling at roughly ~500 options (~400 with longer names). This is a recorder-serialization limit, not a contact-count limit — the select itself functions at any count.

### The fix

Add `_unrecorded_attributes = frozenset({"options"})` to `MeshCoreDiscoveredContactSelect`. Home Assistant's recorder excludes an entity's `unrecorded_attributes` from the serialized attribute payload *before* the size check, so removing `options` prevents the overflow at any contact count.

Why this is sufficient (verified against the HA core recorder source): in `StateAttributes.shared_attrs_bytes_from_event` (`homeassistant/components/recorder/db_schema.py`), the recorder reads `state.state_info["unrecorded_attributes"]`, forms `exclude_attrs = {*ALL_DOMAIN_EXCLUDE_ATTRS, *unrecorded_attributes}`, serializes `{k: v for k, v in state.attributes.items() if k not in exclude_attrs}`, and only afterward evaluates `len(bytes_result) > MAX_STATE_ATTRS_BYTES` (`MAX_STATE_ATTRS_BYTES = 16384` at `db_schema.py:94`; the size check at `db_schema.py:581`). Because the exclusion happens before the size comparison, dropping `options` is enough. Note that `options` reaches the recorder as a `SelectEntity` *capability* attribute, but the recorder filters the already-merged `state.attributes` dict by key name regardless of an attribute's origin, so the `_unrecorded_attributes` exclusion applies to it.

A picker's `options` history has no analytical value (you don't chart or trigger on a dropdown's historical contents), so nothing useful is lost; the select still lists every discovered contact live. This is preferred over capping or paginating the dropdown, which would bound the contact count for the wrong reason (the recorder limit). Only `MeshCoreDiscoveredContactSelect` is changed — the other select entities' option lists are bounded by the added-contact / channel counts and don't approach the cap.

### Testing

**Verification split (stated plainly):** the change is confirmed **non-disruptive on a live instance**, but its **resolution of #243 is research-verified via the HA-core source read above, not observed live** — because no available instance has a >500-contact discovered set, and a synthetic >500-option harness was not stood up, so the before/after on the size-exceeded warning could not be observed.

- **Unit (`tests/test_select.py`):** asserts at the AST level that `MeshCoreDiscoveredContactSelect` declares `_unrecorded_attributes = frozenset({"options"})` — guarding the annotation against accidental removal or a typo. It is asserted via `ast` rather than by importing the entity class because this suite mocks Home Assistant (`tests/conftest.py`) so helpers can be checked standalone. This is by design close to a tautology: it does not exercise the recorder, so it does not by itself prove the overflow is fixed — efficacy against #243 rests on the source read above. Full suite **67 passed**.
- **Live (any density):** after deploy + reload on a live HA 2026.x install, `select.meshcore_discovered_contact` still lists every discovered contact and selecting one still drives the add-contact flow — confirming the "lost options history" change has no live functional impact.
- **Recorder before/after (the size-exceeded warning stopping):** **not run** — requires a >500-option instance, which was not available. Efficacy against #243 rests on the source read above; if a dense-enough instance becomes available the warning's disappearance can be confirmed directly.

author: imrshadow
body:
This PR refactors the MetaStream API, improves internal structure and adds documentation.

### MetaStream
- Added `OpenWrite` and `OpenRead` static functions.
- Added experimental `JsonMetaStreamReader` and `JsonMetaStreamWriter` classes. You can export serialize objects to JSON files.
- Added support for encrypted meta stream files with `LegacyEncryptedStream` which matches with Telltale Tool. This requires a workspace. The user also has the option to encrypt/decrypt using the `LegacyEncryption` class provided with a Blowfish key and an archive version.
- Added experimental support for compressed meta stream resources.
- Renamed the following MetaStream implementations: `MetaStreamReader`/`MetaStreamWriter` to  `BinaryMetaStreamReader`/`BinaryMetaStreamWriter`.
- Added a `Header` section to match Telltale Tool.
- Renamed some fields and methods.
- Added an abstract `Close` method.
- Reworked `Serialize` function to automatically preserialize.
- Made reading and writing processes more robust.
- Removed `PreSerialize`.

### MetaStreamParams
- Renamed `MetaStreamConfig` to `MetaStreamParams`.
- Replaced `SerializedClasses`, `UnregisteredClasses` and `UnregisteredTypes` with getter methods rather than storing them.
- Added `VersionInfo` array which holds all original class information which matches Telltale Tool.
- Added `IsCompiledVersion`. Currently it's unused, but in the future it should check if all classes are registered within the workspace.
- Added `StreamVersion` field that matches Telltale Tool and allows for more flexibility.
- Added `Encrypt` and `Compress` fields.
- Removed redundant `Version`.

### ContainerStream
- Added `ContainerStreamParams`.
- Removed dependencies with archive-related classes.

### Toolkit
- Add `Workspace` parameter in deserialize methods.

### Blowfish
- Added a constructor with a boolean argument.
- Fixed encryption.

### GameProfile
- Added `StreamVersion` to match `MetaStreamParams`.
- Removed redundant `MetaStreamVersion`.
- Removed `AreSymbolsHashed` as symbols are always hashed. `VersionInfo` now knows when it is hashed.

### VersionInfo
- Implemented helper methods.

### MetaClassRegistry
- Exposed `GetClass(ulong, uint)` method.

### Miscellaneous
- Bumped version to 0.3.0.
- Fixed a regression that did not allow files being copied to the output folder. Nuget is unaffected.
- Removed a csproj folder.
- Updated database files with the new changes.

author: robertoandr
body:
## Context
Closes #58 — born during PR #57 (Sprint 10F pagination test).

## Problem
`_paginate` had no upper bound on pages traversed. Tenants
with 100K+ tickets could trigger:
- API rate limit exhaustion
- Memory pressure (in-memory accumulation)
- Request timeouts

## Solution: Option A (warn + break)
- Configurable cap via `ZENDESK_MAX_PAGES` (default 100)
- Per-call override via `max_pages` keyword parameter
- Graceful stop with structured WARN log on cap
- Does NOT raise — dashboard tolerates partial data

## Design Decisions
| Question | Decision | Rationale |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| Hard fail vs soft break? | Soft break + log | UX > 500 errors |
| Cap location? | `ZENDESK_MAX_PAGES` env var | Per-env tunable |
| Default value? | 100 pages (10k records) | Covers 95% tenants |
| Override mechanism? | per-call `max_pages` param | Future flex |

## Changes
- `itgov/services/zendesk_service.py`: cap logic in `_paginate`, `_DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES` constant
- `.env.example`: documents `ZENDESK_MAX_PAGES`
- `tests/services/test_zendesk_pagination.py`: +3 tests (`TestPaginationMaxPagesCap`)

## Validation
- ✅ Suite: 178 → 181 passed (+3)
- ✅ Coverage zendesk_service: 80.26%
- ✅ Ruff clean
- ✅ `cap_reached` event asserted via `structlog.testing.capture_logs()`

## Observability Hook
The `zendesk.pagination.cap_reached` event is structured
for future alerting (Loki/Grafana). Recommend adding alert
when event fires > N times per hour.

### 💡 What
This PR addresses several technical debt and security issues identified during the codebase analysis. Key changes include:
- **Mojibake Fix**: Replaced all `\uXXXX` sequences in `app/admin/page.tsx` with their corresponding literal UTF-8 characters (e.g., `Teléfono`, `Proyección`).
- **Security Hardening**: Removed the hardcoded admin email from `lib/authz.ts` and replaced it with an environment variable fallback.

- Cascading renders in React components (updating state in `useEffect` on mount) can be optimized by setting the correct initial state.

- Improved developer experience (DX) and code maintainability.
- Better security by allowing dynamic configuration of administrative roles.

body:
@
## Symptom

Aurelius / Chronicler never appeared in `/agents` or as a summonable `subagent_type`, despite `.claude/agents/chronicler.md` being present and committed since #193.

## Root cause

The frontmatter `description:` value carried an unquoted **`Voice: Aurelius.`**. That embedded `: ` (colon-space) is read by a strict YAML parser as a nested mapping key:

```
ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here  (line 2, col 411)
   ... cc-018 lifecycle. Voice: Aurelius. The skill-mode count ...
```

Claude Code **silently skips** agent files whose frontmatter fails to parse, so the agent was dropped. The other 9 agents have no embedded colon-space and load fine.

## Fix

Wrap the `description` value in double quotes (verified with PyYAML — parses OK, `Voice: Aurelius` text preserved). Also future-proofs the field against other punctuation.

> ⚠️ Takes effect only after a Claude Code restart — the agent registry is read at startup.

## canon-cc-026 byte-identical exception

`chronicler.md` is a *byte-identical Codex-canon mirror*, so the defect originates upstream. Investigation results:

| File | Status |
|------|--------|
| `Codex/docs/specs/subagents/chronicler.md` (canonical subagent) | ❌ **has the defect** — upstream fix needed here |
| `Codex/docs/specs/skills/chronicler.md` (canonical skill twin) | ✅ clean |
| `SproutLab/.claude/skills/chronicler.md` (local skill mirror) | ✅ clean |

An inline HTML-comment **exception note** documents this local divergence. The exception closes once the Codex canonical subagent source is fixed and re-deployed. The user-global `~/.claude/agents/chronicler.md` was patched identically out-of-band (not in this repo).

## QA gate

canon-cc-008: agent-config diff under `.claude/`, not `split/` Capital code — no Governor jurisdiction touched. Pre-commit HR audits (emoji / hr12 / icon-text) pass.

author: poita
body:
Closes #352. Adds examples/mrtr/ (server.d + client.d + README + dub.json). Client is a self-verifying e2e test (exits non-zero on mismatch).

## What it demonstrates

Stateless draft MRTR (SEP-2322): a tool that needs more input ends the `tools/call` with `ToolResponse.inputRequired([...])` (no server->client channel), and the client resubmits with `inputResponses` + the echoed opaque `requestState`. Contrast with the blocking elicitation flow.

The `book_meeting {topic}` tool needs a date (an `elicitation` InputRequest) and an agenda (a `sampling` InputRequest). Round 1 returns both requests and stashes the topic into `requestState`; round 2 reads the answers + echoed topic and returns the confirmation.

## Self-verifying e2e (client.d)

- First call (no handlers) surfaces the raw `InputRequiredResult`; asserts the two InputRequest ids/types, the elicitation message, and `requestState == topic=Q3 roadmap`.
- After installing mock `onElicitation`/`onSampling`, the SDK drives the MRTR loop to completion; asserts the final text, structured content (topic/date/agenda), and `rounds == 2`.
- Prints `OK: ...` and exits 0 on success; exits non-zero on any mismatch.

## Verified locally

- `dub build -c server` and `dub build -c client` both compile.
- Streamable HTTP e2e: started `mrtr-server` on 127.0.0.1:8765, ran `mrtr-client` against it — exit 0.
- Root `dub build` unaffected (examples/mrtr is its own dub package; root dub.json not modified).

### Motivation
- Prevent physical runtime items (fuse, cable ends, repair kit, etc.) from being silently written into `digital_storage` when placed in the buffer.
- Ensure only true digital records/files (explicit `item_form == "digital"` or legacy digital record types) can be transferred to digital storage to avoid breaking world interactions and item semantics.

### Description
- Added `_is_digital_storage_item(item: Dictionary, allow_untyped_storage_record: bool = false)` in `BipobController` to classify valid digital records and reject physical items and cable/wire-end metadata.
- Updated `move_buffer_to_digital_storage()` to call `_is_digital_storage_item()` and reject physical items by emitting `This item cannot be stored in digital storage.`, returning `false`, and leaving `buffer_item` and `digital_storage` untouched.
- Hardened `move_digital_storage_to_buffer()` to validate stored records with the same guard and set loaded legacy records to `item_form = "digital"` so storage → buffer → storage round trips remain safe.
- Changes are limited to `scripts/bipob/bipob_controller.gd` and do not modify HUD layout, scenes, mission/power/interaction systems, storage backend, or project schema.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` to ensure no whitespace/patch errors and `python tools/check_gdscript_safety_patterns.py` which reported no hard GDScript safety issues (13 unrelated heuristic warnings in UI files pre-existed).

author: bojanrajkovic
body:
The state-machine tests and `atc-server`'s in-memory store tests each carried their own byte-identical `make_run_event` builder, and domain-struct literals (`WorkflowRun`, `Job`, `Step`, `RunnerInfo`, envelopes) were re-declared field by field across both crates. This pulls all of it into one source — the backend analog of the frontend `factories.ts` consolidation (#306).

- Add `atc-core/src/test_support.rs`, gated on the `test-support` feature alongside `TestClock`/`fixed_test_timestamp`. It exposes event-envelope builders (`make_run_event`, `make_job_event`) that keep the prior `octocat`/`Hello-World` defaults so existing assertions hold, and zero-arg domain-struct factories (`make_workflow_run`, `make_job`, `make_step`, `make_runner_info`) that callers specialize with struct-update syntax.
- Replace the duplicated builders in `state_machine/tests/mod.rs` and `in_memory_store_tests.rs` with imports of the shared ones; collapse the in-memory `make_job_event_with_completed_at` to a one-line delegation.
- Factor struct literals onto the new factories across `run.rs`, `job/tests.rs`, and `pure_application.rs` wherever at least one field keeps its default. A few fully-custom literals (diverse `RunnerInfo`s, one all-fields `Step`) stay as literals because a struct-update base would trip `clippy::needless_update` under `#![deny(clippy::all)]`.
- Document the shared fixture surface in `backend-server.md`.

`atc-core` is upstream of every other crate, so the gated module is reachable from any test target without a dependency cycle — the same seam `TestClock` already uses.

Deliberately **not** merged: `atc-server`'s `common/mod.rs` `make_run_envelope`/`make_job_envelope`. They use a different default flavor (`test-org`/`test-repo`) and a different job API (derives `started_at` from the action), and the wider integration suite asserts on those values — folding them in would churn ~30 integration files' assertions for no behavioral gain.

Pure test/fixture refactor: net −302/+238 across migrated files plus the new ~150-line module; no production code touched.

author: skchaudr
body:
💡 What: Refactored the `_reinforcement_score` logic in `ResultReranker` to use a precomputed inverted index mapping tags to document indices, replacing the previous pairwise overlap loop.
🎯 Why: The original implementation iterated over all other documents' tags for each document, resulting in an O(N^2) time complexity. This became a CPU bottleneck when reranking large amounts of results retrieved from Khoj.
📊 Impact: Reduces time complexity from O(N^2) to O(N * K) (where K is average tags per doc), massively speeding up the scoring phase for large queries.
🔬 Measurement: Verified functionality locally via existing unit tests, which continue to pass identically to the old implementation. Local benchmarks showed over a 7x speedup for 1000 records.

author: tixenre
body:
## Qué hace este PR

Tres mejoras de performance independientes, cada una con impacto medible.

## Cambios

### Backend — N+1 en `POST /cotizar` eliminado
El endpoint de cotización del carrito hacía 1 query por cada ítem para traer el precio. Un carrito de 10 ítems disparaba 10 queries independientes → ahora es 1 sola query con `IN (id1, id2, ...)`.

**Antes:** `N queries` donde N = ítems en el carrito  
**Después:** `1 query` para todos los ítems

Los combos siguen calculando con `precio_combo()` porque esa lógica es del motor de reservas — no se toca.

### Frontend — `/estudio` lazy loaded (35 KB code split)
La página de El Estudio (647 líneas de JSX) iba en el bundle inicial que descargaba cualquier visitante del catálogo. Ahora tiene su propio chunk:

- `estudio.tsx` → solo el `head` (meta tags, og:image, etc.) — 36 líneas
- `estudio.lazy.tsx` → todo el componente — chunk separado de 35 KB

Visitantes del catálogo no descargan código de /estudio hasta que naveguen ahí.

### Frontend — Zustand selector granular en `CatalogoMovil`
`useCart()` sin selector suscribía el componente raíz del catálogo mobile a CUALQUIER cambio en el store — abrir el drawer de fechas, cambiar la hora, agregar un ítem — re-renderizaba los 50+ equipos del catálogo completo.

```tsx
// Antes
const cart = useCart();  // re-render ante cualquier cambio del store

// Después  
const cart = useCart((s) => ({
  items: s.items, add: s.add, remove: s.remove,
  startDate: s.startDate, endDate: s.endDate, ...
}));  // re-render solo cuando cambian estos campos
```

## Plan de prueba

- Abrir el catálogo en DevTools → Network → agregar 5+ equipos al carrito → el request a `/api/cotizar` debe terminar más rápido (visible en Timing tab)
- Abrir `/estudio` por primera vez → en Network debe aparecer un chunk `estudio.lazy-*.js` cargándose por separado
- En mobile, agregar un equipo al carrito → el catálogo NO debe hacer scroll-to-top ni parpadear (señal de que el re-render evitado funcionó)

author: jay-nexusascent
body:
## Summary
Two independent chat-chart fixes (both reported in testing):

**1. Agent couldn't overlay actual vs forecast.** `make_chart` / `make_dashboard` / `update_chart` / `update_dashboard` typed `series.data` as `z.array(z.number())`, which rejects `null`. To align two series over different date ranges (e.g. actual revenue on the past, forecast on the future) you must null-pad the gaps — so `Input.parse` threw and the chart silently failed to render (the model still narrated "Here is a chart…"). Now `series.data` accepts `null` entries (a gap; the renderer already skips them — the `forecast` tool's own hand-built overlay relies on exactly this). `make_chart`'s description now tells the model how to build the shared-axis overlay. `seriesMissingData` helper signatures loosened to `Array<number | null>`.

**2. Chat charts rendered dark while the toggle showed light.** `getThemeSnapshot` in `chart-renderer.tsx` defaulted to `"dark"` whenever `data-theme` was absent/unknown, while every other theme reader (the toggle's `getSnapshot`, both `getServerSnapshot`s, and `layout.tsx`'s init script) defaults to **light**. That asymmetry desynced the charts from the toggle symbol. Now defaults to light.

## Test plan

- [ ] Forecast a metric, then ask "map actual daily revenue over the forecast" → a single chart renders with actual (solid) and forecast (dashed) on one shared date axis
- [ ] Chat charts render in light mode for a light-theme user (no dark canvas)
- [ ] Existing single-series charts and KPI tiles still render unchanged

author: romanvolumevision
body:
## Root problem fixed

A session **cannot see its own peer_id** — the broker excludes self from `list_peers` and never echoes own `from_id`, and registration never stamped the assigned id where the session could read it back. This caused repeated session-identity confusion today (two sessions, green + `u60ssaqv`, could not self-identify).

## What changed (file by file)

- **`server.ts`** — `stampPeerId(myId)` after `/register` writes `GUPPI_PEER_ID` into the process env (visible to child shells) + a pid-keyed marker `~/.guppi/sessions/<pid>.peerid`. New `refreshTabTitle()` re-renders + emits the self-identifying tab title via the AppleScript `set name` leg, wired **automatically** into the MCP `set_summary` handler + the initial-register + late-auto-summary paths. Title-emit failure never makes `set_summary` return `isError`.
- **`broker.ts`** — `handleRegister` writes the same pid-keyed marker (belt-and-suspenders backstop) via `body.pid`.
- **`shared/stamp.ts`** (NEW) — shared atomic (`.tmp`+rename) pid-keyed marker writer used by both server + broker so they agree on filename/format. Best-effort; never blocks registration.
- **`shared/tabtitle.ts`** (NEW) — composes `"<emoji> <Colour> · <peer_id> · CONV-<n> · <label>"`, dropping empty segments. Mirrors `scripts/iterm/tab_title.py` in GUPPI.
- **`stamp.test.ts`** / **`tabtitle.test.ts`** (NEW) — 16 tests: `stampPeerIdFile` unit, broker-register backstop integration (spawns a real broker with redirected `$HOME`, asserts the marker lands), composer / `profileToChannel` / conv-normalisation.

## Title approach (CONV-8207 preserved)

The title is driven through `user.name` (daemon paint) + AppleScript `set name` (in-session) — both bypass `Allow Title Setting: false`, so the directive against session-emitted OSC titles stays intact. **No `.mcp.json` env change** (marker is pid-keyed, not session-id-keyed).

## Verification

- `bun test` → **64 pass / 0 fail** (16 new).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- `bun build server.ts` / `bun build broker.ts` → bundle clean.

Branched off `origin/main` (does not include the unmerged `pr-c/ack-only-flag` work).

body:
## Summary

Implements the operator's "rimanere nel passato" requirement. For a **moderated tenant** (Total Trade), a contatto the operator has **not yet promoted** (`operator_released_at IS NULL`) is shown **frozen at its sent-time state**: every prospect *reaction* is withheld until the operator clicks **"Promuovi a lead"**.

The `/leads` list and hot-leads widgets already hide an un-promoted contatto entirely (PR #247). This PR covers the **one surface still reachable** — the contatto's **scheda**, opened from `/contatti` — plus the **global realtime toaster**.

## What gets frozen (until promotion)

- Engagement score (shown 0), advanced pipeline status (rolled back to `sent`)
- Email opens/clicks, WhatsApp/reply timestamps, portal sessions/time/scroll
- Portal activity timeline, inbound replies, **bolletta card**, appointment/contact-request highlight
- Hot-lead alert, follow-up state, feedback
- Reaction **events** on the timeline (allow-list: only operator-send / mail-delivery / system render+score survive)
- The **realtime subscription** on the timeline is disabled (no live reaction can stream in)
- The **global toaster** drops `engagement`/`conversion` toasts for the moderated tenant

What stays visible: anagrafica, tetto, impianto, rendering, ICP score, and the *sent* outreach facts (channel, sent/delivered). Everything reappears in full the moment the operator promotes.

## Changes

- **`moderation-freeze.ts`** (+ unit tests, 7 cases) — pure helpers: `freezeModeratedLead`, `freezePipelineStatus`, `isNeutralEventType` (allow-list ⇒ unknown event hidden).
- **`leads/[id]/page.tsx`** — `frozen = is_moderated && !operator_released_at`; freeze lead + events, blank replies/portal data, suppress `BollettaCard`, force the static timeline.
- **`realtime-toaster.tsx`** — `suppressReactions` prop; **layout** passes `ctx.is_moderated`.
- **`leads.ts` / `db.ts`** — select + type `operator_released_at` on the detail row.

## Trade-offs (documented)

- A **released** lead's *later* reactions also won't pop a toast (they still appear on its scheda) — acceptable for the trial.
- `blacklisted` status is **not** rolled back (compliance/suppression state — hiding it could let the tenant re-send to an opted-out contact).

## Test plan

- [x] FE typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) — pass
- [x] FE unit tests — `moderation-freeze` 7/7, `realtime-toaster` 11/11
- [x] FE ESLint on changed files — clean
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Manual: open an engaged-but-un-promoted contatto's scheda as Total Trade → only "Inviata", no score/timeline/bolletta; promote from super-admin → full live data returns
