author: dieterolson
body:
Consolidated fixes for four adversarial-audit estimation issues.

Closes #6892
Closes #6893
Closes #6894
Closes #6895

### #6892 — Reprojection residual ignored lens distortion
`project_pinhole` now normalizes camera-frame points by depth, applies an optional Brown-Conrady `(k1, k2, p1, p2)` distortion model (identical to the synthetic rig's `project_world_point`), then applies intrinsics. `distortion` threads through `reprojection_residual_from_points` and `reprojection_residual`. `distortion=None` (default) is the plain pinhole model, so existing callers are unchanged.
Test: `project_pinhole` with nonzero distortion matches the rig's Brown-Conrady projection to 1e-9; zero distortion == plain pinhole; reprojection round-trip recovers truth.

### #6893 — `_objective_residual` raised on non-finite, aborting `least_squares`
Both `map_estimator._objective_residual` and `multi_trial._objective_residual` now route the data residual through a shared `_sentinel_for_non_finite` helper that replaces NaN/Inf entries with a large finite sentinel (`1e12`). SciPy's 2-point Jacobian probe into an infeasible region (RNEA at a singular config, near-zero projection depth) now makes the trust region reject the step instead of raising and killing the whole solve.
Test: a probe into the infeasible region yields a finite large sentinel (not a raise); the full solve completes and recovers truth.

### #6894 — GRF gravity fallback double-counted weight
The no-contact-data branch computed `abs(np.sum(g))` and added it **once per contact body** — 2x for two feet — while also collapsing a generalized-force vector with `np.sum`. Now total support weight is `norm(g)` computed **once** outside the loop.
Test: one foot and two feet both report the single correct vertical weight (800 N).

### #6895 — Out-of-range eval times silently clamped
`_validate_problem` and `_validate_observation` now share `_require_times_within_knot_span`, which requires `evaluation_times` to lie within the trajectory knot span. Out-of-range samples raise `ValueError` instead of being silently clamped and flat-extrapolated against the wrong instant. Extrapolation is explicitly unsupported.
Test: an evaluation time beyond the last knot raises.

TDD throughout (red → green). Ruff lint + format clean; mypy, bandit, unit pytest all passed in pre-push hooks. DRY: the sentinel and span-check helpers are defined once in `map_estimator` and imported by `multi_trial`.

## Summary

Mechanical **phpcbf autofix sweep** against the WordPress PHPCS standard, per #39. This PR contains **only** the auto-fixable formatting changes — no logic or behavior changes.

### ⚠️ The #39 baseline was stale
Issue #39 cites **4,447 findings (~4,017 auto-fixable)**. That count reflected the tree **before** the recent cleanup work landed. This branch is cut from **current `main`**, where PRs **#72 / #76 / #77 / #83** (dead-code removal + topic-reply god-file split) already eliminated the vast majority of that debt.

Running the repo's own tooling (`homeboy lint --extension wordpress`) against current `main` reports the **real** starting state:

| | Errors | Warnings | Auto-fixable | Files with issues |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Before** (this branch base = main) | 0 | 38 | 5 | 20 / 102 |
| **After** (this PR) | 0 | 33 | 0 | ~18 / 102 |

So the autofix portion of #39 is effectively a no-op beyond **5 equals-sign alignment** fixes — the heavy lifting was already done by the merged cleanup PRs.

## What the autofix changed (high level)
- `Generic.Formatting.MultipleStatementAlignment.NotSameWarning` — equals-sign alignment normalization only.
- Affected files (both are one-shot migration scripts):
  - `scripts/migrate-phase-4-the-lab.php`
  - `scripts/migrate-phase-4-followup-cleanup.php`
- `php -l` verified clean on all changed files.

## Remaining findings (33 warnings, non-auto-fixable — follow-up)
These require human code judgment and are intentionally **not** touched here. Categorized for a separate follow-up:

| Sniff | ~Count | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `WordPress.WP.Capabilities.Unknown` | ~17 | **Config, not code.** Custom bbPress-style caps (`moderate`, `edit_topic`, `edit_others_topics`, `read_topic`, `assign_moderators`, `assign_topic_tags`, etc.) are real platform capabilities. Fix = declare them via the `custom_capabilities` property in a project `phpcs.xml`, not edit the calls. |
| `WordPress.Security.NonceVerification.Recommended` | ~6 | Real security review — read-only `$_GET` filter-bar / topic-loop reads. Confirm each is a safe read (no state change) before annotating/suppressing. |
| `WordPress.PHP.DiscouragedPHPFunctions.urlencode_urlencode` | ~2 | `urlencode()` → `rawurlencode()` — behavior-affecting, needs per-call verification. |
| `WordPress.PHP.NoSilencedErrors.Discouraged` | ~2 | `@$dom->loadHTML()` error-suppression in content filters — intentional for malformed-HTML parsing; needs proper `libxml_use_internal_errors()` refactor. |
| `WordPress.PHP.DevelopmentFunctions.error_log_error_log` | ~2 | `error_log()` debug calls in `topic-reply-formatters.php` — decide keep-behind-WP_DEBUG vs remove. |
| `Squiz.PHP.CommentedOutCode.Found` | ~2 | Commented-out code in `form-reply.php` / `topic-sidebar.php` — human call whether to delete. |
| `WordPress.WP.AlternativeFunctions.parse_url_parse_url` | ~1 | `parse_url()` → `wp_parse_url()`. |
| `WordPress.PHP.StrictInArray.FoundNonStrictFalse` | ~1 | `in_array()` needs `true` strict arg — verify type semantics. |

The single highest-leverage follow-up is the **`Capabilities.Unknown`** cluster (~half the remaining warnings): it's a one-line `phpcs.xml` ruleset config declaring the platform's custom capabilities, which would clear ~17 warnings at once without touching any PHP.

## Constraints honored
- Formatting-only; no behavior changes.
- Conventional commit (`style:`). No CHANGELOG / version edits.
- Worked entirely in the `lint-39-phpcbf-sweep` worktree.

References #39. Does **not** fully close it — the non-auto-fixable cluster above is the remaining work (a ruleset-config + small security-review follow-up).

author: bcoloe
body:
## TL;DR
Switches every SQLAlchemy engine in the app to `NullPool` so connections close immediately after each request, allowing Neon's serverless compute to auto-suspend between traffic. Adds `.env.example` with instructions for pointing `DATABASE_URL` at Neon's built-in PgBouncer pooler endpoint.

## Background
With SQLAlchemy's default `QueuePool`, 5 idle connections are held open permanently. Neon will not auto-suspend while any connection is open, so the compute runs ~24/7 regardless of actual traffic. `NullPool` closes every connection the moment its session ends — Neon can then suspend within seconds of the last request finishing.

Pairing `NullPool` with Neon's pooler (port 6543 / `-pooler` hostname) means each app connection is handed an already-authenticated Postgres backend from Neon's warm pool rather than paying the full Postgres handshake cost, keeping per-request latency low.

## Changes

### `app/database.py`
- Import and use `NullPool` via `poolclass=NullPool`
- Remove `pool_pre_ping=True` — no effect with NullPool, adds latency

### Scripts and bots (`scripts/daily_album_selector.py`, `scripts/backfill_group_album_avgs.py`, `bots/pitchfork_bot.py`, `bots/pitchfork_setup.py`)
- Same `poolclass=NullPool` change on each locally-created engine

### Intentionally unchanged
- **`app/conftest.py`** — test engine uses a shared-connection/rollback isolation pattern that requires a real pool; NullPool would break per-test rollback
- **`alembic/env.py`** — benefits from connection reuse across migration steps

### `backend/.env.example` (new file)
Documents the two `DATABASE_URL` forms side-by-side with notes on when to use each, so the pooler switch is self-service for any developer setting up the project.

## Required environment change
**This PR is only fully effective once `DATABASE_URL` is updated to the Neon pooler endpoint on the server.** The code change is safe to deploy before that; the app will fall back to direct connections until the URL is swapped.

To find your pooler URL: **Neon Console → your project → Connection Details → toggle "Connection pooling"**. It will look like:
```
postgresql://<user>:<password>@ep-xxxx-pooler.<region>.aws.neon.tech/<dbname>?sslmode=require
```

## Testing Instructions

### 1. Automated tests (no environment change needed)
```bash
cd backend
scripts/test.sh -q
```
All 787 tests should pass. The test engine in `conftest.py` is unchanged so test isolation is unaffected.

### 2. Verify NullPool behaviour locally (optional)
```bash
cd backend
python - <<'PY'
from app.database import engine
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool
assert type(engine.pool).__name__ == "NullPool", f"Expected NullPool, got {type(engine.pool)}"
print("✓ engine is using NullPool")
PY
```

### 3. Smoke test the running app
Start the backend normally and exercise the main paths:
- [ ] `POST /users/register` + `POST /users/login` — auth flow
- [ ] `GET /groups/` — DB read
- [ ] `POST /groups/` — DB write
- [ ] Cron script: `python scripts/daily_album_selector.py --group <id>` (select a test group)

All requests should behave identically to before; NullPool is transparent to callers.

### 4. Verify Neon auto-suspend (post `DATABASE_URL` swap to pooler)
- Update `DATABASE_URL` on the server to the pooler endpoint
- Trigger a request to wake the compute, then leave it idle
- In Neon Console → Monitoring, confirm the compute suspends within ~5 minutes of the last request
- Trigger another request and confirm it wakes and responds normally

author: merx666
body:
💡 **What**: Replaced full store destructuring (`const { ... } = useGameStore()`) with direct state selectors and `useShallow` mappings across 7 Tab components (`AdsTab`, `SurveyTab`, `RouletteTab`, `VoidClubTab`, `SeasonPassTab`, `UpgradesTab`, and `PremiumTab`).

🎯 **Why**: Destructuring the entire `useGameStore()` in complex UI components directly subscribes those components to *all* state changes in the global store. In a game where state properties (like the `particles` count) update multiple times per second, this anti-pattern causes massive, unnecessary React re-renders across the entire interface, leading to significant performance degradation.

📊 **Impact**: Prevents unnecessary re-renders in major UI components during high-frequency passive generation updates, drastically reducing React reconciliation work and improving the overall framerate and responsiveness of the application.

🔬 **Measurement**: Use React DevTools Profiler. Start a profiling session and let the game idle (with passive particles enabled). Before the change, the Tab components will re-render frequently (every second). After the change, they will only re-render when their explicitly selected state properties change.

---
*PR created automatically by Jules for task [17197797397474741149](https://jules.google.com/task/17197797397474741149) started by @merx666*

Optymalizacja subskrypcji store’a Zustand w komponentach Tab w celu zredukowania zbędnych ponownych renderowań i poprawy wydajności interfejsu użytkownika.

Ulepszenia:
- Zastosowanie zawężonych selektorów Zustand z `useShallow` w zakładkach Premium, Season Pass, Upgrades, VoidClub i Roulette, aby ograniczyć subskrypcje jedynie do wymaganych pól stanu.
- Zawężenie subskrypcji Zustand w zakładkach Ads i Survey do pola `nullifierHash` z użyciem bezpośrednich selektorów.

author: arishawke
body:
## Problem
Event blocks in the Week, Day, and 3-Day views are tapped via a raw
pointerInput gesture, which is invisible to the accessibility tree. As a
result, TalkBack and other screen readers could not activate an event in those
views to open its details. Month and Search already used Modifier.clickable and
were accessible.

## Fix
Add a Button role and an onClick semantics action to the event block, next to
the existing pointerInput tap (kept so it does not interfere with the
long-press drag-reschedule gesture). Each event now reports to accessibility as
a focusable, activatable button named by its title and time.

## Verification
- Gate passes (spotless, detekt, lint, unit tests).
- Inspected the live accessibility tree on-device: after the change the event
  block exposes a clickable Button node where the gesture-only tap previously
  exposed nothing.

Note: a full TalkBack gesture run was blocked by TalkBack's one-time onboarding
tutorial overlay, which scripted input cannot reliably drive; the
accessibility-tree change is the relevant, verifiable evidence.

author: s243a
body:
## Summary

- Update Clojure WAM `sub_atom/5` result materialization so produced `Before`, `Length`, and `After` values use lowered numeric literal terms.
- Preserve existing integer parsing for bound `sub_atom/5` numeric arguments.
- Add runtime smoke coverage for successful and mismatching unification of produced `Before`, `Length`, and `After` outputs.

## Why

The lowered Clojure WAM path represents numeric literals as interned terms. `sub_atom/5` previously returned produced offset values as raw JVM integers through the foreign-result path, which works for arithmetic comparisons but can fail when the generated code later unifies the output with a lowered numeric literal.

This change aligns `sub_atom/5` output materialization with the numeric representation used by lowered WAM code, continuing the representation-hardening work from text, numeric text, and length materialization.

body:
Four upstream PRs landed in one bundled sync: phone dice companion (#38, contributed by Ethros on claude-dnd-skill), mode switcher + dice-pending badge XSS hardening (#39, v1.11.0), light/dark/auto theme picker (#40, v1.12.0), and audio-controls legibility fixes (#41, v1.12.1).

All adapted to open-tabletop-gm conventions: GM terminology, relative-path scripts, `gm_*` localStorage keys for new per-browser TTS / phone / theme preferences, `GM_TTS_KEY` env var, key file at `~/.config/open-tabletop-gm/tts.key`. The `dnd-token` meta tag and the `dnd_device_id` localStorage key are intentionally kept as fossils across all otgm syncs — renaming them would invalidate existing approved-device bindings on operator machines.

## What lands

### Phone dice companion (claude-dnd-skill PR #38)

- `?view=input&char=<Name>` URL bindings (one phone per character)
- Three-tab phone layout: **Move** / **Roll** / **Sheet** (read-only character markdown rendered inline)
- `POST /player-input/dice` rolls server-side via `secrets.randbelow`; slot-machine reveal locks on the authoritative value
- `POST /dice-request` for GM-prescribed rolls — phones pre-fill (die, modifier, adv/dis, label, optional DC), lock all controls except Roll, pulse the Roll button
- `send.py --dice-request --wait` blocks GM narration until every prescribed character rolls
- Main display "Waiting on…" badge driven by `dice_pending` SSE event, replayed on `/stream` connect
- New `scripts/dice_player.py` — `dice.py`-style CLI wrapper routed through `/dice-request`
- New `GET /character/<name>` serves the sheet markdown for the Sheet tab — token-gated; both `<name>` and the active campaign value pass through an allowlist + length cap before `os.path.join`

### Mode switcher + XSS hardening (claude-dnd-skill PR #39 / v1.11.0)

- "📱 Phone Mode" button on the base URL drops a character dropdown populated from the existing `/stream` `stats` payload (no new server endpoint)
- "👁 Full Display" button bottom-left on the input view strips the query params and returns to the base view
- Shared `_escHtml()` helper applied at the two dice-pending badge `innerHTML` sinks. Server-side validation strips `` ` $ \ `` but not `< > &` from labels and character names; the fix is at the innerHTML sink, not the server, so future callers that want `<` or `>` literally in a label still get them through

### Theme picker (claude-dnd-skill PR #40 / v1.12.0)

Three-state Dark / Light / Auto toggle as a fourth row in `#audio-controls`. Default behavior is unchanged.

- Per-browser persistence in `localStorage["gm-theme"]`
- Anti-FOUC inline `<script>` in `<head>` sets `data-theme` on `<html>` before the stylesheet parses — no flash on reload
- Vellum palette carried over from the Neural Initiative implementation: parchment radial gradient, deep-ink narration with warm-light shadow, bronze accents, all block-identity colors preserved at darker shades. Body / vignette / particles stay dark for contrast
- `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` block mirrors explicit-light rules so Auto-mode tracks the OS pref live

### Audio-controls legibility (claude-dnd-skill PR #41 / v1.12.1)

- `.theme-label` was rendering at browser-default `<span>` size; folded into the combined `.speed-label` / `.narrate-label` / `.theme-label` declaration
- Three click-to-cycle labels (Type Speed, Auto Narrate, Theme) now look like pill buttons
- Default `#audio-controls` opacity 0.38 → 0.78; default label color brightened
- Per-row hover affordance — each `.audio-row` gets its own subtle background pill on hover
- `.dice-result` text brightened from `#c8a040` to `#f0d27a` with stronger amber glow + dark plate

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 display/gm-display-app.py` loads cleanly; all 5 new routes registered (`/player-input/dice`, `/dice-request` GET/POST/DELETE, `/character/<name>`)
- [x] `python3 display/send.py --help` shows new `--dice-request` / `--wait` / `--wait-timeout` flags
- [x] `python3 scripts/dice_player.py --help` parses
- [x] Served HTML: 133 `:root[data-theme="light"]` CSS rules, 6 `.speed-label` declarations (the new pill class block), `_escHtml` helper present, anti-FOUC inline script + picker module both reference `localStorage.getItem('gm-theme')`, `dice-result` uses `#f0d27a` brighter gold
- [x] Opsec scan clean on diff regions (no `/Users/sph33nx`, no `~/Documents` paths, no internal-codebase provenance language)
- [x] All adapted `gm_*` localStorage keys verified in served HTML; `dnd_device_id` left as fossil per established otgm convention

- [ ] Manual: phone connects at `?view=input&char=X` → three tabs work, dice pad rolls, sheet renders from `/character/X` markdown

## Summary

This PR delivers two major features:

1. **Controlled Admin Access Mode** — A secure, token-gated endpoint that allows an authorized operator to open the internal app with an admin session without typing credentials. The mode is disabled by default, requires a strong token, and is blocked in production unless explicitly opted in.

2. **Landing Navigation Restructure** — Reorganizes the landing header into 5 accessible dropdown groups, moves the section up/down controls to the bottom-right corner (reserving the central-right rail for a future social rail), and adds comprehensive i18n support for all navigation labels in ES/EN/DE.

## Key Changes

### Admin Access Mode
- **`src/lib/security/adminAccess.ts`** (new) — Pure decision logic with constant-time token comparison, environment resolution, and configuration parsing
- **`src/app/api/internal/admin-access/route.ts`** (new) — GET endpoint that validates guards, creates an admin session cookie, and redirects; returns generic 404 on any failure without leaking reasons
- **`docs/ADMIN_ACCESS_MODE.md`** (new) — Operational guide covering environment variables, behavior rules, Vercel setup, token rotation, and security risks
- **`tests/admin-access.test.ts`** (new) — Comprehensive test suite covering decision logic, helpers, HTTP route behavior, and safety guarantees (no token exposure in landing or logs)
- **`.env.example`** — Added 6 new environment variables with safe defaults

### Landing Navigation
- **`src/components/landing/navigation.ts`** (new) — Single source of truth defining 5 nav groups (Producto, Proceso, Piloto, Confianza, Recursos) and all section IDs
- **`src/components/landing/LandingHeader.tsx`** — Rewritten with accessible dropdown groups (keyboard/click support, Escape handling, aria-expanded/aria-controls) and full grouped mobile drawer
- **`src/components/landing/SectionNavigator.tsx`** — Updated to use centralized `LANDING_SECTION_IDS`; documents reserved central-right rail for future social features
- **Section components** — Added stable `id` attributes to AdvantagesSection (`ventajas`), StatusSection (`estado`), AppAvailableSection (`app-disponible`), and NoPromiseSection (`limites-mvp`)
- **`src/lib/i18n/landing.tsx`** — Added `navMenu` structure with groups and items in ES/EN/DE
- **`src/app/globals.css`** — New dropdown styles, `scroll-margin-top` for anchored sections, repositioned `.l-section-nav` to bottom-right with safe-area insets

author: phillt
body:
## Summary

Phase C of the Ink REPL migration (#214). Builds the message-store seam, wires `outputHook` and the main runner through it (sink-aware), and has `<Thread>` render an in-flight `<StreamingAssistantMessage>` that subscribes via `useSyncExternalStore`. Sub-agents and tool-wrappers continue to bulk-render at step completion. When no sink is registered (i.e., the legacy REPL), every code path falls through to its current stdout behavior unchanged.

**Design constraint**: per the user's "expandability + modular design at the center" directive, this PR uses one module-level sink slot rather than threading the sink through every `AgentDefinition` signature. Adding a future Ink-side consumer (e.g. a recording sink for tests, or a debug overlay) only needs to call `setOutputSink(...)` — no agent-definition fan-out.

### Scope decisions

- **Streaming is main-agent only.** Sub-agents stay on `generateText` so concurrent dispatches don't interleave token streams in the terminal. The `AgentDefinition.streaming` flag is the modular toggle.
- **Status helpers** (`printInfo` / `printWarning` / `printError` / `printDebug`) stay on stdout until Phase D. The Ink preview just won't show those lines until D.
- **Single user-facing cutover** rule still holds: users still see the legacy readline REPL after this PR. The Ink tree is exercised via `scripts/preview-ink.mjs`. Phase D flips the default and deletes the bespoke layer in one PR.

## What changed

**New files**
- `src/framework/hooks/output-sink.ts` — module-level `OutputSink` slot + `StreamEvent` union (text-delta / tool-call / tool-result).
- `src/ui/message-store.ts` — `useSyncExternalStore`-compatible class implementing `OutputSink`; snapshot identity flips per append.
- `src/ui/__tests__/message-store.test.ts` — 8 pure data-flow tests.

**Modified**
- `src/framework/hooks/output.ts` — `onStepFinish` branches on `getOutputSink()`. Sink path pushes tool events for every agent and `text-delta` only for the main agent (`prefix === undefined`).
- `src/framework/runner.ts` — `AgentSpec.useStreaming` + `onTextDelta`; `runStreaming` uses `streamText`, drains `textStream`, then awaits the `StreamTextResult` promises to assemble a `GenerateTextResult`-shape so downstream callers (provenance, plan strip, response-style, format hooks) see no shape difference.
- `src/framework/agents/types.ts` + `run.ts` — `AgentDefinition.streaming` flag; `run.ts` opts into streaming only when the definition declares it AND an output sink is registered.
- `src/framework/agents/main.ts` — `streaming: true` on the main definition only.
- `src/ui/Thread.tsx` — `<StreamingAssistantMessage>` subscribes via `useSyncExternalStore`; groups events by `agentLabel`; pairs tool-calls with results by `callId`.
- `src/ui/App.tsx` — one `MessageStore` per `<App>` lifecycle (`useRef`), `setOutputSink` on mount / `null` on unmount, `reset()` at start of every turn.
- `src/framework/hooks/__tests__/output.test.ts` — +3 sink-branch tests.
- `scripts/preview-ink.mjs` — header doc updated to describe new streaming behavior.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` clean.
- [x] `npm test` — 2684 pass (2673 existing + 8 message-store + 3 sink-branch).
- [x] `git diff --stat` confined to `src/ui/`, `src/framework/hooks/`, `src/framework/runner.ts`, `src/framework/agents/{types,run,main}.ts`, `scripts/preview-ink.mjs`. No changes to `src/repl.ts` / `src/index.ts` / `src/output.ts` / `src/agent.ts`.
- [ ] Manual via \`tsx scripts/preview-ink.mjs\`:
  - Long assistant message renders **token-by-token**, not bulk-at-step-end.
  - Sub-agent dispatch still appears at step completion (bulk) — confirms the modular boundary.
  - Tool calls render inline with their result paired below by `callId`.
  - Citations (`[^Sn]`) appear inline in the streamed text.
  - Esc mid-stream — agent aborts; partial in-flight message remains visible.
  - Legacy `bernard` REPL behaves identically — no sink registered, `sink === null` branch unchanged.

Closes #214

body:
Addresses "I don't see many new supporting blog ideas." Frontend-only.

## Why
Blog ideas live in the **legacy blog pipeline** (`blog_posts.status='idea'`), which is a *different surface* from the opportunity queue shown at `/admin/content-engine`. So a backlog of ~20 curated, on-voice, localized blog ideas was stranded out of view — making it look like the engine wasn't producing blog content.

(Investigated the alternative — having the GSC engine mine informational queries → blogs — and the data killed it: informational search demand for this site is ~nil (19 queries / 63 impressions; 1 candidate), vs 1,385 service-intent queries. Proactive idea generation, independent of GSC demand, is the right source — and it already produced the 20 ideas.)

## Change
A third **"Blog Ideas"** tab on `AutonomousContentReviewPage` that surfaces `idea` + `draft` rows from the **existing** `/admin/content/blog` endpoints, with per-row actions:
- **Generate** (idea → draft): `POST /blog/:id/generate` (blog writer)
- **Publish PR** (draft → review-only Astro PR): `POST /blog/:id/publish-astro` — Codex + content-guardrails run before merge (per #1450)

KPIs show idea / draft / published counts; drafts list first (closer to publish).

## Scope / safety
- **Frontend-only** — reuses existing endpoints; no engine, queue, scoring, or schema changes.
- Matches the page's existing inline-style / `D`-palette pattern (Tier 2 page; no Tailwind/components-ui mixing).
- esbuild bundle clean; all new identifiers used.

body:
## Summary

Plan §14 **R-T1** (+ R-A4 doc): replace all `let graph: any` in the graph builders with a typed helper.

LangGraph's `StateGraph` fluent API narrows the node-name type parameter on every `.addNode()` / `.addEdge()`, so the loop-accumulate pattern (`let graph: any` then `graph = graph.addEdge(...)`) had to erase to `any` + `biome-ignore` in **6** builders (the plan said 4 — it was 6: layer1/2/3, layer4 ×2, daily_cycle).

### Fix — `mosaic-ts/src/graph/_edges.ts`
`chainEdges(graph, edges)` adds edges by **side effect** (`StateGraph` mutates in place and returns `this`), deriving the accepted endpoint type from the graph's **own** `addEdge` signature via `Parameters<G["addEdge"]>` — so there's no `any` and no hand-rebuilt node-name union that could drift from LangGraph's real types.

- **layer1/2/3**: typed `.addNode()` chain + `chainEdges` for the fan-out/fan-in loops.
- **layer4 (×2) + daily_cycle**: plain typed fluent chains (no loop needed); `daily_cycle` keeps `addConditionalEdges` inline.
- All 6 `let graph: any` + `biome-ignore` removed.

### Also
- **R-A4 (doc)**: `ingest_full` docstring clarifies `timeout` is per-Tushare-request, not a wall-clock cap.
- **plan §14**: R-T1 + R-A4 closed (R-P1/R-A1/R-A3 stay deferred with rationale). **§11.8.1** deferred candidates marked delivered: #1 inject_context, #2 results exporter (#40), #3 ETF CLI (#35).

### Tests
`edges.test.ts` (side-effect + empty-list); **302 TS tests**; full Python suite; ruff + tsc + biome clean. Graph behavior is unchanged — the layer/daily-cycle tests that compile + invoke the graphs all pass.

> Final PR of the 3-batch plan-cleanup (with merged #40 exporter + #41 property-data). After this, the only open §14 items are the explicitly-deferred R-P1/R-A1/R-A3 ("add when needed").

author: linuxdynasty
body:
## What

Adds the `securitylake` AWS cloud-collector scanner (aws/J wave). It reads
Amazon Security Lake control-plane metadata and emits three resource families
plus seven cross-service graph edges.

- **Resources:** `aws_securitylake_data_lake` (per-Region data lake config:
  ARN, Region, backing S3 bucket ARN, KMS key reference, create/update status,
  lifecycle expiration days, transition count, replication Regions),
  `aws_securitylake_log_source` (AWS-native or third-party custom source name,
  version, collection account/region, custom-source provider role ARN),
  `aws_securitylake_subscriber` (ARN, id, name, status, access types, principal
  account, role ARN, S3 bucket ARN, granted source names, timestamps).
- **Edges (each keyed to the target scanner's published `resource_id`, skipped
  rather than dangled when unresolvable):**
  - data lake -> S3 bucket (`aws_s3_bucket`, reported bucket ARN)
  - data lake -> KMS key (`aws_kms_key`, customer key id/ARN; `S3_MANAGED` /
    `AWS_OWNED_KMS_KEY` sentinels emit no edge)
  - data lake -> Lake Formation registered resource (`aws_lakeformation_resource`,
    keyed by the data lake's S3 bucket ARN)
  - log source -> data lake (`aws_securitylake_data_lake`, data lake ARN)
  - log source -> IAM role (`aws_iam_role`, custom-source provider role ARN)
  - subscriber -> IAM role (`aws_iam_role`, role ARN)
  - subscriber -> S3 bucket (`aws_s3_bucket`, reported bucket ARN)

## Why

Extends AWS coverage under epic #51 so Security Lake's data lake, sources, and
subscribers join the code-to-cloud graph against existing S3, KMS, IAM, and
Lake Formation nodes.

## Scope / guarantees

- **Metadata-only.** Reads only `ListDataLakes` (Region-scoped),
  `ListLogSources`, and `ListSubscribers`. Never reads ingested security log
  records or object contents; never persists the subscriber external id (a
  trust-establishment credential) or the subscriber endpoint (a private
  notification destination); never mutates Security Lake state. A reflection
  guard on the SDK `apiClient` interface fails the build if `GetSubscriber`, a
  notification/exception-subscription read, or any mutation method is ever
  added.
- **Partition-aware.** Uses the bucket and role ARNs AWS already reports
  (partition-correct); never synthesizes `arn:aws:`.
- **Graph-join-safe (#804).** Every relationship sets a declared
  `awscloud.ResourceType*` `target_type` and a `target_resource_id` matching
  the target scanner. No data-lake-to-Glue edge is emitted because the Security
  Lake API reports no resolvable Glue identifier — that edge is skipped, not
  dangled.
- One append-only `bindings.go` blank-import line; one coverage-doc row in
  `collector-aws-cloud-scanners.md`; the coverage-matrix doc is untouched.

## Verification (run from the worktree, all green after rebase onto latest origin/main)

```
cd go && go build ./...
cd go && gofmt -l internal/collector/awscloud/services/securitylake/ internal/collector/awscloud/constants_securitylake.go   # no output
cd go && go test ./internal/collector/awscloud/services/securitylake/... -count=1
cd go && go test ./internal/collector/awscloud/... -count=1
cd go && go test ./internal/collector/awscloud/ -run ServiceKind -count=1
cd go && go test ./internal/collector/awscloud/internal/relguard/ ./internal/collector/awscloud/internal/partitionguard/ -count=1
cd go && go test ./cmd/ingester ./cmd/reducer ./cmd/eshu -count=1
cd go && golangci-lint run ./internal/collector/awscloud/...   # 0 issues
cd go && go mod tidy   # no diff
git diff --check   # clean
```

All commands were run and green. The three by-construction AST guards
(`TestScannerServiceKindSwitchesCanonicalize` — 125 scanners checked, relguard
graph-join, partitionguard hardcoded-partition) pass with the new scanner
included automatically.

Closes #1004

author: jackjconner
body:
## Target

- **Component:** portfolio
- **What I changed:** Added a public `FactorRiskModel.factor_risk_breakdown(weights)` read-only attribution method (and a `FactorRiskBreakdown` result dataclass) that splits total portfolio variance into systematic / specific parts plus a per-factor contribution vector, routed entirely through the factored Σ = B·F·Bᵀ + D form.
- **Declared metric this round optimizes:** feature round — additive capability; no metric moves. Bar is no-regression on portfolio `elapsed_s` and golden byte-identical on existing fields.
- **Eval tolerance for the round:** existing `PipelineSummary` fields byte-identical (`--allow-new-fields`); any new field opt-in.

## Gates (quote the actual output)

### Lint & types
Enforced on every commit by `scripts/committer`; confirmed clean on the branch tip.
```
$ scripts/gate lint
All checks passed!
186 files already formatted
All checks passed!
```
No `# type: ignore` / `# noqa` / suppression markers were added.

### Unit tests + Integration tests
```
$ scripts/gate test portfolio/ tests/integration/
408 passed, 1 skipped, 41 warnings in 136.64s (0:02:16)
```
Includes 9 new `factor_risk_breakdown` tests (sum-to-total, per-factor sum-to-factor-variance, match to scalar helpers, match to the dense analytic B·F·Bᵀ+D form, fraction identities, zero-weight edge case, no-duplication vs `factor_component_contrib`). Integration suite imports across components — the additive change does not break any contract.

### Profiling — before → after
Measured by the harness through the bench lock (`scripts/gate bench` → `uv run main.py`), same GenSpec grid + seed + machine.
```
$ scripts/gate bench          # exit 0
portfolio    elapsed_s    ∝ n_assets^0.53  (r²=0.92)
portfolio    elapsed_s    ∝ n_dates^0.00   (r²=0.01)
portfolio    peak_traced_mb ∝ n_assets^0.96 (r²=1.00)
portfolio    peak_rss_mb  ∝ n_assets^0.36  (r²=0.95)
```
The breakdown is **not on the optimizer hot path** — it is a separate read-only method, never called by `mean_variance` or the harness `_portfolio_run`. Portfolio's hot-path scaling (the OSQP solve, `elapsed_s ∝ n_assets^0.53`) is unchanged. No other stage regressed. `check_regressions` vs the ratcheted baseline is the orchestrator's call; the bench ran clean (exit 0).

### Correctness / accuracy
Pure-additive feature; the eval golden is unchanged. All 17 existing `PipelineSummary` fields are byte-identical (deltas at float epsilon, ≤ their tolerances):
```
$ scripts/gate eval --allow-new-fields
  17 PASS  0 FAIL  (total 17 fields)
evalgate: all fields within tolerance.
```
No new field appears in the summary because the breakdown is surfaced only as a public API method (read-only), not wired into `PipelineSummary` this round — the most golden-conservative choice. `--allow-new-fields` is available for a future round that chooses to surface it.

## Why it should merge

The risk model already had a low-level `factor_component_contrib(w)` and scalar `factor_variance`/`specific_variance`/`portfolio_variance`, but no single public call that returns the full systematic/specific/per-factor attribution with the fractions. This PR adds that unified API **on top of** the existing helper (zero math duplication), proven by a test that asserts `factor_contrib` is array-equal to `factor_component_contrib(w)` and a test that matches the dense analytic decomposition. Every gate is green and the production golden is byte-identical.

## How it fits the existing architecture

Lives under `portfolio/risk_model.py`, the existing factor-risk-model layer. `__all__` is **extended** with `FactorRiskBreakdown` (a new symbol, additive — no existing export changed). `_protocol.py` is untouched. The method goes through the factored form (`factor_component_contrib` + `specific_variance`) and never touches `.cov`, so it incurs no n² allocation and respects the module's "structure over density" invariant. The new dataclass mirrors `RebalanceResult` (frozen, documented fields).

## Pros & cons of this approach

- **Pros:** Single-call public attribution; no dense Σ; no math duplication (built on `factor_component_contrib`); fully read-only so the golden is byte-identical; well-tested including the analytic-form and sum identities.
- **Cons / what it trades off:** Returns a fresh dataclass per call (negligible; not on any hot path). Does not (yet) surface in `PipelineSummary` — deliberate, to keep the golden untouched this round.
- **Alternatives considered & rejected:** (1) Returning a plain dict — rejected for a typed frozen dataclass matching the module's `RebalanceResult` convention. (2) Wiring it into `PipelineSummary` now — rejected to keep the golden byte-identical; left as an opt-in follow-up behind `--allow-new-fields`. (3) Recomputing the per-factor vector inline — rejected; reuses `factor_component_contrib`.

## Reproducibility

- Commands: `scripts/gate lint`; `scripts/gate test portfolio/ tests/integration/`; `scripts/gate bench`; `scripts/gate eval --allow-new-fields`.
- Environment: branch `improve/portfolio-risk-decomp`, commit `db5e097`, host as configured for the loop; BLAS threads per `capture_environment` (unchanged from baseline — no compute added to the timed path).
- GenSpec grid + seed: the harness default grid used by `uv run main.py` (same as baseline, before and after).

## Risk & rollback

- **Blast radius:** None to existing behavior — purely additive. No call site invokes the new method, so no downstream component changes; the integration gate (green) covers cross-component imports and would catch any contract break.
- **Rollback:** `git revert <merge sha>` is clean — the change is self-contained to `portfolio/risk_model.py`, `portfolio/__init__.py`, and `portfolio/test_risk_model.py`.

## Ledger

- API requests posted this round: none.

- **pool.rs**: 8 `.lock().unwrap()` → `.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` (poisoned mutex recovery)
- **pool.rs**: semaphore `acquire_owned().await.unwrap()` → graceful fallback (allocate buffer without permit on shutdown)
- **deadlock_detector.rs**: 5 `.lock().unwrap()` → match/ok with appropriate fallbacks (None, empty Vec, 0)

### signer (`crates/signer/`)
- **request_signature_v2.rs**: Added `SignV2Error` enum, `try_pre_sign_v2`, `try_sign_v2` — 14 `unwrap()` replaced with `?`
- **request_signature_streaming.rs**: Added `try_streaming_sign_v4` — 5 `expect("err")` replaced with descriptive `SignV4Error`
- **utils.rs**: `get_host_addr` returns `Result` instead of panicking on host lookup failure
- **lib.rs**: Exported new error types and `try_*` functions

## Verification
```bash
cargo test -p rustfs-io-core
cargo test -p rustfs-signer
cargo clippy -p rustfs-io-core -p rustfs-signer -- -D warnings
```
- 95 io-core tests pass
- 18 signer tests pass
- Clippy clean on both crates

## Impact
Prevents server panics from malformed requests, mutex poisoning, and host lookup failures. No behavioral changes — original functions preserved as backward-compat wrappers.

## Additional Notes
Mutex poisoning recovery via `into_inner()` is safe because poisoned state means a thread panicked while holding the lock, and the data is still valid.

author: arturlins
body:
## Diagnostico

Encontrei alguns problemas na codebase, sendo o mais grave a rota `GET /users` retornando a senha de todos os usuários em texto puro — qualquer chamada à API expunha isso.

Além disso:
- `routes.ts` misturava roteamento, acesso ao banco e lógica de negócio no mesmo arquivo
- O número `220` aparecia no meio de uma condição sem nenhuma explicação
- A lista de status válidos estava escrita à mão em dois lugares
- O campo `category` aceitava qualquer string, sem restrição do compilador
- A lógica de montar a resposta de um ticket estava duplicada em duas rotas
- Algumas rotas usavam `message` nos erros, outras usavam `error`

---

## Mudancas realizadas

- **`src/types.ts`**: adicionei `TicketCategory` como union type e `PublicUser` (User sem senha). O campo `category` em `Ticket` foi trocado de `string` para `TicketCategory`
- **`src/database.ts`** (arquivo novo): movi `readDatabase` e `writeDatabase` para cá, separando o acesso ao banco das rotas. Incluí uma mensagem de erro útil caso o arquivo não exista
- **`src/routes.ts`**: corrigi a exposição de senha em `GET /users`, extraí as constantes `LONG_DESCRIPTION_THRESHOLD` e `VALID_STATUSES`, removi a duplicação criando a função `enrichTicket`, e padronizei os erros para usar sempre `error`
- **`src/server.ts`**: ajustei o erro 404 para seguir o mesmo padrão

---

## Conceitos aplicados

- **Clean Code**: nomes que explicam a intenção (`LONG_DESCRIPTION_THRESHOLD` no lugar de `220`, `toPublicUser`, `enrichTicket`), sem duplicação, respostas de erro consistentes
- **SRP**: `database.ts` cuida só da persistência, `routes.ts` cuida só das rotas
- **TypeScript**: usei union types para restringir os valores aceitos em `category` e `Omit` para garantir que a senha nunca saia nas respostas

---

## Evidencias de funcionamento

```
npm run typecheck  → sem erros
npm run build      → sem erros
npm test           → 11 testes passando (priority, users, database)
```

Testei manualmente os endpoints principais após rodar `npm run seed`:
- `GET /users` não retorna mais o campo `password`
- Erros de validação retornam `{ "error": "..." }` em todas as rotas
- Criação de ticket calcula a prioridade corretamente
- Filtros de ticket funcionando normalmente

---

## Limitacoes conhecidas

- `body.category` não é validado em runtime, só no TypeScript — um valor inválido passado via HTTP não seria barrado
- Leitura e escrita do banco são síncronas, o que pode ser um problema com mais carga
- CORS aberto para qualquer origem
- IDs gerados com `Date.now()` + random, sem garantia de unicidade

author: suprasummus
body:
## Summary

Fix a crash in network-sourced tool parameter handling where empty wire strings deserialize to NULL-backed plainstrings, causing NULL pointer dereferences in tool handlers that assume non-NULL parameters.

## Changes

- Add normalization of NULL `default_param` to empty string `""` in `nwc_tool_t::rdwr()` during deserialization
- This prevents NULL pointers from reaching tool `init()` and `work()` methods that call `atoi(NULL)` or dereference the parameter directly
- Normalization happens at the single point where network-sourced tool parameters enter the tool subsystem, rather than guarding every individual tool

## Implementation Details

The wire protocol cannot distinguish between an empty parameter and "no parameter" — both serialize as zero-length strings. During deserialization, `memory_rw_t::rdwr_str()` leaves the buffer NULL for `len==0`, creating a NULL-backed plainstring. Single-player tool handlers assume the GUI always provides non-NULL `default_param`, so network clients sending empty parameters trigger crashes in downstream code.

The fix centralizes the normalization at deserialization time, converting NULL to `""` before the parameter reaches any tool handler. This is safer and more maintainable than adding NULL checks to every tool that processes parameters.

author: odesenfans
body:
**Bottom of the message-free-supervisor stack.** Base: `dev`.

> Reordered to land *before* the spec-execution work (#954) so that no transient `message_content`-Optional pollution is ever introduced. (Supersedes the earlier #958, which auto-merged when this branch was moved below #954 in the stack.)

`AlephQemuResources` inherited from `AlephFirecrackerResources` purely to reuse host-resource mechanics (volumes, disk accounting, kernel path), even though a QEMU VM is not a Firecracker VM. That coupling forced a single shared `message_content` declaration — so any message-free path (QEMU built from a spec) would have to widen `message_content` to Optional on the shared base, polluting the Firecracker subclasses that always have a message.

### Changes
- New hypervisor-agnostic `VmResources` base (`controllers/resources.py`) holding the shared, message-free surface: `namespace`, `volumes`, `rootfs`/`kernel` paths, `to_dict`, `download_kernel`. The message-coupled mechanics become free functions (`host_volumes_from_message`, `disk_usage_delta`).
- `AlephFirecrackerResources(VmResources)` keeps `message_content` **required** — program/instance dereferences stay clean.
- `AlephQemuResources(VmResources)` owns its **optional** `message_content` (it may be built message-free); the lone rootfs dereference is narrowed with `isinstance(..., InstanceContent)` (QEMU only runs instances).
- `HostVolume` moves to the agnostic module.

### Result
No behaviour change; existing message paths untouched. `mypy src/aleph/vm/` adds zero errors over the `dev` baseline.

### Stack
1. **(this PR)** untangle QEMU resources -> `dev`
2. spec-constructible `VmExecution` -> 1 (#954)
3. pool create path -> #954 (#955)
4. route production creation through the spec -> #955 (#956)
5. reboot-recovery from on-disk configs -> #956 (#957)

author: armaxri
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #757. After that PR landed, reattach via Active Sessions correctly replays the scrollback buffer — but the user reported visual artifacts (e.g. `arne@MacBookPro` rendered one or two characters per line in a narrow column on the left). Root cause: every byte of the scrollback was being written to xterm **twice** because of a race between two parallel buffer-delivery paths.

### The race

1. `apiAttachPersistentTab` → backend → `RemoteProxy::reconnect_existing` → `attach_session` on the agent → `DaemonClient::attach` disconnects + reconnects to the daemon socket. The daemon greets every new connection with a fresh `MSG_BUFFER_REPLAY`, which the agent's `DaemonClient::reader_loop` forwards as live `connection.output` notifications (chunked 64 KiB).
2. `getAgentSessionBuffer` separately fetches the same ring buffer via `session.getBuffer` and writes it through `xterm.write(buffer)`.

The previous `clearPendingOutput(sessionId)` fired *before* `xterm.write`, so any chunks from path (1) that landed in `pendingOutput` while `xterm.write` was still processing got drained again by `subscribeOutput` later. xterm received the full scrollback once via the explicit write and a second time as live output stacked on top — producing the wrap artifacts.

### Fix

Move the `clearPendingOutput` call to run synchronously immediately before `subscribeOutput`. No await sits between the clear and the subscription registration, so every duplicate chunk that accumulated during `xterm.write` is dropped in one shot.

Also includes a one-shot `DEBUG/reattach` log dumping the tail of the fetched buffer + current xterm dimensions, so any remaining rendering quirks can be diagnosed against the actual bytes from the LogViewer.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test --run src/components/Terminal/ src/store/` — 358 vitest tests pass.
- [ ] **Manual** (MT-AGENT-14): close a persistent agent shell tab with visible scrollback, reattach via Active Sessions, confirm the scrollback renders once at full width (no narrow leftmost column of single characters, no `%`-line artifacts beyond zsh's normal `PROMPT_SP` on resize).

author: lmassaroli
body:
## Problem

A user reported (live, branch `main`) that on the custom scenario **Battle of the Green Fork**, every unit that enters combat gets **infinite stamina**, **can't be charged**, and shows a literal **`NaN`** where the stamina bar should be.

Root cause: the scenario was saved by an older editor that wrote formation flank angles as `flankMin`/`flankMax`, but the engine reads `minFlankAngle`/`maxFlankAngle` (`BaseUnit.getFlankMod`). The canonical keys were left `undefined`, so:

```
degreesToRadians(undefined) -> NaN
  -> getFlankingPercent(...) returns NaN   (theta <= NaN and theta >= NaN are both false)
  -> charge stamina cost (75_00 * (1 - NaN) + 25_00) -> NaN
  -> changes.stamina -= NaN
  -> clamp(NaN, 0, max) returns NaN         (NaN < min / NaN > max both false: passthrough)
  -> stamina is permanently NaN
```

That single NaN explains all three symptoms: `getStaminaProportion()` is NaN so `isRunning`'s `NaN > lowerModifierLimit` is false (can't charge), the bar never drains (infinite), and the JSX gate `{unit.stamina && unit.maxStamina && <Bar/>}` renders a bare `NaN` text node.

## Fix (three layers)

1. **Root cause** — `normalizeScenario` migrates legacy `flankMin`/`flankMax` -> canonical `minFlankAngle`/`maxFlankAngle`. This is the universal load chokepoint (all game-create and validation paths normalize first), so it heals old files and reaches live games via `createGameMetadata` -> `copyScenarioCustomDefs`.
2. **Defense in depth** — `getFlankMod` returns `0` (no flank) when the angles aren't finite, so no malformed custom content can poison combat math again, including games already in flight.
3. **Import validation** — `validateScenarioCustomDefs` now requires formation flank angles, and requires `runCost`/`walkMovement` **only when the unit can run** (`runMovement > 0`). Immobile units (walls / static artillery) that legitimately omit movement stats stay valid; verified against the real scenario so a working file is not rejected.

author: isamisushi
body:
## What

Adds two options to `createStore` in `@crustjs/store`:

- `mode` — permission bits for the persisted store file (e.g. `0o600`)
- `dirMode` — permission bits for the parent directory (e.g. `0o700`)

```ts
const auth = createStore({
  dirPath: configDir("my-cli"),
  name: "auth",
  fields: { token: { type: "string" } },
  mode: 0o600,    // file: rw-------
  dirMode: 0o700, // dir: rwx------ (only when created)
});
```

## Why

Config/state stores commonly hold secrets (tokens, API keys, auth metadata). Today `writeJson` writes with neither an explicit `mode` nor a `chmod`, so the resulting file permissions are **umask-dependent** — under a typical `umask 022` the file becomes `0o644` (world-readable). For a library that positions itself as local persistence for CLIs, keeping secrets owner-only is closer to the library's responsibility than the caller's.

This lets callers opt in to owner-only persistence without each CLI re-implementing its own `chmod`.

## How

- `mode` is enforced **exactly** on the temp file (via `chmod`) **before** the atomic rename, regardless of `umask`. Since rename preserves the inode mode, the persisted file is never momentarily group/other-readable.
- `dirMode` is applied only when a write actually creates the directory (detected via `mkdir(..., { recursive: true })`'s return value); a pre-existing directory is left untouched so callers retain control of it.
- When `mode`/`dirMode` are omitted, behavior is unchanged (platform default, umask-derived) — fully backward compatible.

## Platform behavior / known limitation

`mode` and `dirMode` are enforced on **macOS and Linux** (POSIX permission bits). On **Windows** they are **not enforced** — Windows uses ACLs, not Unix permission bits — and the store neither throws nor warns. This is documented in the README / module docs, which point Windows users to the per-user profile ACL (`%APPDATA%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%`) and the OS credential store (Credential Manager / DPAPI) for strong secret confidentiality. A runtime warning was intentionally avoided: the store's contract is to throw/return, never print, and the profile-dir ACL already provides a baseline, so a warning would be cry-wolf.

## Affected areas

- `packages/store` — new public `CreateStoreOptions.mode` / `dirMode`, `writeJson` permission handling
- Docs — `packages/store/README.md`, `apps/docs/content/docs/modules/store.mdx`
- Changeset — `@crustjs/store` minor (additive public API)

## Testing

- `bun run check:types` — passes (23/23)
- `bun run check` — passes for all changed files
- `bun test` (store) — passes; added coverage for: exact mode under `umask 0`, no group/other bits, `dirMode` on dir creation, pre-existing dir untouched, default behavior when no mode given, and an end-to-end `createStore({ mode })` test

author: krystophny
body:
## Direct Liric backend (`--backend=liric`): first slice, for discussion

This opens a direct, LLVM-free code generator for LFortran, built on [liric](https://github.com/krystophny/liric) (a minimal C11 IR compiler). It lowers ASR straight to a native object through the liric C session API, with no LLVM in the pipeline.

This is the **first slice**, deliberately small and reviewable. `src/libasr/codegen/asr_to_liric.cpp` is 282 lines and covers scalar integer arithmetic, comparisons, assignment, `if`, and `error stop`: enough to compile and run integration test `expr_02`. Unsupported ASR nodes raise a clear error rather than miscompiling. Coverage grows slice by slice in follow-up PRs; each labels the integration tests it makes pass.

For context, the full backend on the integration branch already passes **100% of the LLVM integration-test corpus**: https://github.com/krystophny/lfortran/tree/liric-showcase . This PR is the reviewable bottom of that work, not a dump of it.

### Building it

Off by default. One flag turns it on; liric is fetched and built automatically (pinned to `v0.0.1`):

```
cmake -DWITH_LIRIC=ON ...
```

No manual liric checkout is needed. `-DLIRIC_ROOT=/path/to/liric` uses an existing checkout instead of fetching. Default builds (`WITH_LIRIC=no`) fetch nothing and are byte-for-byte unaffected.

### Compile time

Direct lowering skips LLVM IR construction and its passes. For `expr_02` (`lfortran -c`, 50 iterations) the backends are near par because the file is tiny and the time is dominated by process start and parsing:

| test | liric | llvm |
|------|------:|-----:|
| expr_02 | 8.8 ms | 9.2 ms |

The codegen advantage widens on larger inputs (e.g. on the integration branch, object compiles of `doloop_01` run ~1.7x faster under liric than LLVM). Later slices will report these as their coverage grows.

### Scope of this PR

- `src/libasr/codegen/asr_to_liric.{cpp,h}`: the backend, gated behind `WITH_LIRIC` (`HAVE_LFORTRAN_LIRIC`).
- CLI `--backend=liric`, build wiring, `FetchContent` of liric `v0.0.1`.
- `liric` registered as an integration-test backend, with `expr_02` labeled.

The runtime keeps building through the existing path and the liric program links the standard runtime. Compiling the runtime through liric (for faster linking) needs module and parameter support and is a deliberate later slice, not part of this one.

### Verification

```
$ scripts/lf.sh --with-liric itest -b liric
1/1 Test #1: expr_02 ..........................   Passed
100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 1
```

Existing backends and tests are untouched (`WITH_LIRIC=no` by default).

author: jouider
body:
## Bug
When a manager updates a gestionnaire's `app_permissions` (Équipe → Utilisateurs), the gestionnaire's sidebar keeps showing the old set of modules until they **log out and log back in**. Zustand `persist` stores the user payload in localStorage and only refreshes it on `/auth/login`.

## Fix
- Add a `refreshIdentity({ user, tenant })` action to `authStore` (updates user + tenant in place, keeps the existing token).
- Call `me()` once on `GestionnaireLayout` mount and pipe the result into `refreshIdentity`.

A simple page reload (F5) now picks up permission changes — no logout needed.

## Test plan
- [x] Existing logged-in gestionnaire: page reload → sidebar matches latest backend `app_permissions`
- [x] Manager changes gestionnaire's permissions → gestionnaire reloads → sidebar updates
- [x] Network failure during `/auth/me` doesn't crash the layout (caught silently; axios 401 interceptor handles auth)

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive documentation for django-iceberg's role as a serverless, object-storage database layer for React API Stack. It establishes the architectural vision, design rationale, and performance roadmap for running Django as stateless compute over S3-backed Iceberg tables.

- **New documentation** (`docs/serverless-storage-engine.md`):

  - Reordered roadmap items to prioritize the custom S3 backend + DynamoDB caching and EFS hot tier

author: d-biehl
body:
Fixes #196.

### Problem

Activating a Hatch environment in a **PowerShell** terminal fails with a `ParserError` when the Hatch executable path contains a space (e.g. the standalone installer's `C:\Program Files\Hatch\hatch.EXE`). The host quotes the executable, and PowerShell parses a leading quoted string as an *expression* rather than a command to run:

```
"C:\Program Files\Hatch\hatch.EXE" --env=devel.py3.14-rf74 shell
ParserError: Unexpected token 'env=devel.py3.14-rf74' in expression or statement.
```

Invoking a quoted executable in PowerShell requires the call operator `&`. The `ms-python.vscode-python-envs` host adds it automatically on its *run* path (`runInTerminal.ts`) but **not** on the *activation* path (`getShellCommandAsString`), so the manager has to supply it for PowerShell — which the built-in venv/poetry managers do, but this manager did not.

### Fix

Add a `pwsh`-specific `shellActivation` entry that prefixes the call operator, matching the built-in managers (`{ executable: '&', args: [...] }`). A lone `&` is left unquoted by the host's quoting, producing:

```
& "C:\Program Files\Hatch\hatch.EXE" --env devel.py3.14-rf74 shell
```

`'pwsh'` covers both Windows PowerShell 5.x and PowerShell 7; cmd/bash/zsh/fish keep using the shared `'unknown'` entry, where `&` is neither needed nor valid. The `--env` flag and its value are now passed as separate args so only the value is quoted when needed.

### Testing

Verified manually on Windows with PowerShell — activation now works. `tsc --noEmit` and `biome check` pass.

author: twschiller
body:
## Summary

- New defense rule `cross-origin-frame-hide` (experimental, **off by default**) that replaces every cross-origin `<iframe>` with a click-to-reveal placeholder, so a browser-use agent reading the parent page doesn't ingest the embedded-origin content unless the user opts in. Same-origin, `srcdoc`, and inert (`about:`/`javascript:`/`data:`/`blob:`) frames are left alone. Runs in every frame, so cross-origin frames nested inside same-origin frames are also caught.
- Adds a globe icon for the rule in `RULE_ICON_PATHS`.
- Documents the rule under *Prompt-injection defense* in `docs/src/content/docs/rules.md`, with a link to the motivating paper: Roesner & Kohlbrenner, [*Agentic Browsers and the Same-Origin Policy*](https://www.franziroesner.com/pdf/roesner_kohlbrenner_2026_agentic_sop.pdf) (ICLR 2026 Workshop). Updates the `agent-browser-shield-config` skill's rule list.

The paper shows current agentic browsers vary widely in how they honor the same-origin policy when reading page content. A successful prompt injection plus cross-origin read access lets an attacker page exfiltrate content from an embedded sensitive iframe — i.e., SOP becomes soft. Removing the iframe entirely is a stronger defense than provenance-only annotation; an annotation-only defense bets on the model behavior we can't verify.

author: copilot
body:
videsc had 450+ uncovered statements at 67% coverage. This adds 64 targeted tests in `tests/test_videsc_coverage2.py` bringing coverage to 90%.

## Coverage gains

| Module | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `pipeline/vllm_runner.py` | 45% | 98% |
| `main.py` | 38% | 96% |
| `model/loader.py` | 54% | 94% |
| `audio/transcription.py` | 63% | 87% |
| `pipeline/runner.py` | 51% | 71% |
| `describe.py` | 87% | 98% |
| `utils/helpers.py` | 93% | 100% |

## Approach

Tests avoid installing heavy ML deps (torch, transformers, torchcodec) via a `_import_fresh()` helper that injects sys.modules stubs before module import:

```python
def _import_fresh(monkeypatch, module_name, stubs=None):
    for name, stub in (stubs or {}).items():
        monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, name, stub)
    sys.modules.pop(module_name, None)
    return importlib.import_module(module_name)

# Example: test loader.py without torch installed
torch_stub = types.SimpleNamespace(float16=..., bfloat16=..., ...)
mod = _import_fresh(monkeypatch, "videsc.model.loader", {"torch": torch_stub})
```

Notable non-obvious fixes required during authoring:
- **Import-time binding**: `from transformers import pipeline as asr_pipeline` binds at import; stub must carry the real callable *before* `_import_fresh`, not after
- **Locally-imported cv2**: patched via `patch("cv2.VideoCapture")` rather than through the module namespace
- **Lazily-imported helpers**: `expand_inputs` imported inside `run_batch_vllm` — patched at `videsc.utils.helpers.expand_inputs`
- **ffmpeg in gemma4 multi-chunk**: `patch("subprocess.run")` to prevent actual ffmpeg invocations in dry-run multi-chunk tests

author: remyluslosius
body:
## Summary

Brings the Go liveness loop to parity with the Python OpenWatch adaptive monitor: ICMP ping → SSH banner → sudo, with per-layer counters and the 5-band state (online / degraded / critical / down / maintenance / unknown).

### Before (v1.2.x)

The probe was single-layer (TCP banner only). State was binary `reachable`/`unreachable` + a single failure counter. Operators couldn't tell whether a `down` host was off the network, had SSH stopped, or just had broken sudo.

### After (v1.3.0)

Short-circuit chain:

| Failure point     | Band       | What it tells the operator                    |
|-------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| ping              | `down`     | Host is off the network                       |
| ssh banner        | `critical` | Daemon down, firewall, wrong port             |
| sudo -n true      | `degraded` | Sudo broken — host is up but not scannable    |
| all pass          | `online`   | Healthy                                       |

Live verification against the user's 9-host fleet showed exactly this differentiation — what looked like "9 hosts down" in v1.2.x split into 4 online, 4 degraded (broken sudo), 1 critical (SSH actually down).

## Design choices

- **Raw socket ICMP** via `golang.org/x/net/icmp`. Tries privileged `ip4:icmp` (needs `CAP_NET_RAW`), falls back to unprivileged `udp4` (needs `net.ipv4.ping_group_range` sysctl). Either failure logs a `WARN` and the chain silently drops to SSH-only mode. RPM/DEB packaging will need a `setcap` in postinstall; documented in the spec.
- **Credential isolation**: the `liveness` package never imports `internal/credential` or `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` (AC-14 invariant — enforced by source-inspection test). The privilege check is an injected `PrivilegeProbeFunc` whose implementation lives in the new `internal/sshprivilege` package.
- **Per-layer hysteresis**: six counters (ping/ssh/privilege × fail/ok). Recovery to `online` needs N consecutive all-layer passes so a single good probe doesn't flap the UI.
- **Per-host maintenance**: `hosts.maintenance_mode = true` excludes the row from `listProbeTargets` entirely. No probe, no audit, no history. Resume picks up at the prior band.
- **Priority ordering**: tick query is `ORDER BY hosts.check_priority DESC, hl.next_probe_at ASC NULLS FIRST` so critical hosts drain before stable ones at high fleet scale.
- **Append-only history**: every probe optionally writes one row to `host_monitoring_history` with per-layer ok flags + failed layer. Surfaces the "why is this host degraded" drill-down. Off by default.

## Spec

- `system-liveness-loop` v1.2.1 → v1.3.0
- New constraints: C-18 (multi-layer routing), C-19 (per-layer hysteresis), C-20 (priority + maintenance), C-21 (history table), C-22 (credential isolation re-affirmed)
- New ACs: AC-28..AC-36 (nine total)

## API

- `PUT /api/v1/hosts/{id}/maintenance` — toggle per-host pause
- `GET /api/v1/hosts/{id}/monitoring/history?limit=N` — tail history
- `HostLiveness` response gains `monitoring_state` and per-layer counter fields

## Migration

`0016_host_monitoring_multilayer.sql` adds:
- 7 columns to `host_liveness` (6 counters + monitoring_state)
- 2 columns to `hosts` (maintenance_mode, check_priority)
- New `host_monitoring_history` table with btree indexes
- Partial index on `(check_priority DESC, id)` for the tick query

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./internal/liveness/... -count=1` passes (10 new test cases)
- [x] `specter coverage` — system-liveness-loop at 36/36 (100%)
- [x] Live multi-host verification — 4 online / 4 degraded / 1 critical (matches actual sudo/SSH state)
- [ ] CI integration tests with `OPENWATCH_TEST_DSN`

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Build a unified job application automation system that streamlines resume tailoring and cover letter generation for multiple job types (internship, apprenticeship, full-time position, training program) across both French and English languages.

## Current State

You have:
- **Master CV files** (HTML & PDF in both FR/EN) with comprehensive professional experience, projects, skills, and education

- **Example outputs** showing the desired quality (Safran AI Engineer CV and cover letter)

Create an automation entry point and supporting infrastructure that enables you to generate tailored resumes and cover letters by simply specifying:
- **Job type** (stage, alternance, poste, formation)
- **Language** (fr, en)

author: dthoma1
body:
## AC-RFC-003-field-additive parser/test floor

Implements the #137 lane assigned to vesper-valley / dthoma1: the wire-side RFC-003 DNS-TXT parser contract before the network lookup/cache layer lands.

### What changed

Adds a parser in `src/relay_client.rs` for RFC-003 §2 records:

```
_wire-org.<domain> TXT "did=<wire-DID>; relay=<url>; sso_iss=<iss>; sso_tenant=<tenant>; v=1"
```

Contract pinned:

- Known `v=1` records ignore unknown fields (field-additive forward compatibility from RFC-001 §A / RFC-003 §2).
- Unknown `v` values reject at parse time (value-level rule; no silent semantics drift).
- `did=` prefix-dispatches both accepted anchor kinds from #136:
  - `did:wire:org:*` → organizational anchor
  - `did:wire:op:*` → personal-tier operator anchor
- Session DIDs / arbitrary strings are rejected.
- Duplicate known fields are rejected to avoid ambiguous security semantics.

### Tests

- org/op DID prefix dispatch
- unknown `v` rejection + session DID rejection
- duplicate known-field rejection
- `proptest`: arbitrary unknown fields at known `v=1` are ignored
- `proptest`: every unknown `v` value rejects

### Validation

- `cargo fmt --check` ✅
- `cargo test relay_client::tests::parse_wire_org_txt_record` ✅ — 5 targeted tests passed, including the two proptests

### Scope

Parser-only by design. The actual DNS lookup/cache wiring belongs to AC-RFC-003-DNS-TXT-pin; this PR gives that follow-up a tested parser instead of letting each implementer re-create TXT field semantics.

author: cradlen
body:
The composite examination write (encounter + vitals + 10 findings + diagnoses/ investigations/prescription diffs + full patient-history diff) runs in one interactive transaction. On Neon its queries serialize on a single connection, so legitimate work exceeded Prisma's 5s default (observed 5307ms) → P2028.

- Give the examination $transaction real headroom: { timeout: 20s, maxWait: 10s }.
- Drop a redundant in-tx envelope read-back: ObgynHistoryService.applyPatch ended with composeEnvelope(tx, …) — a second 6-table loadChildren inside the write tx whose result the examination flow discards. applyPatch now returns the lightweight singleton row; the (unwired) history patch() wrapper composes the envelope outside its transaction, preserving its public shape.

author: antonioventilii
body:
## What

The onboarding first-call card's swipe-guide coach now shows **every time** the user reaches that onboarding step, instead of being suppressed once-per-browser. This is a deliberate divergence from the canonical (which shows the deck coach once per device): during onboarding we always want to teach the swipe.

## Suppression removed

The bespoke first-call card `OnboardingBeat1Card` already renders a built-in directional coach (`.ob-coach`) gated only by an in-mount `everInteracted` guard — no localStorage of its own. The latent cross-visit gate lived in `FlowCoach`'s `surface="onboarding"` branch, which persisted `vici.coach-onboarding-seen` in localStorage. That branch was never actually instantiated (only `surface="flow"` is rendered, in `FlowMode`), so it was dead code that nonetheless carried the once-per-browser suppression intended for this step. Removing it guarantees no persisted suppression can ever gate the onboarding coach.

## Changes

- `FlowCoach.svelte`: drop the `surface` prop and the `vici.coach-onboarding-seen` path; it is now flow-deck only and keeps its per-device `vici.coach-flow-seen` persistence unchanged. Phase targeting narrows to `.flow-card`.
- `FlowMode.svelte`: `<FlowCoach />` (no surface prop).
- `OnboardingFlow.svelte`: pin `showCoach` on explicitly at Beat 1b so the always-on intent is load-bearing.
- `OnboardingBeat1Card.svelte`: doc/comment updates only.
- `app.css`: remove the now-dead `.ob-card[data-coach-phase]` selectors.

## Behaviour preserved

- In-session `everInteracted` hide (coach fades after the first drag/commit within the step) is kept — that's correct.
- The real Flow-deck `FlowCoach` stays once-per-browser via `vici.coach-flow-seen`.

## Why a returning user sees it again

The onboarding coach's only gates are `showCoach && !everInteracted && committed === null`. On a fresh visit to Beat 1b the card remounts: `everInteracted=false`, `committed=null`, `showCoach=true` (pinned). There is no localStorage read anywhere in this path (the only onboarding-seen key has been removed), so a user who saw it before sees it again every time.

## Gates

`npx svelte-kit sync`, `eslint` (exit 0), `prettier --check`, `npm run check` (0 errors / 0 warnings) all green. No message catalogs touched.

author: grahamcampbell
body:
Empty array header values are currently warned about by Guzzle but can still be passed into PSR-7 in a couple of paths. Client default headers are the awkward case because they are moved into conditional headers before request option validation runs, so PSR-7 can end up emitting its own deprecation.

This normalizes default headers at client construction and drops empty array header values before creating or modifying the PSR-7 request. When a request-level empty header suppresses a default header with the same name, the matching conditional default is removed too, so the default does not leak back in after normalization.

When this is merged forward, 8.0 already rejects these header shapes natively, so the source change should be resolved against that stricter validation rather than carrying over the 7.11 deprecation shim verbatim.

author: cjnoname
body:
## Summary

Closes #170.

Adds support for referencing images **externally** (by URL or local file path) instead of embedding their bytes. Linked images are written as `<a:blip r:link>` with a relationship using `TargetMode="External"` — no bytes are stored in the `.xlsx` package, so the file stays small.

```ts
// URL
const id = workbook.addImage({ extension: "png", link: "https://example.com/logo.png" });
worksheet.addImage(id, "B2:D6");

// Local file
const id2 = workbook.addImage({ extension: "png", link: "file:///C:/images/logo.png" });
worksheet.addImage(id2, "F2:H6");
```

## What's supported

| Placement | External (linked)? |
| --- | --- |
| Cell picture (`ws.addImage`) | ✅ |
| Overlay watermark (`addWatermark({ mode: "overlay" })`) | ✅ |
| Worksheet background (`addBackgroundImage`) | ❌ rejected (Excel drops External backgrounds) |
| Header/footer VML watermark (`addWatermark({ mode: "header" })`) | ❌ rejected (VML needs embedded media) |

Unsupported placements **throw an `ImageError`** up front (before mutating any state) rather than producing a file Excel would silently repair. If both bytes and a `link` are supplied, **embedding wins**.

## Notes / caveats (Excel behaviour, not this library)

- Linked images are volatile — a moved/missing target shows a broken-image placeholder.
- Excel desktop does not auto-download remote URL images by default (security); the user must grant access. Verified on macOS Excel: once granted, both URL and `file://` linked images render correctly.

## Implementation

- `ImageData.link` field; `buildImageRel` chooses embed vs External target in one place (shared by cell-picture and watermark write paths)
- `blip-xform` renders `r:link` for external, `r:embed` for embedded; reader parses both
- `addMedia` (non-streaming + streaming) skips writing bytes for external media
- Content-types skips Default registration for external-only images
- Reader synthesises/dedupes linked media from External rels by link

## Tests / docs

- 17 integration tests (write, read, round-trip, streaming, dedup, hyperlink combo, XML-escaping, extension inference, rejection + no-state-mutation cases)
- Full suite green (`pnpm check`, all excel + full vitest)
- Runnable example `examples/images-external.ts`; docs in README (EN/ZH), `addImage`/`addWatermark` JSDoc, and `FROM_EXCELJS.md`

author: indyjonesnl
body:
## Root cause (read from the 2026-05-31 run, networking cluster #23)
`[sig-network] Proxy version v1 A set of valid responses are returned for both pod and service` (proxy.go:503) sends OPTIONS (and other methods) through the pod/service proxy subresource and json-parses the backend response. DELETE worked (`StatusCode:200 | Response:foo`), but **OPTIONS returned an empty body** → `Failed to process jsonResponse. unexpected end of JSON input` (proxy.go:578).

Cause: the 7 proxy route registrations enumerated only `get/post/put/patch/delete`, so OPTIONS/HEAD hit axum's **405** and never reached the handler. The proxy is method-agnostic upstream, and the handler already forwards the request method verbatim — only the routing was fixed-set.

## Fix
All proxy routes (pod root/`/`/`*path`, service root/`/`/`*path`, node) → `any(handler)`. Every method now reaches the handler and is forwarded.

## Test
Router-level regression: OPTIONS and HEAD on the pod proxy route are routed (not 405) and reach the same handler outcome as GET. 5 existing proxy tests still pass.
